body:
## Why

사용자 결정(2026-11-27): 이 저장소는 squash와 merge commit 병합도 허용합니다. 따라서 리뷰 중에 브랜치 히스토리를 다시 쓰거나(fixup·autosquash·재적층·force-push) 커밋마다 시험을 돌리는 비용이 더 이상 필요 없습니다.
- 이번 세션에서 PR 하나의 Fix가 커밋별 전체 pytest로 약 26분을 썼습니다(로컬 1회 측정).

## What

AGENTS.md에 "Pull requests and history" 절을 추가합니다.
- **병합 방식:** 기본은 squash이고, merge commit과 rebase도 허용합니다. PR 제목은 Conventional Commit으로 씁니다(squash 커밋 제목이 되므로).
- **브랜치 히스토리:** 다듬지 않습니다. Fix는 위에 쌓고, base 따라잡기는 merge 또는 rebase로 하며, 리뷰 중인 브랜치는 force-push하지 않습니다.
- **검증:** push한 SHA에서 전체 시험을 한 번 돌리고 CI를 봅니다. 커밋마다 시험을 돌리지 않습니다.

- `python3 tools/repo_guard.py` → exit 0.

author: heshanpadmasiri
body:
- Closes #1252

## Goals

A class's `init` method was part of the class's object semtype, so classes that differ only in `init` were treated as different types. This went against §6.8.1.5: "Any init method is not part of the shape of an object". As a result, `Base b = new Derived("d")` was rejected and `is` returned `false` at runtime.

- Remove `init`, both declared and default, from class object semtypes. Assignability, `is` and casts then ignore `init`.
- Reject a method-decl named `init` in an object type descriptor (§5.6.3.3), and stop inclusion from copying one into a class.
- Keep `new`, implicit `new` on a union, the isolated-`new` check and the object filler rule (§5.9.1) working by reading the init type from the class's method table instead of from the shape.

## Non goals

- `self.init()` in a class with no declared `init` is still rejected (#1861).
- `c.init()` on a receiver other than `self` (#1592).
- `readonly & R r = new` and defaulted-init fillers (#1276). Both behave as they already do on `main`.

## Design

```
semtypes
  ObjectAlternative{objectType, initFunctionType}   removed
  ObjectAlternatives(cx, t) []ObjectAlternative  →  []SemType
  objectFiller                                     no longer checks init (no init in the shape)

context
+ CompilerContext.ClassInitFunctionType(cx, objectTy) (SemType, ok)
      sole positive atom → method table → owner must be a ClassSymbol
      → declared init's type, else env.defaultInitFunctionType()
+ CompilerEnvironment.defaultInitFunctionType()    `isolated function () returns ()`, built once (sync.Once)

semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go
  buildObjectDirectMembers
-   initDirectMember (added init to the shape)
+   validateInitReturnType (keeps the "invalid return type for init function" check)
  resolveObjectType          init method-decl → error "method name 'init' is not allowed in an object type descriptor"
  objectTypeMembers          skips init method-decls (so inclusion never copies one)
  isPublicObjectTypeMember / isPublicInclusionMember   init special cases dropped
  constructibleAlternatives  → []model.MethodTable
  resolveObjectInitArgs      init type = t.symbolType(initRef)
  finishObjectNew            result = Intersect(determinedTy, classTy)

semantics/internal/analysis
  constructors.go  + fillerAvailable / initAcceptsNoArgs  (the §5.9.1 filler rule, moved here from semtypes)
  scope/isolation.go  isolationNewExpr uses ClassInitFunctionType
```

- The init type now comes from the method table, not the semtype. Classes whose shapes differ only in `init` therefore remain separate candidates for implicit `new` on a union, because each class has its own atom and method table.
- Implicit `new` now narrows its result to the selected class (`Intersect(determinedTy, classTy)`) instead of widening it to the whole expected type. Once `init` left the shape, the widening typed a value as the whole union when the expected type was a union of distinct classes. It already did this for a distinct class in a union with an object type.
- The filler rule needs the init method, which is no longer in the shape, so it moves from `semtypes` into list-constructor analysis.

## Blast radius

- Public API changes:
  - `semtypes`: `ObjectAlternative` type (with `Type()` and `InitFunctionType()`) removed; `ObjectAlternatives` now returns `[]SemType`.
  - `context`: `CompilerContext.ClassInitFunctionType` added.
- Scope: mostly internal to the compiler front end (type resolver and semantic analysis), plus the two exported API changes above.
- User-visible effects:
  - Programs that assign or test classes differing only in `init` now compile, and `is` returns `true` at runtime (the #1252 reproducers).
  - Non-distinct classes with the same fields and methods are now indistinguishable by `is`, even if their `init`s differ. This follows the spec, but `a is First` on a `First|Second` value can now be `true` for a `Second`.
  - `init` in an object type descriptor (named or inline, including one reached through inclusion) is now a compile error. Programs that compiled before can now fail.
  - Type names in diagnostics and BIR dumps no longer include `public function init(...)`. Many golden files change for this reason alone. Some messages now read oddly, for example `expected object { int x }, got object { int x }` in `member-visibility-field-e`, because the private or distinct parts that tell the two types apart are not printed.

## Foot guns

- `ClassInitFunctionType` returns `ok == false` for types with no sole positive object atom, or whose method table is not owned by a class (for example inline object types). Callers treat that as "not constructible" or "not isolated". A future caller that ignores `ok` would read a zero `SemType`.
- Anything that still needs the init type has to go through the method table (`ClassInitFunctionType` or `t.symbolType(initRef)`). Looking up `"init"` with `ObjectMemberType` now returns nothing.

## Tests

- New corpus tests (subset10):
  - shape: `10-bug/class-init-shape-{assign1,incl1,is1}-v`
  - implicit `new` narrowing: `10-bug/new-union-distinct-{class1,object-type1}-v`
  - default init is isolated: `10-isolated/new-default-init1-v`
  - filler rule: `10-list/object-filler-{init-args1,init-error1,nested-list1,object-type1}-e`
  - union selection: `10-object/new-union-init-shape1-v`
  - §5.6.3.3: `10-object/object-type-init-decl1-e`
- New project test `corpus/project/class-init-shape-cross-module-v`.
- `corpus/project/inclusion-cross-module-init-v` is replaced by `inclusion-cross-module-init-e`, because it included an object type that declares `init`, which is now an error.
- `10-object/new-union-method-default1-v` now identifies the selected class with a `kind()` method instead of `is First`, since `First` and `Second` now have the same shape.
- Existing AST, CFG, BIR and diagnostic goldens are regenerated wherever a printed type used to contain `init`.
- `TestProjectSerializationRoundtrip` now also honours `isSkipKey("project/…")` pending skips, matching the integration test (separate commit).

## For human review

- Classes that differ only in `init` now satisfy `is` for each other (spec-conforming). Confirm this is acceptable for the rewritten `new-union-method-default1-v`.
- Implicit `new` now narrows its result type to the selected class instead of widening it to the expected type.
- `self.init()` in a class with no declared `init` stays rejected; the follow-up is #1861.
- Diagnostics such as `expected object { int x }, got object { int x }` are now ambiguous. Improving how types are printed is left out of this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Class construction now handles initializer selection more consistently across union types, inheritance, and cross-module use.
  * Classes without an explicit initializer can be constructed using the default initializer.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Empty and nested list initializers now report errors when required object values cannot be created, such as when a class initializer requires arguments or can fail.
  * Type checks and diagnostics no longer treat class initializers as regular object members.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified how class initializers are checked when matching values to class types.

author: stxkxs
body:
The vendored id-masking gate and mask core are tested by their own self-tests, which `test_workflow_id_masking.py` runs in the suite's own process. There they reached 98% of the gate's lines and 97% of its branches, and 99% and 98% of the core's. Three things were left unreached:
- rules this repository's policy planted no case for;
- the core's `main()` entry, which CI's `mask-aws-ids.sh --self-test` goes through;
- the gate's refusal to run without tomllib or PyYAML. Its self-test proves that only in a child process, which the coverage run does not see.

This change plants the missing cases and runs both entries in the suite's process. It then holds each file to what that reaches: the core at 100/100, and the gate at (99.9, 99.6).

## What changed

**`scripts/workflow-id-masking.toml`** plants six more cases the gate must reject. Each is rejected at its mutated line, by its rule:

| Case | The rule it plants |
|---|---|
| every variable value through an object filter, `join(vars.*, ',')` | a filter over the `vars` context is refused |
| a variable read in a job granted `write-all` | a job that can hold AWS credentials reads no variable |
| a role ARN assembled around an account id secret | an id-named key takes a secret only whole |
| an id-named key in the workflow-level `env` | at workflow level, only the guard form |
| an environment id whose needs share a job, none refusing the inherited name | the refuse-inherited-config rule, followed through transitive needs |
| a guard written with a double-quoted string | an expression the gate cannot read is refused |

It also adds this repository's first `[[accepted]]` edits. Each is a change the gate must pass with no finding anywhere:
- a comment above the mask command;
- AWS's documentation account id, `123456789012`, in a message;
- a secret named outside the id rule, read in a job that can hold AWS credentials;
- an id-named key fed from an output of the mask step.

**`scripts/tests/test_workflow_id_masking.py`**:
- runs the core's self-test through `main(["--self-test"])`, the way CI reaches it;
- loads the gate first with tomllib unavailable, then with PyYAML unavailable, and requires exit 2 and the refusal each time.

**`scripts/tests/run.py`**:
- holds `mask-aws-ids.py` at 100/100, among the security-critical files;
- holds the gate to the tenth just under what it reaches, so one more line or branch left unreached fails the run. A whole-number floor could not catch that, because one of the gate's 1229 lines is 0.08%.
- `PER_GATE_FLOORS` accepts tenths. The per-file loop names its floor separately from the totals' loop, so mypy reads both as float.

**What the gate still leaves unreached:** line 1018, and the branches 1014→1018 and 1588→1587. Only a tree with no `scripts/vendored.json`, whose policy vendors nothing, takes them. That is landing-zone's own tree, and never a copy's. The self-test plants no such tree. Once landing-zone's self-test does, the gate is re-vendored with its record and held at 100 here.

## Checks run on this branch

All local, at this head (`bb16c19`, on `68320f3`), under Python 3.15.2 with the lock installed `--require-hashes`:
- `scripts/check-workflow-id-masking.py --self-test` passes. It rejects 59 mutations (the policy's 58 and the gate's own quoting case) and accepts the 4 permitted edits. Each new case is decided by the rule it names.
- `scripts/check-workflow-id-masking.py` passes the tree.
- `COVERAGE_REQUIRED=1 coverage run --rcfile=.coveragerc scripts/tests/run.py`: 1483 tests across 42 modules pass, and all 23 per-file floors hold. The gate reaches 1228 of 1229 lines and 514 of 516 branches; the core reaches 184 of 184 and 74 of 74.
- `scripts/tests/controls.py`: 25 controls each complete a proof, the id-masking gate's among them.
- `scripts/tests/empty-corpus.py`: all 36 probed gates refuse an empty corpus.
- `scripts/tests/reverify-tests.sh` runs in CI's gate-tests job. This change adds no probe and changes none: the vendored files carry none, since an edit to either fails its record first.
- ruff, ruff format, mypy over `scripts/`, and yamllint all pass.

body:
Depends on #4535 (casino screens; merged, so this is on main e1127821d). Closes #4762.
Not related to Azza's networking (#3795 and its PRs): no network code.

## What changed

- **Poker tables** (`nvf-play` `poker_tables.rs`, new): the swap itself. The tables are the
  placed references to each casino's `BlackjackTable*` base object; per casino, the ones lying
  furthest toward one side swap [design] (the Ultra-Luxe's two northmost, Gomorrah's westmost,
  the Tops' southmost). A swapped table's script still asks for blackjack; the engine opens
  poker at its casino instead (`blackjack.rs` `scripts_open`).
- The crosshair names a swapped table "Poker Table" with the prompt "Play Poker"
  (`sim.rs`, `reticle.rs`), and `nvforever` `poker_view.rs` draws a poker table over its
  blackjack felt (its collision stays the blackjack table's).
- Row `poker-tables` (Gameplay > Game, after `sound-cover`), **off by default**: `SECTIONS`,
  `KNOWN` and its layout tests, settings-page.md, settings-reference.md; sentence case, a
  note under 200 characters, an on/off row.
- New screen text (the row's label and note, "Poker Table", "Play Poker") goes through `tr()`
  with lines in all six lang files, tagged `[design]` as NVForever's own words.
- Docs: `design/poker.md` §7 "Poker tables in the world".
- Test: `poker_tables::tests` (each casino keeps tables of its own; no tables, no swap).
- No smoke scenario: the swap needs the game's data, and with the row off nothing changes.

**Single player:** no change unless the row is turned on. Off (the default), every table
plays blackjack as in the original. No new control is bound; no new dependency.

New `[design]` values: how many tables swap per casino and which side they lie on; the
names "Poker Table" and "Play Poker".

## How it was checked

Rust 1.100, `--release --locked`, `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0`:
- `cd engine && cargo test --release --locked --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 6585 passed, 0 failed
- `cd engine && cargo clippy --release --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- root `cargo test --release --locked --workspace`: 4413 passed, 0 failed
- root `cargo clippy --release --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `python tools/smoke verify`: 1889 scenarios, fine

**Not run:** the swapped tables have not been looked at in game after this port; please look
at one table per casino with the row on and off.

## Clean-room checklist
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/LootJunkieAzza/NVForever/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#clean-room-rules).
- [x] No game data, goldens or game-derived dumps are included.
- [x] Format and behaviour facts are written in `docs/spec-notes/` and tagged
      `[documented]` (with a source), `[observed]` or `[hypothesis]`.
- [x] Nothing was taken from leaked, decompiled or disassembled Bethesda/Gamebryo code
      (no Ghidra, IDA or similar on the game or the G.E.C.K.), and nv-rs was not opened.
- [x] Every new constant or behaviour is backed by a cited source or an observation
      in the original game, or is tagged `[hypothesis]` or `[design]` and listed in
      "What changed", and no text the game shows was transcribed from it.
- [x] No parity-lab goldens, scenarios, tolerances or comparators were changed to make
      a test pass.
- [x] This is my own work (or I have the right to submit it), I license it under
      GPL-3.0-or-later, and my commits are signed off (`git commit -s`, the
      [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/)).

Jira: https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/OFBIZ-13874

Needs #42, which makes the head template use `metaDescription`. Without #42 these pages keep the shared description, so merging this first does no harm.

Every page uses the same meta description today, so search results show the same text under each page title. This adds a `metaDescription` to the home page and eight main pages. Each one says what the page covers, from its own headings.

| Page | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| Home | Apache OFBiz is a free, open source ERP for order management, inventory, warehouse, manufacturing, CRM and e-commerce. |
| Developers | Get started with Apache OFBiz development: download the source, build and run it with Gradle, and find tutorials and documentation. |
| Downloads | Download Apache OFBiz releases, with SHA512 checksums and signatures to verify them, and release notes for each version. |
| FAQs | Answers to common questions about Apache OFBiz: what it is, whether it is free, who owns it and who maintains it. |
| Getting Involved | Join the Apache OFBiz community: follow what is happening, report bugs, and contribute code, fixes and documentation. |
| Mailing Lists | Subscribe to the Apache OFBiz mailing lists for users, developers, commits and notifications, or unsubscribe. |
| Demos | Try Apache OFBiz online, on the 24.09 release and on trunk, with a web store and the back-office applications. |
| Security | The Apache OFBiz security model and policy, how to report a vulnerability, how to deploy securely, and the list of known vulnerabilities. |
| Source Repository | Get the Apache OFBiz source code from Git: the framework, plugins, tools and website repositories, trunk and release branches. |

#42 covers the module pages, and #45 covers Service Providers and User Stories.

How it was checked: this branch was built together with #42, and each of the nine pages shows its own description. Built alone, it has no errors. It merges cleanly with #42, #47, #48, #49 and #50.

author: bryanapellanes
body:
## Description
TL;DR Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes this repo's README as its GitHub Pages site, https://bryanapellanes.github.io/bam.storage/.

closes #7
part of BryanApellanes/threeheadz-tracker#38

**What the workflow does** (`.github/workflows/pages.yml`, the same file in every public repo; identical to the reviewed pilots BryanApellanes/bamtk#146 and BryanApellanes/bam.base#57 apart from the branch name):
- On a push to `bam_storage` that changes Markdown, images or the workflow, and on demand: checks out the commit that triggered it **without submodules**, copies the repo's tracked Markdown and images (regular files only; symlinks are skipped) into a site folder, builds it with `actions/jekyll-build-pages`, and deploys it with `actions/deploy-pages`. The root `README.md` becomes the index page, and relative links between the repo's Markdown files keep working.
- A page that contains `{{` or `{%` (Handlebars templates, Liquid examples) is wrapped in `{% raw %}`, so that text is shown as written instead of evaluated, and gets a `title:` from its opening heading. Other pages are left as written. A leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped. The site title is the root README's opening heading.
- On a pull request it builds and uploads the site, so a broken page shows up before merge and the built HTML can be downloaded; nothing deploys. `deploy` runs only for `refs/heads/bam_storage`, and only it has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`; the build job has `contents: read` and `pages: read` (so the build gets the /bam.storage/ base URL).
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, with the version in a comment.

**Settings, already applied when this PR was opened:** Pages source switched to "GitHub Actions", and the `github-pages` environment limited to deployments from `bam_storage`.

**Demo:** after merge, https://bryanapellanes.github.io/bam.storage/ shows the README as its home page, titled by the README's first heading. Before merge, the PR's build artifact holds the same HTML.

author: georgeh0
body:
## Summary

A follow-up to #2866, reshaping the Google Docs reader after review. The connector is experimental and unreleased (1.3.0), so there's no compatibility shim.

- **Clearer signature.** `read_doc(account, name, declared) -> DocRead` becomes `read_doc_edits(account, name, *, last_declared) -> DocEdits`. The keyword says the text is the base the changes are read against.
- **Typed per-block result.** The two lists of bare heading paths become `edits: tuple[BlockEdit, ...]`. Each `BlockEdit` has `heading_path`, `declared` (the block as last declared) and `current` (the block in the doc now, in Markdown, or `None` when deleted), so a caller doesn't have to parse `content`. `content`, `last_declared` with the edits applied, stays for a caller that takes them in whole.
- **Deletions only against what was written.** A deleted block leaves no trace in the doc, so against Markdown the doc wasn't written from, a missing block may never have been there. The sink now records the declared content's fingerprint in the doc's appProperties (`cocoindexDeclared`, 49 bytes) on every action. When the doc already reads as declared, that's the only write. If `last_declared` doesn't match, no deletion is reported and a warning names the blocks the doc lacks. Edits are reported either way.
- **A pending suggestion is no edit until accepted.** The reader, and the digest its record validates against, leave suggested insertions out, so a suggestion neither appears in `edits` nor re-runs a memoized reader. The writer still counts them, so it leaves a block holding one as it is.

cocurator#30 moves to the new API in the same pass.

## Test plan

- `python/tests/connectors/test_google_docs_target.py`: 41 tests, 3 new. They cover a `last_declared` the doc wasn't written from (no deletions, a warning), a respelled declaration (only the fingerprint is written, and deletions are then reported against it), and a pending suggestion (no edit, the writer leaves the block, then an edit once accepted). The reader's data-dependency test also covers a suggestion added and then accepted. The fake reports suggested insertions as Docs does to an editor, marked with `suggestedInsertionIds`.
- `prek run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD` passes (mypy, ruff, pytest), and the docs build passes.

author: raczu
body:
## Summary

Adds e2e tests that run the real image in a kind cluster and check what arrives on Kafka. They run CI on k8s 1.35, 1.36 and 1.37. The dev cluster moves from `minikube` to `kind` and the manifests ind `deploy/` can now be applied with `kubectl apply -k deploy/`.

## Why

- Nothing testes the shipped image, manifests and RBAC together against a real API and broker. Unit and integration tests use a fake clientset.
- The compatibility table in the README had no test behind it.
- The `kube2kafka` namespace used by the manifests was not created by any of them.

## What changed

- `kind` instead of `minikube`: `make start`/`stop`/`status` works as before. `K8S_VERSION` now takes a full patch version, because `kind` published node images per patch release.
- `deploy/kustomization.yaml` and a `kube2kafka` namespace. The ClusterRoleBinding no longer sets a `namespace`, which has no effect on a cluster-scoped object.
- e2e suite in `test/e2e`, deployed through a kustomize overlay on the top of `deploy/`, sot the real deployment and RBAC are what gets tested.
- `make test-e2e` builds the image, loads it into the `kind` cluster, deploys kube2kafka and runs the suite; `make test` never runs e2e specs.
- A new `e2e` workflow was introduced.
- `make docker-build` tags image tags image with `git describe --tags --always --dirty`.

## How to test

```bash
make start && make test-e2e
```

Each scenario fails when its behavior is broken: removing the filter, changing a selector etc.

Card 1312 (protocol-bypass-scan), card status slice: fixes the two warnings Validator raised on #531 (letter 7082). Links cards 1312 and 1287.

## What

- W1: a quoted string inside a statement is text.
  - `UPDATE todo SET body = 'a, status = b'` was a false finding, and `UPDATE todo SET body = 'go where told', status = 'done'` was missed: the SET list was split on commas and cut at WHERE without skipping string literals.

## What changed
- Run archived AI Stats, Token Mix and Watch projection in one owned, read-only process. Keep scheduling, pricing authority, durable publication and last-good reads in the Web host.
- Avoid retaining a second, unused account-usage history in that process and preserve qualified revision and coverage behavior.
- Verify that report commits are served on the warm path and that Watch sees committed facts added after its child starts.

## Evidence
- Reproduced two complete-coverage warm switches at 1,121 and 1,238 ms. Full collections in the Web interpreter consumed 923 and 864 ms; the equivalent query against the same committed WAL database completed in 15–24 ms in a separate process during those pauses. A separate trace with GC-untracked timing buffers reproduced the tail, including a full collection after SQL had finished.
- Exact production tree: 350 real-source browser actions across warm Sessions period/sort/pagination, AI Stats, Token Mix and Accounts; worst 522 ms. Independent product review: 56 actions, worst 211 ms. Initial coverage timing was measured separately. An earlier isolated production candidate also measured 1,000 sequential warm switches, worst 698 ms.
- The private development journal and architecture will record the measured cause, before/after evidence and publication boundaries.

## Summary

**Part 2 of 3** of the R2 work.

> **Stacked on #259** (part 1: tools, docs and tests), so its first five commits are #259's. This PR's own change is the last commit, `17eadc3d`.

`src: declare agreeing extern globals once in include/globals.h`, generated by `./conker hoist-externs --apply`. **No function body changes and no type changes.** Every declaration that moves keeps its exact text.

- **`include/globals.h`** (new, generated) declares **3,952 globals** once each. Globals a C unit defines are grouped under that unit; the rest are listed as data not yet owned by a C unit.
- **5,193 unit-local `extern` declarations** are removed from **549 units**, which include the header after their existing includes.
- **What stays local** (the tool's report):

  | reason | globals |
  | --- | ---: |
  | declared with different types in different units (part 3) | 330 |
  | names a unit-private type | 385 |
  | aliased by a macro | 11 |
  | declared in another header | 3 |
  | also declared as a function | 1 |

  The 5 units that define their own storage are left alone; part 1 explains why.

### Numbers (`./conker rules`)

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| matched under the rules | 1,142 | 1,670 |
| `MATCH-PENDING` | 3,674 | 3,146 |
| R2 functions | 2,941 | 1,936 |
| R2 findings | 8,600 | 3,359 |

R4 rises by one function, 1,891 to 1,892: a byte view of a scalar global whose declaration moved to the header. The checker exempts only scalars declared in the unit itself.

author: deanberris
body:
Step 2 of [ADR 0061](docs/adr/0061-lean-proved-facts.md): lemmas proved in Lean are now recorded in certificates and in `--trust-report`.

## What changes

- **Certificates (format 3).** Each proved `by lean` lemma gets a line `proved lean <lemma> <statement hash> <theorem> <toolchain> <axioms>`, using the spelling ADR 0073 gives for per-item Lean lines. `pia-cert dump` prints these lines. piac still writes the oldest format that holds what the object lists, so objects without Lean facts are unchanged. ADR 0073's identity lines move to format 4, and the ADR is amended to say so.
- **`native_decide`** (`Lean.ofReduceBool`, `Lean.trustCompiler`) trusts Lean's compiler:
  - Outside a `@trusted` file, the goal fails with `[axiom Lean.ofReduceBool]` and a hint.
  - Inside one, it is a `trusted native_decide` item, both in the certificate and in the trust report.
- **`--trust-report`** has a Lean section after the trusted items:
  - Each lemma is listed with its theorem, toolchain, axioms and statement hash.
  - With `--why`, it names the goals that use each lemma, then counts how many proved goals use one.
  - The section says what these lemmas rest on: Lean's kernel and piac's translation of the statement.
- **Soundness fix in the translation.** Literals are now emitted as `(n : Int)`. Before this, a term made only of literals elaborated as a `Nat`, where `0 - 1 = 0` holds. So `ensures 0 - 1 = 0` was false in Pia but provable in Lean. Generated statements change, so the receipts are rebuilt. The existing proofs elaborate to the same terms.
- **Decisions, recorded in the ADR's "Step 2 as built" note:**
  - There is still one statement hash, since the Lean closure hash already covers the Pia statement.
  - There is no Mathlib field until Mathlib is in the build.
  - `pia-cert audit` replay waits for `pia-cert audit` itself (abi.md, step 8).

## Tests

- `tests/lean/sums.pia` checks the trust report with `--why`, then builds an object and checks that `pia-cert dump` shows the same statement hash.
- `tests/lean/native_trusted.pia`, with the new `native_proof` target and `Native.lean`, shows `native_decide` in a `@trusted` file: proved, listed as a trusted item, and in the certificate.
- `native_untrusted.pia` is the same lemma, with the same receipt, outside a `@trusted` file, and it fails.

None of this could be built in the cloud session, because Bazel can't fetch its archives here. CI is the first build. I checked the Lean translation locally with a g++ driver over `src/syntax` and `src/meta`.

## Docs and skills

- Public docs: `verifier.md`, `abi.md`, `status.md`, and a `features.md` row, which was missing since step 1.
- ADRs 0061 and 0073 are amended.
- Skills: `pia-lean` (literals, what the build records, `native_decide`) and `piac-build` (the trust report and certificate lines).
- CODEMAP is updated. `tools/codemap/check.py` and `tools/skills/check.py` pass. `tools/docs/check.py` reports 2 problems that are already on main (`const_array_views.pia`, `pull_gpu.pia.md`).

## Remaining

- ADR 0061 steps 3 to 5.
- ADR 0062 cost-bound steps 2 to 6.

author: marcusbandit
body:
## What changed

A series matched to a film record (AniList format `MOVIE`, one episode) whose folder holds one file now reads that file as episode 1, whatever number its name carries. A name like `Some Show - Dai 63-kai Taikai - Movie.mkv` used to read as episode 63, so the film showed Missing, the file sat in Extra files, and Play was greyed out.

- `readings.rs`: a film rule next to the specials record rule. `apply` takes the series kind and a `Record` (format and episode count) in place of the format alone. The rule applies to folders only: a loose film file keeps its file name as its history key. It reads past an episode or a special and leaves an opening or a preview alone. Quick fixes still win.
- `record_matters` knows the film rule, so a match to a film record asks for a rescan, and a match that moves away from one asks for another.
- `scan.rs` passes the kind and the record through.
- `detail.rs`: the `suggest` doc comment now says the film case is handled at the scan. The quick fix stays for lone OVAs and specials.

Per the issue, `-kai` ordinals in names with many episodes are not chased.

## Why

The page knew the file was the film, since the Quick fix banner said so, but the reading itself was never corrected.

## How verified

New tests:

- `readings::tests::a_film_record_reads_its_one_file_as_the_film`
- `readings::tests::the_film_rule_needs_a_one_episode_film_record_over_one_file_in_a_folder` (TV record, 3 episodes, no count, no record, loose film file, two files, an opening)
- `readings::tests::a_fix_wins_over_the_film_rule`
- `scan::tests::a_film_record_reads_its_one_file_as_episode_one`: unmatched, the file reads 63. A `MOVIE`/1 match makes `record_matters` true, and the reconcile then stores episode key `1` and reports the series as changed. Matched to a TV record later, the file reads 63 again.

## Summary

`XeroTimesheetData::forPeriod()` builds one line per day of the pay period. Days without hours get `numberOfUnits: 0` instead of no line.

```
before: {11-03: 7.5}            -> [11-03 7.5]
after:  {11-03: 7.5}            -> [11-02 0, 11-03 7.5, 11-04 0, ... 11-08 0]

## 变更内容

- 关联提案 / 批次：小修（基于真机 E2E 实测、系统审计与 #191 评审意见整理更新）
- 做了什么：
  1. **修复 Linux `/proc/sys/*` 4 MiB 单次读取 `ENOMEM`（`khc_host.py` `_read_text` / `_read_bytes`）**：
     - 改用 `_READ_CHUNK_BYTES = 65536` 分块循环读取至上限，避免 Linux 7.0+ 等内核对 `proc_sysctl` 文件 `read(4194304)` 抛出 `OSError(ENOMEM)`，修复 `swappiness` 显示 `—` 与高版本内核 BBR 检测被误报的问题。
  2. **优化 `journald` 已限额后的归档清理体验（`khc_host.py` + `TuneSegment.tsx` + `zh.ts`）**：
     - 保留 #191 的配置未变免重启 `systemd-journald` 逻辑；`tune.journal-vacuum` 新增可选 `vacuumDays`（`2..30` 天），开启后先执行 `journalctl --rotate`，再按 `--vacuum-time=<vacuumDays>d` 与 `--vacuum-size=<maxSizeMb>M` 清理。
     - 前端在 `journal.managed === true` 时按钮切为「清理归档」（`vacuumDays: 2`），保留近 2 天安全日志（`logs.security`）与 OOM 诊断上下文，同时保留 `100M` 上限配置，Toast 按 `freedBytes` 精确反馈。
  3. **优化小内存机 `swapoff` 内存余量口径（`khc_host.py` `tune_swap_verb`）**：

author: pondorasti
body:
Fixes 851-4495. Part of 851-4479 (Linux desktops), step 6 of the design, command-line parts. No app UI.

## What changes

- **The installer ends on Linux with one line:** `==> Add a desktop: codevisor desktop setup`, worded the way the server's account has to run it (`su - codevisor -c '…'` after a root install). Not on macOS. Not when a desktop that setup made is there (`screen-sharing.json` with `"service": "systemd-user"` or `"process"` in the data folder).
- **`codevisor setup` asks "Set up a desktop?"** on Linux once the machine is signed in, default No, and on yes calls the same function as `codevisor desktop setup` (`cli/desktop-offer.ts` calls `desktopSetupCommand`; there is no second implementation).
- **It says nothing** on a Mac, when a Codevisor desktop is already set up (running or not), when the server doesn't answer about desktops, where setup would stop with "install these yourself", and where a root step is needed that the account can't run (no sudo). Without a terminal `codevisor setup` stops as before, so the question is never reached.
- **A No or a setup that fails** ends in one line that names `codevisor desktop setup`, and onboarding carries on and exits 0. Ctrl-C at the question prints nothing more. Anything that throws inside the offer is caught the same way.

## Things I added to the scope as written

- **The installer line only shows when the installed server has the command.** The installer installs the stable release, and merging this deploys the installer with the website, before a server release with `codevisor desktop` is stable. So the installer asks the installed `codevisor` for `desktop setup --help` and stays quiet when that isn't there. This is one more CLI call at the end of every Linux install.
- **A No is remembered** (`desktop-declined` in the data folder). Without it, every later `codevisor setup`, including a reinstall at a terminal, would ask again. A yes whose setup failed is asked again next time, and so is a question that was cancelled.

## After your review at 8937559b6

1. **Ctrl-C or a failed read at the question is no longer a No.** The question has three outcomes now (yes, no, nothing); only an answered No writes `desktop-declined`. A cancel writes nothing, prints nothing more, and the question comes back on the next run.
2. **The installer leaves its line out when onboarding dealt with the desktop:** when `desktop-declined` is in the data folder (a No, now or earlier), and when the `codevisor setup` this install ran at a terminal asked, got a yes, and the setup failed. For the second, setup writes `desktop-setup-failed` and the installer clears that file before it runs onboarding, so only a failure from this run counts. The line stays for installs without a terminal and wherever onboarding didn't ask.
3. **No usable sudo: not asked.** When a root step is pending, the account has no sudo and the command isn't run by root, onboarding stays quiet, like on "install these yourself" systems. `codevisor desktop setup` still prints the commands for an administrator.
4. **The probe against the real stable release (0.1.117), in a Debian container, with this branch's `install.sh`:**

| | Account installs for itself | Root install (`as_service_user`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Installer | exit 0, no line that mentions a desktop | exit 0, no line that mentions a desktop |
| `codevisor desktop setup --help </dev/null` on that CLI | prints the top-level help (26 lines, nothing on stderr), exit 0 | the same |
| Time, including starting the account's shell | 1.8 s and 3.1 s in two runs | 1.8 s and 1.4 s |
| Contains "codevisor desktop setup" | no | no |
| Files or folders changed under the account's home by the probe | 0 | 0 |
| Codevisor processes afterwards | 0 | 0 |
| Data and logs folders after the install | empty | empty |

The old CLI does nothing but print and exit, so the probe is unchanged.

## Tests

- `cli/desktop-offer.test.ts`: asked and declined, yes runs the same setup, failure and a throwing setup, a cancelled question, every quiet case (no sudo among them), the remembered No, a config Codevisor didn't write.
- `cli/setup.test.ts`: offered after sign-in and before "Setup complete", on an already signed-in machine, not after a failed sign-in, and a breaking offer doesn't fail setup.
- `scripts/release/install-desktop.test.mjs`: the line on a fresh install, the root wording, no line with a Codevisor desktop, after a No, with an older release, or on a Mac; still a line with a config setup didn't write, and after an earlier failed setup when this install has no terminal. The existing installer test file was at the 500-line limit, so its harness moved to `install-test-support.mjs` unchanged, and five of its expectations gained the new CLI call. `deploy-www.yml` runs the new test file too.

## Proof in a container (Debian 12, the real `install.sh`)

The installer ran for real against a stand-in server archive whose `codevisor` is this branch's build. No cloud account was used: a small local pass-through answered the "is this machine signed in" question with yes and passed everything else to the real server.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh install (root, no terminal) | last line: `==> Add a desktop: su - codevisor -c 'codevisor desktop setup'` |
| `codevisor setup` without a terminal | "needs an interactive terminal", exit 1, no question (as before) |
| `codevisor setup`, answered No | "No desktop set up. Add one any time with: codevisor desktop setup", exit 0, no desktop |
| `codevisor setup` again | not asked again, exit 0 |
| `codevisor setup`, answered Yes | the usual setup output, "The desktop is ready", exit 0, Xvnc and Xfce running as `codevisor` |
| `codevisor setup` with the desktop there | no question, exit 0 |
| Second install, desktop present | no line that mentions a desktop |
| `codevisor setup`, Ctrl-C at the question | exit 0, nothing more printed, no mark written; asked again on the next run |
| Install at a terminal, answered No | onboarding's line, installer exit 0, no installer line; `desktop-declined` written |
| Install without a terminal after that No | no line that mentions a desktop |
| Install at a terminal, Yes, but setup can't install (sudo asks, no rights) | setup's own output, "The desktop wasn't set up. Try again with: codevisor desktop setup", installer exit 0, no installer line |
| Install without a terminal after that failure | last line: `==> Add a desktop: su - codevisor -c 'codevisor desktop setup'` |
| No sudo on the machine | `codevisor setup` doesn't ask, exit 0; `codevisor desktop setup` prints the commands for an administrator, exit 1 |

## Code review

Two passes (medium) on the branch before the first push. No pass of mine after your review, as asked.

Fixed: the installer hid its line whenever onboarding had run, also when onboarding never asked; a throw in the offer could fail a finished sign-in; `codevisor setup` built the desktop's system object up front on every platform; my installer tests were a second harness outside the check that gates the website deploy; the "asked" mark was written before setup ran, so a failed yes was never asked again; a mark that can't be written could swallow a yes; the installer matched the word `service` anywhere in the config.

Left, with the reason:

- The question is asked on a second Codevisor server of an account whose desktop unit another server owns; a yes ends in that server's own explanation. The status can't tell this case in advance.
- The quiet status check can take up to 30 s on a server that is slow to answer; it normally answers in under a second.

## Not in this PR

- The "with a desktop" option when adding a machine over SSH from the Mac app (step 4).
- The website's installation page doesn't mention desktops yet.

author: ymote
body:
A camera bridge: Android's camera APIs over OpenHarmony's camera framework (its camera NDK, `libohcamera.so`). Westlake had no `media.camera`, so every Camera2, CameraX and Camera1 app saw no camera, although the D600 has two (lcam001 back, lcam002 front).

**Camera metadata.** Every camera2 characteristic, request and result travels in `CameraMetadataNative`, whose natives Westlake's runtime lacked.
- `third_party/aosp-camera-metadata` adds AOSP's `camera_metadata.c` and its tag table, from `platform/system/media` at android-15.0.0_r1 (0287f16), unmodified, under Apache 2.0.
- `camerametadata_natives.c` implements its 20 natives on top of it, with AOSP's semantics.

**Listing cameras.** `media.camera` (`OhCameraService`) lists OH's cameras as "0", "1" at the LEGACY level:
- preview sizes as YUV/PRIVATE outputs and photo sizes as JPEG;
- facing and orientation from OH;
- the request, result and characteristics key lists, naming native tags only.

**Opening a camera.** `OhCameraDevice` is the app's `ICameraDeviceUser` over an OH capture session.
- Each preview-like stream becomes an OH preview output on the OH surface behind the app's Surface. A JPEG stream becomes an OH photo output.
- Results are made per frame, as a LEGACY device's are.
- `SurfaceUtils`' natives are included.
- OH's open errors map to Android's service errors.

**Camera1.** `android.hardware.Camera`'s natives forward to `OhCamera1`, on the same session:
- preview into the display or texture;
- `takePicture` posts the JPEG bytes;
- the parameters string is built from OH's sizes.

**Feature claims.** `android.hardware.camera`, `camera.front` and `camera.any` are claimed from the same list the service gives apps, so CameraX never sees a claim without a camera.

**Host permission.** The host requests `ohos.permission.CAMERA`, which OH requires to open a camera (versionCode 6). It must be granted when the host or a managed bundle is installed.

Tested on the D600, with a Camera2 probe and Open Camera:
- **Natives:** all 20 metadata natives and all camera natives bind in every app.
- **Listing:** "2 camera(s) from OH". The back camera's characteristics read correctly (facing back, orientation 90, 1280x960 preview and JPEG), and Google Play offers Open Camera once the claims are in.
- **Opening:** OH refused it for the missing `ohos.permission.CAMERA` ("Permission to Access Camera Denied"), which the host commit here adds. Preview, still capture and Camera1 therefore haven't run on a device yet. They wait for that host permission to be deployed.

body:
This changes how the core IR's JavaScript prints an Int's `+`, `-` and `*` when int-ranges.ts can't show the range is small. When both inputs are locals or literals, the small case is now written out:

`typeof a === "number" && typeof b === "number" && (t = a + b) > -2^28 && t < 2^28 ? t : rt(a, b)`

For a product the small case gives `t + 0`, so a result is never -0. Past 2^28, the call goes to int.ts as before and gives a BigInt. `NO_INLINE_INTS=1` turns this off.

Measured on the core IR, alternating runs:
- typeset, 1000 paragraphs: 1.30 → 1.15 s.
- pack, 12,800 words: 155 → 130 ms.
- crew: the same within noise.

All print the same output.

It's dark with a white edge, so it shows on both black and white. The normal mouse pointer is hidden. The crosshair is drawn on its own overlay canvas, so moving the mouse never redraws the plan image.
- **Line ends:** finished lines end in short ticks set square to the line, like dimension lines. Inside corners of a run are small hollow squares. There are no round dots anymore. Points you are still placing and the grab handles on a selected mark are small hollow squares with an exact center. Grab handles keep the same generous tap area.
- **Touch magnifier (iPad and phone):** hold your finger still for a moment and a magnifier appears above-left of it, with the crosshair at the center. It moves to stay on screen near the edges. Slide to adjust, then lift to place the point. A quick tap still places a point, and a quick drag still moves the sheet. The magnifier also shows while you drag a corner of a selected mark. A long-press menu now needs an 0.75 s hold without moving, which only applies while aiming.
- **Snapping:**
  - Points snap to the corners and ends of marks on this sheet, within a set number of screen pixels. A green square shows when a point will snap.
  - A snapped point gets exactly the same coordinates as the existing corner.
  - **Shift**, the new **⊥ Ortho** button, or the Ortho item in the right-click menu locks lines level or plumb. A setting adds 45° lines.
  - Hold **Ctrl** (⌘ on a Mac) to place a point without snapping. **Alt** does the same, except in Area mode, where Alt still means deduct.
  - The small auto-straighten that pulls a line to level, plumb or 45° when it is within 7° is turned off while you drag a corner, so small adjustments stay where you put them.
- **Readout next to the cursor:**
  - Lines: the current leg and the run total, in feet-inches.
  - Areas: SF and the current side. A deduct shows with a minus sign.
  - Scale: the pixel length, plus what that length measures at the current scale.
  - The readout pill at the bottom of the sheet is unchanged.
- **⚙ View → Drawing** (saved on each device). The defaults are marked:
  - Cursor: gap crosshair (default), full-screen lines, or arrow
  - Crosshair color: auto (default), red, blue or black
  - Line ends: ticks (default), dots or arrows. This setting is also used in the markup PDF.
  - Magnifier: auto on touch (default), always or off. Zoom: 2x, 3x (default) or 4x.
  - Snapping on/off, and snap distance S, M (default) or L
  - Ortho on at start (off by default), and level/plumb only or 45° too
  - Readout next to the cursor on/off

Line widths per item (`tkItemWidthIn`), labels and tags, and totals are unchanged. The Plans viewer has no measure tool, so it is unchanged. Nothing in the Bids list code was touched.

- New pure helpers, each a top-level function: `tkSnapVerts`, `tkNearVertex`, `tkOrtho`, `tkSnapPick`, `tkEnds`, `tkEndMark` and `tkReadout`. Five new tests in `.github/scripts/takeoff-test.js` cover them (27 takeoff tests in total).

author: zkochan
body: ## Summary Implements the operator-only metrics item from the optional refinements (section 9) of https://github.com/orgs/pnpm/discussions/16192. The required parts of that plan have already landed. New Prometheus counters, served only through the existing `metrics` token or private listener: | Metric | Labels | Counted when | | --- | --- | --- | | `pnpr_resolution_cache_hits_total` | `footprint="public\|private"` | a resolve is answered from the resolution cache | | `pnpr_resolution_cache_misses_total` | none | a cacheable resolve finds no candidate the caller may use | | `pnpr_resolution_cache_stores_total` | `footprint="public\|private"` | a finished resolution is stored | | `pnpr_tarball_routes_total` | `route="upstream\|gateway\|hosted"` | the resolver makes a tarball routing decision | Design notes: - A miss has no footprint until the resolve finishes. The store counter gives the public/private split of misses. - Lookups are skipped and not counted when the request has no cache key or the cache TTL is zero. - The tarball route counter counts routing decisions. A resolve served from the resolution cache replays earlier decisions and adds none (the hit counter covers it). A decision still counts if its hint frame is later dropped. - Tarball routes are counted in `TarballRouter::classify_tarball`. It is called only from the paths that emit URLs: streamed package frames, frozen frames, and routed lockfiles. The verification paths keep calling `RouteContext::classify` directly, so they are not counted. - The resolver gets the server's `ServerMetrics` through `ResolverShared`, so a registry graph swap keeps the same counters. The resolver counters live in their own `ResolverMetrics` group. - Candidate counts and footprint details are still never returned to resolve clients. The other two optional items (validating a private hit before serving it, and lazy probing of custom registries) are not part of this PR. ## Checklist - [x] I checked the referenced issue and verified that none of the PRs already linked to it solves it. - [x] Added a changeset (`pnpm changeset`) if this PR changes any published package. Keep it short and written for pnpm users — it becomes a release note. - [x] Added or updated tests. - [x] Updated the documentation if needed. --- Written by an agent (Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Added Prometheus metrics for resolution-cache hits, misses, and stores, with public and private results reported separately. * Added metrics showing whether tarball requests are routed through an upstream registry, gateway, or hosted service. * **Documentation** * Documented the new metrics, labels, and routing categories.

author: rikardop05
body:
## O problema

Ao escolher o cartão em "Destino da importação" **antes** de anexar o PDF, o upload zerava o seletor para "Selecione o cartão". A pessoa achava que o cartão continuava escolhido, o que é um erro de uso comum.

## Causa

Em `handleFile`, quando o nome do arquivo não revelava o banco e havia mais de um cartão, a tela marcava a origem como pendente (`sourcePending`). Nesse estado o seletor recebe `sourceId=''` e aparece vazio, embora a escolha ainda estivesse guardada.

## Correção

`keepChosenCard` (`components/import/pdf-queue.ts`, função pura testada) decide se a escolha atual continua valendo. Ela fica, a não ser que:

- seja a **próxima fatura de uma fila** (o cartão da anterior não vale para a seguinte); ou
- o arquivo aponte um banco e o cartão escolhido seja de **outro** banco.

Nesses dois casos a origem é pedida de novo, como antes.

## Para o revisor

- Se o PDF casa com um único cartão cadastrado de outro banco, a tela continua trocando para esse cartão (visível no seletor). Não alterei isso.
- Verificação: `tsc` e `eslint` limpos, suíte completa passando; testes novos em `pdf-queue.test.ts` e uma verificação de ligação em `import-wiring.test.ts`. Não reproduzi o fluxo no navegador.

body:
## Summary

**Part 3 of 3** of the R2 work.

> **Stacked on #275** (part 2, the generated hoist), which is stacked on #259 (tools). This PR's own changes are its last two commits:
> 1. `573d41f9` src: give type-conflicting globals one declaration (`./conker unify-externs --apply`)
> 2. `40196956` src: hoist the unified globals into include/globals.h (`./conker hoist-externs --apply`)

After part 2, 330 globals are still declared with different types in different units, so they can't move to the header. This PR gives **170** of them one declaration, then hoists them. **No function body changes, and every retyped unit compiles to identical object code.**

### How each retype was proven

`unify-externs`, from #259, does this for every type-conflicting global:
- It proposes a candidate declaration that loses no information. Named types outrank sized scalars, which outrank `u8`/`void` placeholders. Among equals, the variant most units use comes first.
- It rewrites the other units to the candidate and compiles each one in the toolchain container.
- It compares each object with the unchanged unit's: code with relocations, `.data`, `.rodata`, small-data sections and section sizes.
- A global passes only when every unit retyped for it is identical. Globals that share a unit are retried apart, and failures try the next candidate.
- `--apply` writes all passing globals at once and re-verifies every retyped unit.

**Results:**
- 170 globals, 263 declarations, 113 units, all identical.
- The second hoist then removes 604 more local declarations from 193 units. The header ends with **4,122** globals.

**Determinism:** two separate report runs gave identical results, and the applied run matched them. `D_800D246D` is `u8` and `D_800CC49A` is `s8`, the types macOS lost to read failures before #259's fix.

### Worth a reviewer's look: pointer and non-pointer changes

All 170 retypes are byte-identical. However, 32 globals (36 declarations) change between a pointer and a non-pointer, or between a named callback typedef and its spelled-out function-pointer type. The ranking treats these as equal, so the most-used variant wins. If you'd rather a global kept another spelling, it can be dropped from this PR, or switched to another candidate with `--only` and a per-global choice, without affecting the rest.

body:
Workflow files are the owner's to merge. This PR is prepared for you to review and merge yourself; `hold` stays on. **Merge after PR 2214 (done):** 2214 is on main and merged into this branch. `tools/merge-gated.sh` refuses this PR (exit 19) because it changes `ios-compile.yml`, so it is a hand merge either way.

## Workflow changes, each with its reason

1. **`auto-ship.yml`: never auto-merges a PR that touches `ios/`.** Your decision, 27 Nov: "make auto-ship refuse any PR that touches ios/". Right after the `hold` check, before the verdict, `test` and author checks and before any veto issue, it asks for `pulls/<n>/files?per_page=100` with `--paginate`. If any `filename` or `previous_filename` (a rename out of `ios/`) starts with `ios/`, in any case (`IOS/` counts, as macOS disks fold case), the run ends: exit 0, no issue, no merge, log line "touches ios/: merged by hand through the session merge gate; the simulator run comes at the checkpoint — not shipping." It fails closed: an unreadable list refuses, and so does a list whose length differs from the PR's `changed_files` (the endpoint stops at 3,000 files). Eight lines of bash plus a comment; the header's list of checks names it. (US-46 AC20; it also closes the auto-ship limit US-64 AC43 names.)
2. **`ci.yml` and `deploy.yml`: one typecheck list.** Decided 26 Nov ("One workflow PR for CI tidying"). Both workflows listed the same four tsc runs. They now run `npm run typecheck:all`, a new `package.json` script with those four, in the same order. A test pins the list, and that neither workflow names a tsc project of its own.
3. **`ios-compile.yml`: header comment only.** It said the check is advisory and "warns, does not block". Since PR 2214 (US-64 AC43) the session merge gate (`tools/merge-gated.sh`, `tools/wait-run.sh`) requires it to pass when a PR changes files the Swift build reads (`tools/ios-compile-paths.sh`), advisory otherwise. Checked against main after 2214 merged. No behaviour change.

## Dropped from the 26 Nov item, by ruling

- **The Pages smoke moving into `tools/`:** dropped. The smoke stays inline in `deploy.yml`, exactly as on main. A gate's definition must stay in an owner-only file: in `tools/`, an auto-shipped PR could blank it.
- **Weighted test shards:** dropped. Earlier test-speed work brought the shards close; not worth a new action and a vitest sequencer.

## Tests

`tests/auto-ship-claim7.test.ts` "PRs that touch ios/ (US-46 AC20)" runs the real step under a fake `gh`: `--paginate` is passed; a list shorter than `changed_files` refuses; an `ios/` file first or after 400 others refuses; a rename out of `ios/` refuses; `IOS/HealthRoadmap/X.swift` refuses; `docs/ios/`, `iosx/` and `tools/ios-compile-paths.sh` still ship; an unreadable list refuses; no refusal opens an issue or dispatches a workflow. With the condition removed the three `ios/` cases fail; without `tolower` the case test fails. `tests/ci-jobs.test.ts` and `tests/engine-typecheck.test.ts` pin the typecheck list. Workflow, deploy, story, merge-gated and wait-run tests pass locally after the merge of main (15 files, 394 tests); `npm run typecheck:all` exits 0.

Net production code: +11/-9 lines (comments and blank lines left out). Deleted: the duplicated typecheck steps in ci.yml and deploy.yml.

author: huhn511
body:
Fixes the priority-1 failure `e2e/chapter-k4.spec.ts:14` at `e2e/helpers/k4.ts:410`. After `shiftQ` at the well (Standpunkt 17), the test expected era `1796` and got `today`.

## Cause (test helper, not the game)
1. `examineHere` takes three clue pages while the 4.4–4.5 fights run: `clue.k4.anschlag`, `clue.k4.graben` and `clue.k4.graben_heute`.
2. The card director (`src/ui/cards.ts`) queues them while the HUD's `combat` action reason holds the slot.
3. That reason lingers 3 s after a fight, and the linger is counted in **rendered frames**. `kq.step(n)` renders once per call, so the pages stayed queued across most of the chapter.
4. They opened only after the station teleport: the "Ein Anschlag am Pfeiler" modal was up when Q was pressed at Standpunkt 17. An open modal disables gameplay input, so the press was lost.

An instrumented run logged the card queue at each step, which is how this was traced. A real player sees the page, closes it and then presses Q, so the game behaves as designed.

## Culprit
There is no culprit merge. The same instrumented run fails the same way on **fcb43ad** (the commit reported as last green) and on current main. Whether the deferred pages open before or after the press depends on how many frames get rendered.

## Fix
- `shiftQ` now calls a new `readPages`, which reads away every page that is open or free to open, as a player would.
  - It steps one render at a time, because the card gap also runs in rendered frames.
  - Pages still held by a fight stay queued.
- `shiftQ` now asserts that the press started a shift. A lost press fails right there, and the message shows the input, modal and card-queue state.
- No game code changed and no timeouts were raised.
- Task file: `.mc/tasks/done/TASK-072-…`

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm validate && pnpm build`: 2367 passed, 0 failed.
- Through heavy.sh, `chapter-k4.spec.ts` (whole spec) plus `smoke.spec.ts`: 11 passed. After merging origin/main (#100, chapter 4 progress) the same run gave 12 passed.

Implements wing puzzle 4 from the finish-the-game plan: **Staff room: map and locker** — "Pins on a wall map plus a note give coordinates and a country order that open a locker with the master key."

Stacked on #21 (puzzle 3); retargets to main once the puzzle chain lands.

**Puzzle**
- A wall map on the staff room's north wall carries six numbered country pins (Egypt 4, Sudan 5, Lebanon 7, Iraq 2, Tunisia 1, Morocco 9). The teacher's note, shown in the lock overlay, names her summer route: Cairo, Beirut, Baghdad, Rabat. Reading the matching countries' digits in route order gives **4729**.
- Solving slides the middle locker's door aside and reveals the master key. Unlike the drawer puzzles, only the door moves: the key sits inside the locker and is revealed, not carried.
- A wrong code clanks the lock and runs the framework's `WrongAttempt()`: Bright Idea meter penalty plus the `PuzzleFailed` noise hook for the Shadow.
- Save restore reopens the door and shows the key without replaying events, sound or the reward message.

**Code**
- `MapLockerPuzzle` : `PuzzleBase` — code, note (EN + AR), door/key wiring, localized solve message. Reuses the shared `CodeLockUIController` overlay from puzzle 1, so desktop (digits + Enter) and mobile (tap wheels) both work.
- Editor placement in `SceneBuilderPuzzles.CreateMapLocker`: map board, six pin cubes with label texts, door and lock plate on `Lockers_2`, and a small placeholder key prop (the real key model arrives with bro's model batch).

**Localization note**: country labels on the map stay in English as diegetic map text (same call as the cipher's language-neutral chalk sums); the lock UI itself — title, note, hints, feedback — is fully Arabic-translated.

**Verified**: code-level review only (no local Unity); CI compile + builds are the gate per AGENTS.md. Checked on paper: 4729 = Egypt/Lebanon/Iraq/Morocco in the note's route order; the (0,0,0.75) door offset slides the 0.7-deep door fully clear; pin labels sit on the map's room-facing side with the same yaw-180 convention as the board texts.

author: otatiaro
body:
`kymo::dwt::ticks<Cycles>()`, called after `start()`, makes the DWT send a tick on SWO every `Cycles` cycles (`CYCEVTENA`, `CYCTAP`, `POSTINIT`/`POSTPRESET`). The local timestamps between two ticks add up to the period: a reference for dating SWO when the probe cannot read the ring. The host side comes in a later PR.

- `Cycles` is 64 or 1024 times 1 to 16. Any other period fails to compile. The finer tap is used when both fit.
- Cost: 40 bytes of flash, no stack (-Os, Cortex-M33 and M4). SWO load is about 2 KB/s at 8 MHz and 16384 cycles.
- `detail::tick_fields()` is checked at compile time (`target/tests/dwt`).
- The board image calls `ticks<16'384>()`. `board.py` clears the tick fields before the reset, because `DWT_CTRL` keeps them, and checks them after.

## Verified

- QEMU dwt tests and the clang-tidy build pass.
- Board test `opsy_board_h563` passes on the NUCLEO-H563.
- Mutants seen red:
  - tap count limit off by one: two compile-time checks fail;
  - `CYCEVTENA` never set: `board.py` fails with "did not set a tick every 16384 cycles".
- Capture, 10 s at 8 MBd: 4879 ticks. A tick that shares its timestamp with another packet is dated a few cycles off, and the next spacing cancels the error.

author: stipsan
body: ## What this is and why it's needed The first release (#1) gave every `useSelector` its own subscription to the actor, Jotai style, and needed extra code to keep readers that mount during a transition consistent. It also detected `startTransition` through React's private internals. The research in PALS-135 found that a single subscriber per actor, passing the snapshot down through React, is the live-actor design that never tears. This PR replaces the per-hook store with that design: - `useStoreSelection` is the only place a snapshot enters React state. `useActor` and the `createActorContext` provider use it. The provider passes the snapshot down through a context per actor, and `useSelector` reads from it. Outside a provider, `useSelector` falls back to one subscription of its own. - `send` always sends in a transition: the caller's, or one of its own. React internals are no longer read. - Urgent sends, like a controlled input's `onChange`, use the new `useOptimisticSend(actor)`, which previews the event with `useOptimistic` and xstate's `transition()`. - The trade-off is that a provider's readers re-render on every snapshot change, since React can't select from a context. `useSelector` keeps the previous selection's identity, so the React Compiler or `memo` lets what they render bail out. One upstream test is adapted to assert this. Follow-up PRs on top of this one cover the remaining sub-issues of PALS-135. Fixes PALS-133

author: sergeyslonimsky
body:
New module `contrib/river` (River v0.47.0, `contrib/sql v0.1.0-rc.2`, otelriver v0.12.0) — a thin lifecycle wrapper over River on `corepgx.DB`.

- `New(db *corepgx.DB, cfg riverqueue.Config, opts...)` — River's config as is (validated by River in `New`, no I/O); `Logger` defaults to the component's, otelriver is appended to `Plugins` (trace propagation on).
- `Start` builds the River client on `db.Pool()` (`ErrNotStarted` if the DB has not started — register after it). `Run` (`lifecycle.Worker`): River `Start` → on stop `Stop` (no new jobs, in-flight finish) → at Shutdown's deadline `StopAndCancel`; `ErrStopped` if River stops on its own. No `Queues` = insert-only client.
- `Insert` / `InsertMany` join the transaction of the context (`corepgx.Tx`), else insert on the pool; `WithTxFrom(db)` for River on a separate pool of the same database. `Inserter` interface for domain code, `River()` escape hatch.
- Options: `WithName`, `WithLogger`, `WithTracerProvider`, `WithMeterProvider`, `WithTelemetry`, `WithOtelRiverConfig`, `WithTxFrom`.
- Migrations stay with the service (README shows rivermigrate).

Tests: unit tests on a fake engine + a lazy pgx pool (~97% coverage, `lifecycletest.Runner`); container tests in `internal/integration` — commit/rollback on a shared and a separate pool, the lifecycle contract on PostgreSQL.

**River pinned at v0.47.0**: v0.48+ requires pgx v5.11, with which pgxmock (in the `sql` tests) does not compile — the Workspace job would break. Services may require newer River.

Also: pgx ≥ v5.11 on Go ≥ 1.27 scans arrays through `database/sql` (`driver.RowsColumnScanner`): `sql` docs and `TestSQL_PostgresValueDecoding` updated (it no longer assumes the failure).

body:
## Summary

### Rating colors: one utility for every screen
`scripts/ratings.js` (`HDRatings`) is the only place the thresholds live:

| Rating | Tier | Original (as specified) | Dark | Light |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 90–100 | elite | #22c55e | #22c55e | #137333 |
| 80–89 | great | #86efac | #86efac | #477012 |
| 65–79 | average | #9ca3af | #9ca3af | #5f6672 |
| 50–64 | below | #f59e0b | #f59e0b | #a14a07 |
| 0–49 | poor | #ef4444 | **#f87171** | #b91c1c |
| missing / invalid | none | normal text color | normal text color | normal text color |

- **Functions:** `tier(value)`, `className(value)`, `text(value)` (shows "—" when a rating is missing), and `el(value, opts)`.
- **Colors are theme tokens** (`--rating-*` in `styles/theme.css`) applied through `.hd-rating--<tier>` classes.
- **Why the theme variants:** I measured contrast instead of assuming it.
  - **Light theme:** the specified colors are unreadable on white. Light green measures **1.4:1**, orange 2.2:1 and green 2.3:1, against a 4.5:1 minimum for readable text. Light uses deeper shades of the same five colors.
  - **Dark theme:** #ef4444 drops to 3.6:1 on its charcoal panels, so Dark uses #f87171.
  - **Result:** every rating color is now at least **4.5:1** on all three backgrounds of every theme. The tests check this in the browser.
- **Only the numbers are colored.** Labels such as "OVR" and attribute names keep their normal colors.

**Applied everywhere a rating appears:**
- **Player profile:** OVR and POT badges, plus all 20 attributes (number and bar).
- **Roster:** OVR and POT columns, and the "Team overall" in the roster header.
- **Dashboard:** starting-lineup OVRs and the Team Overall card.
- **New Dynasty:** team OVR on every franchise card, the selection bar, the review hero and the review's Team Overall row.

### 20 attributes
**Agility, Ball Handling, Blocks, Defensive Rebounding, Dunk, Durability, Free Throw, Interior Defense, Layups, Low Post, Mid Range, Offensive Rebounding, Pass, Perimeter Defense, Speed, Stamina, Steal, Strength, Three Point, Vertical**

`scripts/player-attributes.js` builds them from what each player already is. **Overall, potential, age and every other existing value are never changed.**
- **Position profile:**
  - point guards: handling and passing
  - centers: blocks, rebounding, low post and strength
  - shooting guards: shooting
- **Overall:**
  - Skills are shifted so their position-weighted average sits a little below the player's overall, since overall reflects a player's strengths.
  - Correlation with overall is r ≈ 1.0.
  - Elite players have a few maxed specialties and real weaknesses; weak players are weak across the board.
- **Height, weight and age:**
  - Taller players block and rebound more but move less quickly.
  - Weight adds strength.
  - Agility, speed and vertical decline after 29; durability declines after 30.
- **Personal style:** two strengths and one weakness per player, for variety.
- **Seeded per dynasty and player** and stored once, so they never change.

**Profile layout:** a new **Ratings** section with 6 groups (Inside Scoring, Outside Scoring, Playmaking, Defense, Rebounding, Athleticism). Each attribute shows a colored value and a thin colored bar. At 1280px and wider it sits **beside the Bio**, using the space on the right of the left-aligned layout.

### Saves
- **Save format 9.** v8 saves get attributes for current and archived players.
- **Migration is deterministic:** an upgraded save gets the exact same attributes a new league would.

**Ghost races** in Martlet Drift (ADR 0050): race the leaderboard's best runs, or your own, as see-through cars on the real campus loop. **Needs migration `034_drift_ghosts.sql`.**

It stores a ghost only if the path is plausible: no jump faster than top speed (with slack) between samples, a score that never drops, and a final score that matches the submission. `drift_ghosts` can't be written directly.
- **Race a ghost:** the start card lists the top 5 ghosts (with display names) plus your own best. The ghost drives as a see-through coupe in its own paint, appears as a grey arrow on the minimap, and the HUD shows "vs Maya: +1,230" (green when you're ahead).

author: j5ik2o
body:
Closes https://github.com/j5ik2o/event-store-adapter-rs/issues/380

## 何を直すか

[event-store-adapter-java#871](https://github.com/j5ik2o/event-store-adapter-java/pull/871)（head 834cb5b）の `central-http.py` と同じ直しを、`.github/crates-io.py` に入れます。

1. **本文が途中で切れた応答（#380）**：`read_body` の `read1` は、Content-Length に足りないまま接続が閉じると、例外を投げずに `b''` を返します。そのため受信済みの部分が `Response(200, 切れた本文)` として返っていました。読み終えたあとに `HTTPResponse.length` が残っていれば `IncompleteRead` を投げ、照会の失敗（`code=None`）にします。chunked で最後の 0 の塊が来ない場合は、`read1` がもとから `IncompleteRead` を投げます（直す前から照会の失敗です。今回、試験で固定しました）。
2. **見出しが少しずつ届くと締め切りを超える**（java #871 で CodeRabbit が Major とした指摘）：rs にも当てはまります。`urlopen` の timeout は1回の受信ごとにかかるため、見出しを 1 バイトずつ送られると、締め切り 1 秒で 80 秒待ちました。そこで `http` は照会を別のスレッドで動かし、締め切りの残りまでしか待ちません（接続・TLS・見出し・本文のすべて）。待つのをやめた照会は捨てます。読むだけの照会なので、あとで終わっても何も変えません。本文は、これまでどおり `read_body` の Watchdog が締め切りで socket を閉じます。想定の外の例外は、呼んだ側で投げ直します。
3. **lib-release.yml の Latest の手順のコメント**（中将の追加の依頼）：何度動いても同じ結果になる条件に「一覧に最大の版が反映されている限り」を足しました。ずれたときの回復は「一覧への反映の後に github-release のジョブを再実行するか `gh release edit <最大の vX.Y.Z> --latest`」と書きました（GitHub Actions では手順だけを再実行できません）。正本の `.github/tests/fixtures/release-workflow.yml` も同じに直しました（`release_workflow_canonical.py` はこの fixture と行ごとに比べる道具なので、中身は変えていません）。CONTRIBUTING と AGENTS.md は [rs#379](https://github.com/j5ik2o/event-store-adapter-rs/pull/379) で直すので、ここでは触りません。

変えないこと：判定の関数（`read_version` など）、CLI、workflow の動き（コメントだけ）。`crates-io.py` は aislop の行数の上限（441 行）に収めました。受け入れ一覧には足していません。

### 締め切りなしの道について

java の `read_body` には締め切りなしの道（`response.read()`。こちらはもとから `IncompleteRead` を投げます）がありますが、rs の `http` には締め切りが必ず付きます（precheck は既定 600 秒、confirm は既定 1800 秒）。そこで試験では、短い締め切り（5 秒）と、待ちに効かない長い締め切り（3600 秒）の両方で確かめています。

## 試験（本物の HTTP サーバー、`http.server` のスレッド）

| 試験 | 直す前 | 直した後 |
|---|---|---|
| `CutBodyTest.test_a_body_shorter_than_its_content_length_is_a_failed_query`（200・404 × 締め切り 5 秒・3600 秒。送る部分は、それだけで読める JSON） | 4 組とも落ちる（`Response(200 か 404, b'{"version": {}}')`） | 通る |
| `CutBodyTest.test_a_chunked_body_without_its_last_chunk_is_a_failed_query`（同じ 4 組） | 通る（もとから照会の失敗） | 通る |
| `SlowHeaderTest.test_trickling_headers_are_cut_at_the_deadline`（締め切り 1 秒） | 落ちる（80.4 秒待った） | 通る（2.5 秒未満） |

手元の検査（push の前、前景で実行。head ad5cdcb、base は main の fc80186）：

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/tests -p 'test_*.py'`：160 件、OK
- `npm run check:aislop`：受け入れ一覧と一致。`npm run test:aislop`：58 件すべて通過
- `actionlint -shellcheck=''`（1.7.12）：指摘なし。`shellcheck .github/*.sh .github/quint/*.sh`（0.11.0）：指摘なし
- `bash .github/quint/run-quint.sh ci`：通過

author: samirbgno
body:
This fixes a small slowdown in the v2.9 draft (#812): with `dont_generate_typst: true` and more than one of pdf/png/svg enabled, `get_typst_compiler` never hit its cache, so the typst compiler was rebuilt once per format.

`compile_typst` created a new `rendercv-compile-*` temp dir for each format and passed it as `root`, which is the `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` key. every format got a different key. this pr uses one temp dir per process instead, created like `get_package_path()` and removed at exit. with `dont_generate_typst: false` the compiler was already built once.

Measured on d537e0af (classic theme, minimal cv, pdf+png+svg, 3 runs each):

| | typst.Compiler() builds | build time | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 3 (0 cache hits) | ~187 ms | ~365 ms |
| after | 1 | ~62 ms | ~173 ms |

Output is unchanged, rendering two CVs in one process with the same photo name and different photo contents gives the same pdf as a fresh process, before and after. the new test fails without the change. `ruff`, `ty` and the full suite (2466 tests) pass.

author: thinmintdev
body:
## Problem

A slot whose container fails on every start could restart forever (#3936). Slot units carry `StartLimitIntervalSec=1800` / `StartLimitBurst=10`, and the restart delay ramps from 5 s to a 300 s cap. At the cap only six starts fit in any 1800 s window, so the burst of 10 can be reached during the first ramp only.

Measured on systemd 255 with the exact slot settings and a command that fails at once: restarts at 5, 15, 34, 73, 150, 301, 601, 901, 1201 s, and the limit trips on the next one at about 1500 s. That is 300 s inside the window. Anything that stretches the early attempts by five minutes in total (a slow failing run is enough) misses it, and from then on the limit is unreachable. On one box an FLM slot with a failed NPU reached 427 consecutive restarts, one container launch every five minutes for days.

Also checked while looking for the cause: `daemon-reload` does not reset the start limit on systemd 255, and `reset-failed` resets the limit and the restart counter together, so neither explains a counter of 427.

## Change

`StartLimitIntervalSec` goes from 1800 to 7200.

- A slot that fails at once still gives up after about 25 minutes (same ramp, same burst).
- A slot whose every failing run lasts up to five minutes now gives up within two hours.
- Operator loads and restarts are unaffected: `_write_and_start_unit` already calls `reset-failed` before each start, which clears the limit.

Existing units pick the new value up the next time the slot is loaded, since the unit is rendered on every load.

## Testing

- New test derives steady-state starts per window from the rendered `Restart*` and `StartLimit*` values (failing run allowed 300 s) and requires more than the burst. It failed before the change.
- Updated the two assertions and the golden unit text that pinned 1800.
- `tests/providers/test_container.py`, `test_quadlet_golden_runtime_args.py`, `test_container_unit_failure.py`, `test_runtime_launch_plan.py`, `tests/bench/test_harness.py`: 330 passed.
- Not run on a box with a real crash-looping slot after the change; the 25-minute trip was measured with a transient unit, not a slot.

Fixes #3936

author: fre0grella
body:
Three changes so a PR's checks finish sooner. On a companion PR like #92, CI took about 5½ minutes: the Windows tests (195 s), then the Setup build waiting for them (up to 115 s).

## What changes
1. **Setup builds beside the companion tests**, not after them. It only builds a preview, and a release still waits for the tests (`build` needs `test`). This should save about 2 minutes of waiting.
2. **The importer and library tests run in parallel.** Each test opens an encrypted `master.db`, which is slow on purpose, and they used to run one by one. Locally the importer tests went from about 200 s to 58 s and the library tests from 95 s to 25 s, with no race under `-race`. The two tests that replace a package variable (`quickCheck`, `syncWait`) stay sequential, with a comment saying why. Go runs sequential tests before parallel ones, so no parallel test sees the change.
3. **A `changes` job in `ci.yml`** skips the app's tests, browser tests and image build when every changed file is one they never read: the companion, the docs, the site, or other workflows' files. `lint` always runs, because its ratchet also counts the companion's duplication. A push to main runs everything. Main has no required checks, so a skipped job can't block a merge.

## Checked
- The filter on past PRs: #92 (companion) and #93 (hooks, docs) would skip the app's jobs; #86 (UI) runs them. This PR changes `ci.yml`, so it runs them all.
- `go test ./...` and `go vet` pass, and `-race` passes on the importer and library. The new local hooks (gofmt, commitlint, go vet, staticcheck) passed on this commit and push.
- Architecture 8.8 says which tests run when.

A line that starts with $ was passed through whatever it said. Only the commands of GRBL that ask pass now ($, $$, $#, $G, $I, $N); a jog ($J=), the homing ($H) and every other one are refused with their line, also by stream. A line with a carriage return in the middle is refused too.

Three new tests; the ones that asked for the old behaviour are changed. Documents updated in the eight languages.

author: bryanggara
body:
## What and why

Emailed sign-in codes have limits per address (`SIGNIN_CODES_PER_ADDRESS`, `SIGNIN_CODES_PER_ADDRESS_ALL`) and a shared cap on pending codes (`MAX_PENDING = 1000`). Nothing limited how many different addresses one source could ask codes for. One source asking for codes to many addresses on an allowed domain mails each of them, and fills the shared pending list for ten minutes. Everyone else then gets "too soon".

`server/sign-in-mail.ts` adds `SIGNIN_CODES_PER_SOURCE = 20` codes per source in ten minutes, across all addresses. It is kept, pruned and checked like the existing per-address maps. A request with no source is not counted, as before.

## How you tested it

New `server/sign-in-mail-source-cap.test.ts`: one source asks for codes to 1000 different addresses, then another source asks for one.

```sh
SEIRA_VITEST_E2E=all npx vitest run server/sign-in-mail.test.ts server/sign-in-mail-source-cap.test.ts server/sign-in-code.e2e.test.ts server/sign-in-request.e2e.test.ts
```

- Before the fix: `expected 1000 to be less than 100`, so all 1000 were mailed.
- After the fix: fewer than 100 are mailed and the other source still gets `sent`. 21/21 pass across the 4 files.

`oxlint --deny-warnings` is clean. Typecheck and the full suite run in CI on my fork.
