author: cvsz
body:
## Scope
Remaining findings of the 0.3.17 deep audit (Final-Report §15.2 → §16):

- **#5 IM replies stalled the chat reader**: `Engine.send_im` on the reader thread hands off to a single IM worker (`_im_exec`); `UiaAdapter.send_im` waits for an idle user before `com_lock`. Elsewhere (command workers, tests) `send_im` stays synchronous.
- **#16 hot-reloaded settings ignored by the adapter**: `apply_config` on `UiaAdapter` (recompile `line_regex`/`join_line_regex`, re-find panes), `Composite`, `ReattachingAdapter`; called from `Engine._reload_adapter_config`. Window-selection keys and `music_dirs` are logged as next-start.
- **#15 background send off for good / double count**: single increment, retry after `BG_RETRY_S` (30 min).
- **#17 room users never expire**: last-seen per nick; 2 h presence TTL, 30 min active window for the dynamic voteskip.
- **#19 circuit breaker never recorded**: recorded in `_track_failed` / on success; honest log texts.
- **#20 metadata cache**: snapshot under the lock, unique temp file + `os.replace`, user cache folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\AutoDJ\cache`, `AUTODJ_CACHE_DIR`), tests use a session temp folder.
- Version **0.3.18**; CHANGELOG, README, Final-Report §16.

**Not in this PR (documented, OPEN)**: #2 IM text grouping (needs a live IM to see Camfrog's IM DOM), #21 IM window scan cost, and the second audit (stream/webhook/plugins/updater/config/installer) — the audit agent stopped early on an API rate limit before reporting.

## Tests
`tests/test_audit_0318.py` (9): reader-thread IM handoff vs synchronous elsewhere, background retry, apply_config chain + engine reload, presence expiry, health report of playback failures, `_track_failed` records, cache save under concurrent writes + location. Full suite **936 passed, 1 skipped** with `-W error::DeprecationWarning`; ruff, format, mypy (win32/linux), compileall, shellcheck clean; bandit 0.

## Security impact
Positive: room presence (spoofable nick check for IM commands) now expires; cache no longer written into user music folders. No new network surface.

## Compatibility / migration
- The metadata cache moves to the user cache folder; the old `.autodj_metadata_cache.json` in a music folder is no longer read (it is rebuilt) and can be deleted.
- `send_im` from the reader thread returns "queued" (True) instead of the send result.

## Docs
CHANGELOG, README, Final-Report §16.

## Deployment / rollback
After merge: signed tag `v0.3.18` → `release.yml`; install on the bot PC (0.3.17 exe kept as backup). Rollback: revert; reinstall 0.3.17.

body:
## O que muda

Quem abria o link sem conta caía direto no formulário de login, sem ver o que é a rede. Agora `/` mostra, para quem não entrou:

- a frase "A rede social para quem presta vestibulares.";
- três linhas com o que dá para fazer (postar o estudo, cair na turma, ofensiva), com a linha lavanda da margem do caderno;
- os botões "Criar conta" e "Já tenho conta";
- dois posts de exemplo, desenhados pelo próprio `CardPost` do feed, sem clique (`inert`).

Quem já entrou continua vendo o feed, como antes. No celular o topo esconde o logo, então ele aparece na própria abertura; no computador não repete. Sem mudança no backend. Linha nova na tabela de Features do DECISIONS.

1. `make dev-back` e `make dev-front`, e abra `/` sem estar logado (aba anônima ou depois de Sair).

3. "Criar conta" leva ao cadastro e "Já tenho conta" ao login. Os posts de exemplo não abrem nada.
4. Entre com a `ada` (senha `senha-forte-123`): `/` volta a ser o feed.

author: titostauffer
body:
# Pull Request

## 1. Tarefa relacionada

- **Issue:** Closes #208 (DEV-0150)
- **Tipo de entrega:** Bugfix
- **Épico (milestone):** TD — Débitos técnicos
- **Agent técnico principal:** Backend

## 2. Objetivo

O handler genérico de erro da `java-commons` registrava a exceção inteira. Quando o Postgres recusa uma linha, a mensagem da `DataAccessException` traz o `Detail` com a linha recusada (`Failing row contains (...)`) ou a chave repetida. Nas tabelas do client-service, isso pode ser nome, nascimento, medidas ou saúde. Agora o log leva só o necessário para depurar.

## 3. Alterações realizadas

- **`FithubProblemDetailsHandler`:**
  - para `DataAccessException`, o log leva um resumo com o tipo, o SQLState e o nome da constraint, mais a pilha original para depurar;
  - o nome da constraint vem só da primeira linha da mensagem do Postgres; as linhas seguintes trazem os dados;
  - as demais exceções continuam com a mensagem no log;
  - a resposta segue o 500 genérico, que nunca teve detalhe.
- **`DatabaseErrorLogTest`:** Postgres real (Testcontainers), com um marcador na linha. Cobre:
  - CHECK recusado;
  - chave repetida;
  - NOT NULL com o texto `constraint "<marcador>"` na própria linha;
  - erro de banco sem `SQLException`;
  - erro comum, que mantém a mensagem.
- **README da `java-commons`:** linha do Problem Details.

## 4. Escopo da implementação

### Incluído

- O log do handler genérico.

### Fora do escopo

- Outros pontos de log dos serviços. Os testes `...NuncaApareceNoLog` já cobrem o caminho normal.

## 5. Decisões técnicas

- **Pilha preservada:** a exceção registrada é nova, com a mensagem resumida e o `stackTrace` da original. Mantém onde o erro aconteceu sem levar a mensagem nem as causas, que repetem o `Detail`.
- **Sem dependência do driver:** o nome da constraint é lido da primeira linha da mensagem (`... constraint "nome"`), sem usar a `PSQLException`, que não está no classpath de compilação da lib.
- **Formatação:** o Spotless reformatou o arquivo inteiro do handler, que estava fora do padrão palantir.

## 6. Banco de dados e migrations

- [x] Não houve alteração no banco de dados.

## 7. Estratégia de testes

### Testes executados

- [x] Testes de integração (Testcontainers: banco, RabbitMQ).
- [x] Testes de arquitetura (ArchUnit).
- [x] Build, lint e verificações estáticas.

**Comandos executados** (Docker, Linux):

```text
mvn -pl libs/java-commons spotless:apply checkstyle:check
mvn -pl libs/java-commons install
node tools/repo-checks/mutations.mjs --area java mutations/DEV-0150.json
```

**Resultado:**

- A `java-commons` passou nos 54 testes, 5 deles novos.
- Os 4 mutantes foram derrubados.

**Prova de guarda nova (mutação):** `mutations/DEV-0150.json`.

| Mutante | Guarda | Teste que o derruba |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | erro de banco não vai inteiro para o log | `aRejectedRowNeverReachesTheLog`, `aRepeatedKeyNeverReachesTheLog` |
| M2 | a constraint só vem da primeira linha | `aNotNullViolationDoesNotTakeAConstraintNameFromTheRow` |
| M3 | erro de banco sem `SQLException` | `aDataAccessErrorWithoutSqlCauseKeepsOnlyTheType` |
| M4 | mensagem sem nome de constraint | `aNotNullViolationDoesNotTakeAConstraintNameFromTheRow` |

## 8. Critérios de aceitação

author: akshay-ap
body:
Closes #50

## Summary
Alt Safe hashes Safe transactions with the EIP-712 domain `{chainId, verifyingContract}`, which Safe introduced in v1.3.0. Safes v1.1.1 and v1.2.0 use a domain without `chainId`, so every signature collected here fails on chain, and v1.0.0 doesn't load properly. Import used to accept any version. Now "Add an existing Safe" reads `VERSION` first and refuses anything below 1.3.0 with a clear message.

## Changes
- `src/hooks/useSafeLookup.ts`: new `isSupportedSafeVersion` (major/minor compare, accepts `1.3.0+L2`-style suffixes). `lookupSafe` reads `VERSION` before the storage, so old layouts get this message instead of a storage read error, and throws `NotASafeError` (no retries) for versions below 1.3.0. If `VERSION` can't be read, the lookup behaves as before.
- `src/hooks/useSafeLookup.test.ts`: accepted and refused versions.

## Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added or updated
- [x] Integration / Playwright tests (or a manual browser check, described under Testing)
- [ ] ~~Documentation updated~~
- [x] Typecheck, lint and unit tests pass (`tsc --noEmit`, `biome check`, `vitest run`)
- [ ] Screenshots or a recording attached for UI changes (taken locally, not attached; results below)
- [x] No breaking changes, or they are described under Notes
- [x] No secrets, keys or private data in the diff or description

## Testing
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`, `npm test` (157 passed), `npm run build`, `npx biome check src/hooks/`: all pass.
- Browser check: Playwright on Chromium against `npx vite`, with a mocked mainnet RPC whose Safe answers `VERSION` with each value below (the cloud sandbox can't reach a Sepolia fork, so Rabby + anvil couldn't run). On `/import`, after pasting the Safe address:

| `VERSION` | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0.0 | (not run) | "Safe v1.0.0 is not supported. Alt Safe works with Safe v1.3.0 and later.", Add Safe disabled |
| 1.1.1 | "Safe found on Ethereum", owners shown, can be added | "Safe v1.1.1 is not supported…", Add Safe disabled |
| 1.3.0 | "Safe found on Ethereum" | "Safe found on Ethereum" (unchanged) |
| 1.4.1 | (not run) | "Safe found on Ethereum" (unchanged) |

## Notes
### Approaches considered
| Approach | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Refuse import below v1.3.0 in `useSafeLookup` (recommended, implemented)** | One file, ~10 lines. Stops the problem at the point of entry with a clear reason. No change to signing code. | Pre-1.3.0 Safes can't be used in Alt Safe at all. Safes already saved before this change are not re-checked. |
| B. Support v1.1.1/v1.2.0 by switching the EIP-712 domain (no `chainId`) per version | Old Safes work fully. | Touches every hash/sign path (`utils.ts`, signature recovery, shared-tx verification), needs the version threaded everywhere, and v1.0.0 also has a different `SafeTx` typehash. High risk in security-critical code for few users. |
| C. Import as read-only with a warning | Users can still view an old Safe. | Needs gating of every sign/approve/execute entry point (overlaps #33, view-only mode); much larger diff for a view the official Safe UI already offers. |

### Review outcome
Senior review (ponytail-review): no findings. It checked the single caller (`ImportSafe.tsx`), the no-retry path for `NotASafeError`, that an unreadable `VERSION` keeps the old behavior, and that the RPC call count is unchanged. Out of scope: Safes older than v1.3.0 that were saved before this change still open; a follow-up could show a warning chip in `SafeSidebar` where the version is already read.

author: sahil-vij
body:
Stop-loss orders: hold the coins, and sell at the market once the price falls to the stop. Part of #7 (bracket orders are next, and they need this).

A limit sell takes profit when the price rises; a stop-loss caps the loss when it falls. Bracket orders pair the two, so stops have to exist first.

**Behaviour**

- `POST /api/orders` with `"type": "stop"`, `"side": "sell"` and `stopPrice` (string, 10^-8 USD per coin) returns `201` with `status: "open"` and moves the coins into the user's hold account.
- The first tick at or below `stopPrice` sells them at that tick's price, through the same queue and worker as limit orders. A tick exactly at the stop fires it.
- `DELETE /api/orders/:id` cancels a stop and gives the coins back, as for limit orders.
- A stop and a limit sell can't both hold the same coins: the second one gets `422 insufficient_holdings`. Bracket orders will solve that by holding once for both children.
- New errors: `400 stop_orders_are_sells` and `400 invalid_stop_price`. The $1 minimum is checked at the stop price.

**Decisions worth checking**

- **Sells only.** A stop buy fills at whatever the price is when it triggers, with no upper bound, so there's no amount of cash to hold for it. Holding an estimate could let the user overspend, and refusing at fill time breaks the promise the order made. A stop-limit (trigger plus a price cap) would make stop buys safe; that's left for later if it's wanted.
- **The fill is at the tick's price, not the stop.** If BTC gaps from $801 to $760, the stop at $800 sells at $760. That's how real stop-losses behave (they limit a loss, not guarantee a price), and the test covers the gap.
- **Same code path as limits.** `limit.ts` is now `pending.ts`. Placing, cancelling and filling are shared, and only the trigger test (`crosses`) and the matcher's `WHERE` differ. The row lock and `SKIP LOCKED` race handling from #26 apply to stops unchanged.
- Migration 005 adds `stop_price` and a constraint that a stop is a sell with a hold. It also adds a partial index for open stops, since their trigger is a different column from limits'.

**Testing**

- 106 server tests (7 new), on real Postgres and Redis.
- Changing the matcher's `stop_price >= price` to `>` makes the "fires on a tick exactly at its stop" test fail.
- Live against Binance: bought 0.02 BTC, then placed a stop sell for 0.01 BTC at $70,000. That's above the market, so it fired on the next tick, 1.1 s later, at $61,518.36 for $615.18. A second stop at $40,000 stayed open, and cancelling it returned the 0.01 BTC.
- Known gap, fixed in the trading-screen PR: `GET /api/holdings` doesn't count coins on hold, so the UI shows them as gone while a stop is open.

author: tamnd
body:
Refers to tamnd/singularity#285

This change gives Definition 3.9 of research note 03 (the type `τ`) and Corollary 3.8 of the note in fixed coordinates.

The new file is `Singularity/Invariant/LogJacobianTau.lean`.

- `logJacobianType Δ p g` is the type `τ = d - ρ`, with `d = residualOrderAlong Δ p g` and `ρ = logJacobianOrder Δ g`.
- `residualOrderAlong_eq_logJacobianOrder_add_logJacobianType`: for a clean `g`, `d = ρ + τ`.
- `logJacobianType_le_one` and `logJacobianType_eq_zero_or_eq_one`: for a clean `g`, `τ` is `0` or `1`.
- `logJacobianType_eq_zero_iff`: `τ = 0` if and only if `ρ = d`.
- `logJacobianType_eq_one_iff`: for `g ≠ 0`, `τ = 1` if and only if `ρ + 1 = d`.
- `logJacobianType_eq_one_iff_pderiv` and `logJacobianType_eq_zero_iff_pderiv`: the type by the initial form of `G`, as in the text of Definition 3.9.
- `residualOrderAlong_ne_top` and `residualFactor_zero` are small helper results.

Limits: Corollary 3.8 of the note is about the largest residual order `d^max` over all coordinates adapted to `E`. This change proves the bound only in the given coordinates. The bound on `d^max` needs part 3 of Lemma 3.6 of the note, which is not proved. The file has no `sorry` and no new axiom. It was built with `lake build` on the file and its dependencies.

body:
Script changes of group 05, opened as a separate pull request as requested in the review of PR #2. Group 05: robot R5, motors m10 (right) and m9 (left).

## Why we added them

The phone and the robot drifted during our runs, by up to about 100 px. With the fixed search regions of `track_video.py`, the marker left its search disk, the tracker locked onto the blue laptop screen in the background, and the LED grid read the background, so few LED edges were found (3 of 54 in the left E1 backward run before the changes). E1 was also filmed as two videos, one per sweep direction, and the Pi wrote both log files of the left E1 forward trial (194711) empty.

## Changes

**`scripts/track_video.py` and `scripts/duckiebot_analysis/tracking/track.py`**: four options, each off by default:

- `--wheel-follow R`: recentres the hub and marker search disks on the hub in every frame, up to R px from the given regions.
- `--led-follow R`: moves the LED grid in every frame to the centroid of the LED-coloured blob within R px of its start.
- `--led-offset DX DY`: with `--led-follow`, places the grid DX, DY px from the followed blob, on the lit core of the LED instead of its unlit tint.
- `--led-average N`: averages each LED cell over N frames, which cancels the 120 Hz flicker of the room lighting that a 240 frames/s camera samples in step.

**`scripts/duckiebot_analysis/analysis/case_study.py`**: two changes:

- E1 may be one run or two runs, one per sweep direction; their traces are merged, and each sweep's Pi log is read from the run that holds it.
- A trial without a readable Pi log takes the schedule reconstructed from its row of `trials.csv` (schema §10.4), as `process_raw.py` already does for sync `script+led`.

**`README.md`**: a section "When the camera drifts, E1 is two videos, or a Pi log is empty" explains the options and the two cases.

## Update to the latest main

The branch started from `0e374d5`. We merged `upstream/main` into it (commit `3451757`).

- **Conflicted:** only `scripts/duckiebot_analysis/analysis/case_study.py`, in three places (imports, `command_changes`, and `case_study`). We kept the 2026-11-13 update (`CaseStudyConfig`, Pi logs read through `runs.csv` `pi_log`, `DUTY_TOL`) and ported our two changes onto it.
- **Merged without conflict:** `scripts/track_video.py` and `scripts/duckiebot_analysis/tracking/track.py`.
- `tests/test_guidance.py` requires every option's help to state its default, so the help texts of the four options now do.
- All 260 tests in `scripts/tests` pass.

## Effect on our numbers

`git diff 0e374d5 upstream/main -- scripts/` shows that the analysis scripts changed (`case_study.py`, `case_study_macros.py`, `process.py`, `quality.py`, `step_response.py`, the Pi log readers, and `plot_case_study_csme2026.py`). The tracking code changed only in its header, run naming, and help.

We ran the merged scripts on our raw data (`process_raw.py`, `quality_report.py`, `plot_case_study_csme2026.py`) for both motor folders and compared every macro of `results.tex`:

- **Right wheel m10** (the motor of our report): all 43 macros the report uses are unchanged. Of the 99 macros, only two changed, neither used in the report: `NMotors` 1 → 2 and `SpeedSixMax` 16.9 → 17.4. Both range over every motor folder in `data/processed`, which now also holds our left wheel.
- **Left wheel m9:** only `NTrialsLed` changed, 4 → 5, because the updated `case_study_macros.py` counts the `script+led` trial 194711 as LED-synchronised.
- **Quality reports:** the same warnings as before (none for m10; one for m9, E1 backward, angle scatter k = 10.4).

We also re-tracked two videos with commit `3451757` and compared the frame tables with those in `data/raw`:

- right E2 (`R5-R-m10_C_b060p040_rep01-03_20261118`, 5473 frames, with `--wheel-follow` and `--led-follow`);
- left E1 backward (`R5-L-m9_A_sweep_dense_backward_20261118`, 16 381 frames, with all four options).

Every column is identical; only the tracker commit and time in the metadata differ. Our frame tables were tracked with uncommitted versions of these changes (`56eecba` and `611bf35`, dirty), and commit `3451757` reproduces them. Our report cites this pull request's commit.

author: bryanggara
body:
## What and why

Fixes #683

A routine moved to "after the limit resets" (`deferNextRun`) lost that deferral when the clock went back by more than 2 minutes. `pullBackNextRuns` set it to the schedule's next occurrence, so it ran before the reset.

- `deferNextRun(id, until, notBefore = until)` keeps `notBefore` on the routine. This is the instant the wait is for.
- `/api/limit-resets/after-reset` passes `reset + AFTER_RESET_MS` as `notBefore`. `until` stays `max(that, now)` as before.
- `pullBackNextRuns` takes `max(next occurrence, notBefore)` while `notBefore` is still in the future. A run set far ahead by a fast clock is still pulled back (#569), but not before the reset it waits for. A `notBefore` in the past is ignored.
- `routine-load.ts` loads `notBefore` as an instant and drops it when unset, like `wakeAt`.

## How you tested it

Two new tests in `server/routine-clock-back.test.ts`:
- "keeps a run put after a limit reset when the clock is set back by more than the limit": defer 3 h, then set the clock back 10 min. The run stays at the deferred instant.
- "still follows a clock set right when the run was put after a reset by the fast clock": a fast clock (+30 days) defers the run past the reset, then the clock is set right. The run comes back to the reset instant, not the far-future one.

```sh
SEIRA_VITEST_E2E=all npx vitest run server/routine-clock-back.test.ts server/routines-limit-reset.test.ts server/limit-reset-requests.test.ts server/limit-resets.test.ts server/limit-reset.e2e.test.ts server/routines.test.ts server/routine-file.test.ts server/routine-restarts.test.ts
```

- Before the fix: both new tests fail (`expected 1795585920000 to be 1795597200000`).
- After the fix: 342/342 pass across the 8 files.

`oxlint --deny-warnings` is clean. Typecheck and the full suite run in CI on my fork.

author: tom-hehir
body:
## What does this PR do?

Since v4.52.0, a class whose instances implement a callable protocol is rejected
as `class_path` if the protocol's `__call__` returns a class:

```python
class Loss(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, pred: Tensor, target: Tensor) -> Tensor: ...


class MSE:
    def __call__(self, pred: Tensor, target: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        return ((pred - target) ** 2).mean()


parser.add_argument("--loss", type=Loss)
parser.parse_args(["--loss=__main__.MSE"])
# error: Expected '__main__.MSE' to be a subclass of Tensor.
```

`MSE` instances implement `Loss`, so this should be accepted, as it was in
v4.51.0. A function that implements `Loss` is still accepted.

Separately, a protocol whose `__call__` has no return annotation rejects every
class and function, e.g. with "Expected ... to be a function that returns
_empty".

### Cause

1. A callable protocol is treated as an instance factory when its `__call__`
   returns a type that could itself be given as `class_path`, i.e. a class
   other than a builtin like `float` or `str`, a registered type, a `Path` or an
   `Enum`. `Loss` returns `Tensor`, so it is treated as a factory of tensors.
   A protocol returning `float` is not, so this problem doesn't arise there.
2. For an instance factory, a `class_path` can mean two things:
   - a subclass of the returned class, e.g. `SGD` for a protocol returning
     `Optimizer`: the class is the factory, and calling it gives the instance;
   - a class whose instances implement the protocol, e.g. `MSE` for `Loss`: the
     instance is the value, as for any other protocol type.
3. Before #959, any class with callable instances was accepted, without
   checking it against the protocol. #959 fixed this by accepting only the
   first kind, which also rejects the second. I think this was not intended,
   since a protocol type accepts its implementers everywhere else.

For the second problem, `get_protocol_call_return_type` returns
`inspect.Signature.empty` when `__call__` has no return annotation. That is a
class, so the protocol is treated as a factory of `_empty`.

### Fix

- In `adapt_typehints`, a class that is not a subclass of the return type is
  accepted if its instances implement the protocol. This uses
  `implements_protocol`, the same check as for any other protocol type, so a
  class that doesn't implement the protocol is still rejected, as #959
  intended. A subclass of the return type is still treated as a factory.
- For a protocol, the error message adds "or its instances to implement
  <protocol>".
- `get_protocol_call_return_type` returns `None` when the return is not
  annotated, as `get_callable_return_type` does when there is no return type.

This doesn't change what a config can import: the class is checked against the
import path denylist before this point, as before.

### Testing

- `test_callable_protocol_accepts_class_whose_instances_implement_it`: a class
  whose instances implement the protocol is accepted, and `instantiate` gives
  an instance of it. Run for a protocol that returns a class and for one
  without a return annotation.
- `test_callable_protocol_without_return_type_accepts_function`.
- These fail on main. The existing tests pass, and the changed lines are
  covered.

### Notes for review

Two related cases are still rejected, and this PR doesn't change them:

- **`Callable` with a class return type.** Typed as a `Callable` instead of a
  protocol, `MSE` is rejected for the same reason: `Tensor` is a class that
  could be given as `class_path`, so the `Callable` is treated as an instance
  factory. With a `float` return it isn't, and any class with callable
  instances is accepted:

  | type of `--loss` | `--loss=__main__.MSE` |
  |---|---|
  | `Loss` | rejected on main, accepted with this PR |
  | `Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor]` | rejected, also with this PR |
  | `Callable[[Tensor], float]` | accepted, as is any class whose instances are callable (not a factory) |

  I left `Callable` out because #959 restricted it on purpose, and there is no
  existing check of a class against a `Callable` signature, as
  `implements_protocol` is for protocols.
- **`torch.nn.Module` implementers.**

  ```python
  class MSEModule(torch.nn.Module):
      def forward(self, pred: Tensor, target: Tensor) -> Tensor: ...
  ```

  `MSEModule` is still rejected for `Loss`. The protocol check compares
  `__call__`, and `nn.Module.__call__` takes `*args, **kwargs` with no return
  annotation, which doesn't match `-> Tensor`. Accepting it would mean treating
  a missing annotation as matching any type, as static type checkers do. That
  is a broader change to how protocols are matched, so I've left it out of
  scope and mention it only for completeness.

- [x] Did you read the [contributing guideline](https://github.com/mauvilsa/jsonargparse/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)?

author: cnedwin
body:
## What

The shared WebGL2 2D host now builds its startup and restore programs side by side when the context offers `KHR_parallel_shader_compile`.

- `GLNativeSession.preparePrograms(sources, wait)` compiles and links every program first. It then asks `COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR` with `wait` between asks, and reads `LINK_STATUS` only once all of them are complete. A failed link still reports the failed shader's info log, the same as the one-by-one path.
- `WebGL2Host.initialize` passes it the main, solid, resolve, effect and paged programs, waiting 8 ms between asks. It runs `generationGate(token)` after the wait and takes the programs in their original order.
- Every ask goes through the generation gate. If the context is lost, the host is stopped or closed, or the restore deadline passes during the wait, the wait ends with the same outcome as anywhere else in initialization.
- `getExtension` is read once, between gates, outside the finite capture. The pinned 68 `METHODS` are unchanged, and AGENTS.md / AGENTS.zh-CN.md now say so.
- A context without `getExtension`, or without the extension, still makes and checks each program in turn. The host now waits one zero-delay timer between two programs and passes the generation gate after it, so the page keeps running between programs.
- Layer programs are still made lazily, one by one.

## Tests

`tests/shared-webgl2-controls.test.mjs` G21–G25:
- **G21:** all programs are linked before the first ask, and no link outcome is read before all are complete. Each program is asked until its third ask. The shaders and their order are the same as the one-by-one path. The host renders afterwards and closes safely.
- **G22:** a context without the extension, and one without `getExtension`, produce identical program traces. Each link is checked before the next program is made. One turn of the page after `start`, the host is still `starting` with one program linked, and `whenReady` returns the same barrier.
- **G23:** a failed compile among programs built together gives the same `START_FAILED` and shader log as one by one. Close is safe and no objects are left live.
- **G24:** a second loss during the restore wait hands over to the next restore, and the lost generation is not asked again. The host reaches generation 3 and closes safely.
- **G25:** closing during the startup wait rejects `start` with `CLOSED`. Cleanup is safe and no objects are left live.

Mutation checks against the emitted JS:
- skipping the polling fails G21;
- forcing the one-by-one path fails G21, G24 and G25;
- removing the yield fails G22.

## Real browser

Headless Chromium 153 with SwiftShader does not expose `KHR_parallel_shader_compile`, so the real extension was not run. I ran the layer-light fixture (`tools/verify-webgl2-layer-light.mjs` logic: sampled, solid and effect draws, layer lights, a real `WEBGL_lose_context` loss and restore) at 1× and 2× in two modes:
- **plain:** the browser as is;
- **shim:** an init script reports the extension and completes each program on its third ask, while compile, link and every status read stay the browser's own.

Results:
- Both modes pass.
- All 14 frame pins are byte-identical between the modes.
- In shim mode, each of the two initializations linked 8 programs before reading the first link outcome, with 48 asks in total.

Not run: hardware GPUs, a driver that really compiles in parallel, Safari/Firefox, WeChat.

## Gates

Hygiene, ledgers, publication, boundaries, type lanes, KB and `node tools/format.mjs --check` pass. 211 focused WebGL2, shared-frame and browser-game tests pass.

body: ## Summary This PR fixes remediation plan item **3.5**. `Brew::is_available` returned `run_brew(&["--version"]).is_ok()`, which is true whenever a `brew` binary could be spawned. A daemon running as root, for example from a LaunchDaemon, therefore reported `pm_available: true`, but every real Homebrew command then failed because Homebrew refuses to run as root. ```rust fn is_available(&self) -> bool { let Ok(output) = self.run_brew(&["--version"]) else { return false }; // not installed if self.running_as_root { warn!("Homebrew ... refuses to run as root ..."); return false; } output.status.success() // brew must actually work } ``` - The new field `Brew.running_as_root` is set in `Brew::new` from `libc::geteuid() == 0`. It is a field so tests can set it. - `libc = "0.2"` is now a direct dependency. It was already in `Cargo.lock` transitively at 0.2.191, so nothing new is pulled in. - The warning is logged only when brew is installed, so a root apt-only Linux host doesn't log a misleading Homebrew warning. - **Effect on macOS:** a root daemon now reports Homebrew as unavailable, and `/status` returns 412 (the existing no-package-manager response) instead of failing mid-command. - **Effect on Linux:** a root daemon with Linuxbrew installed now falls back to apt, because `get_package_manager` only picks brew when `is_available()` is true. - `AGENTS.md` documents the new rule under "Non-Obvious Project Patterns". **Tests:** four new tests cover brew working, `--version` exiting non-zero, brew not installed, and running as root. `cd daemon && cargo test`: 97 passed, 1 ignored (Linux). Clippy reports the same findings as on `main`; this PR adds none. author: mckoss
body:
Records how agents reach a brain once it lives on the server. Updates `PLAN.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION.md` and `README.md`. Docs only; no version change.

## Decisions

- **Agents use a remote CLI, not a synced copy.** Each command is a request to the server. A new machine needs only the CLI and a credential, and events are logged on the server, so a disposable session loses nothing.
- **The agent's flow is search, read, edit, commit.**
  - `search` and the activation lists only list notes.
  - `read` places the note in a working folder that mirrors the brain's paths, and logs the read.
  - The agent edits with ordinary text tools.
  - `commit` sends the change with its base hash. A stale base is refused and the current version is saved beside the file.
- **Forgotten commits:** every command reminds the agent about edited files it has not committed.
- **One mutation counter** on the server numbers every change, so clients that keep a full copy catch up cheaply.
- **Offline copies are for the PWA** and an optional `somememos clone` for local model use.

## Milestone changes

- M3 becomes "server and remote CLI".
- Full offline sync moves to M4 with the PWA.
- Local mode (M1 and M2) uses the same flow: the brain's directory is its own working folder, and `commit` runs the index pass.

## Left open

Whether the client should commit forgotten edits itself, instead of only reminding (PLAN.md section 12, question 11).

author: pcorless
body:
Closes #689

## Summary
Redaction redraws a field whose string it masked. I checked this on 149 forms from the local QA corpus, with every text field value used as a term and only `FORM_VALUES` in scope. Each redrawn widget was compared before and after, rendered at 2x in icepdf.

| Symptom | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Value drawn where nothing showed | 363 | 0 |
| Mask not visible | 30 | 7 |
| New border/background | 6 | 4 |
| Cut off at the bottom | 3 | 2 |

- **Redaction:** a widget is redrawn only when its appearance shows a non-empty string or draws a form. 358 of the 363 had no appearance at all; the rest drew only a frame or an empty string (`<>'`). None of them shows anything of the value, so they are left as they were.
- **Missing glyph:** an embedded subset font missing a character the value uses, judged by its `/Widths` (`canDisplay` answers for the substitute and says yes), falls back to Helvetica. The corpus subsets give `*` a width of 0.
- **Oversized fixed size:** when the capitals are taller than the clip, the size shrinks to fit. The mask's `*` sits at the top of the capitals and was clipped away entirely. This deliberately departs from Acrobat, which keeps the size and cuts the text; it applies only when the capitals can't fit.
- **Short multi-line field:** the first baseline is clamped inside the clip. It used to land below the box (y = −0.69 in one form).

The three generator changes apply to every field the viewer redraws, not only to redaction.

## Left as is
- 4 blank masks in PDF417 barcode-font fields; 3 in fields 5pt high.
- 4 new borders: old appearances that drew their text above the box, so it never showed. The redraw shows the mask, plus the `/MK` border and background.
- 2 bold 14pt values in a 14.5pt field, laid out as PDFBox and Acrobat lay them out.
- Only checked in icepdf's own rendering.
- Unrelated NPE found on the way: #702.

## Test plan
- [x] `FieldStringRedactionTest`: no appearance stays none, frame-only kept, empty-string kept, plus a control showing a text appearance is still redrawn
- [x] `FieldAppearanceGeneratorTest`: oversized fixed size shrinks (and a control where it fits), short multi-line baseline, subset missing `*` falls back (and a control where it has every glyph)
- [x] `./gradlew :core:core-awt:test`: 1619 tests, all pass
- [x] Corpus probe re-run (numbers above)

author: kianbazza
body:
## Summary

While a surface's `autoHighlightFirst` is a string (as a `Select` resolves it to its selected value), the surface re-applied it whenever its settings changed identity. So a new inline `onHighlightChange`, a new `items` or `virtualItems` array, or any prop that rebuilt `virtualization` pulled the highlight back to that row on every parent render. A string target is now applied only when it should be:

```diff
 Surface
-  useEffect(() => applyAutoHighlight(), [store, settings])     // any settings identity change
+  useEffect(() => applyAutoHighlight(), [store, autoHighlightFirst])
 ListboxStore
+  open observer          a string is applied when the menu opens
+                          (straight away while the Surface's rows are still mounted, else pending)
+  #pendingAutoHighlight  a string target whose row isn't there yet; applied at the end of the next
+                          registration flush or virtualItems update once it can be reached;
+                          dropped on a keyboard or pointer move, a search, a close,
+                          or when the synced value differs
```

So the row is highlighted (and scrolled into view) when the menu opens, when its rows first arrive (for example `virtualItems` loaded after open), and when `autoHighlightFirst` changes. In between, the highlight stays where the keyboard or pointer moved it.

Two related cases change too:
- A popup kept mounted while closed (`keepMounted`, or a reopen during its exit animation) highlights the row again on each open.
- A string `autoHighlightFirst` on a subpage's surface now highlights its row when the subpage opens.

This is a deliberate behaviour change, from the Ship menu audit (bug 1). A changeset is included.

## Evidence

`auto-highlight.test.tsx`, through the DOM:

```text
                                                                         before   after
moved highlight survives a new onHighlightChange (DropdownMenu)          fail     pass
moved highlight survives a new items array (virtualized DropdownMenu)    fail     pass
moved highlight survives a new virtualItems array (Select "selected")    fail     pass
moved highlight survives a root re-render inside a subpage               fail     pass
a moved highlight isn't taken when the target row arrives later          fail     pass
subpage with a string autoHighlightFirst opens on that row               fail     pass   (opened on the first row)
rows that register after open land on the target                         pass     pass
data-first rows that arrive after open land on the target                pass     pass
virtualized Select opened with no items, then given them → selected row  pass     pass   (scrolled into view)
items replacing a placeholder row → selected row                         pass     pass
keepMounted reopen re-applies the target                                 pass     pass
Select value reset to null while closed reopens on the first row         pass     pass
changing autoHighlightFirst re-applies; reopening re-applies             pass     pass
```

Render counts in `row-renders.test.tsx` are unchanged.

Bundle size (gzip):

| entry | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `dropdown-menu` | 94,120 B | 94,264 B |
| `context-menu` | 94,285 B | 94,432 B |
| `command-menu` | 93,748 B | 93,904 B |
| `suggestion-menu` | 97,152 B | 97,297 B |
| `select` | 97,344 B | 97,487 B |
| `combobox` | 96,797 B | 96,940 B |

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** highlight

Consumers who relied on a re-render to put the highlight back on the `autoHighlightFirst` row lose that; the row is still highlighted on open, on first arrival and on a value change. Published types are unchanged.

Closes [UI-724](https://linear.app/bazzalabs/issue/UI-724/keep-the-highlight-when-a-menus-callbacks-or-items-change)
Closes [UI-647](https://linear.app/bazzalabs/issue/UI-647/apply-a-string-autohighlightfirst-inside-a-subpage)

author: thereal-kaze
body:
Finishes `CTaskComplexBeInCouple`: `CreateNextSubTask` (0x684840) and `ControlSubTask` (0x684930) were the last unreversed hooks.

### Reversed
- `GetPartnerSide` (0x683840, new hook): `LEFT` when the ped is on the left of the partner's right vector, else `RIGHT`.
- `CreateNextSubTask` (0x684840): no partner -> null; leader -> wander standard (walk, random dir 0-7, sensibly); follower -> walk alongside the partner (give-up distance).
  Arm IK is aborted in every branch.
- `ControlSubTask` (0x684930):
  - partner gone / dead, or the partner's `BeInCouple` (4 primary slots, 0x684979) missing, of the same role, or not with us (0x68498F) -> abort arm IK, null
  - follower: the walk-alongside offset is set to -1.05 / 1.05 by the partner side (0x684A07)
  - 2D distance over the give-up distance, or one of the two active `BeInCouple` tasks missing -> null (0x684AB4)
  - leader further than 2 units -> wait for ped (0.75, 20000 ms) unless it already has one (0x684AE2)
  - hold hands: under 1.5 units point the arm on the partner's side at the middle point (abort the IK first when the side changed), else abort (0x684B43)
  - look at each other: each one looks at the other with a 20% chance if not looking already (0x684C28)

### Other
- `m_Partner` is a `CPed::Ref` (no manual register / clean-up; the dtor is `= default`), copy ctor for `Clone`, members renamed (`m_Partner`, `m_IsLeader`, `m_HoldHands`, `m_LookAtEachOther`, `m_GiveUpDist`, `m_PrevSide`) and private.
- `CTaskComplexWalkAlongsidePed::SetOffset` (NOTSA) for the offset write.

### Testing
In-game A/B, the original vs ours: `ControlSubTask` for leader near / near facing away / too far to hold hands / waiting / giving up, follower near / facing away / far,
partner without the task, with the same role, dead; `CreateNextSubTask` for leader / follower / no partner. Returned task, previous side, walk-alongside offset
and the created tasks' fields identical in every case.

body: ## F5.3: mascota en la interfaz y cierre de F5 La web dibuja lo que el daemon ya sabía (`companion.*` de la F5.2). No hay métodos nuevos en el protocolo. ### Qué incluye - **Selector** (botón «Mascota» de la barra de estado): «Sin mascota» es la primera opción y la de por omisión; luego los paquetes válidos y, aparte, los no válidos con su motivo. La elección la guarda el daemon. - **Mascota en la esquina inferior izquierda**, debajo de la lista de espacios (ocupa su propio sitio: no tapa pestañas, paneles, compositor ni barra de estado). Reacciona a `companion.state` con fundido suave, hojas de sprites animadas y `prefers-reduced-motion` (primer cuadro fijo, sin fundido). Nombre accesible y aviso `aria-live="polite"` del cambio de estado. - **Recursos como imagen** (`CompanionAssetCache`): `companion.get` una vez y `companion.asset` por cada imagen distinta, `Blob` + URL de objeto para un `` (nunca SVG incrustado). Caché por id (3 paquetes, el elegido no se expulsa), sin fugas de URL (se crean al final y solo si el paquete sigue vigente; se revocan al expulsar, reconectar y desmontar). - **Carreras:** eventos repetidos o fuera de orden se descartan (`mergeState`), y al cambiar de mascota lo anterior deja de dibujarse al instante y una carga tardía se ignora (nunca se ve la imagen de la anterior). - **Fallos:** si falla el recurso de un estado se usa `idle`; si falla todo (o el paquete se borró del disco) no se muestra nada y la interfaz sigue igual. - **Ocultar:** preferencia de la ventana (`companionHidden` en los ajustes de interfaz existentes, `localStorage`), no del daemon. Decisión y alternativa descartada en ARCHITECTURE. - **Anchos estrechos (360-1280 px):** barra lateral `clamp(132px, 34vw, 232px)`, barra de estado que puede pasar a dos filas, selector centrado respecto de la ventana. Capturas `docs/capturas/f5-ancho-*.png`. - **Docs:** `docs/mascotas.md` (crear un paquete; conectar una externa por MCP o WebSocket), ARCHITECTURE «Interfaz de la mascota (F5.3)», README y ROADMAP con F5 completa. ### Pruebas - Unitarias, adversariales y fast-check en `apps/web/src/companion/` (decodificación base64, fusión de estado, resolución con `idle`, geometría de hojas, caché con base64 corrupto, mime raro, tamaños que no cuadran, descarte a mitad de carga, 500 cambios de estado, carreras de cambio de mascota, ausencia de fugas de URL). - E2E con el daemon real y el paquete de prueba del testkit (`e2e/companion.spec.ts`). - Capturas `docs/capturas/f5-*.png` (`NEXO_CAPTURAS=1 pnpm e2e -g capturas`). La app solo tiene tema oscuro. Closes #72

author: bryanggara
body:
## What and why

Fixes #684

This follows up #653 for three routes that still replied with the raw `error.message`:

- `server/routes/workflows.ts`, step run-again from a routine: this route preserves the message and declared numeric status of public errors, with 409 as the fallback. Any other error gives "The run could not start." with 500.
- `server/routes/phone-push.ts`, push and activity registration: `publicErrorText(…, "Could not save the registration")`. Status is unchanged: 409 for the phone cap, which is a `PublicError`, and 500 otherwise.
- `server/bot-api-host.ts`: the Bot API uses the same public error handling for the settings and request-claim routes. Status still comes from the error, so the 503 "Repair bot-api.json" refusal and the claim's own refusals (a moved Cloud, a backup running) keep their words; an unexpected claim error answers "Try again soon".

`prepareFrom` in `server/workflows/runner.ts` threw the intended refusal "That step is no longer in the workflow." as a plain `Error`. It is now a `PublicError` with 409, so the person still reads it. The webhook and app run-again route added in #732 keeps its own 409 status and now shows this text instead of its generic fallback. The detail of every other error goes to the server log only, with secrets removed, through `publicErrorText`.

## How you tested it

- `server/routes/workflows.test.ts`: a run-again `PublicError` with 409 keeps 409 and its text, one with 423 ("Wait for the backup to finish.") keeps 423 and its text, and an `EACCES …/Users/…` error gives 500 "The run could not start." (this replaces the old assertion that a plain error's text reached the client).
- `server/routes/phone-push.test.ts`: a new test checks that the 409 phone-cap refusal keeps its text, and that an `EACCES` error gives "Could not save the registration" while the detail is logged.
- `server/bot-api-host.test.ts`: a new test checks that the 503 settings refusal keeps its text, and that an `EACCES` error from `enable` gives 500 with no path in the reply while the detail is logged. The request-claim test checks that a `PublicError` refusal keeps 409 and its text, and that a claim failure with an `EACCES` path gives 500 "Try again soon" while the detail is logged.

```sh
npx vitest run server/bot-api-host.test.ts server/routes/phone-push.test.ts server/routes/workflows.test.ts server/phone-push.test.ts server/public-error.test.ts server/workflows/ server/host/workflow-host.test.ts
```

- Before the fix: the new or changed tests fail.
- After the fix: everything passes.

The first revision failed `pnpm typecheck`: `isPublicError` narrows the caught value to `Error`, so the direct cast to `{ status: number }` was rejected. The route now reads `status` once through `unknown`.

Rebased onto `main` (ed4f60d4a). Fork CI on the final head 107320d15 (typecheck, lint, brand-name check, all Vitest shards): https://github.com/bryanggara/seira/actions/runs/46101719149

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, and `pnpm test` pass (fork CI above)
- [x] New server behavior has a test
- [x] UI changes follow `DESIGN.md` and show before and after screenshots: N/A, no UI change
- [x] No secrets, personal paths, version bumps, or `dist-server/` changes

author: xloxn69
body:
## Summary

**Who benefits:** Students checking in on the bus; drivers recording students who have no phone, fixing a record, keeping seat notes, or removing a student; staff reviewing attendance.
**Why it helps:** Everyone on the bus can check in with one code. Each record says where it came from, and changes the driver makes offline are only final once the server accepts them.
**How:**
- Trip check-in challenges tied to one active run (10-minute codes; a refresh replaces the old code).
- `checkIns:record`, which takes the student from the session and keeps one logical record per student per run.
- A driver roster, plus driver actions that re-check the grant when they're accepted (attendance, corrections that keep history, seat notes where the newer change wins, scoped removal).
- Staff fallback and an attendance view, `routes:removeAssignment`, and Python device models.

#33 merged; this PR is now rebased onto main.

## Phase 7 progress

| # | PR | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #33 Backend: enrollment, guardian links, audit | Merged |
| 2 | Backend: check-ins, roster, driver actions (this PR) | Open |
| 3 | Web staff pages | Next |
| 4 | Web family | Planned |
| 5 | iOS family | Planned |
| 6 | Device (Python) queue and UI hooks | Waits on #25 and #27 |
| 7 | Driver UI check-in view | Waits on #26 and #27 |

Done-when items covered by this PR:
- Several students can use one trip challenge.
- Duplicate scans are idempotent.
- Wrong-purpose and expired check-in tokens fail.
- On the server side, an offline driver change is final only after it's accepted. The Pi's "pending sync" display comes in PR 6.

## Areas touched

- [x] backend
- [x] device (Pi) (new wire-model files only)
- [ ] driver-ui
- [ ] ios
- [ ] web
- [x] contracts / docs

## How I verified it

- **Tests first:** commit 8e58770 added 55 tests, and all 55 failed before the implementation (`Tests 55 failed (55)`). Afterwards the backend passes 257, contracts 77, and device 107 (5 new tests check the Python models against the shared fixtures). `bun run check` passes all 17 tasks.
- **What the tests cover:**
  - Two students on one challenge; repeat scans give one record; retrying a lost response returns the same result after the challenge expires; a reused requestId on another run is a conflict.
  - Rejected: an expired challenge, an enrollment code used to check in, another run's challenge, a student on another route, a guardian, a pending account, and any scan after the run ends.
  - The roster has no private fields, and another device's run or a revoked or expired grant is refused.
  - Staff fallback is idempotent. A queued action is accepted only if it was captured inside both the grant's validity and the run.
  - A correction keeps the original. An older seat note is superseded. Seat notes never reach families.
  - Removal keeps the student, links and history, and is audited with the reason and capture time.
  - A driver can't remove another route's student. A removal under a revoked grant is rejected and the student keeps access.
  - Implausible capture times and malformed bodies are rejected.
  - Every staff function denies five kinds of non-staff caller and changes nothing.
- **Live on the Convex dev deployment** (branch functions pushed with `convex dev --once`; never deployed), using fictional identities. I added a test device whose secret exists only in a local temp file, and a grant from `driverGrants:issue`. The run was started and ended through the real `trip-events` endpoint.
  - `qr-codes` issued a 10-minute code.
  - Student 1 and student 2 were both `accepted` on the same code.
  - Student 1 scanning again got `already_recorded` with the same record ID, and retrying the first request returned the same `accepted` result.
  - The guardian got `not_assigned`, a staff enrollment code got `wrong_purpose`, and an unknown account got `access_unavailable`.
  - The roster listed both students with source `student_qr_claim`.
  - The driver correction was `accepted`, and staff saw `not_boarded` (correction) with 2 history rows.
  - The seat note was `accepted`. An older one was `superseded`, and one captured before the grant existed was `rejected`.
  - A removal under a revoked grant was `rejected`, and the student still tracks.
  - After `endRun`, a scan got `run_not_active`.
  - Audit rows show the driver's name, `driver_device` and the capture time.
- **Not run:**
  - Live Clerk sign-in (no Clerk app yet).
  - The device-issued enrollment QR on dev: the seeded dev route version has no `routeId`, so it was correctly refused. The tests cover the success path.
  - The Pi itself: the device code that uses these models lands in PR 6.

## Surfaces checked

- **Clients:** the iOS and web family check-in screens (PRs 4–5) and the staff attendance page (PR 3) follow. Fixtures are ready.
- **Pi and backend:** every rule is enforced on the server. The device credential alone reads nothing; every endpoint also needs the driver grant.
- **Offline and restarts:** the server side of queued actions is done here: idempotent receipts, recheck at acceptance, and explicit `rejected` and `superseded`. The Pi queue is PR 6.
- **Contracts:** additive only (new tables, optional assignment fields, new endpoints and functions). docs/08 §9.2, contracts types and fixtures, and Python models are done. Swift DTOs come with the iOS screens in PR 5; no shipped client calls these.
- **Truthful states:** a check-in says "claim" or "recorded", never "verified boarding". `pending`, `accepted`, `already_recorded`, `superseded` and `rejected` are distinct.
- **Docs:** docs/08 §9.2.

## Review

Self-review of the full diff: done.

**Independent review, round 1** (fresh reviewer, given the brief, the diff and the test results). Four findings: three are fixed and one is rejected. The new tests went in first and failed (`4 failed | 54 passed`), then passed (`270 passed`). All fixes are in cda8001.
- **Expired grant accepted when the capture time was backdated.** Fixed: the grant must still be current when the action arrives (docs/08 §6). The capture time must also fall inside the grant's validity.
- **Attendance accepted between an offline run end and its sync.** Fixed: attendance is checked against `endCapturedAtMs`.
- **An older queued correction overrode a newer one.** Fixed: corrections are ordered by capture time. An older one returns `superseded`; a newer one that arrives later still becomes current.
- **Rejected scans aren't replayed on retry: not changed.** A retry is checked again from scratch against the current state: an approved assignment, an active run and a valid challenge. So nothing gets past the rules. Storing rejections would force every client to make a new ID after each refusal, and families would gain nothing from it.

**Round 2** (fresh reviewer, re-check of the fixes): every fix holds and no new defects were found. The reviewer also accepted the reason for not changing the rejected-scan behaviour. Backend tests ran independently: 270 passed. Ready.

**Live re-check after the fixes** (dev deployment, fictional identities):
- Staff fallback for a student with no phone: `accepted` (`staff_recorded`).
- A newer correction: `accepted`.
- An older queued correction: `superseded`.

The first live attempt found one more problem, now fixed in 2 commits (the test came first and failed, then passed: 285 backend tests). Device capture times were compared directly with server times: the grant's issue time and the run's start. A Pi clock a few seconds behind would therefore see a fresh action rejected. Now the action is compared with the run's start as captured on the same device clock, and 2 minutes of skew is allowed before the grant's issue time (the same `MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS` the device contract already uses). This loosens the check by at most 2 minutes, only around grant issue, and an expired or revoked grant is still always rejected. ## What it adds
- **The tunneling Onix (Rock Tunnel B1F, night):** a once-a-night rumble, then one of seven wall holes is open, a different one each weekday. Every hole leads into the new bore (`RockTunnel_OnixBore_hoenn`): a shiny Onix with Diamond Storm, Iron Ball, Star Piece, Big Nugget, and a hidden Metal Coat where it lay. Knocked out = back the next night. The exit returns you below that night's hole.
- **The Dunsparce burrows (Dark Cave south side):** one burrow hole per time of day, each in a different spot, all dropping into the new burrow (`DarkCave_Burrow_hoenn`). A Dunsparce clears one rubble row per time of day; after all four the passage opens to a Three-Segment Dudunsparce. A ladder leads back.
- **The vine ring (Route 21 islet):** four vine objects block the islet's middle by day (Cut won't work) and shift aside in the morning. The shiny Tangela (AncientPower, Big Root) waits there; a Miracle Seed is hidden there once it's caught.

- The holes keep opening after the Onix is caught; only the rumble stops.

- **Dunsparce:**

author: toddwbucy
body:
The stack for the connector's side of the weaver-admin service's socket. Today it holds the act's brief alone (#237), so its title carries `docs:` for now.

## What the stack will hold

admin-con stops invoking anything itself. It asks the weaver-admin service on the box's local socket for the grants, a verb, the trace and the admin log's lines, per `weaver-admin-operator-contract` section 8 on WeaverAgent's `main` at `265a332dd399ae633147d580e9602f38dd12de6b` (sha256 `040e707942b65ee10f986e1559e21db7b835cfae2cb82e304c63c048cd3e3f31`). The repository then holds no privileged invocation, and each connector's private key moves into a file of its own (the operator's rulings of 2026-11-26).

Child by child, as the brief orders them:

1. **The brief:** `docs/project/brief-2026-11-27-the-connectors-side-of-the-socket.md`. #237, merged into the stack.
2. **The socket's client and a fake service:** the opening, the framing, the eighteen refusal words, every line bounded, and a test-only fake written from the contract's section 8.10.
3. **The grants and the verbs over the socket:** admin-con's invoker asks the service. The sudo invoker and its tests are deleted. A new fault kind, `not_granted`, lands on both sides of the link, and the connector reads the `run` answer after a drop.
4. **The trace through the socket:** the relay's wire after `open`. `relay_unreachable` is a closed door, and a close before the header is confirmed once.
5. **The log through the socket:** `through_service` becomes each entry's `own`, and every close or reopen is a discontinuity.
6. **Each connector's key in a file of its own:** the trust rule on owner, group, mode and the key file's access list, with `request`, `adopt`, `register` and `rotate` following it.
7. **The Spec and the last guard:** sections 7.2, 8, 2.13 and 2.14, and `tests/no_privilege.rs` admitting no exception.

Each child carries its own Spec sections, its section 9 rows and a perturbation for each claim, and passes the repository's gates alone. This body is rewritten as one account of the whole when the last child is in.

Implements: named per child; rewritten at the close.

Closes no issue yet.

author: uakihir0
body: ## Summary Unit-mode blocks in the primitive kernel now admit statements: `pub fn f(x: I32) { let y = x + 1\ny }` and chained bindings, annotated bindings, `Str` bindings, `assert` statements, and expression-statements type through the same machinery as primitive-returning bodies. Expression-statements discard their values (spec 6.11.1) by synthesizing without an expectation exactly like the tail. Annotation mismatches diagnose at the initializer (`let y: I64 = x` with `x: I32` → TYPE_MISMATCH), as do operand mismatches in initializers (`let y = x + 1.5`). Statement checking in the kernel is almost entirely return-mode-independent — only the expression-statement fallback carried the return type as inference guidance, and in unit mode the correct guidance is none. The block-level literal defaulting covers statement literals through the shared floor mechanism. Chained on #475. Design notes: `docs/design/implementation-review.md` IR-1196. ## Failure boundary Statement-only bodies without any tail gate at the driver level (the diagnostics converter keys on the tail — an implementation artifact, not a spec boundary); `if`/`match` tails still fall back to the driver validators; bool-literal arithmetic operands keep the kernel-wide gate. ## Verification - Driver: 795 passed; CLI: 559 passed — extended with let/statement forms in unit bodies - Probes: chained bindings, `Str` bindings, expression-statements, asserts accepted; `let y = x + 1.5` and `let y: I64 = x` diagnose TYPE_MISMATCH; tail-less statement bodies gate Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7a6c267525b045bb8c57b30ba327b0fc Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/7a6c267525b045bb8c57b30ba327b0fc?variant=devin Requested by: @uakihir0 --- 🟢 Devin Review found nothing to fix · [View findings](https://app.devin.ai/review/uakihir0/sai/pull/476) · [Follow Devin's work](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7a6c267525b045bb8c57b30ba327b0fc)

author: ngominhtoan
body:
## Tóm tắt

Triển khai phần server của hợp đồng v2: đọc `resources.arsc`/binary XML, tách icon raster theo version, bind package tự động, và tên phiên bản linh hoạt.

### Thay đổi chính

- **ARSC + binary XML** (`src/apk-resources.ts`): parse ResTable/binary XML thuần `node:zlib`, resolve `android:label`, `versionName` dạng resource, color, và icon descriptor (raster/adaptive/vector) với giới hạn kích thước và follow reference ≤8 (cycle-safe). Lỗi/thiếu ARSC chỉ làm giá trị không khả dụng.
- **Icon raster** (`src/apk-icon.ts`): chọn PNG/WebP/JPEG density cao nhất ≤2 MiB, ghi `<versionDir>/version_icon.<ext>` + `version.json.icon`. Best-effort, không làm fail upload.
- **Icon hiệu lực**: `GET /apps/:id/icon` trả icon app-level → icon version published có `versionCode` cao nhất → 404. `AppSummary.iconPath` phản ánh fallback. `DELETE` chỉ xoá app-level, reset `app.json.icon = DEFAULT_ICON`; `PUT ?if_missing=1` trả `{ iconPath, skipped: true }` khi đã có icon.
- **Package binding**: app mới dùng `packageName = id` làm giá trị tạm; upload/import đầu tiên bind package thật vào `app.json` và `version.json.detectedPackageName`. Sau đó verify strict; package duy nhất (`409 package_in_use`), đổi package khi đã có artifact → `409 package_locked`. `allow_mismatch=package` vẫn hoạt động.
- **Sửa bug import**: khi `createApp` trả 409, đọc lại app và trả `409 package_in_use` nếu package khác, không mutate nhầm app.
- **Tên phiên bản**: `isValidVersionName` (≤200 byte UTF-8, cho space/`+`/`()`/Unicode, chặn path separator/control) dùng thống nhất ở routes, writer, scanner, download; lỗi `400 version_name_invalid`. Import fallback `String(versionCode)`.
- **Docs**: `README.md` viết lại theo skill `readme-optimization` (tiếng Việt), verify endpoint/flag/error/version-name với source.

### Fixtures & test

- Commit fixture thật từ APK release: `test/fixtures/resources.arsc`, `icon-adaptive.xml`, `icon-vector.xml`.
- Thêm encoder ARSC tổng hợp trong `test/apk-fixtures.ts` cho matrix default/en/density/anydpi.
- `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` → **115 test pass**.
- Verify real APK: label `My TestFlight`, versionName `0.2.0` (literal), icon adaptive `res/BW.xml`, không tạo version icon (APK không có raster); import thật tạo app/version thành công.

### Lưu ý

- API mới: `409 package_in_use`, `409 package_locked`, `400 version_name_invalid`.
- Fixture label thực tế là `My TestFlight` (không có dấu cách giữa Test/Flight), khác kỳ vọng ghi trong plan; test dùng giá trị thật từ ARSC.
- Không merge/tag/publish.

author: irisfield
body:
`messages.cancel({ filter: { label: "x" }, all: undefined })` type-checks, but sends `DELETE /v2/messages?count=100`, the same request as `messages.cancel({ all: true })`. `dlq.delete` and `dlq.retry` lose their filter or ids the same way.

`buildBulkActionFilterPayload` picked the `all` and `dlqIds` branches by whether the key exists, so a key set to `undefined` replaced the filter or ids that were passed. The branches are now picked by value. The filter branch also throws a `QstashError` when nothing is left to filter by, for example when the filter only has `api`, which is not sent.

| Call                                                          | Before                          | After                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `messages.cancel({ filter: { label: "x" }, all: undefined })` | `DELETE /v2/messages?count=100` | `DELETE /v2/messages?label=x&count=100` |
| `dlq.delete({ filter: { label: "x" }, dlqIds: undefined })`   | `DELETE /v2/dlq`                | `DELETE /v2/dlq?label=x&count=100`      |
| `dlq.retry({ dlqIds: ["a"], all: undefined })`                | `POST /v2/dlq/retry?count=100`  | `POST /v2/dlq/retry?dlqIds=a`           |
| `dlq.delete({ filter: { api: "llm" } })`                      | `DELETE /v2/dlq?count=100`      | `QstashError`, no request               |
| `dlq.delete({ all: true })`                                   | `DELETE /v2/dlq?count=100`      | `DELETE /v2/dlq?count=100`              |

I added tests in `utils.test.ts`, `dlq.test.ts` and `messages.test.ts` that run without `QSTASH_TOKEN`.

## Additional context

Behavior change: a filter with nothing to send now throws, and from plain JavaScript so do `all` values other than `true` and `dlqIds: undefined` when no filter or ids are passed. These calls were sent without a filter or ids before.

author: emreocell
body:
## What / why

Fixes 4 and 8 of the backlink-task walkthrough ("sign up on many sites with the bot's own AgentMail inbox"). With one inbox and a long job cut into 40-step sessions, verification mail went wrong in five ways; AgentMail dedup did not scale.

**Fix 4 — verification waits (`email_wait_for`)**
- **Origin bound at start.** The wait snapshots the browser's top origin (asked from the browser, as before) when it *starts*. Following the tool's own "do other useful work" hint and opening site B no longer turns site A's `followable_links` into `[]`.
- **Start watermark.** Mail dated more than 3 minutes before the wait started is ignored (it is an earlier sign-up's). Passing `max_age_minutes` explicitly turns the watermark off, so asking for older mail stays possible.
- **Delivered-mail bookkeeping.** A mail handed to one site's wait is not handed to another site's wait on the same inbox; the wait it went to may still ask for it again. (The watermark alone cannot tell site A's mail from site B's when the filter is loose.)
- **`repeat_stop` exemption.** `email_wait_for` with a `wait_id` is waiting, not looping: five polls in a row no longer abort the turn.
- **Persistence.** Pending waits (filter, start watermark, origin, deadline) and the links a wait judged followable are kept in `<data dir>/mail-waits.json` (owner-only on unix, written atomically; read only below 1 MiB, over-long records dropped). The bot's next session (a new run) takes a wait over by its `wait_id`, or by the same ask for the same `site` (same kind of start watermark, and not an earlier one), and remembers the links of the last 24 hours together with the site that allowed each (see review round below). A run that merely ends keeps the wait; an owner Stop forgets it.

**Fix 8 — AgentMail at scale**
- `AgentMailProvider::search` no longer returns outbound mail (`sent`/`draft` labels, own address as sender), like `list_new` already did.
- `email_search` exposes `page_token` and returns `next_page_token`, so the 100-message page is no longer a ceiling. IMAP accounts refuse `page_token` explicitly.
- `account_list` takes `domain` (registrable-domain match, so `www.` and full URLs work), `offset` and `limit` (up to 200) instead of a fixed 50-entry cut, and says "N-M of T" and the next offset.

## Key decisions

- **Missions wave 2's wait store is not in `main`** (no `waiting` state, no wait table; `git grep` over `origin/main`), so this adds a small durable store (`connector_email::WaitStore`, one JSON file, one shared instance per path) instead of a `missions.db` table. When wave 2 lands, the wait record maps 1:1 onto a row; `Waiters` only talks to the store through five calls.
- **The origin is still never the model's word.** `site` is only used to *find* a persisted wait of that site; links are judged against the origin the browser reported at start, and a `site` that disagrees with it still verifies nothing.
- **Watermark grace is 3 minutes** (`START_GRACE_SECS`): the form was submitted a moment before the wait is asked for. If the bot waited on a CAPTCHA handover for ten minutes first, the timed-out answer now tells it to pass `max_age_minutes`.
- **Persisted links keep the existing waiver, scoped narrowly:** same bot, root runs only (a sub-agent starts with none), https only, 24 h, 200 per bot, and `own_mail_waived` still requires an owner-started Full run and the exact URL. Review round: each stored link is bound to its wait's site; it opens without a card only while the browser is on that site and it passes the link check again against the owner's list as it is now.
- **Wait polling is exempt from `repeat_stop`** for ids in the store's own shape (`mw-` + 32 hex), up to 25 identical calls in a row (review round); it stays bounded by the wait's 10-minute deadline, the per-run waiting cap and `max_steps`.
- The tool-list size ceiling test (`tool_schema_bytes_per_call_stay_bounded`, 26 000) was already within ~100 bytes; the new descriptions are trimmed to fit rather than raising the ceiling, so the margin is a few dozen bytes.

## How verified

Commands run from the worktree with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`:

- `cargo fmt --all`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p connector-email -p builtin-tools -p agent-core --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --no-fail-fast -p connector-email -p builtin-tools -p agent-core`: connector-email 214 passed; builtin-tools 452 passed; agent-core 807 passed (1 ignored, as before). Doc-tests of the three crates pass.
- `node apps/desktop/ui/scripts/build-guide-index.mjs --check`: guide index up to date after the `docs/guide/email.md` / `tr/email.md` edits.
- Mutation check (each fix broken in turn, its tests must fail): all ten failed exactly the tests named for them — origin read at collect time (2 tests), no start watermark, delivered mail not skipped, no takeover by the same ask, `repeat_stop` exemption off, links not remembered, sent mail listed, run end forgetting the wait (2 tests), `account_list` ignoring `domain`, page token dropped. The tree was restored after each (`git status` clean).
- `cargo check -p cli -p evals --tests` (reverse dependencies of `connector-email`: `cli`, `daemon-api`, `evals`, `workflow-replay`): clean.

New tests, all on fake mail sources (FakeImap, a wiremock AgentMail, a live-editable inbox) and no real network:
- `connector-email`: `a_wait_ignores_mail_from_before_it_started`, `mail_handed_to_one_sites_wait_is_not_handed_to_the_next_sites`, `a_wait_keeps_the_origin_it_started_on`, `a_wait_survives_the_end_of_its_run`, `a_wait_is_taken_over_by_its_id_only_for_its_own_bot_and_account_until_stopped`, store unit tests (reopen, private file mode, corrupt file, caps), AgentMail `search_lists_received_mail_only_and_pages_past_the_first_hundred` and `search_refuses_a_page_token_that_cannot_be_one_before_any_request`.
- `builtin-tools`: `collecting_by_id_after_moving_on_keeps_the_start_origin`, `a_wait_collected_by_the_next_run_still_knows_where_it_started`, `a_claimed_site_that_is_not_the_start_page_verifies_nothing`, `the_account_list_pages_past_fifty_and_filters_by_domain`, the plan-watermark test; the old "a run that is over takes its waits with it" assertions were rewritten to the new contract.
- `agent-core`: `polling_a_mail_wait_by_id_is_not_a_repeat_loop`, `the_link_a_mail_gave_stays_followable_in_the_bots_next_session`, `stopping_a_run_forgets_its_mail_waits_for_good`, and the two wait-lifetime tests rewritten (a run's end keeps the wait for the bot's next run).

## Review round (Meta review, FIX_FIRST)

Five findings fixed with tests, one needed no change; the table is in the PR comment. After the review round: connector-email 222 and agent-core 886 tests pass, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean. `cargo test -p builtin-tools --lib` has one failure that is not from this PR (`files::guarded::tests::git_commit_and_branch_changes_take_the_write_path` from #923: a same-size rewrite within one second trips git's racy-timestamp check); details in the comment.

## Not verified

- No run against the real AgentMail service or a real browser; the origin probe is exercised through fakes (the real probe, `top_origin` of the browser tools, is unchanged).
- The Tauri desktop crate (it cannot build on this Linux host); it does not use any API changed here (`grep` finds no `connector_email` use under `apps/desktop`).
- An actual 40-step mission crossing a session boundary was not run end to end; the boundary is simulated by ending a run id and collecting under a new one.
- Windows: `write_private`'s `cfg(not(unix))` branch was only type-checked on its own for the msvc target (the crate cannot be cross-compiled here).

## Notes

- Cargo's shim queue was blocked for over an hour by two orphaned `agent_core` test binaries of another lane (parent PID 1, idle) holding both build slots, so the final builds used `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` directly with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, one job at a tim

author: pan93412
body:
Closes #158

## Problem

A node always registered with the addresses of the interfaces that hold the default routes. On a server with a private network on a second interface (a cloud VPC, a LAN in a data centre), the API server, kubelet and flannel traffic went over the public interface, and the firewall had to open the node ports to the internet. There was no setting to choose the interface.

## Change

A new setting, `network.interface`, for the first server and for a joining node (K3s and RKE2):

- `facts` takes the node addresses (`node-ip`) from that interface, with the same rule as before (no temporary IPv6). The default-route addresses that are on another interface become `node-external-ip`, so Ingress and `LoadBalancer` addresses stay public. `plan` shows them on a new `External` line.
- K3s: `config.yaml.d/20-node-ip.yaml` gets `flannel-iface`.
- RKE2: each server writes `server/manifests/zeatend-canal-config.yaml`, a `HelmChartConfig` for `rke2-canal` with `flannel.iface` (docs.rke2.io, basic network options). When the setting goes, a server that wrote the file keeps it with a blank interface (the default route), because RKE2 does not delete the resource of a removed manifest. Canal's interface holds for the whole cluster, so the docs say to give every RKE2 node the same interface name.
- The join address that `zeatend node add` prints and the registry direct addresses follow from the node's `InternalIP` and `node_ips`, so they use the interface without more code.
- Preflight fails when the interface does not exist, has no usable address, or holds an address in `100.64.0.0/10` (Tailscale). The Tailscale message points to the docs section.
- The configuration rejects the setting on KubeSolo, and rejects a string that is not an interface name.

Docs (en, zh-TW, zh-CN): a new page, `operations/private-network`, covers choosing the interface, nodes that join, K3s over Tailscale with `vpn-auth-file` in `90-local.yaml` (`--snat-subnet-routes=false`, `autoApprovers.routes` for the pod CIDR, and `node add --address` on the Tailscale address), and the manual steps to move an installed cluster to another interface. There are also rows in `reference/configuration`.

## Verified

- Unit tests: address choice, the files written for K3s and RKE2 (first server and join, worker vs server canal manifest, the blank manifest once the setting goes), NO_PROXY with the interface address, and each preflight refusal. `scripts/ci/lint.sh` and `scripts/ci/test.sh` pass (292 tests).
- Two Parallels VMs, each with a default route on `enp0s5` (10.211.55.x) and a host-only `enp0s6` (10.37.129.x):
  - `plan` fails on a missing interface, on a dummy interface with `100.100.1.1`, and on one with no address. KubeSolo refuses the setting.
  - K3s server and worker installed without the setting, then moved with the documented steps (server in place, then the worker with `join.server` on the new address). `kubectl get nodes -o wide` showed `INTERNAL-IP` 10.37.129.3/.4 and `EXTERNAL-IP` 10.211.55.38/.39. `flannel.1` was on `enp0s6`. A ping from a pod on one node to a pod on the other crossed `enp0s6` as VXLAN.
  - `node add` then printed `https://10.37.129.3:6443`.

## Not verified

- RKE2 on a real cluster (the Canal `HelmChartConfig` is covered by unit tests only), and the RKE2 server replacement steps.
- K3s over Tailscale: the docs come from the K3s docs and source and the Tailscale knowledge base. They were not run.
- A fresh install with the setting already set. The files are the same as in the move path, which was run.

author: uos-liang
body:
The EOM Lane Descriptor field EDLEN is 32 bits wide in the specification, but struct nvme_eom_lane_desc describes it as __le16 followed by 14 reserved bytes. Eye data lengths above 0xffff are truncated when printed, and the upper half of the field is mistaken for reserved bytes.

Widen edlen to __le32 with 12 reserved bytes, and read it with le32_to_cpu() in the walker and in both output formats. Keep the vendor specific data length in a 32-bit type so the bounds check and the hex dump see the full value.

A mock log with EDLEN 0x10000 shows 65536 in the text output and in JSON.

Fixes: https://github.com/linux-nvme/nvme-cli/issues/4451

- finding `fhirr4:expectedSupplyDurationNotInUnitOfTime` at `/dispenseRequest/expectedSupplyDuration/code`, `/unit` or `/value` -> `fhirr4:expectedSupplyDurationNotCarried` at `/dispenseRequest/expectedSupplyDuration`
- no finding at `/dispenseRequest/expectedSupplyDuration` for a comparator outside `<`, `<=`, `>=`, `>` (only `fhirr4:expectedSupplyDurationBound` at its comparator) -> `fhirr4:expectedSupplyDurationNotCarried` there too
- finding `fhirr4:dosageElementNotCarried` at a dose quantity's `/comparator` or at a later dose's `/value` -> `fhirr4:doseQuantityNotCarried` at `.../doseQuantity`
- finding `fhirr4:medicationNumberNotCarried` at a dose quantity's `/value` -> `fhirr4:doseQuantityNotCarried` at `.../doseQuantity`
- finding `fhirr4:doseUnitCodeOutsideUcum` at the `/code` of a dispense quantity or a dose quantity that is dropped for another reason -> removed
