- `sh:value` of `fhirr4:dispenseDaysSupplyNotCarried` and `fhirr4:expectedSupplyDurationNotCarried` stopped by the unit: the code (`"d"`) where its system is not UCUM's -> the stated system; the number (`"30"`) where no unit is stated -> the empty string
- accounting verdict `bridge:carried` of the `/system` of `dispenseRequest.expectedSupplyDuration`, a dispense `quantity` and `daysSupply` -> `bridge:consumed`
- accounting verdict `bridge:carried` of the `/value`, `/unit` and `/code` of those three and of a dose quantity, and of `/medicationCodeableConcept/coding/userSelected` -> `bridge:carriedInPart`
- accounting verdict `bridge:noHome` of a dose quantity's `/comparator` -> `bridge:consumed`
- `cascade:medicationRequestIntent` absent on a reported MedicationRequest's version -> written there (its version gets a new name)
- no finding for a `userSelected` that marks no selected code -> `fhirr4:userSelectedNotCarried`
- no finding for a reported request's intent outside R4's eight codes -> `fhirr4:medicationRequestIntentNotMapped`

## What each fix was

- [#83](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/83): the `system` of a supply duration, a dispense quantity and a days' supply is `bridge:consumed` under every prefix, as a dose quantity's is. Accounting only, so no entry shows it red by output.
- [#84](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/84): **the ruling on the issue replaces its "Wanted"**: nothing is carried with a comparator and no vocabulary pull request pairs with it. A dispense quantity or days' supply with a comparator is dropped whole, as before, and its one finding moves from the comparator to the quantity. The source's break of SimpleQuantity gets no finding of its own beside that one.
- [#82](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/82): a dropped supply duration, dispense quantity or days' supply is reported once, at the quantity, holding the value that stopped it, and the accounting of its number, unit and code says carried in part. A comparator outside R4's four now drops a duration whole and says so there; a dispense quantity dropped for its number no longer also reports its unit code.
- [#85](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/85): a `userSelected` that marks no selected code is a finding at it (new gap `fhirr4:userSelectedNotCarried`, kind `carriedWithLoss`, so the Bridge reports nothing from the entry beyond the mapping's own finding): on a code in another system, on an NDC that is no 11-digit code, on a later coding after the first selected one, and of `false`. Accounting carried in part naming it.
- [#87](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/87): every MedicationRequest carries its intent where it is one of R4's eight codes, reported or prescribed; outside them it is `medicationRequestIntentNotMapped` for both. Its accounting entry stays `carried`, as the finding sits at the path itself.
- [#96](https://github.com/the-cascade-protocol/cascade-bridge-adapter-fhir-r4/issues/96): a quantity with no `value` is dropped by the mapping (it requires one) and nothing said so, on all four quantities. Each dropped-quantity branch of `medication-dispense-findings.rq` and `medication-findings.rq` also fires when there is no value, holding the unit code, else the unit text; a days' supply or supply duration with no unit of time is already reported by its unit. A unit code outside UCUM is no finding of its own on a quantity with no number or one out of range, as on one with a number in no decimal form.

author: formalcommons-agent[bot]
body:
Proves `blowdown_weightBlowup`, the second half of the `blowdown_weightBlowup` bullet of `design/symplectic-blowup.md` (section `Blowup/Blowdown.lean`): blow down the divisor of the blowup of weight `l` and the result is the manifold `(M, σ)` again, up to symplectomorphism.

## The model chart (`Blowup/Weight/Basic.lean`)

- `WeightBlowup.modelChart hψ hl hε`: the inverse of `inr`, as a partial diffeomorphism from `WeightBlowup hψ hl hε` to `BlowupModel n`. It is Tau Ceti's `PartialDiffeomorph.liftOpens` applied to the inverse of `IsLocalDiffeomorph.diffeomorphOfInjective` for `inr`. Its lemmas: `modelChart_source` (the range of `inr`), `modelChart_target` (`openNbhd n ε`), `modelChart_inr`, `modelChart_toPartialEquiv_symm_apply` (the inverse is `inr` on `openNbhdOpens n ε`), `divisor_mem_modelChart_source` (the hypothesis `hf` of `DivisorBlowdown`) and `isSymplecticMapOn_modelChart` (the hypothesis `hσ` of `blowdownForm`). That last one comes from `mpullback_inr_form` through Tau Ceti's `Diffeomorph.isSymplecticMapOn_toPartialDiffeomorph_liftOpens`. As the issue says, no neighbourhood theorem is needed. These are API of the blowup and use nothing of the blowdown, so they sit with the blowup.

## The blowdown (`Blowup/Blowdown.lean`)

- `DivisorBlowdown.mem_outerPiece_divisor_iff`: the outer piece of this blowdown is `complDivisor`.
- `DivisorBlowdown.blowdown_weightBlowup`: there is a diffeomorphism `Φ` from this blowdown onto `M` that
  - pulls `σ` back to `blowdownForm`,
  - is `complDivisorSymplectomorph` on the outer piece (`Φ (inl x) = complDivisorSymplectomorph ⟨x, _⟩`), so it is the identity on `M ∖ ψ(B(l))`, and
  - satisfies `Φ (blowdownBall w) = ψ w` for `‖w‖ < √(l² + ε²)`.

  `Φ` is `GluedAlong.descDiffeomorph`, built from `complDivisorSymplectomorph` on the outer piece and `ψ ∘ complexToRealEuclidean` (through `IsSymplecticBallEmbedding.complexPartialDiffeomorph`) on the ball piece. Their images are `M ∖ ψ(B(l))` and `ψ(B°(√(l² + ε²)))`, which cover `M`. On the overlap both maps are `ψ` after `shellSymplectomorph`, by `inl_eq_inr_iff` and the two `coe_gluingDiffeomorph_apply` lemmas. `GluedAlong.mpullback_descDiffeomorph` then gives the statement on forms. The two pieces are symplectomorphisms by `isSymplectomorphism_refl` and `IsSymplectomorphism.subtype`, and they are local diffeomorphisms into `M` by `Diffeomorph.isLocalDiffeomorph_subtypeVal_comp`. The remaining steps are private lemmas of the proof.

## Supporting lemmas

- The ball piece uses `IsSymplecticBallEmbedding.isSymplecticMapOn_complexPartialDiffeomorph` (`IsotopyExtension/Ball/Complex.lean`), which #6385 has since added to `main` for #6141; this pull request no longer adds it. The import of `TauCeti.Geometry.Symplectic.Manifold.NeighborhoodGerm` that #6385 removed from `Blowup/Weight/Basic.lean` comes back here, since `isSymplecticMapOn_modelChart` uses Tau Ceti's `Diffeomorph.isSymplecticMapOn_toPartialDiffeomorph_liftOpens` from it.
- `TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm.IsSymplecticMapOn.isSymplectomorphism_toDiffeomorphSourceTarget` (`Manifold/SymplecticMap.lean`): a partial diffeomorphism symplectic on its source is a symplectomorphism from its source onto its target, for `PartialDiffeomorph.toDiffeomorphSourceTarget`. The ball piece uses it. The two older places in `Blowup/Weight/Basic.lean` and `Blowup/Blowdown.lean` that prove the same step inline are left to #6387.

`#print axioms DivisorBlowdown.blowdown_weightBlowup` shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. `lake build --wfail` passes on the branch merged with `main`, and `#lint only simpNF` reports none of the new lemmas.

## Sources

McDuff–Salamon, *Introduction to Symplectic Topology*, 3rd ed. [McDuffSalamon2017], §7.1.

Closes #5604

author: fslongjin
body:
## Problem

S3 (s3lvol) package creation mounted a metadata disk at the final package path and relied on the shim writing into that mount:

- publish could not tell a stale package directory from a live one, because the staging path and the final path were the same;
- sealing had to unmount before the block device was captured, and a live mount could leave catalog/metadata pages in the page cache, so the sealed snapshot could miss them and restore would fail;
- a seal failure left the package, its catalog entry and the published directory behind, so a retry could observe a half-built package.

## Change

Every backend now stages a package under `<home>.tmp` and publishes it with a single rename, so the shim only ever sees plain directories.

- Metadata is encoded onto its disk with `mkfs.ext4 -d` instead of being mounted, and the staged JSON is validated before publish.
- Finalize separates a fatal seal error (discard the sealed objects, the catalog entry and the published directory) from a deferred post-seal cleanup (warn and keep the package).
- Rollback reads the sealed metadata through a plain materialized copy that is released together with its derived volume.
- `mkfs.ext4 -d` support is probed when S3 storage initializes, so an unsupported host fails at init instead of on every request.
- The S3-only tmp/rename branches are removed from the shared pause, commit and app snapshot paths. XFS and JFS keep the same prepare, publish and finalize steps; the package pipeline is a no-op for them.
- Rollback requests validate the sandbox ID, and catalog entries auto-fill their S3 metadata volume reference when it is omitted.

## Compatibility

- **XFS**: unchanged. Same tmp+rename publish, same `metadata/`-only package, same catalog fields with no metadata volume.
- **JFS**: unchanged. Same JuiceFS staging and rename, same writeback wait before a template is reported shared-ready.
- **S3**: on-disk package layout is unchanged (`memory/`, `disk/`, `metadata/`); only the path metadata takes onto its disk changes.

The only cross-backend differences are failure-path strictness: a failed directory cleanup during publish is now reported instead of being logged and followed by a rename, and a pause that fails to expose the shim spec dir now removes the package it just published.

## Testing

- `go build ./storage/ ./services/cubebox/`
- `go test ./storage/ ./services/cubebox/`
- `gofmt` clean; `go vet ./storage/` clean

New tests cover staging and publish, fatal versus deferred finalize cleanup, the rollback metadata copy, the `mkfs.ext4 -d` probe, and a per-backend check that XFS and JFS remain no-ops across the package pipeline.

This is by an automated agent, not a human.

## What this changes

A ticket could pin the model its worker runs on, but not the tools. Worker sessions
therefore ran on one fixed baseline (`WORK_TOOLS`), and a ticket whose work needed a real
browser had no way to say so: the tool was either registered for every worker or for none.

A ticket now declares what its work needs beyond that baseline, and the declaration travels
the same path a pinned model already takes:

- **the routing decision** — `orchestrator_route` with `kind: accept` accepts `tools: string[]`;
- **the triggering request** — a `*.task.md` file carries one `tools: <capability or tool>, ...` line,
  which `toolsOf` reads into `Trigger.tools`;
- **the ticket** — `Tickets.create` fixes `outcome.tools ?? primary?.tools` on the ticket, so a later
  routing change cannot move it, exactly as `Ticket.model` already works.

`Sessions.workOnly` unions the declaration with `WORK_TOOLS` and keeps only names the profile
actually registers, so an **undeclared ticket keeps today's surface byte for byte**, and a
declared one gains exactly the tools its capability maps to (`src/core/capabilities.ts`:
`web-local` → `browser`; `browser-skill` → the six `bsk_*` tools; an unknown name is taken as a
tool name as it stands).

A worker that needs something its ticket did not declare now says so through
`orchestrator_report.tool_request` (`[{ tool, capability?, reason }]`, at most 6). The request is
recorded on the ticket next to the declaration and reaches the main Session through the ticket
card; **it grants nothing** — asking cannot become installing, unmasking or approving, and no
review gate moves.

## Before / After

Both captures are real production tickets in the desktop profile, created by the live
orchestrator from `*.task.md` files, workers fresh-started after the change; the full transcripts
and the worker's own evidence file are quoted below.

**Before — an undeclared ticket (no `tools:` line).** The worker's own tool list, verbatim, has no
`browser`; a `browser` call is unreachable, which is the baseline every ticket ran on:

```
baseline worker tools: read, write, edit, read_image, glob, grep, bash, pwsh, job_output,
job_list, job_kill, web_search, web_fetch, skill, todo_write, subagent, list_subagent_models,
send_message, list_agents, interrupt_agent, compress, decompress, search_context, acp_status,
acp_cache, acp_read_original_image (+ the profile's mcp__ / mnemon_ / ops_ tools)
→ browser absent; ticket card has no `tools`
```

**After — the same kind of ticket with `tools: web-local`.** The declaration lands on the ticket
(`tools: ['web-local']`) and `browser` appears in the worker's surface (item 4 of 64), and it was
really used:

```
browser open {"action":"open","name":"example","url":"https://example.com","waitUntil":"domcontentloaded"}
  → Opened tab "example" (https://example.com/)
browser run  page.title() / page.url() / page.evaluate(...)
  → {"title": "Example Domain", "url": "https://example.com/", text: "This domain is for use ..."}
browser run  tab.screenshot()
  → Screenshot captured: image/png (48.37 KB, 1706x960)
browser close {"action":"close","name":"example","kill":true}
  → Closed tab "example" and killed its browser
```

The worker also wrote the whole evidence file and a screenshot into its own ticket worktree;
both are attached in the ticket report of the delivery (`outputs/tool-policy-evidence/`).

No UI is changed by this PR: the ticket card gains `tools` and `tool_requests` as data, and the
panel renders the card from the same record it rendered before.

**A second capability, and what asking looks like.** A ticket declaring `tools: browser-skill`
gets that other row of the table instead — its worker reported all six `bsk_*` tools present and
made a real call, `bsk_session {"action":"start"}` → `no browser is currently connected` (the
BrowserSkill daemon is up at protocol 1.9; only the browser extension is missing on this machine,
which is the user's own install step). The same worker then asked for a tool it did not have:

```json
"toolRequests": [{"tool":"bsk_page","capability":"browser-skill",
                  "reason":"验证扩展连接后需要用 bsk_page 打开页面",
                  "at":"2026-11-27T03:57:22.789Z"}]
```

`tools` on that ticket stayed `['browser-skill']`: the request left a trail and changed nothing.

## Checks

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
- `pnpm vitest run tests/tools-declaration.spec.ts` — 7/7 pass: `toolsOf` parsing (including
  `tools:   browser ,  `), `declaredTools` expansion and de-duplication, an accept with
  `tools: ['web-local']` reaching the ticket and its card, a `Trigger` declaration inherited into
  its ticket, and `orchestrator_report` recording `tool_request` on the ticket while `ticket.tools`
  stays undefined.
- Full suite: unchanged versus `main` — the same pre-existing Windows-only failures
  (`spawn sleep ENOENT` in `tests/service-script.spec.ts`, one jsdom exception in
  `tests/client.spec.tsx`) and no new failing file.

## Rollback

Reverting this commit restores the single fixed worker baseline with no data migration: an
undeclared ticket is what every ticket is today, and `tools` / `toolRequests` are optional fields
that an older build simply ignores.

author: laurentdanner-bot
body:
## Ce qui a été fait

Tâche `mesure` : **rien n'est corrigé, `lib/` n'est pas modifié.** Question de P2-307 : signaler (état actuel) ou masquer un SIRET de clé juste sans le mot « siret » et une TVA à clé fausse sans libellé ?

- `bench/generate_corpus_references_14.py` : 3 000 textes logistiques synthétiques **sans donnée personnelle** (graine 42, 300 par forme : suivi de colis, commande, lot, facture, horodatage, quatorze chiffres groupés 3-3-3-5 et 4-4-4-2, TVA à clé fausse, TVA à lettre, témoin sans référence).
- `bench/analyse_references_14.py`, `bench/mesure_references_14.sh` (≈ 30 s), `bench/test_references_14.py`.
- Rapport : `agent/specs/P2-311.md`. Statut de P2-311 à « PR ouverte ».

## Mesures (chemin : `Ecluse.redact`; masquage simulé hors du code produit)

| Forme | Documents | Masqués à tort si on masquait | Signalés aujourd'hui |
|---|---|---|---|
| quatorze chiffres (7 formes d'écriture) | 2 100 | **206 (9,8 %)** | 206 |
| TVA à clé fausse ou à lettre sans libellé | 600 | **600 (100 %)** | 600 |
| sans référence | 300 | 0 | 0 |

- Un nombre de quatorze chiffres sur dix passe Luhn ; masquer toucherait **les mêmes documents** que le signalement actuel (contrôle de cohérence : 0 forme en écart entre la simulation et les avertissements).
- Constat hors fiche : ces références sont déjà **partiellement** masquées à tort par d'autres détecteurs (adresse 285 / 300 pour « 3 3 3 5 », téléphone, RPPS) ; aucune entité ne couvre la référence en entier, donc le signalement s'ajoute.
- Les 36 horodatages de Luhn juste se lisent tous comme une date valide ; 0 sur 19 736 nombres uniformes de Luhn juste : un filtre « horodatage valide » retirerait 17 % des signalements de ce corpus.

**Recommandation chiffrée** (détails dans le rapport) : garder le signalement et ne pas masquer (coût d'un masquage ≈ un document sur dix portant une référence, bénéfice non mesuré faute de témoin) ; réduire le bruit du signalement plutôt qu'élargir le masquage.

## Contrôle de fin de tâche

Rejoué : `melos run format`, `analyze`, `test` (tout vert), `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench` (OK). Corpus déterministe (test : deux générations identiques, aucune entité annotée, clés de Luhn notées exactement). `bench/etat.sh` en entier rejoué sur `main` au même commit (`575f246`, répertoire séparé) : aucune ligne ÉCHEC, `controle_etat.py` conforme hors un chemin absolu propre au répertoire de travail ; la branche n'ajoute que des scripts de `bench/`, un rapport et la ligne de statut : aucun chiffre ne peut changer, `etat.sh` n'a pas été rejoué une seconde fois sur la branche. Aucune valeur de texte réel : tout est tiré au hasard ; l'analyse n'imprime que des comptes.

Non vérifié : la fréquence réelle de ces références dans des textes de client (les 9,8 % sont le taux de Luhn d'un nombre aléatoire) ; le bénéfice d'un masquage (aucun témoin de SIRET d'entrepreneur individuel sans le mot) ; l'effet de la fenêtre de 40 caractères (trois gabarits courts par forme).

## À vérifier par le mainteneur

La décision signaler / masquer (recommandation : signaler) et l'opportunité de la tâche de réduction du bruit (horodatages).

## Summary

局所 P1 核が保証する仕事量を作用の事前見積もりに使う。非貫通の元残差と自由後流では、照会間で作用の作業領域を再利用し、照合済み幾何を結果に保持する。N4-06、N4-09、R-03。

## Related

Part of #19. 依存先は #368。

## Verification

- V-AERO・V-MULTI、有限核と理想参照および不確かさ。凍結水平翼・斜翼の M4/N12 で、各2,511アサーションを通し、全循環成分と元残差、近傍・遠方抗力を独立参照と照合した。M8/N24 は初回の事前拒否を切り分け、メタデータ枠128 KiBと修正した仕事量の見積もりで計算を開始した。正式格子 M128/N192 の数値予算と全パッケージの受入は残る。
- 子 Issue の完了。自由後流の2・4・8行で資源を検証した。実務規模の全履歴、写像、J1の受理済み履歴を含む作業を継続する。

- 次のパッケージの入口条件は IM-03 の終了審査で確認する。

- 局所核の実行上限は898,659ステップ。これより大きな許容値を指定しても作用の見積もりを増やさず、1ステップ足りない場合は拒否した。旧算入へ戻す変異を回帰試験が検出した。
- 再利用前後で自由後流3規模、Binary64 と TwoWord、5経路の計90件の結果指紋と相互作用数を照合した。8行の TwoWord 粒子速度は6,335,064 Bから253,040 Bへ、輸送の値・方向微分・転置は6,842,808 Bから760,784 Bへ減った。累積確保を計った。
- [x] GCC 14.2.0 Release と Windows 11 MSVC 19.52.37029 Release で、`aero.p1_induction`、`aero.p1_shared_action`、`coupling.case_uniform_flow`、`coupling.finite_wing_drag_refinement.fw_v01.m2n4` の4件ずつが合格。Windows の無変更の JSON パーサーには MSVC 19.51 の既存オブジェクトを使用した。

- [ ] 全体検証はCIで行う。

- [x] 元残差・自由後流の対象範囲と仕事量の上限が採用仕様に適合
- [ ] 数値認定、実験妥当性、製品規模の性能、実務受入は各終了審査で確認

## Risk / Rollback

仕事量には局所の最悪上限と準備の実行分を計上する。予算上、直列の作業領域を使えない場合は既存の個別確保を判定する。

body:
# Pull Request

## Description

Home Assistant always passes a `float` (for example `49.0`) to `ChargerNumber.async_set_native_value`. Previously, `set_type == "int"` rounding was only applied inside the `if scale:` branch, so unscaled integer-typed number entities such as `pdt` (`pv_battery_discharges_until`) forwarded a `float` to the charger, causing the charger to reject the command with `value must be uint8_t`.

This PR moves the `set_type == "int"` `round()` conversion outside the `if scale:` branch so every generic integer-typed number write (scaled or unscaled) sends an exact `int` to the charger, while preserving `fte` dispatch, scaling, and `float` pass-through behavior.

## What this changes

Lowers same-component `peer-*` sibling variants (`peer-aria-*`, `peer-disabled`/`peer-enabled`, `peer-data-*`, `peer-rtl`/`peer-ltr`, `peer-first`/`last`/`odd`/`even`/`only`/`nth-*`, `peer-read-only`/`peer-placeholder-shown`, interactive `peer-hover`/`peer-focus`/`peer-focus-visible`/`peer-pressed`, and negated `not-peer-*`/`peer-not-*`) on React Native from preceding `.peer` siblings in the same parent element.

- `crates/hozo_native/src/context.rs`, `render/child_list.rs`, `render.rs`, `render/host.rs`, `render/wrappers.rs`: tracks preceding `.peer` siblings per parent without inheriting them into descendants. Prop-driven and compile-time structural peers (`peer-aria-*`, `peer-disabled`, `peer-data-*`, `peer-first`, etc.) add zero runtime components or wrappers. When a following sibling reads interactive `peer-*` state, only the referenced preceding `.peer` controls receive a `hozoPeerId`, the parent wraps its children in `<HozoPeerScope>`, and the consuming sibling reads only its referenced IDs via `<HozoPeerQuery peerIds={[...]}>`.
- `crates/hozo_native/src/conditions/guards.rs`, `conditions.rs`, `conditions/stacked.rs`, `conditions/unwired.rs`: routes `Condition::Peer(_)` through `guards::resolve` with exact CSS general-sibling existential semantics (`∃ preceding .peer`), preserving distinct `peer-not-*` (`∃ peer: !P(peer)`) vs `not-peer-*` (`!(∃ peer: P(peer))`) negation semantics and refusing missing peers, missing drivers, or `-of-type` variants per Decision 003.
- `packages/primitives/src/peer-store.ts`, `peer-context.native.ts`, `runtime-peer.native.tsx`, `generated/peer.ts`, `pressable.native.tsx`, `text-input.native.tsx`: adds a lightweight, zero-host-View external peer store (`HozoPeerScope` / `HozoPeerQuery`) using `useSyncExternalStore` so hovering or focusing a peer only re-renders following siblings subscribed to that peer ID, never the parent container or unrelated siblings. Regenerated `packages/compiler/src/generated-abi.ts`, `packages/core/src/generated/peer.ts`, and package metadata via `scripts/generated-abi.mjs` and `scripts/package-metadata.mjs`.
- `packages/tailwind-conformance/src/native.ts`: adds `'Text after a peer Pressable'` probe context.

### Stack dependencies & merge order

Layer 2 of 3 in this Native variants coverage stack:

1. #2332 (`feat/native-data-attribute-variants`, base `main`)
2. **This PR** (`feat/native-peer-variants`, base `feat/native-data-attribute-variants`)
3. `feat/native-focus-within-and-has-variants` (upcoming)

## What was measured

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — pass
- `cargo clippy -j 1 --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — pass
- `cargo test -j 1 --workspace -- --test-threads=1` — all workspace Rust crates passed (including new `peer_sibling_props_and_interactive_states_lower_in_same_parent`)
- `pnpm --filter @hozo/compiler build:native` — rebuilt `packages/compiler/hozo_napi.node` cleanly
- `node scripts/generated-abi.mjs --check` & `node scripts/package-metadata.mjs --check` — pass
- `pnpm lint` (`biome check .`) — pass
- `pnpm docs:check` — pass
- `node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/primitives/src/runtime-peer.test.ts scripts/native-hosts.test.mjs packages/tailwind-conformance/src/arbitrary-native-audit.test.ts packages/tailwind-conformance/src/snapshot.test.ts packages/tailwind-conformance/src/snapshot-versions.test.ts` — pass
- `packages/compiler` unit suite (`node --test --test-concurrency=1 src/*.test.ts`) — pass
- Conformance snapshot deltas (`packages/tailwind-conformance/snapshot.json`):
  - `nativeVariants.covered`: `13077 -> 13581` (**+504** newly covered single & stacked combinations across `peer-hover` and `peer-aria-expanded`)
  - `nativeVariants.restricted`: `9543 -> 10047` (**+504**; every newly covered combination is restricted to siblings preceded by a matching `.peer` and refused elsewhere)
  - `nativeVariants.refused`: `16326 -> 15822` (**-504**)
  - `nativeVariants.noCounterpart`: `8235` (unchanged; 0 `NO_NATIVE_COUNTERPART` covered)
  - `nativeVariants.silent`: `0`, `noOp`: `0`
  - Unchanged: `native` (`119/124`, `silent: 0`), `nativeContextual` (`40/40`, `silent: 0`), `diagnostics` (`37/39`, `silent: 0`), `arbitraryNative` (`493/2845`, `silent: 0`), `arbitraryNativeAudit` (`validCovered: 493`, `contextCovered: 15`, `implementable: 0`, `layoutMeasurable: 0`, `silent: 0`)

## Anything left open

- Named peers (`peer/name`), peers inside opaque carried expressions (`Child::Verbatim`), and unwired peer states (`peer-open:`, `peer-checked:`, etc.) remain explicitly refused on Native.

body:
## Summary
Modules in one package still carry docstrings and explanatory comments, against the rule that code is self-explaining.

**Goal:**
Remove every docstring and every comment that is not a '# why:' reason, a shebang, an encoding line or a tool directive (noqa, type, pragma, fmt) from the listed scope source files, without changing behaviour. Where a removed docstring or comment carried a reason the code cannot show, keep it as a '# why:' comment; where it only described what the code does, rename or extract so the code says it. Do not change any function signature, name used by another module, CLI help text, log or error message, or line budget. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.

author: dolzaan
body:
Correções das falhas encontradas na auditoria das 14 falhas.

**Graves**
- **Apagar mídia de outros usuários (IDOR):** `updatePropertyMedia` e `updateFreighterImages` apagavam com a chave de serviço as chaves enviadas pelo navegador antes de conferi-las. Agora `removePropertyMedia`/`removeFreighterImages` recebem a pasta (`authUserId`) e ignoram qualquer chave fora dela (`lib/listings/media-ownership.ts`). Arquivos que o anúncio deixou de usar usam a pasta do dono do anúncio.
- **Tomada de conta pelo e-mail:** `syncAuthUser` só vincula uma conta existente a uma nova sessão se o login for Google com o mesmo e-mail confirmado (`canLinkExistingAccountByEmail`).

**Médias**
- Migração `20261127120000_security_audit` (incluída no build de produção, idempotente): RLS em `metricas_diarias_freteiros` e `_prisma_migrations`; remove a policy de UPDATE em `property-images`/`freighter-images` (permitia trocar o conteúdo depois da conferência) e as policies de INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE em `profile-images` (o avatar sempre vai pelo servidor). A policy de DELETE dos anúncios continua, porque o navegador apaga os próprios arquivos quando um envio em lote falha.
- Pausa da moderação zera `publishedAt`: o dono não consegue reativar sem nova aprovação, e o botão "Reativar" some nesse caso.

**Baixas / higiene**
- `generateMetadata` de imóvel e freteiro não expõe título, descrição nem foto de anúncio fora do ar; o redirecionamento de `/imovel/[codigo]` só funciona para anúncios ativos.
- JSON-LD passa por `jsonLd()`, que escapa `<`, `>`, `&` e separadores de linha.
- `getSupabaseServiceRoleKey` saiu de `lib/supabase/config.ts` (importado pelo navegador) para `lib/supabase/admin.ts` (`server-only`).
- `.vercel` e `.claude/` no `.gitignore`.

**Testes novos:** chaves de outro usuário nunca entram na remoção (inclusive com `../`); vínculo por e-mail recusado para login não-Google, e-mail não confirmado ou e-mail diferente; pausa da moderação não pode ser desfeita pelo dono; JSON-LD com `</script>` não fecha a tag.

**Não verificado:** a migração só roda no build de produção (não há banco local); envios de foto e vídeo depois de remover a policy de UPDATE não foram testados contra o Supabase real.

Fetching artifact metadata for "github-pages" in this workflow run

| Action | 이전 | 이후 |

| checkout | v4 | v7 |
| setup-python | v5 | v7 |

| upload-pages-artifact | v3 | v5 |
| deploy-pages | v4 | v5 |

- PR에서는 `check` job만 돕니다. 배포가 고쳐졌는지는 병합 후 main 실행에서 확인해야 합니다.

## 요약

/awards 3D 무대의 계단 완화(안티앨리어싱)를 강화합니다. "안티앨리어싱이 없는 것 같다"는 피드백을 반영했습니다.

- **기존 상태**
  - 데스크톱은 MSAA 4배만 켜져 있었습니다. 배율 1 화면에서는 가는 선 일부 행이 중간값 없이 뚝 끊겼고, MSAA는 윤곽만 다듬어 무광 금 위 가는 하이라이트(기둥 나선, 깃 구슬)의 반짝임은 다듬지 못했습니다.
  - 모바일은 계단 완화가 아예 없었습니다.
- **변경**
  - 데스크톱: 화면 배율이 1이어도 1.5배로 그리고(슈퍼샘플링, 최대 2배), MSAA를 8배로 올렸습니다(GPU가 지원하는 만큼).
  - 모바일: MSAA 4배를 켰습니다.
  - 톤매핑 뒤에 SMAA를 한 번 더 겁니다. 위 둘만으로는 밝은 금속 윤곽(기둥 가장자리)에 계단이 남았습니다. MSAA는 톤매핑 전(HDR)에 섞는데, 아주 밝은 반사는 배경과 반반 섞여도 압축 뒤 거의 최대 밝기라 중간값이 사라집니다.
- **문서:** CLAUDE.md 어워즈 설명을 고쳤습니다.

## 확인 (1920×991, 배율 1, 144Hz)

| | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 그리기 버퍼 | 1920×991 | 2880×1486 |
| 프레임 | 144fps, 간격 p95 7.0ms | 144fps, 간격 p95 7.0ms(SMAA 포함) |
| 아치 왼쪽 가장자리 12행 | 중간값 없이 21에서 111로 뛰는 행이 섞임 | 모든 행에 중간값(30~42 → 63~111) |

- 모바일 폭(390px)에서도 무대가 정상으로 그려지고 콘솔 에러가 없습니다.
- `pnpm lint --max-warnings 0`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:coverage`(100%)를 통과했습니다.

author: victor-von-pooh
body:
## 概要

- ML-Pathfinder を submodule (`ML-Pathfinder/`, main の 60760c4. 中の ML-Quest も recursive で取り出す) で持つ
- バックエンド (`backend/`, `ml_studio`): `create_app(token, allowed_hosts, static_dir)` がトークン (`ML_STUDIO_TOKEN`, Cookie `ml_studio_token_<印>`, ヘッダー `x-studio-token`), Origin, Host を確かめ, `GET /api/auth` を持ち, ML-Pathfinder の `create_api()` を `/api/problem` に mount する (先に呼んで `app.state.problems_dir` を覚える). `/api` の下で合わない経路は 404, 他の経路は画面の `index.html`. `ml-studio` (`--host`, `--port`, `--allowed-host`) で起動し, トークン付きの URL を出す
- 画面 (`frontend/`): pnpm workspace に `ML-Pathfinder/frontend` を加え, `StageApp` と `stage.css` を import する. 上の帯 (名前, プロジェクトの欄, 5 つの段階の並び (今は問題の設定だけ押せ, 他は準備中), 明暗の切り替え) と, 経路の最初の区切りで選ぶ段階の画面 (react-router を使わず, `/` は `/problem` に移し, 段階ごとに key を替え, popstate を見る). 選んだプロジェクトは `localStorage` の `studio-project` に残す. React は `resolve.dedupe` で 1 つにし, Tailwind は `@source` で ML-Pathfinder の画面のソースを拾う
- `make setup`, `make dev`, `make build`, `make serve`, `make check`
- CI に backend (ruff, mypy, pytest), frontend (lint, format, typecheck, vitest, build), e2e (Playwright) のジョブを足す
- TODO.md の高「殻の最小の形を問題の設定の段階だけで通す」を消し, 中の README と GUIDE の項目を今の形に合わせる. README.md に今の起動の仕方を書く

## 確かめ

- `make check` (ruff, mypy strict, pytest 12 件, oxlint, prettier, tsc, vitest 13 件) と `python scripts/check_docs.py`
- `cd frontend && pnpm e2e`: 殻を作業用の置き場で起動し, `/api/auth` で入り, `/problem` で問題の設定を作り, プロジェクトの欄に出て, 選ぶと開き, 再読み込みと知らない頭と戻るでも開いたままで, 画面の誤りが無い
- `make build` と `make serve` で起動し, Playwright で `/problem` が開き問題の設定を作れること, 明暗の切り替えが段階の画面に効くことを見た. `make dev` で Vite の開発用のサーバーから submodule の画面のソースが配られることも見た
- バックエンドと画面を別のエージェントがレビューし, 指摘 (画面の配信の 500, ASCII 以外のトークン, 戻るで殻が経路を置き換えたときの作り直し, 押せない段階の読み上げ, 本文へ飛ぶリンクなど) を直した

author: supritha-kumar
body:
Jira: [DOC-14306](https://jira.issues.couchbase.com/browse/DOC-14306). Engineering: [MB-70444](https://jira.issues.couchbase.com/browse/MB-70444) (XDCR - CE restrictions enforcement) and [MB-70748](https://jira.issues.couchbase.com/browse/MB-70748) (XDCR over CNG), epic MB-70439.

From Couchbase Server 8.5, Community Edition enforces the license rule that XDCR is an Enterprise Edition feature: CE-to-CE replication is blocked. The docs only said the license disallows it. This PR documents the enforcement.

## What changed

- `modules/manage/pages/manage-xdcr/xdcr-management-overview.adoc`: a new subsection under XDCR and Community Edition, **Enforcement from Couchbase Server 8.5** (`#ce-restrictions-enforced`):
  - A source/target edition table: only CE → CE is blocked. CE → EE is still allowed, for example to migrate.
  - **New references and replications:** a reference from a CE cluster to another CE cluster fails with an error.
  - **Existing replications:** after the source upgrades to 8.5, they're automatically paused and can't be resumed. The references remain and no data is lost.
  - **Mixed mode:** one 8.5 node is enough. A request that reaches an older node creates the replication, but it's paused when it starts on an 8.5 node.
  - **XDCR over CNG:** a CE source can't create a CNG reference, with a link to the CNG page.
  - **Couchbase Support** can lift the restriction temporarily, for example during a migration to EE. It can't lift the CE restrictions that existed before 8.5, such as XDCR over TLS, filter expressions, and replication to Ephemeral buckets.
- `modules/introduction/pages/editions.adoc`: the CE note now says 8.5 enforces the restriction, with a link to the new subsection.

The 8.5 release note for this change is already in `docs-server-8.5.0-fixes-and-improvements.adoc`, so this PR doesn't add one.

## Sources

| Content | Source |
|---|---|
| Edition matrix, error on new references, autopause of existing replications, references kept, mixed-mode behaviour, pre-8.5 restrictions not covered by the override | Engineering design "CE restriction enforcement by XDCR" (Sumukh Bhat), linked from MB-70444 |
| No data loss, CE → EE allowed for migration, Support can lift enforcement | PRD "Enforce CE Restrictions" (Hyun-Ju Vega), requirements 7–9 |
| XDCR over CNG | Engineering design, "XDCR over CNG" section and its 11 June update; MB-70748 behaviour matrix (Aditya Sood) |
| Wording of the user-visible effect | MB-70444 Release Notes Description |

## Please review

- **XDCR over CNG:** the design's 11 June update says EE → CE over CNG works by default, and CE → EE over CNG works only with the override. The page says only that a CE source can't create a CNG reference. Confirm that's the right level of detail, or whether to describe the Support override for CE → EE over CNG.
- **Override:** the page says to contact Couchbase Support and doesn't name the `disableCERestrictions` setting or the diag/eval command, since they're Support-only. Confirm.
- **8.0.2:** MB-70444 has an 8.0.2 backport (MB-70754), but the design says the enforcement isn't backported to 8.0.2 because the ns_server diag/eval change wasn't. The page says 8.5. Confirm no 8.0.x docs change is needed.
- **Error message:** the page doesn't quote the error or the paused-replication message, because I couldn't find the final text. The screenshot on MB-70444 shows the UI for a paused pre-existing replication. If you want a screenshot or the exact text, I can add it.
- **5-node limit:** the general CE enforcement (5-node limit) is DOC-14290 (resolved), so it's not covered here.

## Verification

- Checked both changed files on the branch.
- No local build has been run. In the preview, check the new table and the `#ce-restrictions-enforced` xref from the editions page.

author: xrpd
body:
The soundness step for the debate protocol of Brown-Cohen, Irving and Piliouras (arXiv:2311.14125v1, Figure 1) holds under the paper's Definition 6.1 for machines whose every step queries an encoding of the whole transcript so far (#8586 and #8363, both merged). This PR shows that both parts of that assumption are needed, with two machine-checked examples. The reading of the source behind this, and what it costs, are in [this comment on #7579](https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/issues/7579#issuecomment-7141095342).

**Neither example refutes Theorem 6.2 of the source.** The theorem claims that some protocol exists. The examples concern the protocol the source gives for it, Figure 1, with a machine that satisfies Definition 6.1 but not the whole-transcript assumption. Another protocol may meet the theorem's claim.

**1. Every step must be a query** (`Debate/CopyChain.lean`). The *copy chain* writes `false` and then copies the previous bit. It makes no oracle query, so it satisfies Definition 6.1 with every constant; in the strict form printed in the source, with every positive constant against every oracle at positive distance. It outputs `false` with probability 1. A proposer that claims a small positive probability of `true` while the last bit is `false`, below the verifier's tolerance, and probability 1 afterwards, is never rejected: the verifier's samples of a deterministic step are exact, so an abort is accepted, and without an abort each round turns the bit to `true` with the claimed probability.

- `le_evalWith_run_copyChainProposer`: acceptance at least `1 - (1 - k/N)^rounds` against every challenger, for any parameters with at least one verifier sample and any claim `k/N` that is positive and below the verifier's tolerance.
- `not_sound_figure1_of_lipschitzAt_run`: with the constants printed in Figure 1 for `K = 1`, for a run of `T` steps with `307 ≤ T` (at least 307 steps), some proposer is accepted with probability above `2/5` against every challenger.
- `not_sound_default_of_lipschitzAt_run`: the same with the constants of #8363, for a run of `T + 1` steps with `51 ≤ T` (at least 52 steps), so the hypothesis of its soundness step cannot be weakened to Definition 6.1.

**2. The query must determine the transcript** (`Debate/TwoBlock.lean`). The *two-block machine* queries its oracle at every step, with queries of at most two bits. It runs two identical blocks, each a start query answered `false` followed by `m` queries at the previous bit, answered with that bit, and then queries the pair of the two end bits `(u, v)`, answered `true` with probability `c + c (u - v)` for a parameter `c`. The final theorems take `c = 1/4`. The two blocks reuse the same one-bit address. A fixed replacement oracle gives that address one probability in both blocks, so the blocks keep the same law and the machine is 1-Lipschitz; the proposer gives it a positive probability in the first block and zero in the second.

- `lipschitzAt_run_twoBlockMachine`, `evalWith_run_twoBlockMachine`: the machine is 1-Lipschitz at its oracle (non-strictly) and accepts with probability `c`, for every `m`.
- `le_evalWith_run_twoBlockProposer`: the acceptance bound against every challenger, for general parameters, with the verifier's rejection probability in the last round as a hypothesis.
- `not_sound_figure1_two_of_lipschitzAt_run_twoBlockMachine`: with the constants of Figure 1 for `K = 2`, for blocks of length `m` with `1201 ≤ m` (a run of `2 m + 3` steps, at least 2405), some proposer is accepted with probability above `2/5` against every challenger. The constant 1 is attained for this machine, so it satisfies the printed strict inequality only with a constant above 1; this is the statement for the printed definition.
- `not_sound_figure1_of_lipschitzAt_run_twoBlockMachine`: the same with the constants for `K = 1` and `601 ≤ m` (at least 1205 steps), under the non-strict reading of Definition 6.1.

The machine has seven addresses, the strings of at most two bits. The source's oracle has addresses of one fixed length; recoding into three-bit addresses changes nothing in the argument.

**What the statements are about.** The checked conclusions concern the interpreter `Debate.run` of #8363: claims and coins lie on a grid, and the interpreter computes the bit of each round, with the abort after the bit as in Figure 1. In Figure 1 the proposer can announce the same grid probabilities, supply a uniform share of the coin and set the bit as prescribed, with the same probabilities and the same argument for an abort. `Params.figure1` takes the constants printed in Figure 1 and in the proof of Theorem 6.2, with the sample counts rounded up and the natural logarithm (which the proof's own arithmetic fixes). Definition 6.1 is `ProbOracleComp.LipschitzAt`, with `≤`; where the strict form matters the docstrings say which statement covers it.

**Changes to `Debate.lean`** (117 lines):

- Visibility. `runFrom` and `sampleCount` become public and exposed; `Round.bit`, `History.bits`, `run`, `honestProposer` and `Params.default`, already public, become exposed; `countTrue`, `verdict` and the honest coin `uniformCoin` become public without being exposed. `countTrue` cannot stay private, because the exposed `honestProposer` uses it in its body; the law of `uniformCoin` is `evalWith_uniformCoin`. The two example modules reason about the interpreter round by round. This answers open question 1 of #8363 in the direction "open it when a second module needs it".
- `evalWith_uniformCoin`: the law of the honest coin on a nonzero grid is uniform, stated publicly for the example modules; the private `ev_uniformCoin` now follows from it.
- `evalWith_verdict_false_le`: the Hoeffding bound for the verifier's check after an abort, for any parameters. The two-block argument needs it in the last round, where the oracle's answer is a real coin; the private count law stays private.
- `evalWith_verdict_of_pure`: at a deterministic step the verifier accepts every claim within its tolerance of the prescribed bit. Both example modules use it; its count lemma is private.
- `map_coinBit_uniformOfFintype_right_false`: a uniform coin from the proposer's copy makes the bit of a round `false` with probability `1 - k/N`. Both example modules need it; before, each derived it in place.
- `Params.figure1`: the constants printed in Figure 1 and in the proof of Theorem 6.2, beside `Params.default`.

The review of #8363 suggested a plain import of the logarithm file in place of the public one. This PR exposes `Params.default`, whose body uses the logarithm, so the public import stays.

The PR adds four lemmas (`evalWith_uniformCoin`, `evalWith_verdict_false_le`, `evalWith_verdict_of_pure`, `map_coinBit_uniformOfFintype_right_false`) and one definition (`Params.figure1`) to `Debate.lean` and opens the visibility of its interpreter; it changes no statement of #8363.

**Not included.** A repaired protocol; soundness at the constants printed in Figure 1 for whole-transcript machines; anything about running time; and the examples the review of #8363 asked for, applying its two theorems to concrete step laws, which will be a test-only follow-up. These are follow-ups under #7579.

**Changes after review.** In response to the review at `4c9560ca4d`, in seven commits on top, with no headline statement changed and no definition's body changed:

- `one_sub_pow_succ_le` and `ofReal_div_natCast`, general facts about `ℝ≥0∞`, move with their statements unchanged from `CopyChain.lean` to `Foundations/Analysis/ENNRealNatDiv.lean`, as `ENNReal.one_sub_pow_succ_le` and `ENNReal.ofReal_div_natCast`; that module needs no new import for them.
- `Crypto/Protocols/FRI/JohnsonSoundness.lean` is touched because the hosted Duplicate-statement scan matched `ofReal_div_natCast` with its private `natCast_div_eq_ofReal`, the same statement reversed. That lemma is deleted and the shared lemma is used, reversed, at its two uses; the file's only oth

body:
## What and why

Fixes #654.

- `renderToSVG`, `renderFirstView` and `renderToImage` (`src/server.ts`) check that the style has a list `layers` before they use it. A style without one now rejects with `[map-jr-gl] E654 The style has no list "layers". Give a style object with "version", "sources" and "layers", or its URL.` instead of `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`. The map rejects the same style (E539, `src/map.ts`), so the server rejects it too and does not draw it as empty. The text is the same as E539; the code is E654 because `scripts/messages.mjs` requires one code for each text.
- A custom `encoding` of a `raster-dem` source (and of a contour) with a factor or shift that is not finite is read as `mapbox` with a warning, as in the map. The guard is in `src/server.ts` only (code E10654, because the same text cannot share E590); `Engine.setStyle` is unchanged, so no page script or worker file changes (#2342).

Other fields that `src/server.ts` reads from the style: I read them and found no other unguarded read on the path (`styleImages` and `metadata` use `?.`; `resolveStyle` guards sources). Not a complete audit of every field.

## How it was checked

- New `test/unit/server-style-checks.test.ts`: 2 tests. Without the fix both fail (TypeError); with it both pass.
- `pnpm build && pnpm test`: 551 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm test:consistency`: passes (only docs-lint warnings about fence width that are on `main`).
- Size (gzip -9 of every file of `dist/*.js`, on the merge with `origin/main` and without the change): only `server.js` differs, 61333 / 61548 (+215). `pnpm test:size`: page script and worker of a map 136509, with compat 146041, both unchanged; `server.js` 61859, limit 64 KB.
- Not run: browser suites (`test/interact.mjs` has an E590 check that I did not run; the code moved, its text did not).

## Done when

- [x] A test fails without this change and passes with it
- [x] Both entries considered (the check is in `resolve.ts`, shared)
- [x] A mistake by the user gets a clear message
- [x] `pnpm test:size` passes, and the bytes are above
- [x] `docs/reference/messages.md` regenerated

## Needs the owner?

No.

body:
Part of #2092

For $a \gt 0 \gt b$ (or the reverse) with $c$ near $a + b$, the Maclaurin, 1 − z and 1/z series cancel by up to hundreds of digits, e.g. `hyp2f1(630.125, -368.12509, 262, 0.98 + 0.08i)` is off by 1.6e21. The analytic continuation along the hypergeometric equation now also runs for mixed-sign $a$, $b$ with $c \gt 0$, and for the Pfaff transform ([DLMF 15.8.1](https://dlmf.nist.gov/15.8.E1)) with $c - b \lt 0$. Its Maclaurin start moves in to $x_0 \le c / (4 \lvert ab\rvert)$, which bounds the first term ratio by 1/4; later alternating terms can still grow and cancel.

| reproducer above | 1 | 1.6e21 → 3.8e-14 | | |
| $a \in [29, 767]$, $b \in [-398, -3]$, integer $c = a + b + d$, $\lvert d\rvert \le 10^{-3}$, $\lvert 1 - z\rvert \in [0.01, 0.49]$ | 395 | 1.1e308 → 2.6e-10 | 4.7e30 → 2.5e-13 | 1 → 0 |

body:
**What.** The Links category tree moves out of the page into the app sidebar, the way Notes' page tree already does (`PageDef.side`): "‹ Links" on top, then a new-category row, the fixed rows with icons (All, Just saved, Not filed), then each area as a quiet label with its dot and its categories under it. Areas no longer fold; categories still do. When the sidebar has no room (folded, Zirma wide, phone) the tree comes back into the page, with the same layout; a narrow page still taps in. Rows, twists and labels for both trees now live in one `packages/ui/src/side-tree.css`; `notes.css` and `links-tree.css` keep only what is their own.

**Why.** The tree was a second navigation column right next to the sidebar, which pushed the content into a third column. And the two sidebars (Notes, Links) had different grammars for the same kind of thing.

**Design.** `docs/design/links.md` §4.10.8 (v0.7).

**Checked.**
- `npm test` (548) and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- New `packages/desktop/test/links-side.e2e.mjs` (headless Chrome, zh and en): tree in the sidebar and not in the page; picking a category; dragging a row onto a sidebar category files it (and back); no overlapping text in the tree; "‹ Links" then the Links row brings the tree back; ⌘\ folds the sidebar and the tree returns to the page; 880px (sidebar shown, narrow page) and 390px (phone, taps in).
- Screenshots in light and dark; Notes' sidebar looks as before (30px rows, 14px, same labels).

**Not checked.** Notes' fold arrow on a page with sub-pages (my scratch library showed none; it uses the same shared rule as Links, where it works). The real Mac app.

author: lilzj
body:
Fixes **FSOLID-001**. The backend ledger closes it in a separate PR, which opens only after this one merges.

## What the audit asked for

The row: fifteen screens over 800 lines combine rendering, data fetching, domain logic, navigation, permission gating and error handling. The audit's remediation is not a sweep: a file-size budget for `src/app` with the screens over it on a list that only shrinks, and the three largest refactored so that a route holds composition. Its verification: no new file in `src/app` over 600 lines, the list shrinking, and the top three under 400 lines of composition each.

Nineteen screens were over 800 lines by now, not fifteen. The three largest are still the audit's three.

## The three screens, before and after

| Route | Before | Route now | Parts | Hooks | Sections | Longest part |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `(tabs)/discover.tsx` | 2,283 | 214 | 34 | 13 | 19 | `useListingSearches.ts`, 287 |
| `housing/create.tsx` | 1,987 | 209 | 22 | 14 | 8 | `useHousingDraft.ts`, 452 |
| `community-life/events.tsx` | 1,564 | 126 | 22 | 7 | 14 | `useCommunityLifeLists.ts`, 271 |

Each route calls one hook per concern and renders one section per part of the page. The parts live in `src/components/screens/<screen>/`: a hook returns what it holds, typed as `ReturnType` of itself, and a section takes the hooks it reads as props, eight at most. Nothing outside the three screens imports anything differently.

## How the code moved

A script on the TypeScript tree moved every statement and JSX block verbatim, with its comments, and wired what each piece reads to the hook that holds it. It refuses a hook that reads a later hook, a section that captures a `.map` parameter, a module-level `let` assigned outside its own file, and any statement nobody claimed. A line-level comparison confirms the result: every line of each original screen is in its route or its parts, except eleven module-level declarations that gained `export` and one `useNotification()` read, re-declared with only the names each consumer uses. The new glue (imports, signatures, destructuring, section elements, file headers) is wrapped at 100 columns; lines of the original screens are left as they were, however long.

**The hook boundaries follow state ownership.** An effect stays in the hook that declares the state it sets, because `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` and `exhaustive-deps` recognise a setter only in the function that declares it. A first cut by concern alone left three known effects invisible to the first rule and needed three setters added to dependency arrays. Drawn by ownership, **no dependency array changed**, and all eleven `set-state-in-effect` findings in these screens are still reported, each moved with its suppression. That is why Housing and Marketplace share one hook (both fetches set the loading flag pull-to-refresh waits on), and why the origin filter is one hook after the tabs it narrows.

**`globalHousingDraft` decided one file.** It is a module-level `let` assigned in four places, one of them in `handlePublish`, and an imported binding cannot be assigned. Drafting and publishing are two hooks in `useHousingDraft.ts`.

**Effect order.** Grouping by concern moves some effects relative to others. Every pair whose order changed was checked, and each writes disjoint state: the tour (the explore store) against the search effects (the screen's own state and `sentenceLocationKey`); the draft banner's check against the contact, amenity and catalogue loads; `useEffectRefresh` (its own refs) against the sentence effects. The rest are store and context reads with no effect of their own.

## Lint

| | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| errors | 0 | 0 |
| `set-state-in-effect`, suppressed | 11 in the three screens | the same 11, in the hooks that own the state |
| `no-unescaped-entities`, suppressed | 7 | the same 7, in the sections that render them |
| `no-explicit-any`, suppressed | 1 | the same 1 |
| `preserve-manual-memoization`, suppressed | 2 in discover | 0 |
| unused imports | 11 | not carried over |
| warnings, whole app | 1,192 | 1,173 |

Nineteen fewer warnings: the eleven unused imports and two duplicate ones, and nine `require()` warnings that went with the `fs` declarations the repointed tests no longer need, less three that came with the new helper and budget test, which read files the way the other support files do. The two compiler findings were on `clearSentence`, where the compiler inferred two setters as dependencies in the original component. It reports neither for the same callback in its hook. The React Compiler runs only in the linter here, not in the build, so nothing changes at runtime; the two suppressions were pruned and the ceiling lowered from 6 to 4. The dead `cityQuery` state and the unused `lifestyleArr` and `err` are still reported, as they were.

## Tests that read screens

Twenty-two test files read these screens by path, or swept them in a way that would have missed their new parts: `src/app` alone, or `.tsx` files alone. A test asking what a screen does now reads the whole screen through `screenSource()` in `lib/__tests__/support/screen-files.ts`: the route and every part it composes from, so a negative check covers every file of it. A sweep of screen files reads `src/components/screens` too. One exemption list (`photo-source`) names the file the housing wizard's own picker lives in now.

A probe on every file each test read, over the full suite, checked the result: every test that read one of the three screens on master reads its route and its parts now. Five read only the `.tsx` parts, because what they match is JSX alone: avatars, button widths, spotlight keys and the subjects a report modal is opened with.

**A check that compared nothing, found on the way.** `events-no-proximity-claim` sliced the empty-state helper's city branch from a comment, `// Nothing but the city.`, and its own reader strips comments. On master the slice was therefore a single newline, and "never mentions a radius" passed on that. It slices by code now and asserts the marker is found. The helper itself was cut up to the declaration that followed it in the screen; it is cut by its own extent now.

## The budget

`screen-file-length-budget` holds:

- every route under `src/app` to 600 lines, with the 27 still over it listed at their length today; an entry may only come down, and goes once its screen is within the budget;
- every file under `src/components/screens` to 600 lines;
- each composed route to 250 lines, with no `useState`, `useEffect`, `useMemo` or the like of its own; and any route that imports from `src/components/screens` must be named as composed, which is derived rather than listed.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | 0 errors |
| `npm run lint` | 0 errors |
| `npm run lint:cycles` | no circular dependency |
| `npx jest`, the full suite | 433 suites passed and 1 skipped; 7,412 tests passed and 11 skipped |
| `npx expo export --platform android`, then `assert-bundle-shape.js` | exports; the bundle-shape check passes |
| the three screens beside master's copies, same mocks, data and fake clock | identical host trees at all 29 states compared |

The comparison rendered each original (master's file, copied beside a temporary test for the run, not committed) and its composed route under the same providers, fixture data from the app's own mock handlers and a fixed fake clock, drove the same presses, and compared the rendered host tree after each: discover's seven tabs, filter sheet, map and list, a typed search and the place picker; every housing step from a restored draft, and the calendar; every events tab and the reminder dialog. It sees text, accessibility props, input values and the props of host views. It cannot see a prop a composite swallows, such as `className` on `TouchableOpacity`; the line-level comparison covers that. A one-class change on a `Text` failed it at every step.

author: norhiro
body:
## Problem and result

Closes #7030.

Previously, `strata-inkling --layer-split auto` partitioned the 24 physical layers purely in proportion to each GPU's free VRAM (taking peer layers from the tail). On an asymmetric pair (RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB), `auto` put `L13..23` on the slower 3060—including 5 of the 12 looped core layers (`L6..17`, run 3 times per token)—putting 21/48 layer visits and repeated stage handoffs inside the core loop. As a result, two cards with `auto` were slower than one 5060 Ti in both decode and 27K prompt read.

This PR replaces the default `auto` partitioner with a visit-, speed-, and per-stage-KV-aware planner in a host-only header `engine/include/strata/core/ink_layer_split.hpp` (with unit tests in `engine/tests/core/ink_layer_split_test.cpp`) following the plan discussed in #7030:

1. **Loop-visit & handoff aware**: weights each layer by its execution count (`num_passes` for `core_start..core_end-1`, 1 outside) and counts stage transitions along the full 48-visit schedule (with a higher penalty when P2P is unavailable).
2. **Speed-aware (no hardcoded GPU names)**: estimates per-stage relative decode speed from standard CUDA device attributes (`cudaDevAttrMemoryClockRate`, `cudaDevAttrGlobalMemoryBusWidth`, and compute capability).
3. **Per-stage-KV-aware single-card fallback (updated for `v0.2.23` `VramPlan`)**: passes per-visit Stage-0 KV/ShortConv sizes and workspace/vision reserves (`InkLayerSplitKvBudget`) from `ink_cuda_backend.cu` into `load_from_model_file()`. For each candidate partition, Stage 0's KV budget counts only the SWA and global visits owned by Stage 0 (matching `InkCudaRunner::init()`). When all experts and full KV fit on stage 0, `auto` collapses to a single card and logs why; when full KV would otherwise spill to Host KV Offload (e.g. SQ-15 at 32K on 16 GB), it keeps the split and moves only the low-visit tail layers to the peer.
4. **Legacy spread preserved**: `--layer-split spread` (or `vram`) keeps the previous VRAM-proportional spread. Explicit `--layer-split K1,K2,...` is unchanged.

## Related discussion

Issue #7030 (maintainer plan confirmed in https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/7030#issuecomment-7140174208).
Rebased onto `v0.2.23` (`4560d0379`) to adapt to `plan_vram_reserve()` (`struct VramPlan`) and GPU picture reader VRAM reservation, and to extract the host-only planner + unit tests (`ink_layer_split_test`). Note: on `v0.2.23` an unrelated bug (#7352) leaves RTX 5060 Ti fast mode active in `cuda-ls`; see #7352 / its separate fix PR.

## Approach

- `engine/include/strata/core/ink_layer_split.hpp`: host-only, zero-CUDA planner (`ink_plan_layer_split`, `ink_stage_rel_speed`, `InkLayerSplitKvBudget`) that evaluates all valid contiguous partitions across 2..4 stages, minimizing `(host_overflow_bytes, estimated_decode_cost)`.
- `engine/tests/core/ink_layer_split_test.cpp` + `engine/CMakeLists.txt`: 8 host-only unit tests covering asymmetric 2-GPU (both orders, P2P on/off), single-card fit, equal 2-GPU (`6,18` 1-hop vs 3-hop), Stage-0 per-visit KV sizing (`18,6` vs `17,7`), 3-GPU, 4-GPU mixed-speed, and tight-VRAM overflow minimization.
- `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_cuda_backend.cu`: computes `InkLayerSplitKvBudget` from `VramPlan` (`plan.swa_r`, `plan.per_visit_pos`, `plan.dspark_pad`, `plan.c64_host_kv`) plus any GPU vision reader room (`vit_room`) and passes it to `load_from_model_file()`.
- `engine/src/inkling2/cuda/ink_runner.cuh`: calls `strata::core::ink_plan_layer_split()` for `--layer-split auto` and keeps `--layer-split spread` / `vram` for the legacy VRAM-proportional partition.

## Measurements (`v0.2.23`, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB)

Host: i7-7800X, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB, 96 GB RAM, Linux, CUDA 13.3 (`sm_86;120`), `--max-context 32768 --kv fp8 --draft off`, `STRATA_INK_SM120=0` (or with #7352 fix).

| Case (`v0.2.23`) | Split chosen | Host KV offload | Decode (256 tok, tok/s) | 27,859-tok prompt + 64 out (s) | QA (6 short) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Official `v0.2.23` single GPU (5060 Ti) | `3072 VRAM / 0 host` | Yes (`10240 + 22528 host`) | 49.2–49.4 | 29.96 | 6/6 |
| Official `v0.2.23` 2-GPU `auto` (`SM120=0`) | `13,11` (`L13..23` on 3060) | No | 41.4–41.7 | 29.36 | 6/6 |
| **This PR `auto` (SQ-15, 5060 Ti + 3060, P2P on)** | **`23,1`** (`47+1` visits, 1 hop) | **No** | **48.0–48.2 (+16%)** | **20.88 (-29% / -30% vs 1 GPU)** | **6/6** |
| **This PR `auto` (SQ-15, 5060 Ti + 3060, P2P off)** | **`23,1`** (`47+1` visits, 1 hop) | **No** | **48.0–48.2** | **20.99** | **6/6** |
| **This PR `auto` (SQ-15, reversed `0,1`: 3060 first)** | **`1,23`** (`1+47` visits, 1 hop) | **No** | 42.1–42.2 | **21.76** | **6/6** |
| **This PR `spread` (SQ-15, 5060 Ti + 3060)** | `13,11` (legacy spread) | No | 41.7–41.9 | 29.48 | 6/6 |
| **This PR `auto` (SQ-10, 5060 Ti + 3060)** | **Single card (`24,0`)** | **No** | **54.4–54.5** | **17.32** | **6/6** |

## Validation

**Passed:**
- **Revision & environment**: rebased cleanly onto `v0.2.23` (`4560d0379`); Linux x86_64, GCC 15.3.1, CUDA 13.3.73 (`-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;120"`), RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB + RTX 3060 12 GB, 96 GB RAM.
- **Host-only unit test (`ink_layer_split_test`)**:
  ```bash
  g++-15 -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Iengine/include engine/tests/core/ink_layer_split_test.cpp -o /tmp/ink_layer_split_test && /tmp/ink_layer_split_test
  ```
  All 8 cases passed with 0 warnings (`case 1: 23,1`, `case 2 rev: 2,22`, `case 3 single: 24,0`, `case 4 equal 2x12GB: 6,18 1 hop`, `case 5 per-stage KV: 18,6 1 hop`, `case 6 3x8GB: 8,10,6`, `case 7 4-GPU fast stage1: 6,12,6,0`, `case 8 tight overflow: 18,6`).
- **Settings register check**: `python3 tools/settings_register.py --check` passed (exit 0).
- **Engine build**:
  ```bash
  cmake -S engine -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DSTRATA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DSTRATA_BUILD_HY4=OFF -DSTRATA_BUILD_SPLIT=OFF -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES="86;120"
  cmake --build build --target strata-inkling -j 6
  ```
  Clean Release build of `strata-inkling` (0 errors).
- **Hardware runs on `v0.2.23`** (both with `STRATA_INK_SM120=0` on this PR alone, and without env overrides when combined with #7352's fix):
  - SQ-15 normal order P2P on (`23,1`): 48.0–48.2 tok/s, 27,859-tok prompt 20.88 s, 6/6 QA, 0 host experts, 0 Host KV offload.
  - SQ-15 normal order P2P off (`STRATA_CUDA_PEER_PINNED=1`, `23,1`): 48.0–48.2 tok/s, 27,859-tok prompt 20.99 s, 6/6 QA.
  - SQ-15 reversed order (`1,23`): 42.1–42.2 tok/s, 27,859-tok prompt 21.76 s, 6/6 QA.
  - SQ-15 `--layer-split spread` (`13,11`): 41.7–41.9 tok/s, 27,859-tok prompt 29.48 s, 6/6 QA.
  - SQ-10 normal order: automatic fallback to single card (`24,0`), 54.4–54.5 tok/s, 27,859-tok prompt 17.32 s, 6/6 QA.

**Failed:**
- None observed.

**Not run:**
- Equal-card 2-GPU pair and 3–4 GPU rigs on real hardware (covered by unit tests in `ink_layer_split_test.cpp`; no such hardware available locally).
- Windows / WDDM, ROCm HIP, Metal, SYCL builds.

## Limits

- Relative stage throughput is estimated from memory bandwidth and compute capability; unusual link bottlenecks (e.g. x1 PCIe risers) are modeled via the P2P/non-P2P hop penalty rather than live transfer benchmarking.
- "FEWER CARDS" warning line (mentioned in #7030) is left for a follow-up change; this PR already logs when `auto` collapses to a single card.

author: lrobles917
body:
Fixes #4727 (part A of two; draft until part B is in).

## What changed

**Part A (this commit): the ground reference belongs to the worldspace.** The cloud shadows' plane, and the volumetric clouds' domain on it, stood `PLANE_ABOVE_GROUND` (20,000) over the camera's height at the worldspace's first output, so a game loaded on a peak put the clouds over that peak and one in a valley over the valley.

- `cloud_shadows.rs`: the ground reference is now the median of the worldspace's LAND vertex heights (each cell's own 32 x 32, rounded to `GROUND_SNAP` as before), `land_relief`. It is read once a run per worldspace on a lowest-priority thread of its own (`GroundScan`, as lodgen's bakes) while the cloud textures load; nothing is composed before it is known, and the result is kept for the run (going back to a worldspace or switching on again reads nothing). Worldspaces without LAND heights, and runs without world data, keep the camera's height. One log line: `cloud shadows: ground reference ... from the worldspace's land: median ..., range ..., 99th percentile ... (read in ... ms)`.
- [design / engineering choice] The median rather than the issue's "highest land plus a margin": the volume's bend (`shell_radius`) brings the base down to the horizon for a view from the reference, and from far under it no cloud would reach the horizon. The clearance over peaks is left to part B.
- The air's ground reference (`volumetric_clouds_air.rs`, `plane_height - above_ground`) follows on its own.
- Docs: `graphics-enhanced.md` §3.23 "The domain" and the light volume's "Where each level serves"; module notes.
- Smoke `volumetric-clouds`: one ground-reference line from the land is expected, the camera fallback is forbidden.

[observed, 2026-11-27, vanilla data, smoke `volumetric-clouds` at Goodsprings] WastelandNV: 16,386 cells read in 1.4 s; heights -3,104 to 20,672, median 5,720 (reference 6,144), 99th percentile 13,872; plane 26,144, about 5,500 units over the highest land. At 1.4 s once a run, no disk cache.

**Part B (not yet): the deck's height and the sizes with it.** The proposal: one scale factor `k` applied where world space meets the clouds' own (the march's entry, the light volume's camera and reader, the weather layers' published plane and repeat, the water reflection), so every tuned size and measured table stays as it is and the view from the ground stays today's, while a camera `h` up sits at `h/k` and peaks never reach the base. Held until @spooknik has had a say (#4688 and #4738 touch the same files).

## How it was checked

- `cd engine && cargo test --release --locked`: all ok (0 failed); 3 new tests in `cloud_shadows` (the median and the snap whatever the camera, each cell's own vertices, the per-worldspace memory and the camera fallback).
- `cd engine && cargo clippy --release --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tools/smoke/tests`: 209 OK (5 skipped); `python tools/smoke verify`: fine.
- `python tools/smoke run --changed upstream/main` on vanilla data (release-quick build): volumetric-clouds, volumetric-clouds-no-aids, volumetric-clouds-shadows, volumetric-clouds-shadows-switch, cloud-shadows: 5 passed. (The runner warned that the Windows session was locked, so frame times were not measured.)

## Clean-room checklist
See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/LootJunkieAzza/NVForever/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#clean-room-rules).
- [x] No game data, goldens or game-derived dumps are included.
- [x] Format and behaviour facts are written in `docs/spec-notes/` and tagged
      `[documented]` (with a source), `[observed]` or `[hypothesis]`.

author: mathbook3948
body:
## Why

Issue #73 reports that the batched-read window of a typed hop walks every relationship type in its segments and blob-loads their values before filtering. That was true at the review commit b0b4e33, where the window walked with `visit_range`. Commit 4a76ad8 fixed it, and on main the premise no longer holds. The window walks with `visit_range_peek`, which returns a value stored apart as its length only. `visit_adjacency_prefix` drops entries of other types (`Window::holds`) before any value is read. So the only extra work is passing their keys, and those keys share leaves with the asked type.

I built and measured two fixes. Neither beat the current read path beyond noise, and both regressed at some setting. This PR keeps the read path and pins the real invariant in a test.

## What changed

- New test `a_typed_scan_beside_a_heavy_type_reads_no_value_of_the_other_type` (in `graph/adjacency_model.test.rs`). It uses a counting storage wrapper and checkpoints first, so the other type's parts really are stored apart. It asserts three things. A windowed typed hop reads no value of the other type. It walks storage at least 8 times less often than reading each node alone. Its results equal those per-node reads.
- `docs/architecture/column-scans.md`: replaces "reads no more than before" with what the window actually reads. A typed window reads its segments as one key range and passes entries of other types by key, loading none of the values they keep apart.
- No code change to the read path.

## Public API

Unchanged.

## Verification

Release micro-benchmark through the public API. 20k persons, 100 cities, one LIVES_IN per person. The database is compacted and reopened, the cache is warm, and each number is the median of 15 runs. "Pages" are cache hits plus misses for one run.

| Scenario | Baseline | Per-segment typed ranges | Seek after a run of 0 | Seek after a run of 4 or 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LIVES_IN count, no other type | 0.84 ms | 0.96 to 1.02 ms | 0.81 to 0.87 ms | 0.81 to 0.83 ms |
| LIVES_IN count beside 100 FOLLOWS per person | 1.09 to 1.11 ms, 1356 pages | 1.20 to 1.35 ms, 1260 pages | 1.12 to 1.19 ms, 1261 pages | 1.12 to 1.21 ms, 1354 pages |
| FOLLOWS count (heavy typed hop) | 29.1 to 29.5 ms, 1359 pages | 29.0 to 29.4 ms, 2514 pages | 29.5 ms, 2508 pages | 29.4 to 29.6 ms, 1359 pages |
| LIVES_IN count beside 4 other types of 25 each | 0.93 to 0.96 ms, 415 pages | not run | 1.05 ms, 710 pages | 0.93 to 0.96 ms, 415 to 418 pages |

On page reads, a typed window already matches an untyped read of the same segments (1359 vs 1359, 417 vs 415).

Mutation evidence. Each mutation fails the new test:

- Walk the window with `visit_range` (which reads every value) instead of the peek: fails with "type 0 Outgoing read values of type 2".
- Load values stored apart before the type filter: fails with the same message.
- Never open a window (`scanning = false`): fails with "64 walks, 64 alone".

- [x] `mise run check` passes. It ran locally and again in the pre-push hook.
- [x] A user-visible change adds a line under `Unreleased` in `CHANGELOG.md`. Not applicable, since nothing user-visible changed.
- [x] The documents in `docs/` still match, or this pull request updates them. `column-scans.md` is updated.

Fixes #73

author: kapp667
body:
## Why

The translation has two atoms for undefined: `Undefined` for objects and scalars, and `Undefined_Set` for collections. The set operations test for `Undefined_Set`. Several paths used the wrong atom, or did not mark an undefined collection as a set.

- **`null` used as a collection** always became `Undefined`. `ada.luckyNumbers = null` gave false where USE gives true. `let s : Set(Integer) = null in s` gave `Set{null}` where USE gives undefined, and `ada.sizeOf(null)` gave 1.
- **`selectByKind` and `selectByType`** on an undefined set gave `Set{}`. USE's `ExpSelectByKind` gives undefined.
- **`oclUndefined(Set(T))`** was not marked as a set, so `->size()`, `->includes(1)` and the other set operations were refused.
- **A derived many-valued end** whose value is null, or holds null, gave `Set{null}`. USE's `MSystemState.evaluateDeriveExpression` returns no links for an undefined value and skips undefined elements.

## Decision and reasons

- **Coerce null where USE types it.** `DefaultExpressionVisitor.processAs(exp, type)` gives `Undefined_Set`, marked as a set, when an OclVoid expression stands where a collection is expected. It is called at each place where USE gives null a collection type:
  - each operand of `=` and `<>`, which takes the other operand's type;
  - the declared type of a `let` variable;
  - the type of an `if`;
  - an operation's parameter and result types;
  - a derived attribute's type;
  - a derived end's type.
- **A narrower rule was rejected**, because a fix inside the set operations would leave each caller to pick the right atom.
- **No new refusal was needed.** Every place where null is coerced has a USE type. USE rejects null as the argument of the other collection operations at type-check time.
- **Fix `selectByKind` first.** Otherwise marking `oclUndefined(Set(T))` as a set would have turned a refusal into a wrong `Set{}`.

## What changed

- `DefaultExpressionVisitor`: `processAs`, used by `visitIf`, `visitLet` and `visitUndefined` through one helper. The exemption in `branch()` is gone.
- `StandardOperationVisitor`: each operand of `=` and `<>` takes the other's type.
- `OperationExpressionVisitor` and `VariableOperationVisitor`: parameters, results, derived attributes and derived ends.
- `SetOperationGroup`: `selectByKind` and `selectByType` share a helper that keeps `Undefined_Set`.
- `testModel.use` gets the operations `sizeOf(numbers)` and `noNumbers()`, a derived Set attribute on `UndefinedFactory`, and two derived many-valued ends.
- The tests go into the existing set-operation, `Let`, `OperationCall`, `AttributeAccess`, `DerivedEndNavigation` and `OclIsUndefined` classes.

## Verification

- Each failing test came first, in its own commit. On the base code, 13 null tests failed, 2 selection tests and 15 `oclUndefined` operation tests failed, and 3 derived-end tests failed.
- A probe of 226 expressions compared USE and Kodkod. Before this branch, 109 agreed, 58 were wrong and 59 were refused. After it, 207 agree, 6 are wrong and 13 are refused. No expression got worse. The remaining wrong cases are the `flatten` case below and the derived-end cases fixed here.
- The USE values were checked against the 7.5.0 bytecode. `includes` and `excludes` on an undefined source give false, `count` gives 0, and the other operations give undefined.
- The full suite gives `OK (3471 tests)`.
- The oracle matches on both corpora (USE examples and USE tests). CI runs it again on the head.

## Found, not fixed here

- `Set{Set{1}, null}->flatten()` gives `Set{null,1}` where USE gives `Set{1}`. A collection literal that holds `Undefined_Set` becomes `Undefined_Set` as a whole, while USE's `flatten` skips undefined elements. This is pre-existing.
- `oclUndefined(Person) = oclUndefined(Set(Person))` would compare the two atoms and give false. This matters only if USE type-checks the comparison, which is not verified.

author: aldemirkonuk
body:
r108 inventory gap g14. This is stacked on #2222 (DD-r108-36, the "Nutrition not recorded N" chip), which inventory-fix owns. That branch is not edited here.

When the chip is on, owners and managers get **Fill what's in it (N)**. It opens one sheet that walks those goods one at a time. The seeded data has 1,103 of 1,122 goods with nothing recorded, and each of them took about 5 actions through the drawer.

- **First screen.** It says once that each good's name is sent to Open Food Facts and USDA FoodData Central, as the single lookup does. It also says a lookup only fills a draft and never says a good is free of an allergen.
- **Lookup.** A step runs the existing `POST …/item/:id/nutrition/lookup` by the good's name when the step opens, never ahead. The lookup has its own query key (`staleTime: Infinity`), so going back or refreshing the card does not send the name again.
- **Form.** `NutritionForm` gains an optional `seed`. A draft fills the form as the lookup button would and is still unsaved. Choices or none open the form's own lookup panel with what the lookup said. The source is named ("From Open Food Facts."). `onSaved` is new, and `cancelLabel={null}` hides the form's Cancel because the lane has its own Skip.
- **Saving and moving.** Save (the existing PUT) is the only write. Skip saves nothing. J/K and Next/Previous move through the lane, and keys typed in a field are ignored. "N of M filled" sits in the sheet footer, is announced politely, and updates after each save. A save moves on to the next good.
- **Failures.** A failed lookup says "could not be reached" and leaves the form empty to type, never 0. A failed nutrition read says so and offers Read again.
- **Staff.** The button is never drawn for them, and the lane renders nothing for them whoever mounts it.
- **Motion.** A step enters +12 px on Y over 160 ms. Under reduced motion there is no animation and no fade (CSS `no-preference` only). The lane uses the house Sheet with no exit animation, and it is lazy-loaded (`LazyPanels`).

**Decisions (the session's call)**
- The lane's goods are fixed when it opens, so a save does not reshuffle the walk. Coverage is re-read when the lane closes.
- The lookup goes through `useQuery` rather than a mutation, so a step is looked up exactly once while the lane is open.
- A save advances to the next good, as in Linear's triage.

**Tests**: `NutritionLane.test.tsx` (7 cases: no lookup before a step opens and only the open step is looked up; Save sends the draft only on press; Skip saves nothing; J/K and back do not resend; keys in a field do not move the lane; a failed lookup says could not be reached and leaves an empty form; staff draw and read nothing; no allergen is stated free) and `InventoryNext.test.tsx` (the entry is shown for managers and not for staff). Four suites ran 152/152, and tsc is clean. Mutants killed: auto-saving the draft (5 failed), dropping the staff gate, looking up every good ahead, resending on back, no unreached words, keys moving the lane while typing.

**Not verified**: no browser walk (no local stack). The live OFF/FDC answers were not exercised.
