author: paatai
body: Adds a **fast lossless JPEG mode** (`komla compress --fast`, and the web app's default JPEG mode, with "Maximum compression" one click away). Every output restores byte for byte (SHA-256 checked). The final evaluation was run on a **random held-out set** of 66 JPEGs (227.6 MB). The set was drawn for this evaluation with seed 20261127 from a recorded pool of 9,999 Wikimedia Commons files and shares no file with the development or test sets. Komla's code was frozen at 8430279 before its first run, and it was run once. On that set, Komla fast is **the fastest to compress and decompress and uses the least memory of every tool, with one thread and with eight.** Its size beats JPEG XL, brunsli and both Lepton modes except the Rust port's single-threaded mode. It **loses on size to paq8px (−0.78 points), packJPG (−0.32) and Lepton's Rust port single-threaded (−0.24).** ## Random held-out set (66 files, 227.6 MB) Each tool ran one process at a time, with all tools on one file before the next. Times are whole-process wall clock, the fastest of 3 runs (the totals of the three runs differ by 0.1–5.3%). Memory is peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time`. The machine is an 8-core x86-64 VM with AVX2, with files on tmpfs. | Tool | Threads | Smaller | Compress | Decompress | Memory compress | Memory decompress | Failed | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Komla fast** | 1 | **19.88%** | **11.66 MB/s** | **14.78 MB/s** | **42 MiB** | **6 MiB** | 0 | | JPEG XL (effort 7) | 1 | 17.99% | 7.35 MB/s | 13.57 MB/s | 964 MiB | 274 MiB | 0 | | Lepton (Dropbox) | 1 | 14.82% | 3.40 MB/s | 7.74 MB/s | 224 MiB | 19 MiB | 14 | | Lepton (Rust port) | 1 | 20.12% | 9.52 MB/s | 8.68 MB/s | 265 MiB | 505 MiB | 0 | | brunsli | 1 | 19.67% | 8.60 MB/s | 10.46 MB/s | 788 MiB | 266 MiB | 0 | | packJPG | 1 | 20.20% | 3.28 MB/s | 3.18 MB/s | 271 MiB | 268 MiB | 0 | | paq8px (`-8`) | 1 | 20.66% | 0.009 MB/s | 0.009 MB/s | 2791 MiB | 2791 MiB | 0 | | **Komla fast** | 8 | **19.88%** | **34.01 MB/s** | **41.40 MB/s** | **80 MiB** | **77 MiB** | 0 | | JPEG XL | 8 | 17.99% | 12.31 MB/s | 23.39 MB/s | 957 MiB | 286 MiB | 0 | | Lepton (Dropbox) | 8 | 19.78% | 7.50 MB/s | 20.89 MB/s | 290 MiB | 291 MiB | 0 | | Lepton (Rust port) | 8 | 19.80% | 21.37 MB/s | 24.80 MB/s | 277 MiB | 505 MiB | 0 | - brunsli, packJPG and paq8px have no threads. - paq8px ran separately, several files at a time, so its times are indicative. - Lepton `-singlethread` refuses 14 files (its own round-trip check fails), which count at their original size. - No tool crashed or restored a file wrongly, and Komla never fell back to storing a file. ## Wins, ties and losses, all three sets Ties are speed or memory within 5%. Size is exact. | Set | One thread | Eight threads | Not won | |---|---|---|---| | Random held-out, 66 files | 27 wins, 3 losses | 28 wins, 2 losses | size vs paq8px, packJPG, Lepton Rust (1T) | | Test, 80 files | 26 wins, 1 tie, 1 loss | 27 wins, 1 loss | size vs paq8px (19.97% vs 19.68%); 1T decompression ties JPEG XL (−2.8%) | | Development, 80 files (tuning) | 28 wins, 1 tie, 1 loss | 29 wins, 1 loss | size vs paq8px (20.75% vs 20.66%); 1T decompression ties JPEG XL (+0.6%) | All tables, per-group sizes, failures, run-to-run spread and settings are in `bench/results/JPEG_SPEED_REPORT.md`. ## Changes in this round - **Streaming compression with bounded memory.** Each scan has an incremental Huffman decoder, so one stripe's coefficients at a time are decoded from all scans. One thread regenerates and checks the scans in order while the other threads code the stripes. Peak memory on the largest development files drops from 88–126 to 23–29 MiB with one thread, and from 166–216 to 45–51 MiB with eight. Eight threads also compress about 1.8× faster. - **Streaming decompression from file to file.** The `.komla` file is read piece by piece. Scans are written straight to their place in the output, and part CRCs are combined. With one thread, every MCU row goes back into scan data from a ring of two MCU rows, so peak memory is about 6 MiB. Stored trailers and stored files are copied in pieces. - **Parallel scan regeneration.** The side info stores each sequential scan's encoder state at stripe boundaries (offset, bits of the shared byte, DC predictions). Decoding threads regenerate their own stripes' scan data, which makes 8-thread restores of large baseline files about 1.4× faster. - **rANS in chunks** that end between blocks. The chunk header stores the block count, and renormalization is branchless. - **Better fast model.** Cross-validated dev saving goes from 19.69% to 20.57% at the same speed: - a running magnitude estimate from the neighbouring blocks plus coded coefficients of the block; - magnitude contexts by anti-diagonal zone and remaining density; - edge magnitude and sign contexts by the predicted value's class; - a wider edge neighbourhood. - Priors are 272 KB. - **Benchmark tooling:** - `bench/select_heldout.py` records the pool and makes a seeded draw. - `bench/run_paq8px.py` runs paq8px in parallel. - `run_jpeg_speed.py` keeps every run and Komla's container mode. - `make_jpeg_speed_report.py` reports all three sets with per-axis verdicts. - **README, report and site table** now lead with the held-out set. ## Verification - All 80 development files and the test fixtures round-trip byte for byte with 1 and 8 threads, after every change. - Every file of all three sets restored exactly in the final run, with 1 and 8 threads. - `cargo test --release` passes. - CI's native-vs-WebAssembly identity check passes. - The browser end-to-end test passes in fast and maximum mode. - Maximum-mode `.komla` output and PNG/BMP output are byte-identical to before. ## Caveats - **Tuning risk.** On the development set (used for tuning), Komla fast leads every tool but paq8px on size. On the held-out set it trails paq8px, packJPG and Lepton Rust (1T), on camera originals, edited photos and scans. - **Robustness.** Komla fast is new, while the other tools are mature. Its safety net is full re-encode verification at compression time, with a stored fallback, which was never needed here. - **Settings and data.** - JPEG XL runs at its default effort 7. - paq8px ran separately with indicative times. Its test-set figures come from an earlier run. - Komla's maximum mode was not re-timed. - The earlier test-set results were known during this round. No test or held-out file was run with Komla before the final evaluation.

author: thespacedoctor
body:
Closes DY-2348.

## What this changes

SOXS merged spectra (stare, nod and offset) now sit on one fixed log-λ grid per arm, with a flux-conserving merge. X-Shooter keeps `np.interp`, and its output does not change.

- **Grid** (`commonutils/log_wavelength_grid.py`, new and pure): λₖ = 1000 nm · exp(k·Δv/c). The grid points are bin centres, and the bin edges sit at k ± ½.
  - Δv is the yaml key `log-wavelength-step-kms`, measured by DY-2378: 17.83 km/s for VIS and 13.16 km/s for NIR.
  - Δv is multiplied by the spectral binning: `ESO DET BINY` for VIS, and 1 for NIR, which has no binning card. A VIS frame with no card is an error.
- **Resampler:** the weights are pixel/bin overlaps normalised to sum to 1, the flux is their weighted mean, and the variance is Σw²σ². Unit tests show that the integrated flux is kept and that the variance propagates.
- **Merge** (`commonutils/log_grid_merge.py`, new and pure):
  - Each join is a hard cut snapped to a bin edge.
  - End bins that an order covers only partly are dropped.
  - A bin with no input pixels holds flux 0, variance 0 and SNR NaN. It is never interpolated, so the NIR order 10/11 gap is no longer bridged by a fake line (DY-1943).
  - The no-data mask is kept on the extractor as `noDataBins`, for QUAL bit 1 (DY-2352).
- **Rounding:** the 2-decimal `WAVE` rounding is removed for SOXS, in both the merge and the stack writer. X-Shooter keeps it.
- **NOTFLAT spectrum:** `FLUX_DENSITY_COUNTS` uses the same normalised weights. `RESPONSE_BASIS` is unchanged.

## Real-data A/B (develop 26c7f623 vs branch, single SOFs)

| Case | Join zigzag, develop → branch | Continuum ratio (mean / integral) |
|---|---|---|
| VIS stare | 17.1 → 1.6 | 1.0018 / 1.0003 |
| VIS stare std | 9.5 → 1.4 | 1.0019 / 1.0002 |
| VIS nod | 26.4 → 1.6 | 1.0021 / 1.0003 |
| VIS offset | 2.5 → 1.9 | 1.0020 / 0.9999 |
| NIR stare | 1.95 → 1.57 | 1.0043 / 1.0006 |
| NIR stare std | 2.0 → 1.2 | 1.0002 / 0.9999 |
| NIR nod std | 2.8 → 1.0 | 1.0004 / 0.9999 |
| NIR offset | 1.7 → 1.4 | 1.0001 / 1.0003 |

- Zigzag is the median |second difference| divided by the local scatter, within ±10 bins of the joins.
- No QC FAILED on either side. Peak RSS was 3.8 GB or less, with 2 reductions at a time.
- `EXTRACTED_ORDERS` products are identical. `RESP` moves by ±0.03% (VIS) and ±0.34% (NIR, p16–p84).
- Row counts change from 25091 to 15009 (VIS) and from 20595 to 21362 (NIR).
- Figures: `/Volumes/SOXS/scratch-agents/dy-2348/figs/`. Full report: P32.11 `output/dy-2348/report.md`.

**The step at the joins is larger.** The hard cut shows the real flux mismatch between orders, which develop's interleaving blurred. On the VIS standard, the red order is 3.8%, 5.9% and 17% low in the overlaps. The median step divided by the local scatter goes from 2 to 12 for VIS and from 1.2 to 4.6 for NIR. The cause is in the flat and blaze calibration (DY-2444), not in the merge.

## Follow-ups and open points

- The nod and offset stacks still group at 4 decimals. DY-2349 replaces this with grouping by bin index, and it must also leave the no-data bins out of the stack median, which now counts their zeros as data.
- `ERR` is 0 in the no-data bins. A ruling is needed in DY-2352 or DY-2393 before anything downstream weights by 1/σ².
- The 3-decimal rounding of the count columns (DY-2393 story 47) is not in this ticket.
- The real-data gate baselines are re-recorded in DY-2376.

## Tests and review

- New tests: 29 for the grid and resampler, 15 or more for the merge, 33 or more at the horne level (including a real FITS write with no writer mocked), stack pins, and a test that a constant flux density stays flat across a join between orders with different pixel widths (DY-2339).
- The full offline suite at 0b3082af gave 7808 passed and 1 failed. The failure is the known local-only fmultiprocess leak pin, which passes in CI. Diff coverage is 99%.
- The code-review skill checked standards and spec. The 10 review items are in 0b3082af: the refactor is bit-identical on 13 saved merge inputs, the no-data mask is kept, and the X-Shooter WAVE rounding is restored. A re-review approved it with two notes, applied as written in 562ca586: a case-blind instrument check, and the mask reset on each merge. The affected test files pass (263 tests).

author: halonic-dev
body:
## What and why

Binds a Paperclip stepper request's `host` to a Paperclip the user connected. Paperclip requests (`paperclip.connect-and-test@1`, and `paperclip.set-secret@1` / `paperclip.bind-secret@1` from #6728) open pages and guide the user on the host the request names. Until now, the request's own `host` decided that. Now:

- `reviewActionItem` takes `paperclips`, the user's connected Paperclips by host, each with whether this computer holds its key (`online`/`offline` rows). A Paperclip request runs only on a host whose connection holds its key. Otherwise it's refused with one reason: "`<host>` isn't a Paperclip you connected in Settings › Connections", or, for a connection with no key here (`no-key`, `signed-out`), "`<host>` isn't signed in on this computer: sign in to it in Settings › Connections". The card then shows the reason, no steps and only **Decline**. With none given, as in a browser, every Paperclip request with a host is refused.
- A definition with `sign-in` steps (`paperclip.connect-and-test@1`) also runs on a connection with no key: its first sign-in needs only the connection file, and Studio's sign-in already binds it to that file.
- `StepperRun` reads the connections again (as this window last read them) at every check. Disconnect forgets the key and the row turns `no-key`, so the next step doesn't run.
- The Inbox reads them from `AgentConnectionsService` (`useConnectedPaperclips`, new in the action-steppers API) and passes them to the review and the run.
- `core/action-catalog`: the `paperclipHost` comment and two test names now say only what the definitions themselves check. The catalog's generated source hashes change with that comment.

Follows #6728, now merged. While rebasing, the sign-in helpers `hasSignIn` and `signInRunOf` moved from `stepper-run.ts` to `sign-in-run.ts`, keeping `stepper-run.ts` under 480 lines.

## Requirements

- action-steppers.paperclip-host (new, active)

## How tested

- `src/run/paperclip-host.test.ts` (action-steppers), with the shipped `paperclip.set-secret@1`:
  - a request on `paperclip.acme.example`, with that Paperclip connected, reaches the ready stage;
  - a request on another host is refused with its reason;
  - with no connections, the request is refused;
  - a request on a connection with no key on this computer is refused with its reason;
  - a ready request stops (`not-available`, nothing recorded) once its row turns `no-key`, as after Disconnect;
  - `paperclip.connect-and-test@1` on a connection with no key yet reaches the ready stage;
  - every shipped Paperclip definition opens pages and names guide addresses only under `https://{host}/`.
- `src/ui/use-connected-paperclips.test.tsx`: the hook reads the connections with their key state, reads them again on a change, and has none without connections.
- The existing Paperclip sign-in tests now pass the connected `acme` host.

Local check: ran typecheck, lint and test on `@halonicjs/studio-feature-action-steppers`, `@halonicjs/studio-feature-inbox` and `@halonicjs/action-catalog`. `pnpm check` passed on `5a159e8`.

## UX

- [x] Feels human, intuitive and approachable ([product principles](https://github.com/halonic-com/halonic/blob/main/docs/guides/product-principles.md)), or nothing a user sees or reads changes.

## Docs

None needed: the requirement documents the behaviour. No guide describes the Paperclip steppers yet.

## Changeset

A Paperclip request in the Inbox now runs only on a Paperclip you connected in Settings › Connections and signed in to on this computer; otherwise the card says why and offers only Decline.

Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5

- [ ] Every commit is signed off by me (`git commit -s`) under the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/), and I have run and understood this change.

author: shreyas-londhe
body:
whir depends on `provekit-spongefish` 0.2.0, a republish of upstream spongefish at `fcc277f` built against arkworks 0.6 (#280). Upstream 0.9.0 redesigns the API around draft-irtf-cfrg-fiat-shamir and drops its arkworks codecs. This PR moves whir to 0.9.0. Proof bytes change.

## Changes

- whir owns its codecs. Upstream ships none for arkworks, and the orphan rule stops whir from implementing spongefish's codec traits for ark fields, so `transcript/codecs` defines byte-only `Encoding`, `FromNarg` and `FromUniform`. The ark field impls live in `transcript/codecs/ark.rs` and keep the fork's byte maps: ⌈log p / 8⌉ little-endian bytes per limb in the NARG, and ⌈log p / 8⌉ + 32 uniform bytes per limb reduced mod p for challenges.
- The sponge unit is fixed to `u8`. Every sponge whir runs with absorbs bytes, ProveKit's Skyscraper included.
- The session identifier is `derive_session_id::<H>(protocol_id ‖ session_id)`. The instance is absorbed with a `u32` length prefix, so `Empty` still works under 0.9.0's non-empty instance rule.
- The default sponge is TurboShake128 instead of Shake128.
- Hints are read through their own `NargReader`, so one failed hint read rejects every later one. The IRS opening sends its submatrix as one hint per element, without the ark `Vec` length prefix, since the verifier knows the count.
- The verifier rejects field limbs ≥ p in prover messages and hints. The fork reduced them mod p, which made proofs malleable.
- The prover's private RNG is `PrivateRng<TurboShake128>` seeded from OS entropy. `ProverRng` adapts it to `rand` 0.8 for arkworks.
- MSRV is 1.88, spongefish's minimum. At 1.88 clippy flags constant-size `chunks_exact`, so the 19 sites use `as_chunks`.

## Breaking API changes

- In `transcript`: `Decoding` → `FromUniform`, `NargDeserialize` → `FromNarg`, `StdHash` → `DefaultHash`. `NargSerialize` is gone because `Encoding` is the NARG serialization. The codec traits take no type parameter, and `VerificationResult` is a whir alias.
- Sponges are `H: DuplexSpongeInterface<U = u8>`. In `ProverState<H, R>`, `R` is the sponge behind the private RNG (`DuplexSpongeInit<U = u8>`), not a `rand` RNG.
- `ProverState::new(&ds)` and `VerifierState::new(&ds, &proof)` no longer take a sponge. `rng()` returns `ProverRng` by value, so callers pass `&mut ps.rng()`.
- `prover_hint_ark` is replaced by `prover_hints` and `prover_hints_vec`.
- `ProtocolConfig::{prove, verify}` and `irs_commit::Config::{open, verify}` require `M::Source: ProverMessage`.

ProveKit pins `provekit-whir` 0.2.0 from crates.io, so it is unaffected until it upgrades.

## Review notes

- Read commit by commit. The first two prepare on the old dependency (byte alphabet, per-element hints), then the MSRV bump, the port, and the canonical check. Each passed clippy and tests when it was made.
- 855 insertions and 601 deletions excluding `Cargo.lock`, which drops the fork's Plonky3 dependencies.
- `as_chunks` drops the remainder like `chunks_exact`. In post-LTO aarch64 assembly of `ntt_dispatch` for all six fields, the field arithmetic (`mul`, `umulh`, `adcs`, `sbcs`), the SIMD instruction count and the bounds checks (none) are identical. Loop setup differs by at most 11 instructions per function. Over six interleaved runs of `expand_from_coeff` on an Apple Silicon laptop, sizes up to 2^20 overlap within 1%. At 2^22 the medians differ by 2% against a run-to-run spread of 7 to 15%. `joint_opening_bench` at 2^18 stays inside its run-to-run spread. x86 was not checked.
- `MockSponge` tests use a test-only `from_sponge`, which needs spongefish's `yolocrypto` feature as a dev-dependency. `rand` 0.8 with `std` is also a dev-dependency, because the fork used to switch it on for `thread_rng`.
- New tests cover field codec round-trips and non-canonical rejection for all six field types, a transcript round-trip with an `Empty` instance, challenges changing with protocol, session and instance, and rejection of trailing NARG or hint bytes.
- Local checks used stable and nightly; no 1.88 toolchain was run.

author: seanudeke
body:
Part of #382. Slice 2d.19f, split from 2d.19 (core): item (b) of what F-423 left there, for OBAAF-GHA-026. Run `chough`. Decision **D-146** (Proposed).

## The problem (on `flagship` `3bf8e04`)

OBAAF-GHA-026 reads a step that runs an agent CLI with an option the tool's own documentation warns about. Since D-143 it works out `${{ env.X }}` in a workflow's own step where the checker knows the one text GitHub puts in. A step of a local composite action (read by the second pass, 2d.4b2) was always read as written. So in an action, `claude ${{ env.FLAGS }} -p hi` with `FLAGS: --dangerously-skip-permissions` in the job's `env` was the medium "cannot tell" (`command-computed`), where GitHub runs the warned option. A harmless value was "cannot tell" too.

## What was built

For a step of a local action that a job's own step uses:
- **The action's inputs, as the caller works them out.** `_caller_inputs` works out the caller's `with:` in its own context: plain text, or expressions that read only `env`, with the workflow's, the job's and the using step's own `env`, under D-143's conditions. Only the inputs the action's command lines read are worked out (`_command_inputs_read`). Each value is worked out once for the check, for the same caller's mappings, and counts towards `GIVEN_TEXTS_JOB` and `GIVEN_TEXTS_CHECK`. Anything else is put in as a reference to the input, which D-143 does not work out: another context, a `default` with an expression, a `with:` written as one value, or a value past the bound.
- **The line, built piece by piece** from the action's file (`_given_text`, kept on `Step.given_texts`). A line is not worked out unless the expressions the runner's reading finds in it are exactly the ones the action writes, because GitHub never reads a value put in as an expression. Lines are bounded before they are made.
- **The action's own expressions** are worked out by D-143 with the action step's `env`: the workflow's, the job's, the using step's and its own, nearest winning, under the runner's comparison of names.
- **An `env` key holding `${{`** in any scope is "cannot tell" (`rules.expression_keys`), because the runner may work the key out. This also applies to a workflow's own step, which D-143 read as known.
- **Still read as written:** a further local action's step; an action step's or using step's `env` written as one expression; a step after one that may write the `env` context.
- **The premise, in CI.** A new advisory job, `composite-env-premise`, runs the actions in `tests/premise/` on ubuntu-24.04, macos-latest and windows-latest. It asserts:
  - the order of the `env` scopes;
  - that a later step does not see an earlier step's `env`;
  - that the caller's `with:` is worked out with the caller's `env`, its own included;
  - that a value put in is not read again.

## Review

One Opus 5.5 sub-agent that did not write it. The record is in `docs/bypass-attempts.md` under "2d.19f".

| Pass | Commit | Blocking findings | Fixed in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First | `99e81ba` | 2 ways past, 1 false high, 1 cost (13 to 23×), env keys holding `${{`, and a premise action GitHub refused | `6535379` |
| Second | `32dbbae` | 1 cost (3.3×) | `efe0a6a` |
| Third | `efe0a6a` | 1 memory case (2.1 GB against 327 MB) | `2f6791d` |
| Fourth | `2f6791d` | none | — |

- **The first pass in detail:** a value ending in `$` before `{{` made an expression GitHub never works out, which hid a warned option or gave a false high.
- **Left, and in the base too:** #401 (opened). The second pass's own text can hold such an expression, and an unterminated `'` in a value gives a high that bash would refuse. `0318223` after the fourth check is wording only.

## Run, with results

- **New tests:** `tests/test_env_expression_local_actions.py`, 27 tests, 17 of which fail on the base. One existing test changed its expected value from "cannot tell" to high: `test_env_expression_options.py`, now `test_a_local_actions_input_is_worked_out_in_its_callers_context`. This is the case D-143 left, and GitHub hands the action the caller's value.
- **Full local suite** (Python 3.13, package installed in a local venv, `TMPDIR` outside Git): 3,520 OK on `6535379` (2 skipped). The run on the final code is reported below once it ends.
- **CI premise:**
  - Run [45951941363](https://github.com/Obaaf/OBAAF/actions/runs/45951941363), on `99e81ba`: GitHub refused the first premise action ("Unrecognized named-value: 'env'" in its descriptions and its input `default`).
  - Run [45955337311](https://github.com/Obaaf/OBAAF/actions/runs/45955337311): every asserted value was as recorded on all three systems. GitHub refused the input default that reads `env`, so such an action does not load at all.
- **Byte-identical with `3bf8e04`** in stdout, stderr and exit status:
  - this repository: the CI command with its baseline, JSON, SARIF, `--summary` and `--lanes`;
  - Expectrail `d9011bec`, a read-only export without `bugs/` or `fresh-*`: the same five. It exits 1 as before.
- **Cost, base against head:**

  | Case | Base | Head |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 20,000 references over 5,000 entries on 200 lines | 5.0 s | 4.8 s |
  | Three aliased steps, 400 lines of five `\|\|` defaults and a ternary over 1,000 entries | 2.7 s | 2.6 s |
  | The same in a local action, three aliased uses | 5.2 s | 5.1 s |
  | An input read 2,000 times, given a 100 KB value | 1.3 s | 1.5 s |
  | 300 jobs using a 20-step action | 11.1 s / 105 MB | 11.3 s / 65 MB |
  | Reviewer's 3,000 inputs × 20 aliased steps | 8.5 s | 8.7 s |
  | Reviewer's `toJSON(inputs)` with a different `env` per step | 13.1 s | 18.2 s |
  | Reviewer's 100 KB × 1,000 inputs × 20 steps | 17.3 s / 327 MB | 20.4 s / 240 MB |

  The first three rebuild 2d.18's first-review cost cases from #382's description; that review's own directories are gone.
- **Not run:** GitHub itself for the checker's readings (only the premise ran there); self-hosted runners; PyPI.

## What is left

- #401, for the lead.
- D-143's stated limits: a writer the checker cannot see.
- A line is sized against every input's value, whether the line reads it or not, so large inputs it does not read make it "cannot tell".

author: the-anonymous-aspirant
body:
system_3 #12521.

`scripts/lake-skeleton.sh verify` fails four content checks on a lake that has received real uploads. Those checks were written for phase 0, when the lake held only fixtures, and they asserted the fixture set's shape on every row. This scopes each check to what it can answer:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A sensitivity=high row exists | exactly one `high` row in the whole lake | exactly one among the fixture rows (`dataset_id = catalog.SYNTHETIC_DATASET_ID`); SKIP when there are none |
| Content addressing | `sha256(stored bytes) == sha256` for every row, which every encrypted row fails by design (keyed by plaintext digest, stored as ciphertext) | every row: key ends in its digest; plaintext rows hash to it; encrypted rows carry the `AOBJ` header, read with a 4-byte range GET |
| No fixture value could be mistaken for operator data | scanned every row, and printed up to three values into the log | unchanged on a fixtures-only lake (still fails closed); SKIP with the reason, printing no value, once any non-fixture row exists |
| Fixture dates are all in 2999 | every row | the fixture rows only; SKIP when there are none |
| Gmail linker is provisioned | | unchanged: it finds a real gap |

The checks move into `scripts/lake/skeleton_content.py`, which is pure and stdlib-only. The fixtures' dataset id moves into the catalog contract, so the seed and the verify read one constant. The header comes from `dek_envelope.AOBJ_MAGIC`.

**Tests:** `tests/lake_skeleton_content_unit.sh`, which is new. It runs static checks, plus 20 cases against an in-memory DuckDB built from the catalog DDL, using DuckDB 1.5.4, the lake image's pin. It covers a fixtures-only lake, fixtures beside real rows, real rows only, and a row with no dataset id. Run against a copy with check 1's scoping removed, it fails on the mixed lake. `lake_catalog_unit.sh` (33/33), `lake_skeleton_unit.sh` (89/89) and `lake_catalog_ddl.sh` (6/6) pass. `changelog.sh check` is OK.

**Not done here:** running `verify` on the cell. It is a read of the production lake, and it waits for this merge and for `lake-skeleton.sh up`, which provisions the Gmail linker.

author: puchu-ai
body:
## Why

#6136 bumps only the tag (`5.1.3` → `5.2.1`) while leaving the `digest:` key on the **5.1.3** image digest. The chart (`fluent-bit 0.58.3`) renders `repository:tag@digest` and containerd resolves **by digest**, so merging it would deploy nothing: the pods would keep running 5.1.3 content under a `5.2.1` label, after an unnecessary 4-node rolling restart.

Registry evidence (GHCR index digests):

| tag | digest |
|---|---|
| 5.1.3 | `sha256:c55425…a70845` ← the one pinned in #6136 |
| 5.2.1 | `sha256:8db4e4fc1009fd6dabac7e6a3366ad006ca0c3a140ea938db79044d52964943d` |

## Root cause

The app manifest pinned the digest on a **separate `digest:` key** — the only HelmRelease in the repo using that form (the 52 others inline it as `tag: X@sha256:…`, e.g. #6091). Renovate's `helm-values` manager does not extract that sibling key (the dependency dashboard lists the dep as `ghcr.io/fluent/fluent-bit 5.1.3` with no digest), so tag-only bumps freeze the digest forever.

## What this does

- Moves to the repo-convention inline form `tag: 5.2.1@sha256:8db4e4…` (drops the `digest:` key), so Renovate keeps **tag and digest in sync** from now on.
- The comment in the manifest documents why, so the separate-key form does not come back.

Verified locally:

- `flate test hr fluent-bit --path ./kubernetes/apps` → ✓ HelmRelease renders
- `helm template` with the PR values → `image: "ghcr.io/fluent/fluent-bit:5.2.1@sha256:8db4e4…"` (no double-`@`, digest matches the tag)

## Notes

- Upstream 5.2.0/5.2.1: nothing breaking for this config — Lua filter still supported (FTS is opt-in), our paths are absolute so the config-relative-path precedence change doesn't apply, `out_http` now honors `Retry-After`/429 (good with `retry_limit no_limits`). Hardening in 5.2.x: static CRI parser, symlink-traversal hardening, `in_forward` compressed payload validation.
- `app.kubernetes.io/version` stays `5.1.3` until the chart appVersion is bumped (chart 0.58.3 — cosmetic only; Renovate tracks the chart separately).
- Post-merge check: `kubectl get ds -n observability fluent-bit -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'` should show `5.2.1@sha256:8db4e4…` and the rollout completes on all 4 nodes. Flux reconciles via webhook on push — no forced reconcile needed.

Closes #6136 (superseded).

author: xiaoyi728
body:
## 现象

在一台 glibc 2.28 的机器（Rocky Linux 8.10）上试用，两步都卡住：

**1. 官方 AppImage 直接起不来**（不是"装"的问题，是动态链接阶段就拒了）：

```
[PYI-336940:ERROR] Failed to load Python shared library
  '/tmp/.mount_xxx/_internal/libpython3.12.so.1.0':
  /lib64/libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.38' not found
```

**2. 改用源码构建后，产物能起来但面板不出来**，Qt 只丢一行：

```
qt.qpa.plugin: From 6.5.0, xcb-cursor0 or libxcb-cursor0 is needed to load the Qt xcb platform plugin.
qt.qpa.plugin: Could not load the Qt platform plugin "xcb" in "" even though it was found.
```

RHEL/Rocky/Alma 8 的官方仓库里没有 `libxcb-cursor`（只有 EPEL 的 `xcb-util-cursor`），
所以"从源码构建就能用"这条路对 RHEL 系老系统其实还是断的。

## 这个 PR 做什么

1. **新增 `linux/fetch_vendor_libs.sh`**：系统缺 `libxcb-cursor.so.0` 时，从发行版仓库下包、
   只取出那个 `.so` 放进 `linux/vendor/lib/`。不需要 root（dnf 系 `repoquery --location` +
   `rpm2cpio`，deb 系 `apt-get download` + `dpkg-deb -x`，openSUSE 走 zypper）。
   幂等；取不到只报错退出，不破坏构建。
2. **`linux/ocrsnip.spec`**：`linux/vendor/lib/libxcb-cursor.so.0` 存在就加进 `binaries`，
   落到 `_internal/` —— PyInstaller bootloader 设的 RUNPATH 已经覆盖 `_internal`，
   **用户不用配 `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`**（实测确认过这一点）。不存在则构建行为完全不变。
3. **`linux/build_app.sh`**：构建前调用上面的脚本，失败仅警告。
4. **`.gitignore`**：忽略 `linux/vendor/`，仓库只放提取脚本，不提交二进制。
5. **`linux/README-Linux.md`**：补两条 FAQ（`GLIBC_2.38 not found`、xcb 插件加载失败），
   「系统库」一栏点名 `libxcb-cursor`，第五节补老系统源码构建的做法与实测数据。
6. **`src/ocrsnip/cli.py`**：`ocrsnip doctor` 在 Qt 后端下不再把「gi 缺失」算作失败。
   现在的打包版是 Qt-only，但 `_doctor_linux()` 无条件 import gi，导致**每个打包版用户
   跑 `doctor` 都会看到一行红字 + `结论: 有问题`**，而实际抓屏是好的。改成按 `_pick_ui()`
   判断实际后端；GTK 后端机器行为不变。

## 验证

环境：Rocky Linux 8.10 / glibc 2.28 / X11 / GNOME Classic / 1920×1080 / Python 3.12.1

- `python -m pytest -q` → **38 passed, 1 skipped**（改动前后一致）
- `rm -rf linux/dist linux/build && ./linux/build_app.sh` 干净重建通过，
  `_internal/libxcb-cursor.so.0` 由 spec 自动带入，**没有手工拷贝步骤**
- 产物在**不设** `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` 的情况下 `./ocrsnip doctor`：
  `GTK 后端: 跳过（当前是 Qt 后端，抓屏在上面测过）`，`结论: 就绪`（不再是失败）
- 端到端（XTEST 合成 `Ctrl+Alt+Q` + 鼠标拖框 → 读剪贴板）：**PASS**，
  剪贴板拿到 `OCRSNIP 端到端測試 2026 快速識別`；systemd 用户服务版同样 PASS
- 性能（供参考）：抓屏 8–10 ms、OCR 26–79 ms（640×120 选区）、松手→剪贴板 414 ms、
  常驻 231 MB

`GLIBC_2.38` 那条属于**构建基线**问题（AppImage 是在 glibc 2.39 的机器上打的），
本 PR 不去改它，只是把"本地源码构建"这条路补通、并在文档里写清楚。

## 兼容性 / 可讨论的点

- 系统或发行版自带 `libxcb-cursor.so.0` 时：脚本直接跳过，产物与之前**逐字节等价的构建流程**
  （不会多带一个库文件）
- 构建过程会多一次网络请求（下载几十 KB 的包）；离线环境会警告并继续
- 如果不想让构建脚本联网：可以只保留 `README` + `spec` 两部分，
  把 `fetch_vendor_libs.sh` 变成手动可选的准备步骤——我按"自动但失败不阻断"来做，
  是因为本机上 `linux/build_in_container.sh` 那条容器路线走不通（容器仓库被代理拦），
  老系统用户只剩源码构建这一条

Tooling only (CI and release); closes #861. The release checks that used to run only on a tag now also run on a pull request that touches release contents.


author: digitalishealth
body:
## Problem

The Markdown evaluation export omits use limitations, provenance metadata and repeated-run statistics that are already present in EvaluationReport. A reader of the exported report therefore loses information available in the structured result.

## Changes

- Render the report notice before the score.
- Include the existing ReproducibilityMetadata only, preserving input/rubric identity, judge configuration and zero-valued parameters.
- Render supplied repeated-run statistics with an explicit limit to judge-run variability.
- Mark missing metadata and missing repeated-run evidence explicitly.
- For fewer than two runs, mark variability and the interval as not estimable instead of presenting a point interval.
- Preserve scoring/model semantics and exclude raw judge responses.

## Validation

Six focused offline synthetic regression checks pass on the candidate. Against the reviewed baseline, five of those checks fail and one passes. Checks cover notice placement, input identity and zero values, repeated-run scope, the single-run interval boundary, missing evidence, absence of raw-response export, no report mutation and matching file output.

Reviewed source: 5b58cb7691022072b0f30990d225ce68ae43fa57. A complete isolated checkout with only these two candidate files applied passed the full offline suite (pytest -q -m 'not live': 208 passed), ruff check src/ tests/ scripts/, public_release_audit.py, validation_pack_audit.py, audit_validation_evidence_runs.py, scribeval list-dimensions and git diff --check. Declared dependencies were installed in an isolated environment; this run used Python 3.12.14 and Pydantic 2.14.4.

The earlier focused regression run used Pydantic 2.13.4 and demonstrated five baseline failures becoming six passing tests on the candidate. No external model, FHIR or clinical-reviewer calls were made in either verification stage. The fixtures are mechanical rendering examples; passing software and structural audits adds no clinical-validity or independent-clinician evidence.

Independent read-only review found no material issues. Merge and release remain separate decisions.

## Published candidate

Head: `2bce55751f74bd065c6a5fa5a9d68975549c1792`. Both [PR CI](https://github.com/Digitalishealth/Scribeval/actions/runs/45951943725) and [push CI](https://github.com/Digitalishealth/Scribeval/actions/runs/45951931362) passed the Python 3.11 and 3.12 matrix. The two published file blobs match the locally tested files. No merge or release has been performed.

author: therenery
body:
### Summary
Tested running macOS Tahoe 26.3 (via `reims-vgpu` / `WSM`) on a Windows 11 laptop with **Intel(R) Arc(TM) 140T GPU (16GB)** (driver `32.0.101.9175`). These two small fixes resolve two immediate Vulkan runtime refusals on Intel Arc:

1. **`image_plan.rs` — Allow `DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT` usage for emulated `Stencil8` (`D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT`)**:
   - Intel Arc 140T does not support `VK_FORMAT_S8_UINT`, so `Stencil8` falls back to `VK_FORMAT_D32_SFLOAT_S8_UINT` (`FormatEmulation::StencilInCombined`).
   - `plan_held` previously checked `m.format == direct` / `format == direct`, which excluded `StencilInCombined` and `DepthInCombined` from receiving `DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT` usage, causing `render_pass` target validation to fail.
   - Allowing `FormatEmulation::StencilInCombined | FormatEmulation::DepthInCombined` fixes this cleanly.

2. **`depth_copy.rs` — Enable `FragDepth` fallback on `DriverId::INTEL_PROPRIETARY_WINDOWS`**:
   - Adds `DriverId::INTEL_PROPRIETARY_WINDOWS` to `FRAGMENT_DEPTH_CHANGES` so depth/stencil copy uses the `FragDepth` draw fallback instead of refusing with `MultisampledBufferCopy`.

### Verification
- `cargo test -p metal2vulkan-runtime --lib`: 845 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- Verified with `reims-vgpu` + macOS Tahoe 26.3 (`25D125`) on Intel Arc 140T.

### Note on Remaining Intel Arc 140T Observation (Issues are disabled on this repo)
During testing on Intel Arc 140T (`32.0.101.9175`), `InterleaveCopy::record` in `sample_interleave.rs` (54x54 MSAA color and depth/stencil buffer<->texture copies) triggers Windows TDR / `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` when executing `BufferRows`, `Merge`, `CopyImage`, or `Move` steps (`Barrier::everything()` alone does not hang). That workaround is intentionally **not** included in this PR (kept only on a separate fork branch `intel-arc-140t-workaround` for personal use).

*(Note: I do not have capacity for ongoing maintenance, so please feel free to adapt or merge these two fixes as you see fit.)*

body:
## Workstream
proof/k4-ksens (session branch `claude/k4-ksens`). This follows #159, which is merged. It was closed out at the campaign wind-down (2026-11-27 06:53 UTC): every run is stopped, and each partial log ends with a `PARTIAL` line giving its count. Write-up: `k4/ksens.md`, status block (burst 5) and §8. `origin/main` is merged in.

## What changed and why
Labels: [Cert] certified for every strict profile of the stated class (single CEGAR, validated against independent code at k ≤ 4); [R] refuted, with two checkers; [E] evidence or partial.

**Refuted [R]**
- **Conjecture RF, "every receiver-first maximum-matching order satisfies OC₁", fails at k = 5, n = 4.** `refute_rf_k5.py`, brute force and ocsat.
  - **RF5:** sets [[0,1,2,5,6],[1,2,4,5,6],[3,4,5,6],[3,4,5,6]], vals [[3,35,33,43,39],[20,26,16,43,32],[8,2,7,4],[8,2,7,4]]; agents 2 and 3 are twins.
  - At the start (6,5,4,3), a maximum matching, OC₁ fails, even with the free completion.
  - The unique receiver is agent 2. Its order (2,1,0,3) gives (6,5,3,4), the twin swap, and OC₁ fails there too. The other 5 receiver-first vectors work.
  - The coordinator confirmed this independently and added the row K4.SDC.RF.K5EVERY.
  - **RF5b:** same hypergraph and start, but agents 2 and 3 are not twins: same ranking, different types. So "up to relabelling exact twins" fails too (`rfcegar.RFT`).

**Certified [Cert]**
- **RF∃ ("some receiver-first order works")**, which still gives OC₁^∃max (`rfcegar.RFE`):
  - all 13 n = 3, k = 5 hypergraphs where OC₁^max fails (elsewhere at n = 3 it is vacuous);
  - RF5's hypergraph;
  - the 11 k = 4 cores.
  - Control: with no chain allowed it fails, and brute force confirms.
- **RF up to ordinal twins** (same relevant set, same single-good ranking): certified on RF5's hypergraph (`rfcegar.py --ordinal-twins`).

**Partial [E]**
| run | done | result |
|---|---|---|
| RF every-form, k = 5, n = 4 core-like, m ≤ 7 | 784 of 1,138 | 780 certified, 4 FAIL (688, 807, 816, 826), brute-force rechecks only. Each is a swap of two agents' picks; in 807 and 826 the two agents have nested, unequal sets, so ordinal twins are probably not the whole story |
| RF∃, k = 5, n = 4 core-like, m ≤ 7 | 471 of 1,138 | all certified |
| two chains, k = 6, exact mode | n = 3: 19 of 950; n = 4 core-like: 93 of 891; designed: 4 of 18 | all certified; none needs a third chain |
| two chains, k = 5, n = 4 core-like, m ≥ 8 | 875 of 8,870 | all certified |

**Tools**
- `rfcegar.py`: RF, RFE (RF∃) and RFT (up to exact or ordinal twins).
- `kcegar_batch.py`: `--rf`, `--rfe` and `--rft`.
- `refute_rf_k5.py`.

## Ledger changes
None: LEDGER.md is not edited here. The coordinator added K4.SDC.RF.K5EVERY. A ledger-ready row for RF∃ at n = 3, if wanted:

| ID | Claim | Status | Artifact | Lean | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| K4.KSENS.RFE5 | RF∃: at every OC₁-failing maximum-matching start, for every receiver u, some u-first order gives maximum-matching picks satisfying OC₁; for every strict profile of every connected n = 3 hypergraph with k ≤ 5, and of RF5's hypergraph | CERTIFIED | `k4/ksens/rfcegar.py`, `results/k4_ksens/rfecegar_k5_n3.log`, `results/k4_ksens/rfecegar_k4_cex.log`, `results/k4_ksens/kcegar_k5_n3_D1.log` | | Computational, single CEGAR. At n = 4, 471 of 1,138 core-like hypergraphs were certified before the wind-down (`results/k4_ksens/rfecegar_k5_core5_n4.log`, partial). RF∃ gives OC₁^∃max |

## Checklist
- [x] Read PROMPT.md and LEDGER.md; this does not duplicate an open PR
- [x] Every ledger status change comes with its artifact: none
- [x] New certificates are under `results/`: no frontier certificates
- [x] `python tools/check_ledger.py` passes locally (507 rows, 0 problems after merging main)
- [x] Only this workstream's files are edited
- [x] Partial runs are labelled `PARTIAL` in their logs and in `k4/ksens.md`

## What remains open
- Does any maximum-matching start at k = 6 need a third chain? 116 hypergraphs certified, none needs one; the sweeps are incomplete.
- RF∃ in general.
- The right refined RF statement: 807 and 826 suggest that swaps between agents with nested sets matter. The four failures still need a second checker (ocsat).
- RD² at every k.

body:
上一轮分块验收日志里 `failures=36` 无法归因，而且文档给的时间参数会让测试立刻超时。
两处都修掉。

## 改了什么

- `frontend/tests/e2e/latex/template-compile.spec.ts`：进度行的 `failures=` 改为只统计
  **传输失败 / 5xx / 409**；普通缺文件单列 `missing-404=`。TeX 的 kpathsea 会探测大量可选
  文件，404 是正常路径，之前把所有非 2xx 都算失败，才会出现「36 个失败但说不出是哪些」。
  真实失败一出现就把该行打进日志（最多 20 条去重），即使运行被中途杀掉也能看到具体 URL。
- `frontend/tests/e2e/latex/TEMPLATE-ACCEPTANCE.md`：`--timeout 8m` 是错的——Playwright
  的单位是毫秒，`8m` 会变成 8 毫秒并立刻报 `Test timeout of 8ms exceeded`；改为
  `--timeout 480000` 并注明单位。

## 为什么

分块验收的价值在于「每次运行结束后，日志本身能回答问题」。上一轮日志只有计数没有明细，
运行被杀后无法判断那 36 个非 2xx 是正常探测还是真故障，只能重跑。

## 验证

- `pnpm lint` → 0 errors（仅 `public/latex-engines/stet/*.d.ts` 两条既有 warning）。
- `pnpm typecheck` → 通过。
- 未跑真实模板编译：本轮只改日志分类与文档参数。

## 没覆盖

- 分块复跑仍需一次完整结束的运行来产出 PDF.js 页数结论；这次日志会直接列出任何真实失败
  的 URL。

## 复用 / 替换 / 删除

- 复用既有进度行与 spec 结构，没有新增机制。
- 没有删除代码，没有留下 TODO。

author: eunchaipark
body:
## 무엇을 왜

편집 화면에서 PowerPoint 손버릇대로 눌렀을 때 일이 사라지거나 엉뚱한 것이 켜지던 곳을 맞춥니다. 앱 전체를 써 보며 사용 편의를 점검하다 나온 것입니다.

- **글을 고치다 Esc:** 쓴 글을 남기고 마칩니다(PowerPoint · Google Slides 와 같습니다). 전에는 쓴 글을 모두 버렸고, 파일에 쓰이지 않아 Ctrl+Z 로도 살릴 수 없었습니다. 되돌리려면 Ctrl+Z 를 씁니다.
- **쪽 넘김 키:** PageUp · PageDown · Home · End 는 요소를 고른 채로도 쪽을 넘깁니다. 슬라이드를 한 번 누르면 거의 늘 무언가 골라져, Esc 를 먼저 누르기 전에는 PageDown 이 듣지 않았습니다. 방향키는 그대로 요소 옮기기에 씁니다.
- **도구 키:** 요소를 고른 채로 글자를 치면 도구 키(C 비교 · S 이어 보기 · F 서식 · 1~4)가 켜지지 않습니다. 상자를 고르고 타자를 치면 비교 · 이어 보기가 켜졌습니다.
- **Delete 키:** 리본 「지우기」와 같은 것을 지웁니다. 글 하나만 든 카드면 카드째 지웁니다. 전에는 글만 지워 빈 카드가 남았고, 리본 「지우기」와 결과가 달랐습니다.
- **지난 판 보기:** 슬라이드를 보기만 합니다. 끌어 옮기고 글을 고칠 수 있게 보였지만 아무것도 저장되지 않았습니다. Esc 로 지금 판으로 돌아옵니다.
- 쪽을 넘기기 전에 아직 쓰지 않은 방향키 이동을 먼저 씁니다.
- 고르기 도구 안내에 「Shift+Enter 줄 바꿈 · Esc 마치기」를 적습니다.

**동작이 바뀌는 것:** Esc 와 Delete 키입니다. 둘 다 일이 사라지거나 리본과 결과가 달랐던 것을 고치는 것이라 스위치 뒤에 두지 않았습니다. 스위치가 낫다면 말씀해 주세요.

## 확인한 것

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `cargo test --lib` (src-tauri): 52개 통과
- [x] `npx vitest run`: 21개 통과
- [x] 개발 실행(`npm run tauri dev`)에서 시험 덱으로 실제 키를 눌러 해 본 것. 같은 변경을 넣은 fork 의 작업 줄기(0.15.0 위)에서 했습니다.
  - 제목을 고르고 Enter, 글을 바꾼 뒤 Esc 를 누르면 바꾼 글이 파일에 남습니다.
  - 제목을 고른 채 C · S 를 눌러도 비교 · 이어 보기가 켜지지 않고 제목 글도 그대로입니다.
  - 제목을 고른 채 PageDown 을 누르면 2쪽으로 넘어갑니다.
  - 카드 글을 고르고 Delete 를 누르면 카드째 지워지고, Ctrl+Z 로 돌아옵니다.
  - 지난 판을 보는 중에는 눌러도 골라지지 않고(「요청에 넣기」가 뜨지 않음), Esc 로 지금 판으로 돌아옵니다.
- [ ] 협업 브라우저 팀원 화면에서는 해 보지 못했습니다.

## CHANGELOG 에 넣을 줄

> - 글을 고치다 Esc 를 누르면 쓴 글을 남긴다. 요소를 고른 채로도 PageUp · PageDown 으로 쪽을 넘기고, 고른 채 타자를 쳐도 도구가 바뀌지 않는다.
> - Delete 키가 리본 「지우기」와 같이 카드째 지우고, 지난 판을 보는 중에는 슬라이드를 고칠 수 없다(Esc 로 지금으로).

author: the-mysterious-baffler
body:
## Summary

Design Phase 1 for maps (VTTER-86). This is a design story: documents, a mockup and one rule, with **no feature code**.
It defines what every Emberreach map is made of, so the map editor (VTTER-74), triggers, fog of war, slabs and the
GM-only layer all build on one model. The model comes from Heath's cartography program.

- **`docs/map-model/`**: the vision (now, later, maybe), the glossary, the property catalog (acts or describes, with triggers and stacking rules),
  the data model (JSON shape, 400 KB size math, versioning, storage, who receives what), four paper tests that need no
  special cases, and an inventory of every place type and material in the cartography program, marked keep, fix, later or drop.
- **`docs/adr/0010-layered-map-objects.md`**: one item per map, the map as the author's template versus the Game's table state, and
  API-side filtering of GM-only objects and fog of war.
- **`docs/mockups/map-editor.html`**: the editor on desktop and phone, including the GM's "view as" over party or per-token fog of war.
- **Six kinds, using Heath's names:** Environment space, Enclosure, Route, Portal, Static Object, Entity.

## Rules changed

**Core rules v0.3 → v0.4.** A new *Terrain* rule in §6.3: entering a Difficult zone costs 2 zones of Speed, and never
more when layers stack. You can't enter an Impassable zone. 1 hex = 1 zone. `data/core.json` gains
`movement.difficultCost` (2) and `difficultCap` (2).

Decisions logged in `docs/decisions.md`:
- Terrain (the rule above).
- The layered map object model, which answers the nine open questions in the ticket.
- **Fog of war comes into scope** as a GM toggle between party vision and per-token vision. This amends 2026-11-25.
  Dynamic lighting and 3D terrain stay out. CLAUDE.md and README are updated to match.

The hero and handler tests now read `core.version` instead of a hard-coded `0.3`.

## Checks

- app: `npm test` (403 passed), `npm run lint`, `npm run build`
- api: `npm test` (176 passed), `npm run typecheck`
- `/security-check`: no findings. The filtered player view is a design here; VTTER-74, VTTER-111 and VTTER-91 each re-check it when it's built.
- Rebased onto VTTER-73. The map ADR is 0010, because friends took 0009.

## Jira

https://morris-heap.atlassian.net/browse/VTTER-86. VTTER-74 is rewritten against the model, and the later phases are VTTER-110 to VTTER-114.

Merging deploys the app and the API. That deploys only docs, the new `data/core.json` key and the rules version string.

author: kenvandine
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"kenvandine"} -->
_Requested by **Ken** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01PqwTnXpzoX9sUccjScBD5Q?thread=cmsg_01PqwTnXpzoX9sUccjScBD5QKi6WrpZWBCYowXo7tdyLjw)_

The first step of M4's "the API at 1.0 with its promise". Every module stays at 0.x: when to call 1.0 is Ken's decision.

## What changes

**`@potluck/world` 0.2** (only adds to 0.1):
- `world.after(seconds, fn)`, `world.every(seconds, fn)` and `world.cancel(id)`. Timers run on the world's ticks (0.1 s is the shortest), with at most 64 waiting per creation. A creation with no creatures can now run a game.
- `world.on("player_joined" | "player_left", fn)`, called with the player. There are at most 32 handlers.
- Timers, events and creature handlers share the creation's 15 ms each tick.

**`@potluck/store` 0.1** (new):
- `store.get`, `store.set` (nil forgets a key), `store.keys` and `store.used`.
- Values are JSON-able Luau: numbers, strings, booleans, vectors and nested tables. The quota is 64 KB per creation per world.
- The store lives in `GameShared` beside the boards, so it survives hot reloads. The server saves it as `store.json` next to `boards.json` and reads it before any creation starts. `Vm::load` now gets the world's shared state, so a creation's top level can read its store (and boards) as it loads.

**Tag Bot** keeps each player's tags in the store and greets players it remembers when they join.

**Fixes found on the way:**
- `print()` inside handlers and timers never reached Look inside: only prints made while the code loaded did. The log is now read after every call into a creation.
- The market rejected creations made for an older 0.x minor version, which the game itself accepts. Now both take the same major and any minor up to theirs. Without this, every creation needing `world = "0.1"` would have failed the API check once the market knew 0.2.

**docs/api.md** is the promise:
- Minor versions only add, and every major stays.
- Deprecated things keep working, and only their maker sees a note.
- The limits only loosen.
- Beta modules have no promise and can't be shared to Everyone.
- 0.x stays loadable after 1.0.

It also lists every module, every limit and a change list. AGENTS.md, the types file, the README and CLAUDE.md are updated to match.

## Testing

- `cargo build --bins`
- `cargo test --workspace`: 31 game tests and 14 market tests pass. New tests:
  - `timers_and_world_events_run_a_creation_with_no_creatures`: every, after, cancel, joins and leaves, the timer cap, unknown events
  - `creations_keep_things_in_the_store`: lists and vectors round-trip, the quota, no functions, a reload, another creation's own store, and save and load as a server does
  - `module_versions` now checks that a 0.1 creation passes on 0.2

   퇴소 때 프로필 파일 삭제가 실패하거나, 복원 뒤 다시 적용(`after_restore apply`)으로 경로만 비워지면 파일이 남았어요. 이제 `profiles/` 파일을 `children.profile_photo_path`와 대조해 고아로 잡아요. 복원 절차의 `media_sweep --apply --min-age 0` 단계에서 같이 지워져요. `meals/`는 원별 행이 있어서 대상에서 뺐어요.

DB 설계서 0021 절과 마이그레이션 주석도 이에 맞게 고쳤어요.

## 시험
[TEST] 임시 PG에서 사진·고아 점검·백업 복원 시험 13개가 통과했어요. 새 시험 `test_sweep_finds_profile_files_left_without_a_child_path`를 넣었어요. ruff와 `tsc -b`도 통과했어요.

body:
## Copy changes, page by page

Most of the copy in scope was already plain. No em-dash chains, filler words, sparkle or rocket icons, or emoji turned up. The changes below fix tagline fragments, padded headings and one inaccurate claim. The second commit also removes Sensors selling from the public copy this ticket owns, because FIZ-4 is hiding Sensors from fizzlayer.com.

**/gateway** (`site/gateway_page.gleam`)
- "Three ways a tool call goes wrong." → "What goes wrong when an agent connects directly."
- "Clear about what it checks." → "What it does and doesn't do."
- "Short answers." → "Common questions."
- Step "Approve, and it retries" → "The agent retries". The old step said the gateway retries the call. The agent does, as the app's Approvals tab says.
- The closing panel now recommends Pro: "We recommend Pro, at $25 a month: 25 MCP servers, 100 phone calls a month for approvals, and 3 seats." It has a "Start Pro" button to `/app?plan=pro` and a "Start free on Hobbyist" link. The page has no separate Pro callout, so it doesn't end with two calls to action in a row.

**/pricing** (`site/pricing.gleam`)
- Hero: "Start free. Upgrade when you need more. Every plan covers Gateway and Sensors." → "Start on Hobbyist for free, and upgrade when you hit a limit. Every plan includes a hosted MCP gateway, and self-hosting is free. We recommend Pro if you want approvals by phone."
- Cards and the compare table no longer list Sensors-only rows: connected devices and Fizz credits. They list "1 shared hosted gateway", MCP servers, phone calls and seats instead. Hobbyist shows "Approvals by webhook or log".
- Prices and the remaining limits are unchanged.
- The Pro card has a **Recommended** badge and a "Start Pro" button. Its tagline "For serious setups" is now "For up to 3 people".
- The closing CTA recommends Pro and links to `/app?plan=pro`, with Hobbyist and Enterprise as the other links.

**/enterprise**: rewritten for the gateway. The old page was all about sensors (cold storage, device keys, simulated sensors). Each claim was checked against the `enterprise` plan in `src/gateway/limits.rs`:
- Gateway, MCP server and seat limits are set per team.
- Phone approvals are set by contract. The gateway phones a paired number and reads the request, and you approve in the app (`notify.rs` `approval_script`).
- Hosted (shared, gw.fizzlayer.com) or self-hosted with Docker. Dedicated hosted gateways are marked as not ready yet.
- No SSO claim, because SSO doesn't exist in the code.
- The contact form posts the same ids and fields as before. Only its label and placeholder changed, from "What would you like Fizz to watch?" to "What do you need from the gateway?".

**/status**: "Fizzlayer right now." → "Is Fizzlayer up?"

**/changelog** (intro only): "What shipped." → "Merged changes, newest first"

**Footer**: "Control what your AI agents can do." → "Rules and approvals for the MCP tools your AI agents call."

**llms.txt, app.html and settings.html** (first commit)
- llms.txt: dropped "the secure connection layer" and a link to a `/gateway#plans` anchor that doesn't exist.
- app.html and settings.html: replaced the "Your world has a sidekick." sidebar text.
- The Sensors text in these files is left for FIZ-4.

**Gateway app** (`gateway.gleam`, `signin.gleam`, `checkout.gleam`, `ui.gleam`): audited, nothing changed. The plan line was not touched.

## Pro callout

`site.pro_callout()` in `app/src/ui/site.gleam` has a "Start Pro" button to `/app?plan=pro` and a "Compare plans" link to `/pricing`. The figures are gateway limits from the Pro column in `pricing.gleam`:

> **Fizzlayer Pro is $25 a month.** Hobbyist stops at 3 MCP servers and does not place phone calls. Pro allows 25 servers, includes 100 phone calls a month for approvals, and has 3 seats.

It appears near the end of Enterprise, Self-host, Status and Changelog. The new CSS (`.pro-callout`, `.pro-callout-actions`, `.plan-badge`) is in `app/assets/fizz.css`.

## Tests
- `public_pages_end_with_the_pro_callout_test`: Enterprise, Self-host, Status and Changelog render the callout with both links.
- `gateway_page_closes_on_pro_test`: /gateway has no callout, and its closing panel links to `/app?plan=pro` and offers a free start.
- `public_copy_does_not_sell_sensors_test`: no device or Fizz credit rows on these pages, and no "sensor" in the Enterprise page body.
- `pricing_recommends_pro_test`: the Pro card is featured and has the Recommended badge.

## Checks
- `gleam format --check src test` and `gleam test`: 54 passed.
- `check-ui-classes.sh`: passed.
- `build-spa.sh`: regenerated public files are committed.
- `agent-cards.mjs --check`, `node --check public/*.js` and `check-no-build-output.sh`: all passed.
- Playwright screenshots of every changed page at 1280px and 390px, served statically from `public/`. No horizontal scroll at either width.

author: leonardozerpa2497
body:
Keep dispatch comparison snapshots in device-local memory behind `NXRT_VK_WB_BASE_DEVICE=1` (off by default), with the synchronization and lifetime fixes required to make that path safe. Compact comparison output remains host-visible. This PR changes neither performance defaults nor the launcher.

## Correctness and fallback
- Order snapshot COPY reads before the guest COMPUTE writes in both host and device modes.
- Prepare the complete writeback plan, ring space, landing metadata, oracle masks and completion-post capacity before dispatch; failed preparation rolls back before choosing a host plan.
- Hold reservations until posted so one landing cannot release later ranges' still-live records. Publish the tail only after the callback's final read.
- On completion-queue allocation failure, terminate explicitly before the recording submission can be reported complete with missing effects.
- Require genuine device-local memory; keep `WB_GPU=2` as an independent host-snapshot oracle. Forced host fallback is available for testing.

## Evidence and limits
The prior source implementation was built and tested in one Windows co-op ship scene: the differential oracle compared 1,832,592 ranges without differing blocks or dropped writebacks; forced-host fallback compared 1,672,583 ranges without differences/drops. Alternating source runs improved average FPS at 1800p and 2160p, but 2160p p95 overlapped and long-frame share increased. Long-frame share increased at both tested resolutions; no stable-60 claim. Full measurements and methodology are in `docs/vulkan-writeback.md`; those measurements are not a benchmark of this isolated upstream branch.

Independent contrast review found no P0/P1. The extracted branch's real helper tests pass GCC ASan/UBSan, including 200,000 modeled mixed dispatches and allocation-failure regressions. MinGW syntax checks pass using placeholder generated shader arrays for syntax only, with an existing SetThreadDescription warning. No full shader build, driver validation or game boot is claimed for this extraction; those remain before-merge gates.

## Cost and rollback
The optional ring consumes another 256 MiB of device memory without reducing host-ring reservations. Set the option to 0/remove it to retain the host snapshot path; this preserves the correctness fixes. Revert the PR to restore the whole prior implementation. Dirty-page tracking and reuploads are unchanged. No assets, saves, private machine configuration or experimental default tuning are included.

Addresses four bug fixes and Phase 2 cleanup across ACP, audio, embeddings, notebook, vision, app/menu/hooks, and the UNO test runner (68 files changed, +1143 / -1431 lines vs `origin/master`).

### Bug Fixes
- **Kokoro env override protection** (`plugin/audio/model_cache_paths.py`, `plugin/audio/tts_models.py`, `tests/audio/test_tts_models.py`): Shared `env_override()` between `model_cache_paths.py` and `tts_models.py`, stopped requiring `os.path.exists(...)` for override detection, and gated `model_ok`/`voices_ok` on `(is_env_m and model_exists)` so missing or undersized `KOKORO_MODEL_PATH` / `KOKORO_VOICES_PATH` overrides (including `~`-prefixed paths) are never overwritten or downloaded. Added `test_kokoro_missing_override_never_downloads` and `test_kokoro_tilde_small_override_never_overwritten`.
- **Translated local Whisper empty-stdout error** (`plugin/audio/stt_service.py`, `tests/audio/test_stt_service.py`): Attached `_WHISPER_NO_TRANSCRIPT_CODE = "WHISPER_NO_TRANSCRIPT"` to `ConfigError` in `parse_whisper_stdout` and matched `exc.code` in `_transcribe_local` instead of English message text. Added `test_empty_stdout_reports_exit_code_when_message_translated`.
- **Single-pass prose extraction** (`plugin/embeddings/embeddings_fs.py`, `tests/embeddings/test_embeddings_fs.py`): Removed the duplicate `extract_indexable_passages(norm)` call in `indexable_chunks_from_path` and built `body_sample` from `passage_runs[:20]`. Added `test_indexable_chunks_from_path_extracts_prose_once`.
- **Config monkeypatch cleanup in UNO runner** (`plugin/testing_runner.py`, `tests/framework/test_testing_runner.py`): Wrapped `run_all_tests` in `try: ... finally:` to restore `plugin.framework.config.get_config`, `.save`, and `.get_config_dict`. Added `test_run_all_tests_restores_config_module`.

### Cleanups & Refactors
- **ACP** (`plugin/acp/acp_connection.py`, `acp_backend.py`, `base.py`, `builtin.py`): Consolidated duplicate error/permission helpers (`cancelled_permission`), removed dead code, hoisted imports, and updated present-tense comments.
- **Audio** (`plugin/audio/kokoro_worker.py`, `kokoro_pool.py`, `kokoro_g2p.py`, `voice_catalog.py`, `tts_voices.py`, `tts_endpoint.py`, `tts_service.py`): Extracted shared helpers (`_model_or_raise`, `_piper_pair_ready`, `provider_or_none`), made `py_exe: str | None` a required parameter on `_kokoro_audio_file`, `_piper_audio_file`, and `_synthesize_sentence_clip`, hoisted `provider_or_none` to the top of `tts_endpoint.py`, and cleaned up string formatting and comments.
- **Embeddings** (`plugin/embeddings/*.py`, `plugin/embeddings/venv/*.py`, `docs/embeddings.md`): Shared `_chunk_from_piece`, `_store_dir_populated`, `_finish`, `_refresh_status_if_open`, hoisted `KEY_RETURN` in `search_ui.py`, added `zlib.error` to `_read_zip_member` in `embeddings_locale.py`, and updated `docs/embeddings.md` links to `_store_dir_populated`.
- **Notebook** (`plugin/notebook/*.py`): Consolidated the ODF span walk (`paragraph_span`), simplified `_form_and_container` and `wire_all_notebook_run_buttons -> bool`, imported `com.sun.star.text.ControlCharacter.PARAGRAPH_BREAK` in `layout.py`, and updated present-tense comments.
- **Vision, App, Hooks, Testing Runner** (`plugin/vision/**/*.py`, `plugin/app.py`, `plugin/menu_state.py`, `plugin/writeragent_hooks.py`, `plugin/testing_runner.py`, `compute_service/server.py`, `plugin/mcp_server/*`): Shared `HELPER_NAMES`, simplified `_apply_pipeline_params` import in `vision_docling.py`, dropped redundant `list(tool_list)` copy in `writeragent_hooks.py`, imported `PARAGRAPH_BREAK` in `vision_egress.py`, restored why-comments in `vision_common.py` and `testing_runner.py`, and removed history/stale comments in `testing_runner.py`.

## Behaviour Changes
- Track Changes off: none.
- New refusals: none.
- Runtime changes are limited to the four bug fixes above (missing/undersized Kokoro env overrides are preserved without downloading; local Whisper empty-stdout errors match `exc.code` under translation; `indexable_chunks_from_path` extracts prose once; `run_all_tests` restores `plugin.framework.config` functions in `finally`).
- Deleted test id: `test_resolve_search_mode_reads_config` (in `tests/embeddings/test_embeddings_cache.py`, removed with the redundant config wrapper).
- Merge dependencies: none (base is `master`).

## Skipped / Left for Keith / Adaptations
- **Left for Keith (`DECIDE` items):**
  - `plugin/embeddings/embeddings_cache.py`: `CorpusMeta.write_row_count` `"row_count"` key.
  - `plugin/embeddings/embeddings_fs.py`: renaming `WriterFileEntry` to `IndexableFileEntry`.
  - `plugin/notebook/notebook_controls.py`: `supportsService("com.sun.star.text.TextDocument")` vs `is_writer`.
  - `plugin/vision/venv/vision_paddle.py`: `show_log` comment wording.
  - `plugin/vision/venv/vision.py`: reserved `context` parameter.
- **Skipped / adapted where HEAD differed:**
  - `plugin/acp/acp_backend.py`: kept `import plugin.framework.config as _config` so `test_acp_backend.py` monkeypatching `user_config_dir` continues to work (`daemon=True` was already absent on HEAD).
  - `plugin/audio/tts_models.py`, `plugin/embeddings/embedding_client.py`, `plugin/app.py`, `plugin/vision/venv/vision_layout_html.py`: kept `getattr(resp, "headers", None)` (unit tests pass `io.BytesIO`), `isinstance(payload, dict)` (`test_embed_texts_malformed_worker_result` tests non-dicts), `isinstance(..., dict)` on `_manifest.MODULES` (required by type checkers), and `isinstance(block, dict)` (`test_box_xywh_tolerant` passes `"not a dict"`).
  - `plugin/notebook/layout.py`: kept `height_for_text` (`insert_code_input_in_flow` needs unclamped `raw_h` for `vscroll`, while three test files assert `height_for_text` directly).
  - `plugin/vision/venv/vision_docling.py`: kept `importlib.import_module("docling.datamodel.pipeline_options")` inside `if acc_kwargs or norm.table_mode == "fast":` because unit tests pass `MagicMock()` without `docling` installed.
  - `plugin/vision/venv/vision_paddle.py`: reverted the two Paddle 2.x hunks per review.

## Checks
- `make typecheck`: passed (exit 0; ruff, `fix_bare_underscore_throwaways.py --check`, bandit, ty, mypy, opengrep, pyspector, basedpyright).
- `make test-bot`:
  - Pytest phase: `5456 passed, 29 skipped, 2 warnings in 46.48s` (0 failures).
  - UNO phase: `388 passed, 2 failed` in the shared long-lived soffice run (`calc.test_prompt_function_matrix_uno.test_array_blocks_survive_save_and_reload` and `draw.test_draw_tables_uno.test_draw_table_structure_row_column_and_delete` after VCL `Unspecified Application Error` `soffice_exit=134`).
  - Both UNO tests passed 1/1 when run in isolated `uno-probe.sh`:
    - `tests/calc/test_prompt_function_matrix_uno.py test_array_blocks_survive_save_and_reload`: passed (1/1).

author: jacob-chamney
body:
The registry owns rebinding, and the editor can bind a leader chord.

## The two gaps the review named

1. **Rebinding onto another action's default** was only caught by a round trip to
   the core, and the editor never consulted the table it renders.
2. **A new leader chord could not be captured at all**: `captureBinding` only
   ever built direct bindings, so a direct action could never become `Space x`.

## What changed

- `KeymapRegistry.rebind(actionId, binding)` is the write path's decision:
  accepted (with the resulting table), cleared, or refused with the **core's own
  sentence** (`Space c is already bound to surface.chat.`). It compares effective
  bindings, so a default and an override are equally authoritative.
- The editor calls it before writing; a refusal is shown on the row and nothing
  is sent. The core still re-checks as the second gate.
- `captureBinding(event, leader: true)` builds the leader's second half, and a
  second activation on a waiting row switches the capture to the leader (shown as
  `Space …`). `Space` itself can't both open the leader overlay and start a
  capture, so the affordance is explicit.

## Tests (+9)

```
registry-owned rebinding: free chord accepted · duplicate refused with the core copy
                          · onto another action's default refused · direct↔leader
                          · unknown action refused
editor: leader chord captured and written · collision refused in the editor
```

## Verification

```
bun run check              0   2207 core pass · 0 fail
scripts/desktop-check.sh   0   1132 widget (+9) · 2207 core · analyze clean
```

Add route-scoped GitHub API secret allowlist to eri-restate proxy

Allowlist configured Infisical secret keys on route-scoped GitHub API webhook endpoints in eri-restate's loopback GitHub proxy (/internal/github-api/) while preserving unconditional secret blocking on git pushes, repository content writes, comments, and MCP egress.

- services/eri/pkg/guard: Add AllowedSecretSamples to PushScanPolicy and filter valueHits on request body writes (filePath == "") when AllowedSecretSamples is populated, while keeping file and blob writes unconditionally blocked.
- services/eri/pkg/githubproxy: Add allowedSecretSamples helper loading shared secrets on matching allowlisted routes, wire into scanAPIWrite for non-file payloads, and verify route-scoped webhook config forwarding alongside comment and file write rejections.

author: sebastienrousseau
body:
This PR records every connector registration in the audit log (FR-10) and adds a gate that fails the build when `Cargo.lock` gains a third-party crate.

Registrations were the gap in the audit trail, and from this release new capabilities are built here rather than taken from new dependencies.

## Highlights ⭐️

* **Every connector registration is audited**: accepted, refused or failed, each is a `registration` entry in the hash-chained log with the SPIFFE ID the certificate proves, the one the frame claims, the routes and domains, the peer as a pseudonym and the error id when refused. `audit export` maps it to an OCSF Authentication event (class 3002). Only connections past mutual TLS reach a decision, so a source without a certificate cannot write to the log.
* **Which statement admitted a connector**: an admission by passmcp attestation records the SHA-256 of the statement it used, closing ADR 0009's follow-up.
* **Dependencies only go down**: `.dependency-baseline` lists the 97 third-party crates in `Cargo.lock`; `scripts/deps-baseline.sh` fails `cargo xtask ci` when one is added or a listed one is gone (`~/Code/AGENTS.md` section 11, sebastienrousseau/standards#23).
* **Moved out**: QUIC, HTTP/3 and the Kubernetes operator. `quinn` and `h3` would add 20 crates and `kube` more; QUIC waits for an ADR on an in-house design, and the operator is planned in-house for 0.0.20.

## What's Changed

* `feat: audit connector registrations` by @sebastienrousseau
* `build: gate new third-party dependencies` by @sebastienrousseau
* `chore: version 0.0.18 and its changelog` by @sebastienrousseau
* `docs: re-render the demo for 0.0.18` by @sebastienrousseau

## Validation

* `cargo xtask ci`: all 13 checks pass, including the new dependency check (97 crates, none new) and complexity at 0 offenders.
* The two tests in `crates/tw-gateway/tests/registration_audit.rs` failed before the change (no entry written) and pass after; so does the attestation-digest test in `tests/attestation.rs`. Removing the refused-path record, or recording no digest, turns them red again. The log with a registration entry verifies offline.
* `scripts/deps-baseline.sh` fails when a locked crate is missing from the baseline and when the baseline lists one no longer locked.
* Measured, not added: `quinn` 0.11.12 with the aws-lc-rs backend leaves 14 crates no imported cargo-vet audit covers, 20 new crates in all; `tokio`'s `signal` feature would add `signal-hook-registry`, so graceful shutdown on a signal stays open.
* `make demo` re-rendered the GIF; its first frame shows `tunnelward 0.0.18`.
* Not done: the Helm and Java jobs run in CI only for this PR (no chart or SDK code changed beyond the version).

## Checksums

SHA-256 of the artifacts produced by `cargo build --release --locked -p tunnelward` on this branch (aarch64-apple-darwin):

```text
4eca8b542d47c3fdd63c3db4bc754caeb994915219ea95bc55e1f9bcedc5c379  target/release/tunnelward
```

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/tunnelward/compare/v0.0.17...feat/v0.0.18

author: nlemoff
body:
## Driving
- **Keyboard steering:** raw key steering is now speed-sensitive. A held key winds on toward the angle for the car's full cornering grip at that speed (understeer included, plus a margin to overdrive the fronts); at walking pace it reaches full lock; in a slide it allows extra opposite lock. Pedals stay on/off. SN5 on Ridge now gets round in every keyboard test with assists on.
- **ABS assist:** the rears are held short of peak brake slip, and both rear wheels get the pressure the worse one can take (select-low), as real units do for stability.

## Views
- **First person:** the driver and onboard cameras show only the gloves on the wheel; the arms read as poles on some screens.
- **Full screen:** the cursor hides while driving once the mouse is still.

## Wheel
- **Force feedback:** the homepage's game iframe now allows `hid`, which WebHID force feedback needs. There's also a **Test** button and a clearer error message when the browser blocks the request.
- **Setup codes:** a setup code copies the wheel bindings, rotation and FFB settings as text; pasting it back restores them in any browser.

## Site
- **Refresh-friendly deploys:** the game iframe URL now carries a per-deploy version, so updates show up on a normal refresh.

## Summary
Phase 3 backend for contracts: seeded and custom categories, contracts CRUD with a computed schedule, an upcoming-events endpoint, a pure schedule service, and shared Money types in `core/money.py` (HEM-019 and HEM-023 reuse them). Migration 0006, OpenAPI and TS client regenerated.

## How to test
- `cd api && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check . && uv run mypy src && uv run pytest` (with `DATABASE_URL` set so the db tests run; CI does this)
- `npm run gen:api` leaves no diff.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Migration 0006 in schema `app`: `categories` (system seed plus per-space, unique keys per scope), `contracts` with checks
- [x] Categories GET/POST/DELETE; system and in-use deletes are 409
- [x] Contracts CRUD, cursor pagination, filters category/status/member_user_id, computed `schedule`
- [x] `GET /contracts/upcoming?days=` (1..366), sorted events payment/renewal/notice_deadline
- [x] Pure schedule service with `as_of`, month-end clamping, end dates, auto-renew rollover, notice deadlines
- [x] Validation: ISO-4217 currency (shared `Currency`), amount > 0 within minor units, end >= start, category and member must belong to the space (422)
- [x] Every route uses `require_space_member()`; non-members 404; foreign ids 404 or 422
- [x] Money is Decimal, serialised as strings; shared `Money`/`MoneyBase` in core
- [x] Tests: schedule table, money, space isolation, cross-space ids, problem+json, pagination
- [x] TS client regenerated

## PM scope additions (HEM-017 design)
Categories have a display `name` (seeded English names; custom `name` 1..60, `key` derived from it when omitted). Upcoming events carry `date`, `type`, `contract_id`, `contract_name`, and `amount` as `{amount, currency}`.

body:
Refs Kosinkadink/comfy-vibe-station#1473
Owner thread: https://ampcode.com/threads/T-01a21c37-17bc-732e-8d67-f9001a1ac647

Editors and media controls now use the configured node details cutoff (30% by default), rather than a second 75% gate. Below the cutoff, editor pins disappear with their panels. Media controls scale with their node so they remain contained and usable at low zoom. Output paging and 3D actions follow the same threshold.

## Evidence

On 270K-Plus1L, CPU, 2026-11-27: the original head reproduced the empty curve panel at 71%. The regression exercises curve point dragging and saved target edits at 75%, 71%, 50%, 31% and 30%; media seeking, audio playback and video mute at 71%, 50% and 31%; disappearance at 29%; and changing the configured cutoff. All seven media-overlay browser cases pass.

Twenty open curve editors plus one save editor at 40%: 240 pan/zoom animation frames per run, discard 30 warmup frames, three runs before and after. Median frame interval was 16.7 ms in every run; p95 was 16.7/16.8/16.7 ms before and after. Mounted editors increased from 0 to 21. This browser measurement detected no frame interval regression.

The changed surfaces retain existing ProductButton/ProductSlider and editor primitives. Compared media controls with the adjacent in-node save target and curve editor; both now scale inside their node instead of clipping fixed-size controls. No new host control or primitive is introduced.

Reviewed the complete change and consumers of the removed threshold: no findings. Existing gallery fixtures retain their explicit 75% view, rather than defining a second product cutoff. Coordination with the automatic-details owner is recorded on both wrapper issues.

## Validation

- Fast format, lint, types and unit-subset checks pass.
- Native startup passes against the pinned backend, connected with 74 schemas and no page errors, using isolated lane state and CPU.
- Seven media-overlay browser cases pass, including the new regression (which fails on the unchanged head).
- Whole unit suite passes (6,195 tests passed, 22 existing skips); production build passes. Hosted exact-head checks and independent verification are still required before landing.
- Dark screenshots rendered and inspected, and sent to design before head freeze.

author: rafjtb
body:
## Problème
Pour décider quelle app construire, il faut voir quels **besoins précis** sont les plus demandés, et où. Il n'existait encore aucun outil pour ça.

## Ce qui change
Ce prototype est uniquement front-end, avec des **données fictives** (la mention « DÉMO : données fictives » reste toujours visible).

- **Globe 3D** (MapLibre GL JS 6, projection globe), avec les contours de pays Natural Earth stockés en local. Aucune clé d'API.
  - Rotation automatique lente, qui s'arrête à la première interaction. Bouton « Vue monde ».
  - 5 pays colorés selon le nombre de demandes, avec une légende. Les autres pays sont gris (« Données insuffisantes »).
  - Au survol : nom du pays, demandes, besoin le plus demandé. Au clic : zoom animé et top 10 du pays.
- **Liste** : top 10 mondial ou par pays, tri par score ou par nombre de demandes, accès aux 32 besoins sans passer par le globe.
- **Fiche d'un besoin** :
  - score sur 100 avec le détail du calcul (douleur 25 %, croissance 20 %, faiblesse de la concurrence 20 %, disposition à payer 20 %, faisabilité 15 %) ;
  - volume et évolution, avec les dates comparées et les volumes avant → après ;
  - graphique quotidien ;
  - messages et solutions existantes (fictifs) ;
  - pays concernés, mis en évidence sur le globe.
- **Filtres** catégorie et période (7, 30 ou 90 jours), appliqués partout. **Recherche** de besoins et de pays (Ctrl K).
- **Données** : `src/data/demo-needs.json` est généré par un script avec une graine fixe. Tous les chiffres sont calculés à partir des séries quotidiennes (`src/domain/aggregate.ts`). Pour brancher une vraie source, il suffit de remplacer `src/data/source.ts`.
- **Mobile** utilisable (fiche en volet par le bas), `prefers-reduced-motion` respecté, message clair si WebGL est indisponible.

## Point technique
MapLibre 6 charge son « worker » par une URL que Vite n'inclut pas dans la build : le globe fonctionnait en dev mais pas en production. Le worker est maintenant importé explicitement (`?url` + `setWorkerUrl`), et le rendu en production a été vérifié.

## Tests
- `npm test` : 9/9. Couvre le score, ses pondérations et la cohérence des chiffres entre le globe, la liste, la fiche et le graphique.
- `npm run e2e` : 11/11, deux fois de suite. Couvre la mention démo, la liste complète, la concordance liste/fiche, les pays, les filtres, la recherche, le survol et le clic sur le globe, l'arrêt de la rotation, le mode « réduire les animations », WebGL absent, axe sans violation et la fiche mobile.
- `npm run build` : OK.

## Limites connues
- Un trait fin apparaît sur deux parallèles du globe avec le rendu 3D logiciel du serveur de test. Il reste à vérifier sur un vrai GPU.
- Le zoom sur un pays est un peu serré en 1920 × 1080.
