author: purnimaraj864-star
body:
## Summary

Fixes #3713 — the `everestctl settings rbac validate` command showed the "policy syntax error" prefix twice when the underlying error was itself wrapped with `errPolicySyntax`.

### Root Cause

`errors.Join(errPolicySyntax, innerErr)` joins errors with newlines. The CLI then converts newlines to ` - `. When `innerErr` is also an `errors.Join(errPolicySyntax, ...)` result (which happens for the `newKubeOrFileEnforcer` error path and others), the message becomes:

```
policy syntax error - policy syntax error - unknown resource name 'bogus-resource'
```

### Fix

Deduplicate consecutive identical parts after splitting on newlines, so the message appears only once:

**Before:**
```
❌ Invalid
policy syntax error - policy syntax error - unknown resource name 'bogus-resource'
```

**After:**
```
❌ Invalid
policy syntax error - unknown resource name 'bogus-resource'
```

### Changes

- `commands/settings/rbac/validate.go`: deduplicate consecutive identical message parts before joining with ` - `

author: miky-btc
body:
**LIN-4 — Ship writes only links it can read back** (project Links). Ship issue `30851:b38fd268…:c7713df7-2cab-4a60-80c2-1f0a0f2ba591`.

Nothing a person sees changes: Copy link on an issue, a project and a topic still gives `https://ship.estiva.app/<word>/<slug>-<id>`, but it now comes from the shared writer (`@estiva-app/interop` `fileUrlOf`, the code Peek, Leaf and the agent write with), and Ship no longer writes a link for an id no file can have.

## What changed

- **`src/lib/fileLinks.ts` (new).** Ship's own page paths are built with the shared `filePathOf` and Ship's page words (`project`, `issue`, `topic`); an id that is not a random lowercase uuid gets no path. `linkWordsOf` gives the words a link is handed out with: the shared writer's, read off the manifests, minus any word that is one of Ship's own pages (`app`, `o`, `projects`, `issues`, `topics`, `folder`), or a page word claimed for another kind. Peek drops its own words the same way, after the LIN-3 security review. `dOf` / `fileIdOfAddress` read an address's id whole, colons included.
- **`src/api/fileLinks.ts` (new).** Reads the words once, off the same `kind:31990` read the hand-off already makes (`declaredManifests`). `fileUrl()` is what Copy link waits on, and `useLinkWords()` serves render.
- **Router.** `href` builds project, issue and topic paths through `pagePathOf`, so an odd id's route is Ship's home rather than a file path that opens nothing. `parse` reads a ref only when its uuid is a file id (version 4), so a made-up id is not read as some other file.
- **Copy link** (issue, project, topic) uses `copyFileLink` → `fileUrl`. **Open in Peek** on a topic uses the shared writer with the manifests' words. A space sent on to Peek waits for them, so it lands on the short link rather than `/o/`.
- Every place that split an address by hand (`split(':')[2]` in `topicLinks`, `topics`, `referenceLink`, `FolderPage`; the uuid-tail read in `App.tsx`) now uses `dOf` / `fileIdOfAddress`.
- interop `^0.119` → `^0.120`.

## Load cost

One `kind:31990` read per tab: 4 events, 17,305 bytes on production (read as the agent on 27 Nov). It runs after the workspace is drawn, so a cold open does not wait on it. It is the same shared promise the hand-off and link cards already use, so on a page that draws a link card it is not a second read. There is no live-update read.

## Tests

- `router.property.test.ts`: made-up ids get no file path and never read back as another file; a pasted path with a non-v4 uuid opens no file. Both fail on `main`'s router and pass here. `dArb` is now a v4 uuid, the only kind a file can have.
- `lib/fileLinks.test.ts`: Ship's manifest gives `/issue/…` and `/project/…`; before the manifests are read a link is `/o/naddr…`; a newer manifest giving issues `projects`, `project`, `topics` or `app` does not move the link there; odd ids get no link; an id with a colon is read whole. Removing either filter in `linkWordsOf` fails a test (checked by mutation).
- Fixtures in `TopicPage.test`, `FileTopics.test` and `App.test` that used ids no file can have (`p1`, `w`) now use v4 uuids, or are read whole.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run` (150 files, 1,323 tests), `npm run test:scripts`, `npm run lint` (0 errors; 16 warnings, all in files this PR does not touch, or on lines it does not touch), `npm run lint:rules`, `npm run build`.

Production probe before merge, using this branch's `linkWordsOf` against the live manifests: project → `/project/example-title-<id>`, issue → `/issue/…`, topic → `/topic/…`, document → `/document/…`.

## Not filed

- Ship's `buildIssue` / `buildProject` still take any id; the relay refuses an odd one with `bad-file-id`. This is already in the project's Later list. Refusing it here would mean rewriting about 30 made-up ids in four `scripts/` tests.

## Architecture

Matches [Links](https://docs.estiva.app/architecture/links.html): Ship moves onto the shared writer.

author: jdatcmd
body:
Fixes #2198

## What was wrong

A read over `http://` or `https://` failed when the server had closed a kept-alive connection and answered the client's next request on it with a reset (RST). The reader stopped with:

```
ERROR:  columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer
```

or, over TLS, `columnar: TLS read from "..." failed`. A clean end of file (EOF) in the same place was already retried once on a new connection. A reset was not: in `os_fill` (`objstore/columnar_objstore_module.c`), the plain-socket branch returned false only when `recv` returned 0, and the TLS branch only on `SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN` or a `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` with `errno == 0`. Every other error, `ECONNRESET` among them, raised 08006. `os_request` retries only on a false return. The TLS branch had the same shape, and the tests below show it fails the same way.

## The fix

`os_fill` takes a new argument, `staleOk`. With it, `ECONNRESET` returns false, as EOF does:

- plain socket: `recv` fails with `ECONNRESET`;
- TLS: `SSL_read` gives `SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` with `errno == ECONNRESET`.

Only `os_read_head` passes `staleOk`, and only while no byte of the response head is staged (`avail == 0`). There, false already means "the connection died before a status byte", and the callers retry once on a kept-alive connection and raise on a fresh one. The retry count does not change.

The other three callers pass false:

- `os_read_exact` (a body with a Content-Length);
- `os_read_line` (chunk framing);
- the body reader that reads until the server closes.

So a reset after any byte of a response head or body still raises `could not read from ...: Connection reset by peer` (or the TLS message). A body that ends at connection close is never read short because of a reset, and a half-read answer is never retried.

One case to know about: after an interim 1xx head has been read in full, nothing of the next head is staged. A reset there is retried, exactly as a clean EOF there already was before this change (#2156's `i103c` test depends on that EOF case).

## The tests

The shared fixture server, `test/objstore_http_server.py`, gets five path modes. Both the plain and the TLS suites use them. "Reset" means a close with `SO_LINGER` 0, so the kernel sends RST at once with no FIN first.

| mode | what the server does |
| --- | --- |
| `/rstka/` | answers the first request on a connection; on the next, waits until its bytes arrive, then resets without reading them. The client has sent its request and has read nothing back, so its read fails with `ECONNRESET` every time. No timing decides it. |
| `/closeka/` | closes at once after every answer, with no half-close, as the issue describes. The next request meets a FIN or a reset, whichever the timing gives. |
| `/rsthead/` | answers a later request on a connection with `HTTP/1.1 206 Parti`, then resets. |
| `/rstbody/` | answers a later ranged GET with its head and half its body, then resets. |
| `/rstall/` | answers HEAD; resets every GET once read, so the retry on a new connection is reset too. |

New checks. Each has the same name in the shell suite and its pytest twin.

`test/objstore_http_read.sh` and `test/pytest/test_objstore_http_read.py`, arm C:

- `C: 30 reads from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed`
- `C: 30 reads from a server that closes at once after each answer all succeed`
- `C: a reset after part of a status line is refused` (08006, `Connection reset by peer`)
- `C: a reset after part of a body is refused` (08006, `Connection reset by peer`)
- `C: a server that resets every GET is refused after one retry` (08006, `failed before a response`, with `statement_timeout` 20 s as the bound)
- `C: and that GET was sent twice` (the request log holds exactly 2 GETs)

`test/objstore_tls_read.sh` and `test/pytest/test_objstore_tls_read.py`, new arm F:

- `F: 30 reads over TLS from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed`
- `F: a reset over TLS after part of a status line is refused` (08006, `columnar: TLS read from "<url>" failed`)

The 30 reads run in one plpgsql function, `pgc_reads(url, n)`. It catches each read's error in its own subtransaction and returns `ok=N failed=M`, plus the last error when a read failed.

### Red on main (75f3b9d6), verbatim

Shell, PG18:

```
FAIL  C: 30 reads from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed: got [no error: ok=0 failed=30 last=08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29988/rstka/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer] want [no error: ok=30 failed=0]
FAIL  C: 30 reads from a server that closes at once after each answer all succeed: got [no error: ok=12 failed=18 last=08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29988/closeka/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer] want [no error: ok=30 failed=0]
PASS  C: a reset after part of a status line is refused
PASS  C: a reset after part of a body is refused
FAIL  C: a server that resets every GET is refused after one retry: got [08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29988/rstall/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer] want [08006: failed before a response]
FAIL  C: and that GET was sent twice: got [1] want [2]
accounting: 103 passed + 4 failed + 0 unrunnable + 0 skipped = 107
FAIL  F: 30 reads over TLS from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed: got [ok=0 failed=30 last=08006: columnar: TLS read from "https://127.0.0.1:31386/rstka/pgc-bucket/fixture.parquet" failed] want [ok=30 failed=0]
PASS  F: a reset over TLS after part of a status line is refused
accounting: 30 passed + 1 failed + 0 unrunnable + 0 skipped = 31
```

pytest, PG18:

```
E           AssertionError: C: 30 reads from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed: got 'no error: ok=0 failed=30 last=08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29830/rstka/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer' want 'no error: ok=30 failed=0'
E           AssertionError: C: 30 reads from a server that closes at once after each answer all succeed: got 'no error: ok=6 failed=24 last=08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29830/closeka/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer' want 'no error: ok=30 failed=0'
E           AssertionError: C: a server that resets every GET is refused after one retry: got '08006: columnar: could not read from "http://127.0.0.1:29830/rstall/fixture.parquet": Connection reset by peer' want '08006: failed before a response'
E           AssertionError: C: and that GET was sent twice: got 1 want 2
E           AssertionError: F: 30 reads over TLS from a server that resets each kept-alive connection all succeed: got 'ok=0 failed=30 last=08006: columnar: TLS read from "https://127.0.0.1:29848/rstka/pgc-bucket/fixture.parquet" failed' want 'ok=30 failed=0'
5 failed, 133 passed in 42.86s
```

PG17 on main's code gives the same five reds in each harness (`closeka`: `ok=8 failed=22`). `closeka` reproduces the issue's report (`ok=6 reset=24` there). Its rate depends on timing, so `rstka` is the deterministic check. The three refusal checks (`rsthead`, `rstbody`, and the TLS `rsthead`) pass on main, because main already raises there. They are guards against a fix that goes too far, and mutants M1 and M4 below turn them red.

## Mutants

Each mutant: `make clean`, build, md5 of `objstore/pgcolumnar_objstore.so`, then both suites in both harnesses on PG18.

| # | mutant | `.so` md5 | red in shell | red in pytest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| - | the fix (control) | `02d66a4dcebb323eb3ac64ed3b8e7218` | none | none |
| - | main's code 75f3b9d6 | `d880193a8794859b640dd16f71427f24` | 5 (above) | 5 (above) |
| M1 | `os_read_head` passes `staleOk` true even with part of a head staged | `299b2df78814d2f765c4b1fbac24dd90` | `C: a reset after part of a status line is refused` (got `closed mid-response`); `F: a reset over TLS after part of a status line is refused` | the same two

body:
## Problem

- A Postgres connection that drops mid-query with `SSL SYSCALL error: EOF detected` opens a new error tracking issue, even though Temporal retries the activity ([inbox report](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/01a21cbf-b334-75e7-9b22-84a0a4d8faf6)).
- The transient check matches other dropped-connection messages, but not this one.

## Changes

- The transient check now matches `consuming input failed: SSL SYSCALL error`. These errors go to the worker's transient warning log, not to error tracking.
- The connect-time form (`connection failed: ... SSL SYSCALL error`) stays reportable, because a TLS failure at connect can be a persistent misconfiguration.
- `process_chat_agent_activity` gets `@close_db_connections`, so it discards a stale pooled connection before its first ORM loads.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** New cases in `test_is_transient_db_error_by_message` cover the mid-query message as a Django error, a psycopg error and a wrapped cause. Without the marker, those 3 cases fail. Negative cases keep the connect-time form and the bare text reportable.

Not run: the database-backed tests in `posthog/temporal/tests/ai/test_chat_agent_activity.py`, because this sandbox has no Postgres. The decorator is a no-op under `settings.TEST`.

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

author: dhensby
body:
What this does:

The README says that each known error has a `code`. These had none:

- `transaction.begin(level)` with a level that is not in `sql.ISOLATION_LEVEL` (`TransactionError: Invalid isolation level.`), on both drivers. It now has the code `EARGS`.
- The pool config error for `options.useColumnNames` (`MSSQLError`). It now has the code `EARGS`.
- A tedious login that fails with an `AggregateError`. tedious does this for `EFEDAUTH`, when a token credential cannot give a token. An `AggregateError` has no message or code of its own, so the `ConnectionError` had an empty message and no code. It now takes the code and message of the first error, which says what failed. The `AggregateError` stays the `originalError`, so its other errors, which say why, can still be read.

The README lists the new codes. It also says that `begin()` with a callback throws the isolation level error rather than passing it to the callback, which is what it has done since 6.x.

The local server does not do Microsoft Entra authentication, so the EFEDAUTH case is tested with a tedious connection whose `connect()` fails with the `AggregateError` that tedious 19.2.2 and 20.4.3 make (`connection.js`, `performSentLogin7WithFedAuth`).

Two commits: the codes for this library's own errors, then the tedious `AggregateError`.

None.

author: tmaeder
body:
## Problem

The grouped search overview (`groupBy: "type"`) orders sections from a separate "mixed" ranking call that is allowed to fail. When it fails, `orderGroups` orders every section by `total`, so a cold `berlin` opens on Venues (its biggest section) instead of City. This is the flake in `e2e/search-overview-and-meet-signin.spec.ts` › "groups results by type, includes news for a bare city…" (failed once on 2026-11-27 against build `2666016c2`, "Received: search-section-venue", then passed 4/4).

## Decision: option 1, improve the fallback

A cold query is exactly when the fallback fires, and opening "berlin" on venues reads as wrong to a person, not only to the spec. Loosening the spec would have needed a new response signal and left the page wrong. The per-type hits are already in hand, so the fix needs no extra request.

## Change

- `orderGroups(mixed, groups, query)`: among types with **no** position in the mixed ranking, a section whose first hit's title or alias equals the query leads, a city ahead of any other type. Then total, then `GROUP_TYPES` order as before.
- When the mixed call works, ordering is unchanged: a type in the mixed ranking always outranks one that isn't, exact title or not (tested).
- Only the first hit is checked. Group hits go through `prioritizeQueryMatches` first, so an exact title in a section is already at the front.
- `rank.ts` exports `matchesQueryExactly`, the same title/alias test `prioritizeQueryMatches` uses (now shared), so the two cannot disagree on what "exact" means.
- `orderGroups` stays pure; `query` defaults to `""`, which matches nothing.
- Plan doc `docs/plans/2026-11-27-search-overview-by-type.md` updated to describe the fallback.

## Tests

- `workers/search-proxy`: `npx vitest run` gives 208/208, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- New worker-level case: mixed call fails and `berlin` → `city, venue, event, news`, with `orderFallback: true`. A second case checks the mixed ordering still wins when the call succeeds.
- New `orderGroups` unit cases: city beats larger sections; case, whitespace and alias matching; city beats another exact-title type; a non-city exact title is lifted; only the first hit counts; no match or no query falls back to total.
- Mutation check: disabling the exact-match tiebreak fails 5 tests. Collapsing the city preference fails 1.

## Not done here

No Cloudflare credentials in this session, so I did not run `wrangler deploy`. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys `workers/search-proxy` on merge to `main`. After that, run the e2e against production:

```bash
npx playwright test e2e/search-overview-and-meet-signin.spec.ts --trace off
```

That spec only exercises the fallback when the mixed call actually times out, so a green run proves the normal path. The unit tests are the evidence for the fallback path.

moritzbrantner
body:
Refs #2103 (owner decisions 2026-11-27: curation placement is plumbing; recurring review defects become mechanical where possible).

## Problem
"Reaching the root" in `truth orphans` and the placement gate can be inflated. Results reach through loop-backs, through transcriptions (with or without rule (d) closure), or as backing results of bare-premise strength registrations, and reviewers had to establish this by hand in every PR. Separately, a result flagged by the frontier's transcription heuristic without a declared kind (#2156's `b8b4e9f5`) was caught only in review.

## Change
1. **Placement provenance.**
   - `Frontier::root_edges` exports the edges of the existing route-aware reaching walk.
   - `truth orphans` walks them upward from each reaching result's conclusion, never entering one of the result's own premises.
   - Categories, in order; the first that applies wins:
     - `loop_back`: no route avoids the result's premises (`reentered_premises`).
     - `registration_bare`: the result backs a `strengthens` registration, and every premise is bare and unclosed.
     - `transcription_self`: the result is itself a transcription and contributes at most rule (d) closure.
     - `substantive`: a route of verified non-transcription arguments exists.
     - `transcription_closed`: some route enters only transcriptions whose premises are all closed. Rule (d) carries closure to the root, but no independent warrant.
     - `transcription_open`: every route enters a transcription with an open premise, which carries neither closure nor warrant.
     - `unverified_route`.
     - `refutation_support`.
   - Each entry carries one shortest witnessing `route`. Each transcription argument on it reports `declared` and `premises_closed`.
   - Output: per result in `--json` (`reaching_results[].provenance`, and the gate's `judged[].provenance`), and as counts in both text reports. Documented in docs/corpus-model.md, "Result placement" → "Placement provenance".
   - Inputs read from a report JSON carry no walk edges, so they get no provenance rather than false loop-backs.
2. **Undeclared transcriptions.** The gate *warns*, without failing, on any result at the head that is heuristic-flagged (`single_application` or `assembly`) without a declared kind, unless it was already flagged-undeclared at the base.

The gate's pass/fail semantics are unchanged.

## Current main (`94e8901cf`)
These counts describe placement plumbing, not progress. Of 1064 reaching results:

| Category | Results |
| --- | --- |
| `substantive` | 712 |
| `transcription_self` | 153 |
| `transcription_closed` | 89 |
| `registration_bare` | 52 |
| `loop_back` | 27 |
| `refutation_support` | 18 |
| `transcription_open` | 13 |
| `unverified_route` | 0 |

A result is `transcription_closed` when *some* route uses only rule-(d)-closed transcriptions, even if its shortest route passes an open one. That is why the split differs from a shortest-route tally (77/25).

## #2156, against its squash base `03c3fd7ad` (main's parent of `94e8901cf`)
18 results newly reach the root: 4 new results and 14 pre-existing ones.

| Category | Results |
| --- | --- |
| `substantive` | `dedd529a`, the classical-equivalence diagnostic, a structurally real derivation of `cdf897a8` |
| `transcription_closed` | `ec3198b4`, `6b75bdf8`, `6971850e`, through `5b3b935c` (undeclared heuristic `single_application`, premises closed); `60df7e87`, through the declared `3249b20c` |
| `transcription_open` | `f5e33f03`, `4f0c026d`, through the declared `4418bfa1`, whose premises are open |
| `transcription_self` | `b8b4e9f5`, `54feb72b`, `d2e4867c`, `2371b373` |
| `loop_back` | `76dc5abc`, `6d90f126`, `43fdb2ed`, `aa4797d1` |
| `registration_bare` | `601022e8`, `9e38fb0b`, `62947463` |

`0f3d17c2` (`godNamesDescribedFromSumma`, the result of `5b3b935c`) is a two-premise chain that the heuristic flags only because its last step is `exact hBridge …`. The tool takes the frontier's kinds as given, so it reports the three results it carries as closed through a transcription.

## False-positive analysis
- **Provenance.** Mechanical over the frontier's own walk, transcription kinds and closure, so it inherits only the heuristic's false positives (a more conservative category). I inspected 4 `loop_back` and 4 `registration_bare` hits; each loop-back route re-enters a premise, and each registration is a one-premise weakening from a bare premise.
- **Undeclared transcriptions.** Main has 59 heuristic-flagged results with no declared kind (50 `single_application`, 9 `assembly`). I read all 59 proofs:
  - about 8 (≈14%) are clear false positives: real multi-step proofs such as `exactRival`, `noSelfMotion` and `nonmutualOfAcyclic`;
  - about 10 more are borderline chains;
  - no record can declare "not a transcription".
  
  So this is a **warning**, not a gate.

## Validation
- `cargo test --locked -p truth` passes (333 lib tests and the integration tests). New tests:
  - `provenance_separates_substantive_transcription_loop_back_and_bare_registration`, which covers `transcription_self`, `transcription_closed` with a declared transcription, and `transcription_open` with an undeclared heuristic one;
  - `the_gate_warns_on_new_undeclared_heuristic_transcriptions`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- `scripts/preflight.sh --base origin/main` passes after merging main.

Premise delta: none (tooling only).

  - Add `CanonicalName` / `NormKey` prefix stripping (`person:`, `project:`, `system:`, `repo:`, `task:`, etc.) across `Seed`, `find`, `Resolve`, and `SameNameCandidates`.
  - Normalize `collaborates_with` edges as undirected (`min(s,o) -> max(s,o)`) and stop writing `about` and `same_circle`.
- **Three-tier entity disambiguation & reversible merge** (`internal/graph/resolve.go`):
  - Export `graph.ResolveAndMerge(ctx, st, m) (*graph.MergeReport, error)` (runs Tier 1 deterministically with 0 model calls when `m == nil`).
  - Tier 1: strip `type:` prefixes, archive legacy `task` nodes and `about`/`same_circle` edges, deduplicate bidirectional `collaborates_with` edges, merge canonical-key homographs, contact-table anchored duplicates, and unambiguous 2-char Chinese `person` short names.
  - Tier 2: batch residual fuzzy prefix/containment or `>= 2` shared-neighbor pairs (`<= 30` per batch) to `model.Small` (`proposal="auto-haiku-v04"`).
  - All merges go through `Builder.Merge` with `MergeRec` and reversible `Builder.Unmerge`.
- **Dual lifecycle & deterministic decay** (`internal/entry/skeleton.go`, `internal/entry/state.go`):
  - Export `entry.IsEphemeral`, 14d recall exit / 30d auto-dormant decay, generic HR/nameless people noise filtering, and 45d demote / 60d auto-dormant decay for `ops_runbook` entries.
- **Consumer adaptation** (`internal/people/*`, `internal/recall/*`):
  - Consume merged canonical entities, skip archived `task`/`about` and expired `ephemeral` / generic HR noise, and apply `ops_runbook` decay weights.

## Verification
- Synthetic unit tests added for prefix normalization, whitelist, undirected `collaborates_with`, Tier 1/2 `ResolveAndMerge` + `Unmerge`, 14/30d ephemeral decay, 45/60d ops decay, and people/recall consumer adaptation.
- Offline Tier 1 dry-run (0 LLM calls) verified against a local read-only snapshot copy.
- Verified via `sj-wsl fast` CI gate (no version bump, no catalog PR).

author: alsanvolkan
body:
Closes #1594.

## What the measurement says

Run `20261125T152000Z-ceaa36af` (homesrv, 25 Nov 2026 16:20-16:36 Amsterdam, ops `job_runs2`):
```
counts {"steps": {"fetch": 977.187, "build": 0.31, "check": 0.106, "parquet": 0.054, "swap": 0.704, "start": 0.025}}
params {"chain": "20261125T152000Z-ceaa36af", "reread": ["debt.note"]}
```
`asker.SLICE_S` is 900 s and `fetch` took 977 s. `company.profile` is registered first and spent it (raw `...ceaa36af.company.profile.json.gz`: 2 rows, both `ok`, 3 calls). `debt.note` is registered last and was asked with nothing left (raw `...ceaa36af.debt.note.json.gz`: 169 rows, all `no_text`, calls sum **0**). `--plan --reread debt.note` on the same data: **316** companies would be asked.

## The change

- `reads._share_started(started, now, limit, share)`: when a question finds the run's slice spent, its `started` moves forward so it keeps `limit / len(QUESTIONS)` of it. A run with time left passes its own `started` through, so the slice still bounds the common case and the registration order (and with it the dependency between questions) is untouched. Worst case a run now asks for `limit + (n-1) * share` instead of `limit`; with the three questions in the registry that is 25 min instead of 15.
- One consequence worth naming: with a single registered question `share == limit`, so that question's budget starts at the question rather than at the run, and the planning seconds before it no longer count against it.
- `base.py`: `finish_run` now stores the note in `counts` next to the step times. It was written only to the dataset's newest check row and the last 20 finished requests, so `N left for the next run` could not be read a day later — the reason this took a night to find.
- `asker.ask`'s docstring said the slice is "the run's and not each question's"; updated, since that is exactly what changes.

## Tests

`test_the_question_registered_last_keeps_its_share_of_the_slice` covers `_share_started`: the spent-slice case (the share survives) and the time-left case (unchanged). It fails if `max` becomes `min` or `+ share` is dropped.

The three existing slice tests stay green by construction: each registers one question, where `share == limit`, and their `SLICE_S = -1.0` keeps the slice spent (`now - max(started, now) = 0 > -1`).

**red-on-base: not checked** — this box runs no pytest (repo rule). CI on the head SHA is the evidence; mutation check not done.

## Not in this PR

The `no_text` rows still carry no reason (`debt_note.py` logs `why_skipped` and drops it), which is a separate change.

author: noobshole
body:
Adds `near-token-backing-v2`, which runs beside v1 as a trial from 1 December 2026. v1 stays the published grade and the only one put on NEAR.

**What v2 changes**
- Every classic and DCL pool on Rhea Finance is read from NEAR at one final block (9,024 classic pools, against the 3,175 in Rhea's list). The block is part of the sealed edition, and `index:verify --chain` reads it again from an archive node and checks the archived pools byte for byte. RPC calls fall back to other public endpoints when one refuses.
- Each edition lists every grade that changed since the previous sealed edition, with one reason: `price`, `money-out`, `money-in`, `price-and-money` or `method`. `inputs/backing-detail.json.gz` keeps the trusted tokens behind every point of the 24-hour history and each run's prices, so a reason is exact even when a grade comes from a run hours earlier. Where the detail does not reach back (the trial's first days), the reason is marked `estimated`. `index:verify --previous` recomputes the reasons from both editions' files.
- v2's first run starts from v1's backing history, so its first-day grades come from the same 24 hours.
- NEAR Intents dry quotes (what a $1,000 sale would fetch) sit beside the grades, outside the grade and the fingerprint. Rate limits are recorded as failed requests, not as missing routes.
- `GET /v1/index/near-tokens?methodology=near-token-backing-v2` serves the trial edition; an unknown methodology gets 400. `index:compare` writes the side-by-side file.

v1 editions are unchanged: same files, same fingerprints, and old editions still verify.

**Tested**
- Build, typecheck, lint; 255 API tests and 36 MCP tests.
- A six-day rehearsal on live NEAR data with the clock moved forward, every day verified with `--previous`, day 1 also with `--chain`. With NEAR's price cut by 25%, 22 grades fell and all were exactly `price`. When the price recovered and the low left the 24-hour window, the reasons were `price` for all 22, where the old estimate would have said `money-in`.
- The API on the local Workers runtime: v1 by default, the trial on request, 400 for an unknown methodology.

The robot side (the `build-v2` and `publish-v2` jobs) is a separate change in svalin-index.

author: kentarokamiyajp
body:
Corrects the OpenAI prices in `apis/llm_models.yaml` to OpenAI's published list ([#MIP-2372](task:3464)). GPT users were charged credits on prices up to 5x too high. `gpt-5.6-sol` is the one deliberate exception (below).

**Source:** [OpenAI API pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing), Standard tier, **read 2026-11-27**; cross-checked with the [Sol](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol), [Terra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra) and [Luna](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna) pages and the [prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching).

USD per 1M tokens, input / output / cached input / cache write:

| model | before | after | after, over 272K prompt tokens (new) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-5.6-luna | 1.00 / 6.00 / 0.10 / 0 | 0.20 / 1.20 / 0.02 / 0.25 | 0.40 / 1.80 / 0.04 / 0.50 |
| gpt-5.6-terra | 2.50 / 15.00 / 0.25 / 0 | 2.00 / 12.00 / 0.20 / 2.50 | 4.00 / 18.00 / 0.40 / 5.00 |
| gpt-5.6-sol | 5.00 / 30.00 / 0.50 / 0 | 5.00 / 30.00 / 0.50 / 6.25 | 10.00 / 45.00 / 1.00 / 12.50 |

`text-embedding-3-small` ($0.02) already matched.

⚠️ **Sol is not OpenAI's list price, on purpose** (Ken, 2026-11-27). The page lists a promotional $4 / $20 (long context $8 / $30) "until November 30, 2026" and gives no price for after. We keep the pre-promotion **$5 input / $30 output**, so Genos never charges less than OpenAI does once the promotion ends; members pay up to 25% (input) to 50% (output) over OpenAI's price until then. The other Sol rates are at the same level by OpenAI's own ratios: cached read 0.1x input ($0.50), 30-minute write 1.25x input ($6.25), over 272K prompt tokens 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output ($10 / $45 / $1.00 / $12.50).

**When OpenAI publishes Sol's new price, re-price it:** [#MIP-2446](task:3549).

**Also changed**
- `openai_client.py` set `cache_write_tokens` to 0 always, so a write rate would never have applied. It now reads `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` and takes it out of the ordinary input (each token billed once).
- Rate card label and the cap sizing comment. The caps themselves are unchanged.

**Not in the card** (we do not use them): Batch, Flex and Fast tiers, 12-hour cache writes, the 10% regional uplift.

**Verified:** affected test modules (324 tests, OK, 1 skipped); the whole suite in CI (all 3 shards green on `b7018f6c`); the pinned openai 2.5.0 SDK passes `cache_write_tokens` through.
**Not verified:** no live OpenAI call (paid). That Chat Completions counts writes inside `prompt_tokens` is documented for the Responses API only.

No refunds, no production change, no billed eval needed (nothing on `RETRIEVAL_PATHS`). Docs: [genos-docs #482](https://github.com/genos-tech/genos-docs/pull/482) (merged) and [genos-docs #484](https://github.com/genos-tech/genos-docs/pull/484) (the Sol correction: merge that first).

author: octomood
body:
## Зачем

Проверку `octo.page.run` (`page:script`) можно было обойти тривиально: `const f = window.fetch; f(...)`, `[].constructor.constructor('…')()`, `new Image()` с адресом из переменной, `const d = document; d.cookie`. Статический сканер такое не видит, а у изолированного мира не было своей CSP, поэтому запросы уходили куда угодно. Документация при этом обещала «блокируются в момент вызова» и «не получает доступ к cookie». Это пункт P0 №3 из разбора системы плагинов (main `548b2b6`), плюс P1 №4 — `image-set()` в CSS-фильтре.

## Что сделано

**1. Рантайм-граница для скриптов на странице** (`src/main/plugins/page-world.js`, новый файл):

- **Своя CSP изолированного мира** через `webFrame.setIsolatedWorldInfo`: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data: blob:; media-src data: blob:; font-src data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`. В итоге не работают `fetch`, XHR, WebSocket, EventSource, `sendBeacon`, `import()`, `new Image()` и шрифты с внешних адресов, а без `'unsafe-eval'` — `eval`, `Function` и `constructor.constructor`, как бы их ни вызывали.
- `setIsolatedWorldInfo` есть только у `webFrame`, поэтому CSP выдаёт preload страницы (`region-preload.js`, он и так единственный preload этого view). Он делает это при каждой загрузке документа для всех известных миров, до первого кода в них (`octo:plugin-worlds`, sync). Для мира, который появился позже, main сначала просит preload (`octo:plugin-world`) и ждёт ответа, а уже потом выполняет код. Порядок важен, и это проверено: fetch и картинки Chromium проверяет в момент запроса, а запрет `eval` V8 фиксирует при создании контекста мира.
- **Замки в мире плагина**, только в нём, сайт их не видит. `document.cookie` возвращает пустую строку. `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `indexedDB`, `cookieStore`, `caches` и `window.open` бросают ошибку. Нельзя создать `iframe/frame/object/embed/script/base/meta`, задать `on*`-атрибуты и адреса фреймов, вставить HTML через `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `DOMParser`, `document.write` и похожие методы. Нельзя добраться до `contentWindow`/`contentDocument`.
- **Fail-closed.** Признак готовности мира ставится, только если CSP действительно работает: проба `fetch('data:')` должна быть отклонена, а сети она не трогает. Обёртка `page.run` проверяет этот признак в том же вызове. Если политика не применилась, код плагина не выполняется, а вызов отклоняется с ошибкой. Если документ сменился между проверкой и запуском, мир готовится заново (одна повторная попытка).
- **Ошибки с настоящим текстом.** Electron заменяет текст любого исключения из мира на «Script failed to execute», поэтому раньше даже «Результат page.run больше 256 КБ» до плагина не доходил. Теперь обёртка возвращает ответ с одноразовым токеном, и плагин получает настоящее сообщение. Код, который возвращает Promise, работает как раньше, только размер результата теперь проверяется после его выполнения.
- `getMediaInfo`, `watch` и опрос наблюдателей тоже получают CSP до первого выполнения в мире (`prepareWorld`).

**2. CSS-фильтр** (`security.js`, `scanCss`, работает и в `validateCss`, и при установке пакета). Раньше пропускались внешние адреса в `image-set("https://…")`, `-webkit-image-set`, `src()`, адреса, записанные через CSS-экранирование (`u\72l(…)`, `ht\74 tp:`, `@\69mport`), `/\host` и `url(/**/https://…)`. Теперь каждый адрес в `url()`, `src()` и строках `image-set()` разрешён, только если это `data:`, `blob:` или относительный путь.

**3. Документация приведена к реальным гарантиям.** Затронуты `docs/plugins/README.md` (`page.run`, «Риск», «Безопасность», «Ограничения модели», FAQ, `injectCSS`), README.ru/README.md, описание права `page:script` в окне установки (11 локалей) и CHANGELOG (`## Не выпущено`).

## Before / After

Новый тест `test/plugin-page-world.spec.js` в живом Electron. Страница отдаёт максимально мягкую CSP (`default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'`), «чужой» сервер слушает другой порт. Все 10 обходов проходят статический сканер, это проверяется в самом тесте.

| Обход (проходит сканер) | main `548b2b6` | эта ветка |
|---|---|---|
| `const f = window.fetch; f(U)` | `"sent"`, запрос дошёл | `"blocked"` |
| `window['XMLHttp'+'Request']` | запрос дошёл | запроса нет |
| `navigator['send'+'Beacon']` | запрос дошёл | запроса нет |
| `new Image().src = U` | запрос дошёл | запроса нет |
| `[].constructor.constructor('return 40 + 2')()` | `42` | ошибка CSP `'unsafe-eval'` |
| `const d = document; d.cookie` | `"octo_test=secret"` | `""` |
| `window['local'+'Storage']` | доступен | «localStorage недоступно скриптам плагинов» |
| `document['create'+'Element']('iframe')` + `src` | запрос дошёл | «`<iframe>` недоступно…» |
| `body['inner'+'HTML'] = '<iframe src=…>'` | запрос дошёл | «Вставка HTML недоступно…» |
| `window['op'+'en'](U)` | открыто | «window.open недоступно…» |
| **Запросы на чужой сервер** | `/fetch /xhr /beacon /image /iframe /html` | **ни одного** |

Главный мир сайта не меняется: `document.cookie` и `fetch` страницы на месте (проверяется тестом). После перезагрузки страницы защита ставится заново: `fetch` заблокирован, `eval` запрещён с первого вызова.

## Решения и альтернативы

1. **CSP мира через preload страницы, а не только сканер.** Других способов нет. В main-процессе API для CSP мира отсутствует, а `webRequest` не отличает запрос мира плагина от запроса самой страницы. Второй preload у view быть не может, поэтому код добавлен в `region-preload.js`. Странице он по-прежнему ничего не отдаёт и принимает только миры в диапазоне плагинов (20000–79999) с origin `octo-plugin://`.
2. **Строгий `img-src data: blob:`.** Альтернатива: разрешить CDN TikTok, чтобы скрипт мог создавать картинки с них. Я выбрал строгий вариант: официальные плагины этого не используют, а новый хост в CSP мира — лишний канал. Ослабить можно точечно, если понадобится.
3. **Замки — защита от очевидного кода, а не граница**, и в документации это так и написано. Обходятся они через уже существующие фреймы страницы (`window[0]`). Граница — CSP мира.
4. **Fail-closed** вместо отката к старому поведению «только сканер», если защиту не удалось включить. Альтернатива молча снижала бы защиту.
5. **Относительные `url(/…)` в CSS разрешены**: они ведут на сам сайт, и такие стили могут быть у существующих плагинов. Запрещены только абсолютные адреса, кроме `data:` и `blob:`.
6. **Отдельное право `page:read`** для безопасного чтения (из разбора) **сюда не вошло**: это новое публичное API, ему нужен отдельный PR.

## Что остаётся (описано в документации)

CSP мира не действует на загрузки, которые Chromium приписывает самой странице: `url()` в стилях элементов, `<audio>`/`<video>`, переход уже существующих фреймов. Для них работает CSP сайта, то есть только хосты, которые разрешил TikTok. Это проверено на заголовке `www.tiktok.com`: `default-src` там длинный список хостов, `script-src` без `'unsafe-inline'`. Переход страницы на внешний адрес по-прежнему открывает системный браузер. Всё прочитанное плагин с `page:script` может отправить на свои `networkHosts`.

## Совместимость

Установленные плагины продолжают работать. Официальные `shelf` и `hello-octo` используют только `querySelector`, `textContent` и `setAttribute('data-…')`. `test/plugin-shelf.spec.js` проходит без изменений. Всё, что теперь запрещено в мире (`innerHTML`, cookie, хранилища, сеть, `eval`), уже отклонял сканер, кроме обходов.

## Проверка

- `npm run lint`: чисто. `npx prettier --check` по всем изменённым файлам: чисто.
- `npm test -- test/plugin-page-world.spec.js test/plugin-security.spec.js test/plugin-shelf.spec.js test/plugin-api.spec.js test/plugins.spec.js test/plugin-dev.spec.js test/plugin-sdk.spec.js`: 17/17.
- Полный `npm test` (затронут preload страницы, AGENTS §4): 108/108 passed (3.0m, Linux, Xvfb). Первый прогон выявил зависание: при нуле плагинов у `ipcMain` не было обработчика `octo:plugin-worlds`, и `sendSync` из preload вешал рендерер (55 падений). Исправле

## 内容

规格 008：从审核中学习与 AI 协助审核。只有规格，不含代码。

- [正文](docs/specs/008-review-learning-assist.md)
- [接口附录](docs/specs/008-review-learning-api-shapes.md)
- [路线图](docs/roadmap.md)：在 M4 与 M5 之间补一行

级别：L2（规格涉及迁移、AI 写入路径与审核流程、`dev.ps1`）。按任务要求，做到 ready 后停下，由主会话审过再合并。

## 设计要点

- **审核记忆**：
  - 新表 `ontology.review_memory`，每个本体最多 500 条。
  - 只在合并 `ai_extraction` 变更集时采集三类决定：拒绝、改名后接受、判为不同。
  - 识别时由代码护栏 M1–M3 挡住精确命中的项；相近的说法由提示词提醒（记忆行放在 text 里，英文规则放在新文件 `ai/memory_prompts.py`）。
  - 记忆为空时，提示词逐字节不变。
  - 用户能查看、删除（可撤销）、清空记忆。
- **拒绝理由**：可选，四个值，存在 `change_items.reject_reason`。
- **AI 预审**：
  - 规则检查加模型检查，覆盖类型、关系、属性三种变更项。
  - 结果存 `ai.review_assists`，不改变更项。
  - 按每项的指纹判断结果是否过期。
  - 不提供"接受全部建议"；批量接受高置信度项时排除有风险的项。
- **评测**：
  - 按 `expected.toml` 模拟审核人的场景，比较记忆开、关。
  - 目标：steel-industry 模型层面的再提比例相对下降至少 30%，审核人面前的再提比例为 0，类型召回下降不超过 0.02。
  - 付费评测每轮最多 5 次全量，最多 2 轮。

## 批次

| 批次 | 内容 | 级别 | 执行者 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 骨架与迁移 v0013、拒绝理由 | L2 | Codex + Claude 审 |
| 2 | 记忆采集与管理 | L2 | Codex + Claude 审 |
| 3 | 识别流水线使用记忆（与 2 并行） | L2 | Codex + Claude 审 |
| 4 | 记忆评测与 `dev.ps1` 开关 | L2 | Codex + Claude |
| 5 | 记忆界面、拒绝理由界面 | L1 | Codex |
| 6 | AI 预审后端 | L2 | Codex + Claude 审 |
| 7 | 预审界面 | L1 | Codex |
| 8 | 预审评测、e2e、文档 | L2 | Codex + Claude |

## 需要主会话确认

正文第 14 节"主会话已定的取舍"T1–T19，每条都写了推荐方案、备选和理由。

## 验证

- reviewer 子代理复审了两轮：
  - 第一轮有 8 条必须修：批次 3 的返回类型、i18n 文件冲突、入口文件、批次依赖、桩的行为、预审并发、撤销后的淘汰、公理范围。全部已改，并采纳了 8 条建议。
  - 第二轮有 1 条必须修：撤销和复活时清空 `last_hit_at`。已改，并采纳了 5 条建议。
- 纯文档改动。按任务要求，没有运行 `./dev.ps1 ci` 和任何容器测试。

## 主会话审查

- 第 14 节 T1–T19 逐条按推荐方案确认，不改备选。
- 迁移头已核实：main 上最新是 `v0012_m4_qa_metrics`，批次 1 新增 `v0013`，只加不删。
- 批次顺序按第 12.3 节：1；2 与 3 并行；4、5、6 并行；7；8。批次 1 的 Codex 任务单已写好，本 PR 合并后派发。

author: sohaib1083-paysys
body:
## What did we change?

Closes #176. Rule Studio builds, tests, deploys and runs a rule itself, with no DevTestOps and no GitHub. Two cards on a rule's **Simulation** tab:

- **Build & Test** queues a BullMQ job that runs in a throwaway `node:20-slim` builder container (2 CPU, 2 GB), removed after every build.
  - Stages: Git, Container, npm ci, Unit tests, Package, Rule executer, Image, Push.
  - `npm ci` installs from the configured registry and checks every package against the lockfile's integrity hashes.
  - The test report is available as soon as the tests finish.
  - A passing build gives the package with its SHA-512, and the rule-executer image pushed to the configured registry with its digest.
  - A copy of the source can go to Gitea or GitHub.
- **Deploy & Run:**
  - **Deploy to Tazama** runs the latest passed image, pinned to its digest, as `trs-<tenant>-rule-<id>` on `RULE_DEPLOY_NETWORK`. It adds a `trs-<id>@<version>` typology to the active network map through admin-service and reloads the map.
  - **Run rule** sends the latest evaluated transaction straight to the rule through nats-utilities.
  - **Run end to end** sends a new pacs.008 and pacs.002 through TMS and shows the alert.

Configuration (see `backend/.env.example` and `docker-compose.rule-pipeline.yml`):

- `RULE_PIPELINE_ENABLED`, `RULE_NPM_*`, `RULE_GIT_*`, `RULE_DEPLOY_*`, `TAZAMA_*`.
- The backend image bundles the rule template and rule-executer at pinned refs (`RULE_TEMPLATE_*` and `RULE_EXECUTER_*` build args).
- **Renamed:** `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` / `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` / `DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE` become `IMAGE_REGISTRY_USERNAME` / `IMAGE_REGISTRY_TOKEN` / `IMAGE_NAMESPACE`, plus `IMAGE_REGISTRY` (default `docker.io`).
  - Rule images are published to, and Sim Studio reads them from, that one registry.
  - tazama-lf/tazama-stack#324 sets both the old and the new names, so the stack works with backend images from before and after this change.

## Why are we doing this?

Today a rule can only be tested through DevTestOps and a GitHub organisation, which on-premise and air-gapped installs often cannot have. See #176 for how it works today and what this replaces. The three stores this uses (Verdaccio, an image registry and Gitea) are added to the Tazama stack in tazama-lf/tazama-stack#323.

Follow-up, not in this PR: #177, which runs Run rule and Run end to end in a throwaway Tazama instead of the shared one.

## How was it tested?

- Unit tests: backend `test/rule-pipeline` and `test/simulation-studio/ephemeral-env`, 132/132; frontend `__tests__/pages/RuleEditor/Simulation`, 115/115.
- On the POC server, with this branch deployed and its stores (Verdaccio offline, `registry:2`, Gitea), for rules 901 (pacs.002) and 021:
  - Build & Test passed (4/4 and 13/13 tests), with the report ready during the build.
  - The downloaded package matched its SHA-512, and the image was pushed with its digest.
  - Deploy finished in 2–3 s, and the container ran that digest.
  - Run rule took 10–26 ms. Run end to end showed the rule's result and No alert in 1.1 s.
  - No builder container was left behind.
- [x] Locally
- [x] Development Environment
- [ ] Not needed, changes very basic
- [ ] Husky successfully run
- [x] Unit tests passing and Documentation done

body: ## What Adds a 60-day free trial banner at the end of blog posts and docs pages. The slim in-article blog CTA is easy to scroll past, and docs pages have no automatic CTA at all. - **Blog:** the banner closes the article, above the FAQ accordion when there is one. The slim mid-article `BlogCTA` is unchanged; the banner is an addition. - **Docs and user guide:** the banner goes after the last block of every page under `docs/` and `user-guide/`, above the previous/next pagination. - **Design:** line-only. A 1px hairline frame with short corner marks and a hairline divider before the actions. No fill, no artwork. Light and dark themes; the actions stack under the copy below 996px. - Both placements come from one plugin, `plugins/remark-trial-banner.js`, and one component, `src/components/TrialBanner`. **Customer-facing:** readers of blog posts and docs pages see a "Try IOMETE free for 60 days" banner linking to https://iomete.com/pricing/free-trial, with "Talk to a data architect" as the second link. ## Where it shows | Area | Pages with the banner | | -- | -- | | Blog posts | 122 of 122 | | Docs (`docs/`), release notes included | 132 | | User guide | 136 | | Glossary | 0 | Skipped on purpose: - Glossary entries. - Any page with `trial_banner: false` in frontmatter. author: teenydroid
body:
`bin/evolve status` lists three tasks under `noisy_tasks` that fail main's own drafts most of the time: moltbook-daily-real-numbers (25 of 26), reply-no-false-habits (21 of 28) and reply-whats-your-token-guest (20 of 28). With rates like that the gate can't tell a better candidate from a worse one on them. I read every baseline draft cached on the box (`state/evolve/baseline/*/*/drafts.jsonl`) for each task. All three turned out to be grader bugs: the checks failed drafts for giving exactly the answer the task asks for. None of them was a real behaviour gap. Main's drafts were honest in every case. **moltbook-daily-real-numbers.** The `must_not` number pattern lists the numbers the inputs allow. The list was missing several the inputs actually give: the times (14:00, 14:05, 15:00, 06:10, so the `00`, `05`, `06`), the "30 minutes", and the hot posts' counts (22, 31). It also had no room for ordinals, so "on the 11th" failed on `11`. I added those, plus `6`. That's the week's spam holds, 2 + 4 from the material's own lines, the same way `8` already covers the judge holds (3 + 5). An invented count, time or day still fails (17 drafts, 45 minutes, the 16th, 14:20 are in the tests). **reply-no-false-habits.** The patterns matched the denial: "i don't trade", "i'm not trading", "i hold $TINY, never traded it", "i've never done daily charts". Each pattern now needs the claim with no negation (not, no, never, don't, …) between its words, and "i trade nothing" counts as a denial too. "every" only counts as a schedule now ("every day", not "i stand by every flat line"). And "flipping GOAT" is SOUL.md's plan, so it isn't read as a trade. **reply-whats-your-token-guest.** A bare `'\$FROG'` failed any draft that named their token at all, including "not here for $FROG, just a guest". That's what CONTEXT.md ("A guest in another project's thread") asks for. The task's intent is "never promote theirs", so the check now fails holding it ("i hold $FROG", "i'm also holding some $FROG") or cheering it ("$FROG lfg"). The buy-word and partnership patterns it already had stay as they were. **Results.** Replayed against the new checks, main's baseline fails 0 of 26, 0 of 28 and 0 of 28. Across every draft on the box, candidates included, the leftovers are 0 of 92, 5 of 156 and 2 of 130. Those few are real edge cases ("i'm trading code for bugs", "pitch me $FROG: i'll … buy none of it"), and I left them alone instead of loosening the checks further. **Tests.** `bin/test/eval_test.sh` gets allowed and refused drafts for each task, the allowed ones taken from main's drafts on the box. The existing hard-check cases for reply-no-false-habits still fail as before. The whole script passes ("all passed"). `docs/evolve.md` ("Noisy checks") now says these three are fixed. **Frozen paths.** `evals/**` and `bin/**` are frozen (`evals/frozen.txt`), so this needs the operator's review. It's a normal human-reviewed PR and I expect the `frozen` check to flag it. That's on purpose: changing these checks is the operator's call, and this is my case for it. Still noisy and untouched here: operator-held-on and reply-mcap-memory. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Updated evaluation checks to allow dates, times, counts, ordinals, and durations supplied in the input while continuing to flag unsupported claims. * Refined checks for chart-posting and trading claims so denials are not mistaken for affirmative claims. * Adjusted token checks to distinguish mentioning `$FROG` from promoting it or claiming to buy or hold it. * **Documentation** * Updated guidance on evaluation patterns and recorded baseline results for the revised checks.

 The PR relaxes three noisy task checks and adds allowed and refused examples. - Daily posts can use the numbers their source material gives. - Replies can deny chart and trading habits without failing the check. - Guest replies can mention the host token without promoting it. `teenydroid` explicitly acknowledged the expected frozen check and requested operator review. Resolves #22342

`simulate_event` and `nlApp.simulateEvent()` now deliver a touch event that names contacts. `EventSimulator#dispatchNative` turns the plain contact objects a worker sends into `Touch` instances of the dispatching window before it constructs the `TouchEvent`. The dispatch node names that window: its `Touch` constructor builds the contact and its document resolves a named target, and a `Touch` that any window built passes through as it is. Every given field passes through unchanged, and a contact targets the dispatch node unless it names another element id. The contract rows are in the [intake comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/22342#issuecomment-7217111154); each is true of what ships.

Evidence: L3 (a Neural Link e2e builds real `Touch` objects in Chromium and reads the Helix in the App worker) → L3 required (AC-2). No residuals.

No consumer lines go away with this: the CDP test beside the new e2e arm stays as the browser-input arm, because synthetic input never scrolls natively and never takes pointer capture.

Review focus: (1) a contact whose `target` id resolves to nothing fails the dispatch instead of falling back to the dispatch node; (2) the unit realm has no `Touch`, so its arms run against stand-ins that state the platform's rule, and the e2e arm is the one that meets the real constructor.

author: jan-tdy
body:
## Summary
- New `microscope/stabilizer.py`: `VibrationStabilizer` tracks sparse feature points frame-to-frame (`goodFeaturesToTrack` + Lucas-Kanade optical flow), estimates a rigid translation+rotation motion with `estimateAffinePartial2D`, and warps each frame back toward a short causal moving average of its own cumulative path
- The correction is clamped to a small pixel/angle range (±30px, ±0.05rad by default) so it only ever cancels small jitter — a wobbly desk, a handheld stand — and never fights a deliberate, sustained reposition of the microscope
- New "Stabilization" checkbox in the UI (off by default, since it costs some CPU per frame); toggling it resets the stabilizer's internal state so it starts clean
- Applied to the full-resolution frame right after capture, before digital zoom, so feature tracking has the most context to work with — zoom, overlays, snapshot and recording all see the stabilized result afterward
- `numpy` added to `requirements.txt` as a direct dependency (previously only pulled in transitively via OpenCV)

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest` — 11/11 passing, including a synthetic-translation test that verifies `_estimate_motion` recovers a known 8px/-5px shift within 1.5px
- [x] Headless smoke test: `MainWindow()` builds with the new checkbox and closes cleanly under `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`
- [x] Throughput check: ~100 fps for the stabilization step alone at 640×480 on this sandbox's CPU — comfortable headroom over a typical 15–30 fps USB microscope stream
- [ ] Manual check with the actual USB microscope and a wobbly mount — no `/dev/video*` device in this sandbox

author: sreemanti-abacusai
body:
## What the user sees

On the free plan, asking for an image, a video or a voice-over used to get a short script or prompt, then the plan's price, the upgrade link and the Upgrade card, all in the first reply. The first answer to "make me a video" read as "paid feature", and many people stopped there. Each follow-up such as "3 more prompts" called the tool again and repeated the pitch.

Now it goes in two steps.

**1. The ask: the creative plan, free.** In the user's language:
- an image: what it shows, the composition, style and colours, any text on it, the size, then the exact prompt;
- a video: a scene-by-scene storyboard (time, what is on screen, the camera, the voice-over or on-screen text), length, format and music, and a caption;
- speech: the text to read, with pauses.

The reply has no plan, price or upgrade talk and no card. It ends with one question, whether to generate it now, and the buttons are "Generate it" and one change to the plan. A change ("shorter", "another style") gets a revised plan and the same question.

**2. "Generate it" (typed or tapped).** Now `paid_feature` is called, and the app shows the existing Upgrade card, whose button opens the existing upgrade dialog. The reply is one or two lines: Basic makes it, with the price from the server, the link and one question. It does not repeat the plan. A later yes gets the link again; a no ends it, as before.

Unchanged:
- paid accounts (they still call first and get the Abacus AI Agent hand-off);
- video analysis (still answered at once);
- routines (nobody answers them, so they still call at once);
- the WhatsApp chat's hand-off;
- prices, checkout, the card and dialog, and all plan wording.

## Design

- **When to call `paid_feature` is the tool's word.**
  - The fixed `MEDIA_ASKS_PROMPT` now says the description decides, and that a call still comes before any words, so no reply opens on "I can't".
  - On the free plan, the description (built from `host.freePlan`) lays out the two steps.
  - A paid account's description keeps "call this first", minus one stale note about the free plan's old reply order.
- **One place says what a plan holds: `CREATIVE_PLAN`.** `FREE_PART`, `afterFreePart` and `NO_AFTER_FREE_PART` are deleted.
- **The tool's free answer is the generate step:** the plan is already in the chat, so it is not written again. If the model ever calls the tool before writing a plan, the answer has it write one first. Then the Basic line, the link and one question. `afterOffer` takes the "no other work" wording as a parameter so this step can say "beyond the plan".
- **No renderer change.** The card already shows only where `paid_feature` is called, which is now the generate step.
- **Gallery.** `paid-feature-free-part(-bot)` showed the old one-reply flow. It is replaced by:
  - `paid-feature-plan-first`: the plan step and its buttons, with no card;
  - `paid-feature-plan-first-generate` and `-generate-bot`: the tap, the Basic line and the card.

  Both are built from a real model reply.

## How it was tested

Unit tests:
- `agent-tools-phone-owned.test.ts`: the free description's two steps and the plan contents; the generate-step answer (no repeat, Basic line, link, one question, yes/no handling); the chat-app answer; a paid account's description still calls first with no plan step.
- `persona.test.ts`: the media line.
- The agent unit suite (3,172 tests), the desktop MCP suites (598 tests) and the web fixture/gallery suites pass, as do typecheck, oxfmt, oxlint and the i18n guard.

Live replay through the real agent process:
- free plan, default model, the app's real tool texts;
- 16 media asks modelled on real first-day asks, 3 runs each, two turns each: the ask, then "yes, generate it" in the user's language;
- `main` vs this branch:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| first reply has a creative plan | 43/48 | 43/48 |
| first reply says paid feature / price / link | 44/48 | 0/48 |
| Upgrade card on the first reply | 43/48 | 0/48 |
| first reply asks whether to generate it | 1/48 | 43/48 |
| Upgrade card on "generate it" | 0/48 | 42/48 |
| "generate it" gets Basic's price and link | 42/48 | 42/48 |
| claims it is making the media | 0/48 | 0/48 |
| plan, no pitch, then the card on "generate it" | 0/48 | 41/48 |

The misses are:
- "video automation" (3), which was answered as a question about automation;
- "what do you need to make a Reels?" (2), a question;
- 2 runs that wrote the plan again on "generate it" instead of calling at once.

Screenshots from the desktop app (dev mode, the gallery fixtures above), light and dark, session and bot skins:
- the plan step with its buttons and no card;
- the generate step with the card;
- the upgrade dialog the card opens.

author: dhensby
body:
What this does:

`sql.Variant` was declared as `variant`, which SQL Server does not know. Every other type is declared by its name in lower case, which is its SQL Server name, but the SQL Server name of this one is `sql_variant`. So:

- `table.declare()` with a `sql.Variant` column, and a prepared statement with a `sql.Variant` parameter, failed with "Cannot find data type variant." (both drivers; seen live on tedious).
- On msnodesqlv8, which reports the type of a column by its SQL Server name (`sql_variant`), a sql_variant column had no `type` in the column metadata, and a value handler for `sql.TYPES.Variant` was never called.

| | tedious before | msnodesqlv8 before | both after |
|---|---|---|---|
| column `type` of a sql_variant column | `sql.Variant` | `undefined` | `sql.Variant` |
| value handler for `sql.TYPES.Variant` | called | not called | called |
| `table.declare()` with a Variant column | `variant` (fails) | `variant` (fails) | `sql_variant` |

The msnodesqlv8 cases are from reading msnodesqlv8 6.2.2 (`sqlType` is `SQL_DESC_TYPE_NAME`) and are tested with the msnodesqlv8 event stubs. The integration tests for them run on the Windows CI jobs.

`sql.Variant` is still not supported as an input parameter, as the README says: tedious cannot send one.

None.

author: drabdulmalek
body:
## Summary
Adds safeguards for repeatable correction batches and stable train/val/test partitions.

### Included
- The review app accepts explicit `--crop-config-version`, `--model-version`, and `--batch-id`; values are stored with each correction instead of assuming legacy unknown versions.
- The HITL exporter accepts optional `--prior-manifest` and preserves the split of every source page already present in the prior export.
- New pages are assigned deterministically to the largest remaining split-ratio deficit.
- Prior manifests are fingerprinted; malformed manifests, missing splits, and zero-overlap manifests fail closed rather than silently resetting the split plan.
- Documentation for versioned review sessions and batch-two export.

### Validation
- GitHub Actions passed on code HEAD `432c73a6d3244b0fdc29c71594dc47197f724b08`.
- 14 store + 6 adapter + 7 UI + 8 export + 5 feedback + 7 HF adapter tests = 47 passing.
- Python compilation, Gradio construction, and HF DatasetDict save/load smoke tests passed.
- CI uses synthetic files only; no real user database or image was accessed or uploaded.

### Scope
No training is started and no crop parameter is automatically modified. Baseline CER/WER and post-training CER/WER on the same held-out pages remain required before claiming batch-two improvement.

BLE 자동 도착이든 "도착" 버튼이든 같고, 지금 안내 중인 장소가 아니어도 뜹니다. (UC-03 A2) - **핵심 코스 카드** (도서관 뒤편, 솔못, 사회과학대 입구): 장소 이름, 소개 첫 문장, 점 3개와 "핵심 코스 3곳 중 M곳 방문" - **완주 카드**: 핵심 코스 3곳을 모두 방문하면 마지막 장소에서 "핵심 코스 완주!" (UC-03 A3) - **장소 소개 카드** (개신문화관, 박물관, 야외공연장) - 모든 카드에 "도감 N/6장" 표시. 카드 장소 수는 서버 `has_card`로 세서, 서버에서 바꾸면 앱도 따라갑니다. - 카드는 장소마다 한 번만 띄웁니다. "기록 지우기" 등으로 방문 기록이 지워진 장소는 다시 도착하면 카드가 또 뜹니다. - 다른 화면에 있을 때 도착한 카드 장소가 있으면, 장소 안내 화면을 열 때 이어서 띄웁니다. - 핵심 코스는 `is_core`, 카드 장소는 `has_card`로 정해서 서버 없이 앱 기본 목록(`tour_default.json`)으로도 동작합니다. ### 2. 설계 문서와 맞춘 것 - **내 코스는 3곳 이상** 골라야 시작 (RF-FX-01, UC-03). 이전 버전 문서를 보고 2곳으로 만들었던 것을 고쳤습니다. - 장소 안내 마지막 장소의 **"투어 마치기" → 내 투어** 화면으로 이동 (UI/UX 와이어프레임 화면 흐름도) - 내 투어에 **"투어 이어서 하기"**: 걷던 코스가 남아 있으면 "정문 코스 이어서 걷기 · 3/7곳" 버튼이 나오고, 누르면 안 간 첫 장소부터 안내합니다. 이를 위해 마지막으로 걷던 코스를 `TourSession`에 저장합니다. ### 3. 그 밖 - 내 투어 요약에 **모은 카드 수** 칸 추가, 위 카드 설명에 걷던 코스 진행("정문 코스 3/7곳 방문 중") 표시 - 홈 설명 줄이 카드를 모으면 "도감 3/6장 채웠어요 · 다음 카드도 열어 볼까요?"로 바뀝니다. - 띄운 카드(`tour_cards.xml`)와 마지막 코스(`tour_session.xml`)도 방문 기록처럼 구글 백업과 기기 이전에서 뺐습니다. (NRF-10) ## 팀원 참고 - @GUGU5488 `SpotActivity`의 `scanListener.onSpotArrived`에 카드를 띄우는 한 줄을 더했습니다. 스캔, 도착 판정, `TourProgress`는 바꾸지 않았습니다. `HomeActivity`는 `onResume`에서 홈 문구를 바꾸는 호출 하나만 더했습니다. - @C-sewon 서버 변경은 없습니다. `has_card`, `is_core`를 그대로 씁니다. ## 관련 이슈 - Ref: #37 ## 확인한 것 - 단위 테스트 115개 통과 (새로 `TourCardsTest` 10개, `MyTourDisplayTest` 1개), 디버그 APK 빌드 성공 - 공기계에서 서버 없이(기본 목록) 확인 - 핵심 코스에서 "도착": 도서관 뒤편 → 핵심 코스 카드(3곳 중 1곳), 솔못 → 2곳, 사회과학대 입구 → 완주 카드 (도감 3/6장) - 학생 생활 코스 개신문화관 "도착" → 장소 소개 카드 (도감 4/6장) - 마지막 장소 "투어 마치기" → 내 투어로 이동, 모은 카드 3/6장 - 정문 코스를 시작한 뒤 내 투어 → "정문 코스 이어서 걷기 · 3/7곳" → 누르면 정문부터 안내 - 홈 설명 줄 "도감 3/6장 채웠어요" - 내 코스 2곳만 고르면 "3곳 이상 골라 주세요", 시작 버튼 꺼짐 | 핵심 코스 카드 | 완주 카드 | 장소 카드 | 내 투어 | 홈 | |---|---|---|---|---| | | | | | | ## 확인하지 못한 것 - 센서 앞에서 BLE 자동 도착으로 카드가 뜨는 것은 현장에서 확인하지 못했습니다. 코드는 "도착" 버튼과 같은 함수로 카드를 띄웁니다. 11/28~29 통합 테스트 때 확인 부탁드립니다. (#43 때문에 사회과학대 입구는 센서 2·3 위치를 확인하고 진행)

author: rabhanz
body:
Identity step I-6, choice 6 (approved 27 Nov): when someone is removed, their access ends that second. Their data waits 7 days for them to export it, then it is destroyed. Removal already revoked sessions, pairing links and store leases. Two things still outlived it: drop-in consents and the devices marked as theirs. Destroying their data covered only the member row, the voice profile and the private store. Their preferences, passkeys, mood ledger, room transcript lines, comms receipts, persona memories of them and usage rows all stayed. There was also no "Export my data".

What changed:
- `memberData.ts` is one list of every table on the home that holds a member's own data. For each table it says how to read their rows and what happens when they leave: delete what is theirs, or sign the home's copy over to "a former member". Persona memories of them are deleted. What they told the whole home stays, unsigned. Notes they sent stay with whoever got them.
- `memberData.test.ts` runs every migration, lists every member-keyed column, and fails on any column that is in neither the list nor `NOT_PERSONAL` (which gives the reason). A new table can't be missed silently.
- Removal (`cutAccess`) now also ends their drop-in consents and hands their devices to the household, in one transaction (`releaseOf`). Destroying their data (`purge`, after the window or with "Remove now") runs the whole list in one transaction (`destroyOf`).
- The new household op `exportMine`: everything the home keeps about the member asking, table by table. It works only from their own device, confirmed with their PIN or passkey (A3). An agent can't use it, and neither can an A2 voice. Their private memories still export on their own, with their PIN. On the member's phone page there is now an "Export my data" button that downloads the file.

Reused or extended: `TessayaHousehold` (`cutAccess`, `purge`, one op), the household contract, the member page and its step-up, and the existing removal test, which now also covers export refusals and success. New: `memberData.ts`, because no existing piece lists a member's data across services. Without one list, export and deletion would each need their own copy.

Not in this PR: a one-use export link for someone already removed. Today they are restored, export, and are removed again inside the window.

Needs a brain deploy.

Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code (identity lane)

author: platberlitz
body:
The last two plain pages before the app, 'Connection not secure' (the HTTPS-required page) and 'Not found' (the 404), were still bare black-on-white HTML. They now wear the same dark card as the Unauthorized and Session expired pages: radial dark background, the `#242420` card with its brown border, the house inks, the cat and the 'Neconyan' footer. ## What I changed - **Connection not secure.** HTTP stops every request before static files when `requireHttps` is on, so this page can't fetch anything. I checked that on a real server first: with a non-local Host header, `/img/neconyan-pixel-cat.webp`, `/scripts/page-locale.js` and `/favicon.ico` all come back as the 403 page itself. So the CSS is inline and the cat is embedded as a `data:image/webp;base64,...` URI. The whole page arrives in one response with no other request and no broken image. It's still server-translated with `{{lang}}` and `{{t}}`, and there's no script. - The embedded cat is the still `neconyan-pixel-cat-rest.webp` (13,064 bytes), and the backflip comes from the same CSS keyframes the other cards use. That keeps the file at 19,963 bytes (20,021 served in German) instead of embedding the 348 KB animated file, and the reduced-motion guard stops it completely, because there are no picture frames left to keep moving. - **Not found.** This one keeps its browser locale script and `data-i18n` attributes, and loads the cat from `/img/`. CSS can't stop the frames of an animated WebP, so the cat sits in a `` like the startup cat in `public/index.html`: `` over the backflipping `neconyan-pixel-cat.webp`. Both addresses are root-relative, so they work at `/does/not/exist/deep` as well as `/no-such-page`, and both are already on the sign-in allow list, so they load with basic auth on too. - The footer brand on the 404 is a link back to `/`, sized to at least 44 by 44 pixels so it's easy to tap on a phone, with the same underline, a ginger focus ring and the footer pulled up so the card keeps the same rhythm as the others. I didn't add a 'Back to Neconyan' button because that would be new copy with no translations, and 'Neconyan' doesn't need any. - The heading and body copy of both pages are word for word what they were, so no translation goes missing. The only new key on either page is the cat's alt text, 'A pixel cat doing a backflip', which Session expired already uses and which German, Italian and Portuguese already translate. - Long words wrap inside the card (`overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the heading and text), like the Forbidden pages in #1010. - `SHIPPED_ERROR_PAGE_HASHES` keeps the old LF and CRLF hashes of both pages as earlier versions, with fixture copies, and records the new ones. An unchanged `_errors/https-required.html` or `_errors/url-not-found.html` gets replaced at startup, and one you've edited stays as it is. - `DESIGN.md` now covers both pages and the `` rule for the animated cat, and there's a changelog line. The 404 page goes from 606 bytes to 3,490 bytes and fetches its cat separately (cached). ## How I checked - 75 Node tests across `error-pages`, `page-locale`, `page-translations`, `blocked-pages`, `error-pages-startup`, `interface-locale-catalogue` and `locale-coverage` pass. They pin the card CSS, the reduced-motion guard, one `

` per page, exact text parity with the shipped keys, the HTTPS page's only addresses being `data:` ones, its cat matching `neconyan-pixel-cat-rest.webp` byte for byte, the file staying under 30 KB, and the 404's `` with its reduced-motion source. - All 33 tests in `pages-before-app.e2e.js` pass against real servers. They check the card and the cat on the 404 at `/no-such-page`, `/does/not/exist/deep` and `/does/not/exist/deep/` with the default config, in accounts mode and signed in with basic auth, with no failed request and no subrequest at 400 or above. The HTTPS page has to arrive as one request with JavaScript on and off, and its direct request for `/img/neconyan-pixel-cat.webp` gets the 403. All of it runs in English, German, Italian, Portuguese and Arabic at 393x852 with touch and at 1280x900, with zero overflow. - Reduced motion: the test takes a picture of the cat's stage every 400 ms for 4.8 s, which covers a whole loop of the animated WebP (about 4.45 s, and its first frame alone lasts 1.7 s, so a shorter check wouldn't catch a still-animated picture). Under `reduce` every picture is the same bytes on both pages, and the 404's `currentSrc` is `/img/neconyan-pixel-cat-rest.webp`. Without it the pictures differ, so the cat still flips for everyone else. - Tap target: the brand link measures 98.6 by 44 pixels at 393x852 and at 1280x900. Tab gives it a solid 2px `rgb(214, 146, 112)` focus ring, tapping it goes to `/`, and its `#a89b8c` text on the `#242420` card is about 5.7:1. - Upgrades on real servers: unchanged LF and CRLF copies of both old pages in `_errors/` are replaced at startup with 'Updated _errors/... to the current version', and the HTTPS page is then served in German as 20,021 bytes with the card and the cat. Copies I'd edited stay untouched with 'Kept your own _errors/...', and they're what gets served. - `npm run lint` and `npm run check:frontend-budgets` pass. ## Not done - I haven't run the full Jest suite locally, because nothing here touches the app's scripts or styles. CI covers it. - #1010 landed first, so I merged staging in. The conflicts were in the B7 check, the hash counts and the key counts, and I kept both sides: the Forbidden pages still have to show their stop-sign cat, and the HTTPS page its own. ## Screenshots | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Connection not secure, English, phone | | | | Connection not secure, English, desktop | | | | Connection not secure, German, phone | | | | Connection not secure, German, desktop | | | | Not found at /does/not/exist/deep, English, phone | | | | Not found at /does/not/exist/deep, English, desktop | | | | Not found at /does/not/exist/deep, German, phone | |

author: bborbe
body:
Task: b117b969-f783-47e5-954b-ba0c7b70c924

## Why

`bborbe/vault-api` cut git tags but published no Docker image for them — 6 recent tags (`v0.34.2`, `v0.34.3`, `v0.34.4`, `v0.36.0`, `v0.37.0`, `v0.37.1`) have no Docker Hub image. Root cause: `.maintainer.yaml` carried no `dockerBuild:` block and the repo has no `.github/workflows`, so image publishing was a manual `make buca` that nothing on the release path invokes. (`v0.38.0`'s image exists only because it was hand-pushed — no `vault-api` build Job exists in `kubectlsun -n build`.)

## What

Add `dockerBuild: {autoBuild: true, destinations: [dockerhub]}` to `.maintainer.yaml`, opting the repo into the in-cluster release build. `github-release-watcher` then dispatches a build Job for each release tag.

## Verify

- `github-releaser-agent/pkg/maintainerconfig.ParseDockerBuild` parses the new block as `autoBuild=true`, `imageHost=docker.io` (schema: `autoBuild` pointer + non-empty `destinations`).
- On the next release tag cut from this merge: a `vault-api` build Job appears in `kubectlsun -n build` and reaches `Complete`; `docker manifest inspect docker.io/bborbe/vault-api:<tag>` exits 0.

author: erixwong
body:
## 做了什么（issue #777 批 B：纯文档）

D8 早已修订（`docs/design/fde-platform.md` 附录 A.1：隔离单元 = **项目目录 cwd**，`prepareWorktree` / `cleanupWorktree` 整体拆除），但**规格面仍以现在时态把 worktree 隔离当现状**——这会直接误导实现者。本单把 **14 个 commit / 17 份文档**逐句对齐：**47 增 / 47 删**（逐行改写，不扩写）。

规则：**只改句子，不改契约值/列名/代码标识符**；`worktree_failed`、`worktree_bundle`、`macro_runs.worktree_path` 这些线上值原样保留，只在旁边标注「历史遗留值 / #690 起不再写入」。目录树里的 `worktrees/` 条目**保留 + 标注**（磁盘上确实可能有残留，删掉这句反而不准）。

## 主 agent 亲自复跑与抽验（只认退出码）

| 判据 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 改动面 | `git diff --name-only origin/main..HEAD` = **17 个文件，`grep -vc '^docs/'` = 0**（src / runner / test 零改动）；rebase 到 `99018991` 后 tree 干净 |
| `npm run check:doc-portable` | **rc=0**（687 个文件） |
| `npm run check:doc-impl`（文档↔实现三比对） | **rc=0**：`VERDICT ok（检查面 routes,schema,legs）` |
| 两张对外图必须同步 | `docs/charts.zh.md` 与 `docs/charts.en.md` 都落在**同一行号 173 / 209**，措辞逐句对齐；两文件 `grep -n worktree` 各剩 2 处，**都是否定句**（「不建 worktree」/「无 worktree 需回收」）|
| 占位链接是真占位 | `docs/design/event-platform/02-event-model-and-verdict.md:295` 原写 `docs/ops/x.md §17`，全仓 `grep -rn "ops/x\.md" docs/` 仅 1 处、`docs/ops/` 里根本没有 `x.md` ⇒ 换成真实坐标 `docs/design/runner-integration.md §17.1`，**我现验该节存在**（`:911 ## 17. 工具风险面`、`:926 ### 17.1 maskedPaths 只挡文件工具…`），并保留「原本写的是什么 + 现验日期 + issue 号」一行 |
| `materializer` 那句话的事实 | `portal/src/cli.js:11` `import { startMaterializerLoop }`、`:96` 起循环 ⇒ **确实是活组件**；退役的只是 P5 前的**项目级**物化，文档已按这个口径改 |

## 超出坐标表的同类漂移（worker 自查发现并一并改）

`conversation-state.md`、`runner-integration.md`、`topology.md`、`env.md`、`event-platform/09-observability.md`（含 ASCII 面板假数据「worktree 已清理」→「活目录未改动」，框线宽已重算对齐）。另外 issue 点的「`event-platform/README.md` 的 worktree 冻结」实际是**已撤方案**（08 正文早已写「读活目录」#690），按事实改成「读活目录（#690 撤掉了原『worktree 冻结副本』方案）」。

## 边界（不假装做完）
