author: jnixy
adamshiervani
body: ## Problem The Mini answers its web interface on each of its network addresses. A user who cannot change the router (#41) has no way to keep the login page away from the local network, where the Mini serves plain HTTP. Tailscale is built in and gives an encrypted path, but turning it on does not close the local address. ## What exists The web server listens on all addresses, and `jetkvm_access` guards each request. The firmware already knows the Mini's Tailscale address. The web UI has upstream's Loopback-Only control, but its text names `127.0.0.1` and SSH, which the Mini does not have, so this change does not use it. lwIP takes a packet for an address of the device on each interface. So a host on the local network can send to the Mini's Tailscale address through the local interface. While a tailnet peer has a WireGuard session, lwIP routes the answer by its source address to the tunnel, and the host does not get it. While no peer has one, the link of the tunnel is down, lwIP routes the answer by its destination, and the host completes a connection whose local address is the Tailscale address. This is from the code of lwIP and of the WireGuard library, and the host test shows the first step with lwIP's own input; it was not tried on a device. ## Fix A new setting, "Web interface through Tailscale only", is stored in NVS and is off by default. A factory reset turns it off. - **Rule.** While the setting is on, the web server admits a connection only when it arrived on the Mini's Tailscale IPv4 address (`jetkvm_access_tailscale_only_admits()`). The rule names what is admitted, so an address of any other kind is refused. While the Mini has no Tailscale address, it admits nothing. - **Stack.** The local address shows the path only when the stack takes the Tailscale address from the tunnel alone. A rule in front of lwIP's IPv4 input (`tunnel_input.c` in `jetkvm_tailscale`, linked with `--wrap=ip4_input`) now drops a packet for the address of the tunnel that arrived on another interface. It is in effect with the setting on or off, because the same path went around the packet filter of the tailnet. It looks only at the destination, so it also holds for a control server that hands out another range than 100.64.0.0/10. - **Where.** The plain HTTP listener closes each other connection when it opens, before any HTTP exchange (`http_session_opened()`). HTTPD closes such a connection twice, so a close hook leaves the second close to HTTPD; without it, the second close could reach a socket that another task opened under the same number. The `Host` check also shuts down a refused connection at its next request. That covers a connection that was open before the setting turned on, and the HTTPS listener, whose open hook cannot refuse. The `Host` check sees a signaling WebSocket only at its upgrade, so that socket checks its own connection again with each frame and each poll; otherwise a socket from the local network that stayed open could send a new offer. Turning the setting on shuts down the open connections that the rule does not admit, on the HTTPD task. - **Who turns it on.** `setTailscaleOnlyAccess` turns the setting on only in a session whose signaling connection arrived through Tailscale, and only while Tailscale is enabled and running with an address, so a working Tailscale path exists at that moment. A session from the local network and a JetKVM Cloud session get an error. Any session turns it off. - **The way back.** While the setting is on, the Advanced menu on the Mini's screen starts with the entry `Tailscale Only: On`. A hold on it turns the setting off; the Mini does not restart. A hold that is in progress when the entry appears or goes is cancelled, so it does not act on the entry that took its place. The RPCs of the setting are installed also when Tailscale does not start, so the screen can turn a stored setting off. - **Tailscale stays.** While the setting is on, the RPC layer refuses the calls that can take the Mini out of its tailnet: disabling Tailscale, a new auth key, another control server and the logout. This guard is not in #41; it prevents a lockout by one click on the same page. - **Web UI.** The Tailscale page has one more switch, shown when the firmware reports the new `tailscale_only` capability. It is disabled when the page is not open through Tailscale. While the setting is on, the page locks the controls that the Mini would refuse: the Tailscale switch, the logout and the control server. A settings call of this page that is not sent, because the RPC channel is closed, is now reported and unlocks its controls. Turning it on asks first: > **Limit the web interface to Tailscale?** > The web interface will no longer be available on your local network. If you lose access through Tailscale, you can turn this setting off on the KVM's screen: Menu > Advanced > Tailscale Only. A JetKVM Cloud session does not use the web server, so it goes on, and its RPC can turn the setting off. ## Testing | Test | Result | | --- | --- | | `test_access_contract.c`: the rule, with the setting off and on, for the Tailscale address, a local address, a neighbour in the Tailscale range, no IPv4 address and no Tailscale address | passes | | `test_setup.c` (the production `jetkvm_access.c` with platform doubles): open connections shut down, requests on a kept connection unanswered, no turning on without a Tailscale address, the setting across a restart and a factory reset | passes | | `test_tunnel_input.c` (the production `tunnel_input.c` in front of lwIP's own IPv4 input, with the tunnel interface of the WireGuard library): lwIP alone takes a packet for the tunnel's address from the local interface; with the rule it does not, for each address that the tunnel gets, also from a host with a tailnet address; the tunnel itself and the addresses of the other interfaces are not affected | passes | | `test_websocket_tailscale_only.py` (`poll_client()` and `websocket_handler()` of the signaling socket): a socket that is not admitted is closed at the poll, and a frame on it is not read | passes | | `test_jetkvm_control.c`: turning on from the three kinds of session and with a Tailscale that is not connected, turning off from each and from the screen's call, the refused Tailscale calls | passes | | `test_tailscale_only_menu.c` (production screens and button code, both boards): the entry only while on, first on the page, text inside the entry at each strip position, the hold asks for `setTailscaleOnlyAccess` with `false` once, a hold while the entry appears or goes does nothing | passes | | Complete host suite (`tools/run_all_tests.sh`) | 57 suites pass | | Device, `tailscale_only.test.mjs`, first test: a session from the local network reads the setting, cannot turn it on, and the local address keeps answering | passes on an Ethernet Mini | | Device, second test, with the Mini joined to a test tailnet: turned on through Tailscale, the local address closes each connection without an answer, the Tailscale address serves and its session goes on, the Tailscale calls are refused, the same after a restart, and the local address answers after turning off | passes on an Ethernet Mini | Both device tests ran on the build of this branch, which has the input rule, so Tailscale traffic passes that rule on a device. No device test sends a packet for the Tailscale address from the local network: that needs a route on the test machine. The host test covers that case with lwIP's own input. The new host tests use functions that the old code does not have, so they do not build against it. ## Screenshots Addresses and names in the images are documentation values. ### Web UI The images show the Tailscale card of the Tailscale settings page. The KVM is not in a tailnet. The card does not have the switch.

author: jordan-lee-code
body:
Finding a command meant knowing which overlay it belonged to and reading down that overlay's README. This adds `commands.html` to the website, linked from the landing page, with every overlay's chat commands and examples in one place. It has quick links to each overlay and a search box, and on a phone each command stacks into its own block.

## Where the commands come from

`scripts/commands-page.js` builds the page from any README table whose first column is headed `Command`, so each command is still written down once. A command repeated in a second table is shown once. `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says so.

The test fails for an overlay with a command word and nothing listed, or whose section names the wrong word. **It cannot tell whether every single command is in a table**, so that still relies on the READMEs being kept up to date.

## README changes

- Be Right Back gains rows for `!brb meeting` and `!brb custom`.
- Two Truths and a Lie gains a table of the `!lie` server commands, and a row for how chat votes.
- Chat Feed, Spin Wheel and Subathon have real examples where there were placeholders. Subathon also gains an `!incentive` row, since its sub goals use those commands.

## Worth knowing

- The page shows each overlay's starting command word. Anyone who has changed theirs will see the default.
- Local Time and Socials Bar have no chat commands, and the foot of the page says so.
- Subathon has two command settings. The page labels it `!subathon`, the clock's own word.

## Checks

- The full suite passes (5,290 tests in 24 suites), with new tests for the page, the table reading and escaping of README text.
- In headless Chromium, search and the quick links worked, and the page did not scroll sideways at 1100 or 360 pixels wide. I looked at screenshots at both sizes.
- The commands were not each tried in live chat.

author: robcohen
body:
## What

Deletes convert.rs's `quiet_after_invalid_tokens` (#2872), the hand-modeled pass that dropped every error after a line's first invalid token. Three things now cover what it did:

- the error oracle's reconciler, which holds each line's errors to beancount's;
- the `bom-in-account` overlay (#3065), which keeps the one-BOM-per-line rule this pass also applied;
- #3067's deletion of `drop_errors_inside_a_line_error`, which leaves the token's own error as the one the reconciler keeps and names.

Also deleted: the pass's `header_grammar_reaches` and `indented_grammar_reaches` helpers and their unit tests. Comments that named the pass are reworded.

## Why stacked

This PR is stacked on #3067, which is stacked on #3065. Deleted on main alone, the pass's removal measured:

- parity unchanged;
- the BOM matrix 7 rows worse without the overlay;
- with the overlay, messages drift to `unexpected trailing tokens after posting amount` (in 3 corpus files and in the surface-agreement cases), because `drop_errors_inside_a_line_error` then dropped the token's own error.

On top of #3067, nothing changes.

## Gates

- **No output change:** parity is 122,378 of 123,394 inputs, with no re-pin; the BOM matrix, `STRICT_BASELINE` and the parser suite pass.
- **Other suites:** workspace clippy with `-D warnings` is clean; the validate, loader, lsp, wasm and rustledger tests pass.

## Caches

WASM cache v155. The loader cache is unchanged.

On Windows, an elevated administrator creating a directory owned it as their own account, which Verify refuses. body:
## Changes

- Make the implicitly nullable parameter explicitly nullable: `AbstractValidator::validate(array $values, array $ruleSet, ?string $prefix = null)`. This removes the `Implicitly marking parameter $prefix as nullable is deprecated` notice on PHP 8.4+, which is printed whenever the class is loaded.
- Add PHP 8.4 and 8.5 to the `run-tests.yml` matrix.
- Bump the version to 0.2.1, add a CHANGELOG entry and refresh `phpunit/phpunit` in `composer.lock` (9.6.16 → 9.6.39).

Behaviour is unchanged and PHP 7.4 is still supported.

## Known remaining notices

`madesimple/php-arrays` v2 still declares `Arr::column()` and `Arr::pluck()` with implicitly nullable parameters, so PHP 8.4+ prints 2 notices when `Arr` is loaded. The dependency stays on `^2.0` on purpose:

- v3.0.0 does not fix them and adds new ones in `ArrDots` and `Collection`.
- Only v4.0.0 is clean, but it requires PHP >= 8.3, while this library supports PHP 7.4.

## Verification

`php -l` with `E_ALL` on `src/` plus the PHPUnit suite (47 tests):

| PHP | Dependencies | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 7.4.33 | lock / prefer-lowest | OK, no deprecations |
| 8.4.24 | prefer-stable | OK, only the 2 madesimple notices |
| 8.5.13 | prefer-lowest / prefer-stable | OK, only the 2 madesimple notices |

author: jbjuniorworks-prog
body:
Relato do dono na rota, 27/11: "fui finalizar uma entrega que estava na minha frente, apareceu a Rua Dionísio 208 e foi marcada lá".

**O que muda**
- O cartão de um pino aberto fechava quando o entregador andava 50 m de onde o abriu (regra de 07/11, para quem entregou e foi embora). Quem abre o cartão chegando e anda até a porta também anda 50 m: o cartão fechava e o da próxima aparecia debaixo do dedo. Agora, chegando perto do pino do cartão (mais perto que ao abrir, ou a menos de 50 m), com entrega por fazer nele, o cartão fica. Indo embora, fecha como antes.
- Por 1 s depois de o cartão trocar sozinho, os botões de entregar do cartão da próxima não fazem nada.

**Como foi verificado**
- Na nuvem (só leitura): a 208 não ficou como entregue nem com porta marcada; nenhuma parada a menos de 400 m da que ele entregava (não foi pino empilhado). A causa é a provável pelo código; o toque em si não fica registrado.
- Local, nuvem simulada: 3 testes de unidade e 2 e2e novos, cada um quebrando com a sua sabotagem. Tipos, 818 de unidade e 434 e2e. Não visto no celular.

**Fica para depois**
- Confirmar ao entregar uma parada longe do GPS.

author: deryferd
body:
## What and why

Fixes #7753

The `oc integration` workflow answers a `/oc` or `/opencode` comment and runs an agent with `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, `issues: write` and `id-token: write`, plus an app token minted from `OC_REVIEW_APP_*`. The job condition only looked at the comment text, so any account that could comment started it. `pr-review.yml` already asks GitHub for the commenter's repository permission before it runs a command, and `opencode.yml` uses the same trigger with read-only permissions.

The workflow now has a small gate job that asks for the commenter's permission and requires `admin` or `write`. The `opencode` job waits on it, so a comment from an account without write access starts no privileged job at all. The command matching, model, checkout, and permissions of the main job are unchanged, so the bot behaves the same for the people who already use it.

`author_association` was not enough here: it hides private org members, so the check asks the API for the actual repository permission, which is what `pr-review.yml` already does.

## Affected surfaces

Only `.github/workflows/oc-integration.yml`. No package, runtime, route, or persisted state changes, and the workflow has no code of its own in a runtime.

| Runtime | What you ran and saw |
|---|---|
| Web | Does not run here; this is a CI workflow. |
| Desktop (Electron) | Does not run here. |
| VS Code | Does not run here. |
| Hosted mobile | Does not run here. |
| Capacitor mobile | Does not run here. |
| Relay | Does not run here. |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| YAML parse of the workflow | Valid. |
| `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --ratchet-only` | All checks passed. |

**Live run:** Not applicable. The change only decides who may start a workflow job, so there is no user-reachable behavior to exercise in an app, and the gate runs on GitHub's side where it cannot be started from a local checkout.

## Visual evidence

No visible change. The diff changes a workflow gate and no rendered surface.

## Known problems

None.

author: marcusbandit
body:
## Summary

Quick controls, rebuilt after the owner's look at the first version: the split pills looked bad, and the chevrons on the right edge of the screen opened menus at the sidebar on the left edge. Everything now happens inside the panel that slides out of the right edge.

- **Tiles for things with more inside.** Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Sound and Power mode (Battery on a laptop) are two-line tiles: name, then what it is doing now (the network, the connected device, the output, the mode). The round button on a tile switches it; the rest of the tile opens its page.
- **Pages open in place.** A tile opens its page inside the same panel: back button and title on top, the existing network, Bluetooth, sound and battery menu below, scrolling when long. The panel morphs to the page's height. Escape or the back button returns. Nothing opens on the far side of the screen any more, and these menus keep a home when the full sidebar goes (#923).
- **Switches for plain on and off.** Do not disturb, Keep awake, Microphone, Dark mode, Record and VPN sit in two columns: a round button and its name beside it, lined up with the tiles' buttons. The whole row is the target.
- **Level bars.** Volume, brightness and warmth are thick bars: a white fill that grows from the icon, the reading at the right end. Pressing the warmth icon turns the night light on and off. The 100% mark on volume shows on hover or above 100%.
- **Look.** Clear-glass family, zero colour: white with ink when on, the neutral fill when off, rim light, no accent hues. The colourful slider beads are gone from the panel.
- **Width.** The panel is the menu width, or wider when a tile or switch name would not fit on one line.
- Power mode choices in the battery menu read "Energy saver, Balanced, Performance" instead of the daemon's raw names; the labels live in `services/powerprofile.js`. The battery menu no longer starts with a separator and a "POWER MODE" heading when there is no battery.
- The keyboard starts on the first tile: `focus-chain.js` counts a tile that is half a row wide beside its twin as a first stop.
- The sound page's sliders lost their purple: zero colour, like the rest of the panel.
- `MixerQuickRow` and the in-panel mixer fold are gone; the sound page has the app levels and "Open volume mixer".
- New IPC verb `quickcontrols page <network|bluetooth|sound|power>`, and `page ""` goes back.

## Evidence

- `bash scripts/qml-compile-check.sh`: 0 failures. `node scripts/lint-rules.js`, `node scripts/check-modules.js`: no new violations.
- `node --test tests/quick-switches.test.js tests/power.test.js tests/focus-chain.test.js`: all pass, with new cases for the network and power tile text, power labels and the first keyboard stop.
- Full-shell headless rig at 2560x1440, before and after, over six rounds: the panel at rest, each of the four pages opened through IPC, and back to the panel. Round three caught the tiles vanishing after a page closed (their count read the children's visibility while the panel was hidden); fixed and checked. Shots stay local; the rig reads the real system bus.

## Merge danger

Visual rebuild of an always-reachable panel; do not auto-merge, look at it live first. Network, Bluetooth and power switching were not pressed in the rig because they reach the real system bus.

Closes #903
Closes #664
Part of #893

author: kalmarv
body:
With `XCL_TWO_PASS_BATCH=2` (off by default) a run of deferred two-pass draws is recorded before nearly every other title call on the list. On the title we run, `OMSetStencilRef` was the most frequent single reason a run ended (470,956 of 1,048,576 run ends), ahead of a full batch record buffer (249,518), `IASetPrimitiveTopology` (90,177), the console's method #142 (69,975; a stub in XCL: it records nothing) and `RSSetScissorRects` (32,433), so runs were 12.7 draws long. These sets now go into the run and are made among its mesh passes where the title made them; #142 no longer ends a run. Runs are then 24.3 draws long. Nothing changes without `XCL_TWO_PASS_BATCH=2`. Part of #2688.

**What is in it**
- `hle/d3d12x/bind.rs`: `RunItem` / `Step` / `Cmd` `StencilRef`, `Topology`, `Scissors`, queued by `queue_stencil_ref`, `queue_topology`, `queue_scissors` while the list defers, and set among the mesh passes in the title's order (`batch_commands`, `emit_commands`); a run with no draws applies them as they came (`flush_two_pass`). `keeps_two_pass_batch` keeps slots 20, 22, 24 and the newer layout's 142.
- `hle/d3d12x/list_x.rs`: the console's `IASetPrimitiveTopology`, `OMSetStencilRef` and `RSSetScissorRects` go into the run when it takes them (`apply_*` for the rest).
- Tests: the kept slots; `state_sets_in_a_run_come_between_the_mesh_passes_in_the_titles_order` (stencil, scissor, topology and empty scissor sets between draws: the mesh passes and sets in the order and with the state the unbatched path gives them, none among the compute passes).

**Tested**
- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (driver 610.74), Ryzen 9 9950X, Windows 11 Pro 26200, Rust 1.99.0 MSVC, debug tests, release smoke; DXC 1.9.2609 via `XCL_DXC_DIR`.
- `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` on 6f3ad70c (with `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`: no debug info, for disk space): 1825 passed, 8 failed, 48 ignored. The same command on `nvidia-dev` `a5e2d851`: 1822 passed, 10 failed, 48 ignored.
- Failed here and on `a5e2d851` as well: `async_compute_pso_registers_real_pso_and_not_standin`, `console_ms_in_as_slot_and_ms_with_as_are_refused_cleanly`, `hle::d3d12x::texture_upload::tests::gpu_parts_of_a_texture_go_up_and_the_rest_stays`, `hle::d3d12x::texture_upload::tests::pieces_hold_the_texels_of_their_levels`, `split_compute_prefers_the_offline_whole_pipeline`, `two_pass_driver_cache_reuses_both_passes_and_recovers_corrupt_blobs`.
- 26 `SKIPPED`: 8 no wave64; 1 const_mask, wave64: no wave64; 1 f16 arithmetic, wave32, per-lane form: refused (unsupported V_MUL_F16 (its #1426 semantics differ from the console's)); 1 f16 arithmetic, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 arithmetic, wave64: no wave64; 1 f16 packed, wave32, per-lane form: refused (unsupported V_PK_MUL_F16: VOP3 modifiers (its #1426 semantics differ from the console's)); 1 f16 packed, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 compares, wave64: no wave64; 1 mask_ff0_flbit, wave64: no wave64; 1 f64, wave64: no wave64; 1 integer arithmetic, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 conversions, wave32, per-lane form: refused (unsupported V_CVT_F16_F32 (its #1426 semantics differ from the console's)); 1 f32 conversions, wave64: no wave64; 1 integer carries, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 rounding, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 transcendentals, wave64: no wave64; 1 f32 three-source, wave64: no wave64; 1 no heap windows (opt-in: XCL_HEAP_WINDOWS=1); 1 no heap windows.
- On the title (timed 480 s runs on the hardware above, one run each; with the change: our team branch's build `75d9b05e`, which has it; without: the same build plus two local switches set to restore the old run ends; same env: `XCL_TWO_PASS_BATCH=2`, `XCL_TWO_PASS_SHARED=1`, `XCL_UMA_UPLOAD_PRIORITY=1`, `XCL_VRAM_HOT_PRIORITY=1`, `XCL_DECLARED_LDS=1`, `XCL_PER_LANE=1`, and `XCL_TWO_PASS_INDIRECT_MB=4`, a knob of our branch that is not in this PR): 10.2-10.3 fps with the runs ended as before, 11.1-11.2 fps with this change, steady to 526 s, no errors, no device removal. A repeat of both: 10.1 and 10.6 fps. So +0.5 to +0.9 fps over two pairs (run-to-run spread about 0.5 fps). Two-pass compute passes per frame 317 before, 168 with it.
- For context (not this PR): on `75d9b05e` with the same env, `XCL_TWO_PASS_BATCH=1` ran 6.6-6.7 fps. So mode 2 with `nvidia-dev`'s run ends (on our build, with a 4 MiB indirect reservation where `nvidia-dev` reserves 32 MiB) was worth about +3.6 fps against mode 1 on this card and title. The default is mode 0 (off).
- Picture (the runs' dumped frames, compared by a teammate agent; severe transient obstruction = 25 % or more of a doorway's normally bright pixels darkened, in the last ~78 s): first pair, both in the scene's common state: 7 of 30 frames with this change, 0 of 27 without (for the run without: median mask overlap 97.8 % with a reference run, median edge shift 0 px). Repeat pair, both in the scene's other state: 2 of 28 with this change, 2 of 27 without (frames 4580 / 4640 of the run without lost 57 % / 43 % of those pixels). So the obstructions also occur without this change; two runs per arm do not show equal rates either way.
- CI: `Build and test (Windows, no GPU)` is red on `nvidia-dev` itself and on every PR into it, this one included: the lib test process ends with `0x887a0020` in a sparse test on the runner's software adapter, with no test reported failed. #2837 fixes that test; nothing here touches it.

**Regression run**
150 s runs, same title, same env (`XCL_HEAP_WINDOWS=1 XCL_DIRECT_DXIL=all XCL_DIRECT_SPLIT_INSTRUCTIONS=0 XCL_PSO_JOURNAL=0 XCL_DRED=1 XCL_GPU_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000`, DXC 1.9); the head with `XCL_TWO_PASS_BATCH=2` as well (the mode this change acts in). The `main` run from a hard-link copy of our team branch's DXIL cache; the base and head runs from hard-link copies of one cache warmed on `nvidia-dev` `a5e2d851` (on this branch the title starts after about 75-90 s of startup shader preparation, so 60 s would end inside it).

A commit of `main` (`b49be183`, the last one before the shader preparation screen of #2555):
```
xcl-smoke v1
commit: b49be1836844fe0b0cdb3211dce3cb7fb4e21ac7
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
title: ea3b5e4d
seconds: 150
exit: 0x0
frames shown: 1917 (PresentX 1917)
presents per 2 s (last 3): 0 0 2
device removals: 0
crashes: 0
peak commit: 33080 MB
```

The base, `nvidia-dev` `a5e2d851`:
```

commit: a5e2d851a503fc0e04609f773ea53f2d2c4e3269
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
title: ea3b5e4d
seconds: 150
exit: 0x0
frames shown: 2464 (PresentX 2464)
presents per 2 s (last 3): 0 0 0
device removals: 0
crashes: 0
peak commit: 34597 MB
```

This PR's head:
```
xcl-smoke v1
commit: 6f3ad70ccc22acb777205cdea1d512bf24421299
gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti
title: ea3b5e4d
seconds: 150
exit: 0x0
frames shown: 2672 (PresentX 2672)
presents per 2 s (last 3): 2 1 0
device removals: 0
crashes: 0

```

**Not tested**
- AMD, Intel, Wine. Whether the intermittent obstructions above are as frequent with and without the change (two runs per arm). Titles other than this one. The older console layout (no #142 there; slots 20, 22, 24 are kept in both).

**AI use**
- The queueing was written on our team branch with Antigravity (Gemini 4 Neon), as its commits there record. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) split it out of those commits onto `nvidia-dev`, wrote the new test, ran the suite and the smoke on the hardware above and wrote this description. The timed runs and the picture comparison were run by teammate agents (strange: Claude Code; batman: Codex).

body:
This is the post-release PR for 5.20.0. It is published on PyPI and has a GitHub release, [v5.20.0](https://github.com/Masterplanner25/Nodus/releases/tag/v5.20.0).

- **`docs/evals/v5.20.0/`:**
  - `CREATOR_VALIDATION.md`: Gate 10a passed 8/8 suites on the first round, and Gate 10b passed 173/173 probes.
  - `POSTPUBLISH_EVAL.md`: Stage 5 against PyPI passed 173/173. Coverage reports real figures, and `--coverage-min` passes at 50 and fails at 90 on a 57.1% project.

author: 8088-braxdev
body:
Testing the Swahili insight on a real day's reviews showed the language was right and the writing was not: Swahili words in English sentence order, English words left standing where Swahili has its own, the app's vocabulary borrowed instead of said — a translation, and an unprofessional one. The prompt only said "write in Swahili", which a model satisfies while still thinking in English.

## Change

One shared `NATIVE_VOICE` rule, added to the Swahili rule and to the `auto` rule (so French, Arabic, Hindi and the rest get it too; English already has the model's own shape and is left alone):

> Write it the way a careful native speaker of that language writes: its own word order, its own idioms, and the plain, professional register of a well-edited newspaper. Do not render an English sentence word for word, do not leave English words inside a sentence that is not English, and do not borrow them when the language has its own word — a reader should find nothing awkward and nothing that looks like a translation.

The Swahili rule also asks for correct agreement and no English word standing in for a Swahili one, because Agreement and noun-class concord are where a translation shows first.

## Honest limits

This is a prompt change, not a verified output: the model was not called from here (no `GROQ_API_KEY` in this environment). The proof is the next insight generated on a real review, in Swahili and then in a third language; `/api/insight` reuses a cached insight per period, so the test needs a period with no insight yet.

`node --check api/insight.js` passes.

author: w3d3
body:
Missions can now correct a misread dart the same way every other game does, and the run comes out exactly as if the right dart had been thrown.

**What was missing.** The engine already has one shared correction path for every mode. `correct_dart` and the board's `dart.corrected` replace the dart in the open visit, `undo_dart` removes it, and `refoldVisit` replays the open visit from the committed state through the module's pure reducer. No game reimplements this, so there was nothing per module to extract. Missions failed for two reasons:

1. **Time.** A mission's clock only heard the time of the latest input (`onClock`). Refolding a corrected visit timed every dart at the correction, so a step completed late, and a correction after the time limit failed a run that had in fact finished in time. Now `refoldVisit` gives a game that keeps time each dart's own thrown time (`session.openDarts[].thrownAt`, already logged) before the dart. A correction (`correct_dart`, `undo_dart`, `dart.corrected`) takes no time. A mission's turn time never goes back, so the takeout still hands the turn on at its own time. Only modules with `onClock` (missions) are affected; for every other mode `refoldVisit` behaves as before.
2. **The screen.** The mission screen drew its own chips (`role="img"`), so a dart couldn't be selected. It now uses the shared `DartSlots` with the correction popover (pick a segment, Other…, or tap the board to move it), like Shanghai, Cricket and the rest. `missionSlots` in `lib/dartSlots.ts` is the mission's entry. A dart that ended the attempt keeps its red **Reset** look through a new `alert` slot flag. Undo was already the engine's `undo_dart`, so it is the same shared path.

Who may correct is unchanged (`session/access.ts`), as is the rule that a finished game can't be corrected.

| | Before | After: correcting | After: corrected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/3a6b5c9e4bcb3c1fb6072597f360355b24a4ef6c/docs/missions/play-desktop.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/718576b517b256034e12fab963f49e89487a61de/docs/missions/correct-desktop.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/718576b517b256034e12fab963f49e89487a61de/docs/missions/corrected-desktop.png) |
| Phone | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/3a6b5c9e4bcb3c1fb6072597f360355b24a4ef6c/docs/missions/play-phone.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/718576b517b256034e12fab963f49e89487a61de/docs/missions/correct-phone.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/W3D3/dartcade/718576b517b256034e12fab963f49e89487a61de/docs/missions/corrected-phone.png) |

In the scene, the second twenty was read as S1, which reset the streak (red, attempt 2). After correcting it to S20, the streak is 2 of 3 and the run is back on attempt 1.

**Tests.** `games/mission.test.ts` corrects a dart in every step type and checks that the whole state and view equal a game where the right dart was thrown at the same time. The step types are: hit (a streak a miss reset, in order, a completing dart corrected away), marks, visits, score, a checkout bust undone, a fast leg and average. Further cases: a Start over undone (restarts and attempts go back), a corrected dart timed at its throw, a correction after the time limit counting a dart thrown in time, undo, two players taking turns, a log replay with corrections (restart rebuild), and a finished game taking no correction. 8 of these fail on the old engine. Also `session/refold.test.ts` (dart times reach `onClock`) and `lib/__tests__/dartSlots.test.ts` (`missionSlots`), plus the Playwright scene `37-missions.spec.ts` "correcting a dart" (desktop and phone). Typecheck, lint, lint:tw and format:check pass in backend and frontend. The frontend suite passes 2294/2294. The backend suite passes 3507/3511; the 4 failures are 5 s timeouts under load in untouched files (auth hooks, tournaments browse), and they pass when run alone. The visual baselines have no mission scene, so none change. I ran pstack:thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review over the diff; it found no structural problems.

**Not in here.** The mission scene creates its own mission rather than using the shipped official ones, which another PR removes. Independent of [PR 740, inner bull, tries and lights](https://github.com/W3D3/dartcade/pull/740); the two touch different lines.

- **(c)** Without `postId` the editor link is built from a draft the caller owns (`fetchOwnedDraft`), not from the raw `draftId`.
- **(d)** The next step says "call this tool with the same draftId and postId and upload_link: true and no url". With `replace` no upload link is suggested, because it cannot replace an image.
- **(e)** PR 609's checklist said the matrix rows were not needed, but its commit changed the "Error messages" row in `docs/architecture/client-matrix.md`. That row is kept as it is in this PR.

Net lines in `server/` grow slightly, hence the `Implements #273 Task I1 C1` line.

## Tests

`tests/api/mcp-chat-image-error.test.js` (`// @vitest-environment node`), 7 new cases that fail on main:
- each parser-accepted form (leading space, leading tab, `https:` without slashes, backslashes) reaches the server, is refused as a private address, and makes no fetch;
- credentials are refused by the server, with no fetch;
- each refused scheme (ftp, file, javascript, blob, data) gets the chat-only error and nothing is uploaded;
- a draft the caller does not own is "not found" without postId;
- the "and no url" wording;
- `replace` gives no upload link.

No test was skipped, weakened or re-limited. `npm run precommit:checks` passes (193 files, 3131 tests). In a fresh checkout `server/generated/` is missing and `tests/api/mcp.test.js` fails on the changelog count until `node scripts/build-info.mjs` has run; this is the existing build step, not part of the change.

body:
Closes #551

## What

- `queueVoiceTurn` (permission, AskUserQuestion, elicitation): while the question is spoken and the answer window is open, the registry is polled every 500 ms. Once the session was seen `waiting` and stops being `waiting`, the owner answered on screen. Then `assistant:ask` is cut, the open mic closes (`WakeListener.cancelAnswer`, `DictationService.cancelAnswer`), the hook returns an empty reply and Marshal says "Бачу, відповів." When the question had not started playing yet, it is dropped silently.
- "Session waits" sentence and closing question (#547): dropped once none of their sessions waits or the session is busy again. The acknowledgement is said only when the phrase was cut mid-way.
- `SpeechService.drop(key)` / `isActive(key)`, `SpeechQueue.remove(key)`.
- Words already being heard in the wake answer window when the answer is cancelled do not become a command.
- No poll in idle (#281): each watcher lives only while its phrase or answer window is live.

- `npm run check`: 1929 tests pass. The new wake test fails without the capture guard (mutation-checked).

## Not verified live

Whether the registry shows `waiting` while a synchronous `PermissionRequest` hook runs. The watcher acts only after it has seen `waiting`, so without that nothing is cut.

author: benjaminmichaelis
body:
Fixes two chat findings from the recent security review: the chat budget counted requests, not cost, and chat history survived logout on a shared browser. This PR is independent of the email-uniqueness PR.

## Chat budget
- **Hourly cap wired:** `ChatThrottling` (`MaxMessagesPerWindow` 50 per `ThrottlingWindowMinutes` 60) is now bound and validated as `ChatThrottlingOptions`. Before, no code read it. The `ChatEndpoint` policy (`Services/ChatRateLimiterPolicy.cs`) chains it with the existing 15-per-minute limit using the existing `CombinedRateLimiter`, per user (per IP when anonymous). Rejections still go through the global JSON 429 handler.
- **Output cap:** every Responses API request sets `max_output_tokens` from the new `AIOptions:MaxOutputTokens` setting (default 8192; 0 disables the cap). The cap includes reasoning tokens, so raise it if answers come back cut off.
- **Truncation:** `truncation` is set to `auto` on every request, so a long conversation continued through `previous_response_id` is truncated by the provider instead of failing or growing without bound.
- **Unknown response IDs are still accepted when the ownership cache has no entry for them (not changed):** `ResponseIdValidationService` already documents the reasons. The cache is in-process, so restarts, other replicas and the 2-hour sliding expiry would otherwise lock users out of their own conversations. With the per-user hourly cap, the output cap and auto truncation, a forged or replayed ID can no longer turn one permitted request into unbounded cost. The client-side fix below also stops IDs leaking to the next user of a shared browser. Closing it fully needs a shared store (for example `IDistributedCache`).

## Chat history after logout
- **Clear-Site-Data on logout:** Logout now sends `Clear-Site-Data: "storage"`, which browsers honor over HTTPS.
  - Besides the chat keys, this resets the `sidebarShown` preference and analytics session storage.
  - Consent is a cookie, so it isn't affected.
- **Per-user marker:** pages expose `window.CHAT_STORAGE_OWNER`, a hash of the user ID that is `null` when signed out.
- **Owner-tagged storage:** `chat-module.js` now saves `aiChatHistory` and `aiChatLastResponseId` together with that marker. A new `readOwnedChatState` function, run at load, discards stored state when nobody is signed in, when it belongs to a different user, or when it uses the old unowned format.
- **Cookie Policy:** the page now says both keys also clear at logout.

## Tests
- **`ChatRateLimitTests`:** with the window cap set to 3, the 4th message gets 429 and another user isn't affected.
- **`AIChatServiceCostLimitTests`** (Chat.Tests): captures the request sent to the provider and checks `max_output_tokens` (configured value and default), `truncation: "auto"` and `previous_response_id`.
- **`ChatStorageIsolationTests`:** logout sends `Clear-Site-Data: "storage"`; the marker is stable per user, differs between users, doesn't contain the user ID, and is `null` when signed out.
- **JS check:** I checked `readOwnedChatState` locally with a Node script and fake storage: same user keeps state; another user, signed out, legacy unowned values and expired history are all discarded. The repo has no JS test runner, so that script isn't committed.
- **Frontend:** `npm run build` succeeds.

Against unmodified `main`, the logout and marker tests fail. `ChatThrottlingOptions` and `MaxOutputTokens` don't exist there, so the rate-limit and cost tests can't compile on `main`.

Full runs locally: `EssentialCSharp.Chat.Tests` 43/43. `EssentialCSharp.Web.Tests` 370/372; the 2 failures come from local AI user-secrets (an embedding call returns 401) and fail the same way on `main`.

author: dmatov
body:
Each span has a level, `call` or `step`. A bound process records only the spans at or below its level, and `POSITRONIC_TELEMETRY_LEVEL` names it; a spawned process inherits it.

- `call`: `eval.pass`, `episode`, `reset`, the spans of each policy call (`policy.submit`, `policy.prepare`, `policy.encode`, `policy.infer`, `wire.send`, `wire.recv`), and the `record.io` that opens and closes the writer.
- `step` adds the spans of each control step: `harness.step`, the span of each processor per step, `record.io` at a step, `step.record_wait_ms`, `driver.command`, the client `env.step` and `materialize`, and the codec spans of a codec that wraps a processor run.

`span`, `traced`, `record_span` and `start_span` take `level` as a positional-only argument (default `CALL`), so no attribute name collides with it. `enabled(level)` answers whether a span at that level records. `Codec.wrap` takes `level` for a wrapped callable; a wrapped run gets `STEP`.

## Why

On a real robot a process writes about 1,000 spans per second, most of them step spans. The export thread encodes each batch of 512 spans while it holds the interpreter lock, for 13-38 ms, and the control loop waits. Most late harness steps on a real robot line up with these batches.

A span above the level returns one shared inert context manager: no attribute dict, no OTel span, nothing queued. A call span inside an unrecorded step span parents to the innermost anchor, the episode.

**Defaults.** `bind`, used by a caller who asked for telemetry (`eval run --timing`), records at `step` unless the environment names a level: the timing report reads the step spans. `bind_from_env`, the sidecar that a recording run writes without being asked, records at `call` unless the environment names a level: that user did not ask for a profile and should not pay its latency. The changelog states this change. A level name that is not valid stops the run.

**Which level.** A span that opens once per control step, or more often, is `step`; every other span is `call`. So a span that code outside positronic opens records at both levels. The per-hold span of positronic#1296 opens once per chunk, so it takes the default `call` with no change there, and its parent is the episode at `call`.

**Other shape.** A table from span name to level in `telemetry_keys.py` would leave the call sites as they are, but puts the level away from the code that knows how often its span opens.

**Not covered.** The stdlib env-server writer of a simulation records every span at both levels. A timing sink outside a bind gets every span.

## Evidence

Cost of one span with two float attributes, `timeit`, best of 5 x 200,000 calls, `nice -n 19` on a shared 48-CPU box at load 90-110:

| Case | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| step span, bound at `call` (below the level) | — | 528 ns |
| step `record_span`, bound at `call` | — | 401 ns |
| `enabled(Level.STEP)`, bound at `call` | — | 87 ns |
| span, unbound | 1,387 ns | 595 ns |
| `record_span`, unbound | 1,498 ns | 459 ns |

author: virtualcodewarrior
body:
## What this does

An approved, conflict-free pull whose checks are still running no longer waits for a person — or for the next activation — to finish its merge. At the moment the row verifies **APPROVED + CLEAN with checks *pending***, the queue hands the merge to GitHub's own auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto --merge --delete-branch`), and a sweep every pass collects what the queueing became.

This implements the operator directive of 27 Nov: *"the factory should merge any fully approved PR that is passing CI and has no conflicts … It would even be better for it to enable auto-merge if that is enabled on the repo."*

## What does NOT move: the gate

The safety was never the merge call — `factory_merge` already re-reads review decision, `mergeable`, `mergeStateStatus` and every check at the moment of merging. What the directive retires is *who ends the wait*, and this moves only that:

- the enqueue **re-reads the same four facts** before asking GitHub, so an unapproved, dirty or red pull never reaches GitHub's queue at all;
- GitHub's queue is *more* conservative than a shell loop could be: it merges at check-completion only if the pull is **still** approved and clean then — a re-verification between activations no pass can perform;
- the plain direct arm stays: a row that re-reads fully green at verification still merges on the spot. The two arms cover the two moments — at verification, and at completion.

## The mechanics

- **Capability is asked, never assumed.** `.allow_auto_merge` over the same REST shim every read uses; a repository that does not enable auto-merge fails closed to the old plain wait, journalling `AUTO-ENQUEUE-REPO-NO`. `--merge` is pinned because this repo's settings (`allow_squash_merge=false`, `allow_rebase_merge=false`) make any other named method a refusal.
- **Judged by read-back, not gh's exit** (`#1180` one remove from the merge): the enqueue is confirmed by `autoMergeRequest` answering on the pull; a null read-back journals `AUTO-ENQUEUE-REFUSED` with gh's stderr captured as the reason.
- **Once per pull**: stamped `pr:<n>.auto-enqueue`; an enqueued row is never re-offered.
- **The closeout is mandatory, not a courtesy.** A server-side merge is `#1180`'s phantom with GitHub's clothes — a thing that really happened leaving no journal. So the sweep runs `factory_merge_finalize` — the *same* finalize the direct arm runs — for completed merges: `AUTO-MERGED`, closure verification, worktree and branch retirement, byte-identical records whoever merged. Closed-unmerged drops (`AUTO-ENQUEUE-CLOSED`); an **unreadable** read is skipped **stamped** with rc 1 — dropping the stamp on a 404 is how a completed merge becomes an orphan tree; and a queueing re-read that answers `null` — auto-merge switched off behind the queue, or GitHub dropping it — journals `AUTO-ENQUEUE-CANCELLED` and clears both stamps so the offer re-presents; an **unreadable** queueing read keeps them, because guessing there orphans a real queueing.
- **Knob**: `FACTORY_AUTO_ENQUEUE=0` declines loudly (`AUTO-ENQUEUE-OFF` every pass), per the H-0409 rule that a capability which quietly stops running is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Five defects the legs and the suite measured into existence (H-0411)

1. **awk ate the escapes**: the leg's extraction built its pattern through `awk -v pat="^fn\\(\\)"`; `-v` consumes one backslash level, `()` arrived at awk as an *empty group*, and the extract grabbed the `…_offer` heading before `factory_auto_enqueue`. Extraction now compares literal prefixes and fails closed when a name appears twice.
2. **redirects open before commands run**: `2>"$gh_err"` into an absent `$FACTORY_RUN` fails the merge command *before gh runs* — gh_reason stays empty and the enqueue is refused for a reason that is nothing about the pull. A `mkdir` on the same command line cannot help; the directory is created on its own line and an unopenable scratch file refuses the enqueue loudly.
3. **The sweep compared a REST answer against a GraphQL spelling.** `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N` answers `.state` as `closed`; the queueing read tested it against `"CLOSED"`, the `PullRequestState` value nothing in this harness queries. A queueing that closed unmerged therefore never dropped. The first repair moved the *fixture* to match the code, so this entry recorded that repair as the measurement — corrected by the review, see below; `factory_close_read` already normalises at the boundary and the queueing read now does the same.
4. **The suite caught what the leg could not**: splitting `awaiting_merge` out of the dispatcher's joined wait-list line silently blinded an unrelated *mutation control* — the one that blinds `mergeability_pending` out of that line by literal count and demands the row arrive `UNKNOWN-CLASS`. The count went 1→0, the control `exit 3`, and the run died INCOMPLETE at 579 legs with zero FAILs. Shape-locked controls are canaries for exactly this; the control now carries the line's current shape (same blinding, same verdict) and says why in its own comment.
5. **The same suite reddened a shipped shape-leg** — `cv_leg_call_site`, which proves the closeout's ledger stamp precedes the closure verify inside `factory_merge`. The split moved both lines into `factory_merge_finalize`, so the leg's window found nothing. The contract is unchanged; where it lives moved. The rewritten leg holds stamp-before-verify INSIDE `finalize` and demands `factory_merge` reach the closeout through exactly ONE finalize call — falsified with four mutants plus the deleted-call control: swapped lines (906>900), removed verify (empty), removed call (count 0), duplicated call (count 2), each red on its named clause, the shipped tree green at `900<906, calls=1`.

Also hardened in the leg itself: claim bodies run inside `if "$@"`, where errexit is off — every standalone assertion now gates with `|| return 1`, so no intermediate failure can hide behind a later `return 0`.

## Verification

- `factory/selftest.d/006-auto-enqueue-arm.sh` — fourteen claims through a fake `gh` that records **every** call: enqueue lands and stamps; repo refusal; non-pending shapes make no call; no double-offer; knob off; read-back null refuses; dry run rehearses without write or stamp; completed merge runs the closeout incl. closure verification; closed drops; unreadable keeps stamp + rc 1; pending keeps its stamp and escalates on the *enqueue's* clock; a vanished pull is cancelled and both stamps clear; and a control that strips `ascii_upcase` out of the extracted arm at runtime demands the closed-drop go **red** — arm and fixture can no longer drift apart quietly.
- Red proof is fail-closed: the runner names the tree it ran, refuses a tree that already ships the functions under test (`PRECONDITION-FAIL`, rc 70 on `origin/main`) — the H-0409 lesson that a red control must die loudly rather than pass vacuously.
- Full `make verify` on `c024a00`: **1097 passed, 0 failed**, `MAKE_VERIFY_EXIT_CODE=0`, fixture root `/tmp/plock-factoryselftest-ztXQ9n` on tmpfs (git 2.53.0) — selftest is the last layer of the `verify` recipe, it ended with that summary, and the log carries zero `make: ***` lines. (The run's `Killed` lines are the shipped proc-pass fixture's own `timeout --kill-after` kills at `factory/selftest.sh:3980` — wedged-tick controls whose existence is itself a leg; they reproduce identically on a clean rerun.)

**Does not close an issue** (none open). This pull removes the human wait for *target-queue* merges once approval+clean+green hold; the harness-queue sweep keeps its asks-only boundary, so nothing in this repo self-merges this pull, and the merge is still the operator's call.

Decision: H-0411 (entry: `factory/DECISIONS/H-0411.md`, checkpoint `cf6ddb2` beneath fix `1c077cb`; the review correction rides fix `c024a00`).

Four findings. Each was reproduced before anything was changed.

author: smagala
body:
## Summary

**`modules/amd-ph-core/fastplong` (new):** a fork of nf-core/fastplong with one change.
- fastplong, 0.7.1 (the latest release) and earlier, leaves a zero-byte file for an output it writes no reads to:
  - `--failed_out` when no read fails;
  - `--out` when every read does.
- A zero-byte file is not valid gzip, so anything reading it fails with "unexpected end of file". fastp had the same bug until 1.4.0.
- The module now rewrites such a file as a valid empty gzip. Inputs, outputs, container and arguments are unchanged from nf-core.
- The new tests cover the no-failure case (quality and length filtering off). That test fails without the fix: the failed-reads file comes back with 0 bytes.
- `fastq_trim_merge` now uses the fork. nf-core modules aren't patched in place.

**`deacon/filter`: CPU split and `$args2`.**
- On the bgzip path, deacon and every bgzip stream each got `task.cpus`, so a pair ran three times as many threads as CPUs.
- They now share them: half to deacon, half split across the bgzip streams.
- bgzip takes `task.ext.args2`, and `meta.yml` gives it `args_id: "$args2"`.
- The output doesn't change: BGZF blocks are the same at any thread count, and deacon runs `--ordered`.
- The existing BGZF test runs the bgzip path and matches its snapshot.

**Join guards:** the one-to-one joins in `bam_to_fastq`, `fastq_trim_merge` and `qqq_read_prep` now use `failOnMismatch: true, failOnDuplicate: true`.
- Each pairs outputs of the same tasks on the same key, so a mismatch is a bug.
- Before, the unmatched item was dropped silently.

**Public-repo wording:** comments in `deacon/filter`, `bbmap/bbduk`, `rasusa/reads` and `samtools/collatefastq` no longer name an internal platform or configuration repository.

## Test plan

- [x] `fastplong` (3 tests, new snapshot). The no-failure test fails with the fix removed.
- [x] `deacon/filter` (6 tests), including the BGZF path.
- [x] Subworkflow tests: `bam_to_fastq` (1), `fastq_trim_merge` (3), `fastq_dehost` (7), `qqq_read_prep` (3).
- [x] nf-core lint:
  - `fastplong`: 0 failures. Its 2 warnings come with nf-core's container pin and meta format, which the fork keeps.
  - `fastq_trim_merge` and `qqq_read_prep`: 0 failures. `bam_to_fastq` has its one known `main_nf_include` warning.
  - `deacon/filter`: only the existing `container_links` failure.
- [x] prettier is clean.

body:
Card #1183 of the VMLab board.

ists the finished block keeps, plus its box.
- **Region drop.** The region is now four parts of 16 MiB, and a full region drops only the part written longest ago. Jumps linked into the dropped part go back to their stubs. A new JIT test covers this.
- **Region size stays 64 MiB.** Recompiles after a drop now cost about 0.6 to 0.8 s of a boot. Keeping all of a boot's code would need 256 MiB per vCPU for at most a 1 to 1.4 % gain.
- **Recorded.** The results are in the new section "J11, measured by card J11" of `hv/docs/plans/phase-3e-aarch64-jit/DESIGN.md`, and H13c is rewritten. 26 rows went into `hv/bench/history/aarch64.jsonl` with the note "card J11". The bench ran from trees exported without git, so I filled in each row's commit field afterwards; the note says so.

**Measured (helios, before `f0d5a25e`, after `33c67ec8`):**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Heap calls per compile (`tests/alloc.rs`, 603 blocks) | 117.6 | 0 |
| Heap calls per translation | 71.2 | 13.5 |
| Compile time, 1 vCPU boot at 18.0e9 instructions | 8.0 to 8.5 s (7.3 to 7.8 µs a compile) | 1.53 to 1.60 s (1.6 to 1.7 µs) |
| Translation time, same point | 2.50 to 2.67 s | 1.86 to 2.09 s |
| Recompiles after a region drop | 608k to 617k | 444k to 478k |
| Compile time, 4 vCPU boot (vCPUs summed) | 9.9 to 14.2 s | 2.1 to 2.2 s |
| Boot to agent ready, 1 vCPU, side-by-side pair (median of 3) | 68.66 s | 58.38 s |

- **Boot runs done one after the other** differ by less than the before side's spread (24 to 29 s). The host load changed between them, and this card's own merge bar ran during some of them.
- **Flat CoreMark and the scalar loop** ran the same within noise, as expected.
- **K3 on a Debian boot (1 vCPU, `VMLAB_HV_JIT_CHECK_RUNS=1000`)** reached agent ready in 132.3 s with no difference, over 121.2M checked runs.
- **K2** (`tests/jit.rs`) passes.

**Open:**
- **J10 overlap.** J10 is not in `next`, but the card says J11 is released after J10 is merged. Both cards change the Rust loop in `exec.rs`, so merging may conflict.
- **Profile not repeated.** I did not re-run the J9a profile, so the share of the boot spent in translation and in libc after this change is not measured.
- **bench-check.** `bench/check.py --arch aarch64` reports 5 regressions on QEMU and interpreter rows that were already in the history, none from my rows.
- **Shared code changed.** I changed shared code in `vmlab-hv-tcg-ir` (new `Lowering::reset`, `Graph::clear`, `Graph::retain_into`, `BlockOf::clear`, `schedule::scalars_into`, `dce::prune_scalars_with`). I also changed `LazyCondition::cases` in the JIT crate from a `Vec` to a borrowed table.

- **Changed:** compile counters by cause; emitter, shape, lifter and lowering buffers reused per CPU and per JIT; a full region drops only its oldest quarter; results in DESIGN.md J11 and the bench history.
- **Check:** `stc check card-1183` (`just ci::check`) on `a799b2d8`, exit 0, 5214 passed, 0 failed, 256 ignored. No flaky test failed.

body:
Atiende lo de comparables del video 8.13 (27 nov). Aplica a todos los mercados (venta, renta, terrenos en venta y en renta) y, donde cabe, a maquinaria.

## Qué cambia para el valuador

- **Búsqueda aproximada (06:14).** Al escribir «Bugambilias» en Colonia (o en Fraccionamiento, o en el texto) aparecen «Ciudad Bugambilias», «Bugambilias Segunda Sección», «Bugambilias 1a Secc.»… También si se escribe mal («Buganbilias», «Bugambilas»), sin acentos o con otra grafía («2a» = «segunda», «fracc.» = «fraccionamiento», «cd» = «ciudad»). Colonia y fraccionamiento se buscan uno en el otro. Igual en «Buscar comparables», en la página Comparables y en su mapa.
- **La ubicación es la misma en todos lados (07:16–11:15).**
  - El pin que se pone y guarda en un avalúo queda en todas las fichas de ese comparable (mismo número C-…): la búsqueda desde otro avalúo, «Ver ficha» y los mapas lo muestran de inmediato, aunque después se quite del mercado.
  - Un comparable sin pin pero con dirección muestra su **ubicación aproximada** (círculo punteado y la leyenda «ubicación aproximada») en su ficha desde el mercado, desde la búsqueda y en Comparables, en la captura, y en el mapa de la búsqueda (círculo translúcido). «Buscar alrededor de» también lo encuentra. **Cómo se guarda (términos de Google y matriz legal):** la respuesta de Google no se escribe en el comparable ni en el avalúo. Vive en una caché temporal del despacho (campo personalizado `UBICACION_APROXIMADA_CACHE`, por ficha, con `geocodedAt`) y se usa 30 días como máximo; pasado ese plazo se ignora y se vuelve a buscar al mostrarla, con el mismo límite de búsquedas. Nunca es un pin, no se copia a otros comparables ni versiones y no se imprime (dictamen, PDF ni memoria). Si cambia la dirección o se pone un pin, se olvida. El pin que pone el valuador sí es dato suyo y se guarda y comparte entre sus fichas.
- **Mapas grandes (11:17).** El mapa de la ficha y el de la captura ocupan todo el ancho y son más altos; «Ver mapa grande» los abre casi a pantalla completa (en la captura se puede poner el pin ahí). En «Buscar comparables» el mapa va a todo el ancho de la ventana con su panel debajo, y también tiene «Ver mapa grande».
- **Estados con color (12:25).** En «Editar estados» se agrega, borra o renombra un estado y se elige su color entre diez (los cinco de siempre y violeta, naranja, celeste, azul vivo y marino), con muestras y una vista previa de la etiqueta. El color se ve en la revisión, en la ficha y en cada renglón del mercado.
- **Revisión por mercado (12:39).** Abierta desde un mercado, primero aparecen sus comparables («El mercado que abriste») y después los demás. Cada mercado tiene un título grande con su color (el mismo de su pestaña) que se queda fijo arriba mientras se recorren sus comparables.
- **Revisión en lote (13:44).** Casillas para elegir comparables, «Seleccionar todos» y «Seleccionar los de terrenos en venta» (o del mercado que sea). Abajo aparece una barra fija: estado (cualquiera, con su color), «Marcar todas las casillas de la lista» y «Guardar revisión de N», una sola vez para todos. La revisión uno por uno sigue igual.
- **Mismas funciones en cada mercado (05:31).** Venta, renta y terrenos comparten el mismo panel: «Exportar Excel» aparece al haber comparables en todos (como vio en rentas). Maquinaria ahora también tiene «Exportar Excel» de sus ofertas.

## Migración

No trae migración. La ubicación aproximada es una caché temporal (30 días) en un campo personalizado del despacho, fuera del avalúo, y la búsqueda aproximada usa `pg_trgm`, que ya instala la migración 001.

## Rutas nuevas

- `POST /api/mapas/comparables/aproximar`: ubica por dirección los comparables sin pin (usa la llave de Google del servidor, con el límite de geocodificación por usuario).
- `PUT /api/avaluos/[id]/mercado/revision`: revisión en lote.
- `GET /api/avaluos/[id]/maquinaria/exportar`: Excel de las ofertas de maquinaria.

Documentadas en `docs/ROUTES.md` y `docs/COMPARABLES.md`.

## Qué no se pudo verificar o queda pendiente

- El mapa de Google en «Buscar comparables» no carga en local (la llave del navegador rechaza `localhost`); se revisó el acomodo, pero los círculos aproximados en ese mapa hay que verlos en producción. Los mapas de la ficha y la captura (OpenStreetMap) sí se revisaron con capturas.
- En local no se llamó a Google para geocodificar: las pruebas usan un geocodificador falso.
- **Fuera de alcance por ahora:** «Buscar comparables» y «Revisión de comparables» para las ofertas de maquinaria (sus ofertas viven en el cálculo, no como comparables del avalúo).
- Los comparables que ya tenían un pin guardado en una ficha que luego se quitó del mercado se recuperan al abrir el mapa o la ficha (se toma el pin de otra ficha del mismo número).

author: teuschop
body:
## Qué veía el cliente

Al reservar (y en el cobro/webhook de Culqi al confirmar el pago) la respuesta esperaba a que saliera el correo. Si el servidor SMTP no responde, nodemailer espera ~10 s y falla; antes de eso el proxy de la web corta y el cliente ve **error 502 al reservar o pagar**, aunque la reserva sí se creó. En los logs de staging: "request aborted" y luego "Email booking_created failed: Connection timeout".

## Qué cambia

- `NotificationsService.sendEmail` sigue creando la fila `notification` en el momento (con el `db` que reciba, así queda dentro de la transacción del llamador si la hay), pero el envío SMTP, el título del tour y el paso a `SENT`/`FAILED` van a la `BackgroundQueue` y la llamada vuelve de inmediato.
- La parte en segundo plano usa siempre `this.prisma`, nunca el cliente de la transacción. Mantiene el mismo manejo de errores y la redacción de correos (`redactEmails`).
- Si la cola está llena, la fila queda `FAILED` con "Cola de envío llena; no se envió" en vez de perderse sin rastro.
- Se arregla una sola vez, en el servicio: todos los que llaman (creación de reserva, pagos, ciclo de vida, vencimiento, "mi reserva", reclamos, contacto, alertas al staff) dejan de depender del SMTP sin tocarlos.
- `QueueModule` ya es global en `AppModule`, no hizo falta importarlo.
- La evidencia de disputas (`evidence.service.ts`) solo lista los correos `SENT`; se arma mucho después, así que no cambia.

## Pruebas

- Unitarias de `NotificationsService`: vuelve antes de enviar, el envío llega después, un fallo queda `FAILED` y redactado, la fila se crea con el `db` recibido y se actualiza con `prisma`, y la cola llena marca `FAILED`.
- e2e: se espera a la cola (`BackgroundQueue.drain()`) antes de revisar los correos enviados en admin, bookings y compliance.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` (313), `npm run build` y `npm run test:e2e` (304) pasan.

## Límite conocido

La cola es en memoria: si el proceso se reinicia con correos pendientes, esas filas quedan en `QUEUED`.

author: goetchstone
body:
## What

A money-tier item from the back-office audit of 2026-11-17 (batch 4 of its plan): the customer ledger, the record of what each customer owes.

### One writer at a time per customer

A ledger write reads the customer's stored balance, writes rows that carry it forward, and stores the new balance. Nothing held the customer between the read and the write:

- two payments for one customer at the same moment each read the same balance, and the stored total lost one of them;
- two backfills of one customer each counted no entries and each wrote the whole history;
- a payment landing during a backfill was overwritten by the total the backfill stored at the end.

`appendEntry` and the backfill now take the customer's row first (`lockCustomerForLedger`, a `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). The write that follows already locked that row; this moves the lock ahead of the read.

### The backfill

The backfill builds a customer's ledger from their imported orders and payments. It is run once per store, at onboarding.

- **It treated any existing entry as proof it had already run.** A customer whose one entry was a payment taken before the backfill ran was skipped as clean, diff 0, and their history left out for good. It now counts only its own rows. A customer with entries from before it ran, and none of its own, is handed back for review with the gap between their stored balance and what their orders and payments say; nothing is written. The screen counts them as "Left for review".
- **It wrote a quote as money owed.** Only a sale is owed (`isRevenueStatus`: ORDER, FULFILLED, RETURNED). A deposit taken on a quote still counts as paid.
- **It wrote an unpaid payment link as money received**, and that stayed if the link was later voided. Only money in hand is a payment (`isPaymentExcludedFromBalance`, the list every other balance reads).

The same two rules apply to `computeSourceBalance`, the figure the daily drift check and the backfill compare the ledger against. Each order's `status` is now required by its type, so a caller that leaves it out does not compile.

### One more flaky test, fixed where it starts

`errorRecorder.integration.test.ts` timed out "waiting for the ErrorEvent row to reach count 2" in this branch's first local coverage run. Its helper polled the database for the new count and then let the next record in. The recorder drops a record that arrives while it is still busy with the one before, and it stays busy after the row is written, while it alerts. When the poll's answer came back first, the next record was dropped. The helpers now wait for the recorder itself (`errorWritesSettled`) before the next record, and a new case holds the alert at a gate to show the drop on purpose. This test is on main, so it can fail any PR's run the same way until this merges.

## Not verified

- Lock order was reasoned through, not exercised. `appendEntry`'s own update already took the customer's row, so no new lock is held; it is only taken earlier.
- The backfill has not been run on a store's real import. The tests use small made-up customers.

## Tests

The full coverage gate ran locally on the branch tip (587fb6cf) and passed: the unit suite and all 204 integration files, Statements 74.29, Branches 63.26, Functions 76.8, Lines 75.68. The first run, before the error-recorder fix, failed on that test alone.

- `customerLedgerLocking.integration.test.ts` (new, 6 cases, real database). A second connection holds the customer's row, so two writers are lined up one behind the other on purpose:
  - two payments at the same moment both reach the stored balance, in one chain;
  - a payment landing during a backfill is added to the backfill's total, not written over by it;
  - two backfills at once write the history once;
  - a customer with an earlier entry is handed back for review with the real gap (-700), and listed by the run;
  - a customer the backfill has written is still skipped on the next run;
  - neither a quote nor an unpaid payment link is ledgered.
- `errorRecorder.integration.test.ts`: 11 cases, run three times in a row after the fix; the new case shows a record arriving while the recorder is busy being dropped, and the next one taken.
- Unit: the event builder leaves out a pending payment and writes no SALE for a quote, and its events add up to `computeSourceBalance`; `computeSourceBalance` owes nothing on a quote's or a cancelled order's lines.
- Watched failing, then passing: with `customerLedger.ts` and `customerLedgerBackfill.ts` as they are on main, five of the six database cases and the four new unit cases fail (the sixth holds either way). On the branch they pass, among the seventeen suites that write the ledger (282 tests in all).
- In a headless browser against the dev build, with the two endpoints' answers stood in: the backfill screen shows "Left for review (ledger entries from before this ran)" with its count, and lists that customer under "Drifted customers".

## Trace (Rule 45)

- `appendEntry` is called five times, from `paymentService.ts`, `returns/bookReturn.ts` and `billing/invoiceService.ts`. Its signature is unchanged.
- `computeSourceBalance` is called from the backfill and `customerArDrift.ts`; the drift runner's query now selects `status` and passes it.
- `backfillCustomerLedger` and `backfillAllCustomers` are called from the one admin route. The route's answer gains `customersNeedingReview`; `CustomerLedgerBackfillView.tsx` is its only reader.
- `isRevenueStatus` is new in `salesOrderRevenue.ts`, beside `isCountedLine`.

## Scans: lint, Semgrep, OSV, CodeQL (Rule 48)

Lint: no new warnings; each changed file was compared with its copy on main. Semgrep and the dependency scan were not run locally; no dependency changed. CI runs all of them.

## Docs (Rule 36)

`docs/domains/accounting.md` (one writer per customer, what is owed, and what is still missing), `tools.md` (the backfill's idempotency, as it now is), `returns.md` (one line), and the stale comment on `selectCustomersForCheck`, which described a cold-start fallback that does not exist.

## Left open

- **Nothing posts a SALE to the ledger when a quote becomes an order**, so the drift check reports every sale made after the backfill. That is the audit's next ledger item; it waits on one decision: what an edit or cancel after submit posts.
- A customer handed back for review is not backfilled around their existing entries. Someone has to look.
- After a backfill the daily drift check looks at no one until there is activity; checking them needs their ids passed in.

body:
## Summary

The gene page now hides the "prevalence data" section only for "Other Biomarkers" (`entrezGeneId === -2`). Before, it was hidden for every gene with `entrezGeneId <= 0`.

## Problem

`SomaticGermlineGenePage` required `entrezGeneId > 0` before showing the prevalence data section. That also hid it for curated genes with other negative IDs, such as `CDKN2A (p14)` (`-1029`).

## Root cause

The `entrezGeneId > 0` check was meant to exclude "Other Biomarkers", but it covered every non-positive ID.

## Fix approach

Changed the check to `entrezGeneId !== -2` and added a comment saying `-2` is used for "Other Biomarkers". The section still needs at least one prevalence record and still doesn't show on germline pages.

## Testing

- `npx prettier --check src/main/webapp/app/pages/genePage/SomaticGermlineGenePage.tsx`: passes. The pre-commit lint-staged hook also passed.
- No manual check of the gene page in a browser.

## Risk / Rollout

Low. Genes with negative IDs other than `-2` now show the section only if they have prevalence data. `CDKN2A (p14)` currently returns 0 records from `/utils/mutationMapperData`, so it stays hidden for now.

## Related issues

No issue filed. This comes from user feedback that the CDKN2A prevalence plot shows the p14 transcript.

This PR does **not** fix that report. The CDKN2A prevalence data is in p16INK4a coordinates (ENST00000304494, which matches OncoKB's CDKN2A isoform). But `AnnotationStore.ts` passes `isoformOverrideSource: 'mskcc'` to the mutation mapper, and Genome Nexus resolves that to p14ARF (ENST00000579755, 132 aa) for CDKN2A. That problem is still open.

body:
Fixes M1 and M4 being solvable by pressing an arrow key.

M1 (number) and M4 (date) used `min` = `max` to make one answer the only valid one. Browsers let you step these fields with arrow keys, the scroll wheel or the spinner, and stepping always lands on a value the field accepts, so it went straight to the answer. Any range or step limit has the same weakness.

Both are now text inputs with exact patterns, like Rooms 1 and 5:
- M1 accepts `3` or `three`.
- M4 accepts `1996-08-21`, `19960821`, `21/08/1996`, `21.8.1996`, `21-08-1996`, `08/21/1996`, `21 August 1996`, `21 Aug 1996` and `August 21, 1996`.

Wrong-answer messages now appear as you type, like the other text rooms, and these two panels no longer shake.

`build-plan.md` has a new rule: never give a single answer as a range or step limit.

Tested in headless Chromium: arrow keys leave both fields empty, all eleven date formats are accepted, wrong dates are rejected, and the track still finishes.

Upstream's ea3328c50c ("perf(web): one shared tooltip serves every trigger in the app", in 5258..5332) moved its tooltips to `SharedTooltipTrigger`: one tooltip at the root that each trigger points at. The fork's own components still mounted a Base UI `Tooltip`/`TooltipTrigger`/`TooltipPopup` each, one per row in the Tracker's lists and per agent message in the timeline.

## Changes

- `UnreadFromHere.tsx`: Mark unread from here uses `SharedTooltipTrigger`, the same as the timestamp next to it in `AssistantMessageMeta`, which upstream already switched.
- `ParkedContextChip.tsx`: built like `EnvironmentContextChip.tsx`. Its `whitespace-pre-wrap` is kept through `className`.
- `ThreadArtifacts.tsx`: a row's Open in browser and Copy link.

author: ausboss
body:
## What

`tools/setup-remote-control.sh`: run it once per machine (arch5090, arch3090) so project sessions can start Remote Control with nobody at the keyboard. Running it again only reports what's already in place.

1. **Name**: devices show up under their hostname. If the hostname follows `<prefix><4 digits>` and the digits don't match the GPU (an `arch5090` with an RTX 3090), it renames the host with `hostnamectl` and fixes the loopback lines in `/etc/hosts`.
2. **Blocking variables**: it comments out `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS` and `DISABLE_GROWTHBOOK`, with backups. It checks shell profiles, fish, `environment.d`, `/etc/environment` and the `env` block of `~/.claude/settings.json`, and also unsets them in the systemd user environment. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the token variables only get a warning.
3. **Settings**: it merges allow rules and a short deny list into `~/.claude/settings.json`. It also marks the folder as trusted in `~/.claude.json` and answers "Enable Remote Control", so the server never waits on a prompt.
4. **Service**: it installs `~/.config/systemd/user/claude-remote-control.service`, which runs `claude remote-control` in `~/code/ausboss`. The service restarts on failure, keeps running after logout and at boot (linger), and starts with the blocking variables unset. It creates the folder if it's missing and keeps mise/asdf shims on the service's PATH.
5. **Check**: it prints the name, the service state and any error from the journal.

`docs/remote-control-setup.md` records the causes, the verified facts and the tradeoffs.

## Testing

body:
## Summary
Follows #875, which made `POST /api/dlq/retry-matching` and `/purge-matching` submit batch operations. The CLI and Python client bulk DLQ actions now do the same: the maintenance leader applies the operation a chunk at a time, where these commands used to retry or purge every matching row in one transaction.

**CLI**
- `awa dlq retry-bulk` and `awa dlq purge` submit a `retry_from_dlq` or `purge_dlq` operation (`submitted_by: "cli"`), print its id and state, and say how to follow it with `awa batch-ops get <id>`.
- `--wait` polls the operation until it is completed, cancelled or failed, prints its `processed`, `skipped` and `errored` counters and `last_error`, and exits non-zero if it failed.
- The filter flags, `--all` and the production confirmation are unchanged. The CLI no longer records `awa.job.dlq_retried` or `dlq_purged` for these commands; the maintenance leader records them as it applies the operation.

**Python** (breaking return types)
- `bulk_retry_from_dlq` and `purge_dlq`, async and sync, submit an operation (`submitted_by: "python"`) and return it as the dict `submit_batch_operation` returns, instead of a count.
- `purge_dlq` no longer takes `before_id` or `before_dlq_at`. Batch-operation filters have no DLQ position bound, so the cursor purge moved to the new `purge_dlq_before` (async and sync). It takes the same arguments, raises `ValueError` unless at least one cursor argument is given, deletes in one transaction and returns the count.
- `python -m awa dlq retry-all` and `dlq purge` print the submitted operation.

Out of scope: single-row `retry_from_dlq` and `purge_dlq_job`, `awa dlq move` and `bulk_move_failed_to_dlq`. The `awa_model::dlq` bulk functions and `/api/dlq/bulk-retry` and `/bulk-purge` are unchanged.

`BatchOperationState::as_str` is now public so the CLI can print the state.

## Testing
- New `awa-cli/tests/dlq_bulk_cli_test.rs`. It checks that `retry-bulk --queue` submits a pending `retry_from_dlq` operation and leaves the DLQ untouched, that an unscoped `retry-bulk` is refused and submits nothing, and that `purge --wait` reports the finished operation's counters and removes only the matching row.
- Python: `test_dlq.py`, `test_job_filter.py` and `test_cli.py` were updated for the new return types, the `purge_dlq_before` cursor purge and its `ValueError`. `test_batch_operations.py` passes unchanged. 40 passed locally against PostgreSQL 18.
- `cargo test -p awa-cli`; `cargo clippy -D warnings` for `awa-cli`, `awa-model` and `awa-python`; `cargo fmt --check`.

body:
## Summary

T3 Code runs Antigravity with its own data root, so every Antigravity session started from T3 Code was missed: the collector read `~/.gemini` only, and the data site showed no Antigravity at all.

```diff
 collectUsage
   extractClaude(~/.claude/projects)
   extractPi(~/.pi)
-  extractAntigravity(~/.gemini)
+  extractAntigravity(
+    ~/.gemini
+    ~/.t3/userdata/providers/antigravity      # brain/<conversation>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl
+  )                                           # one call: model inference and dedupe span both roots
```

- The walk moves to `src/stores/antigravity.ts` (file access stays out of `extract/`).
- `transcript_full.jsonl` and the chunk copies (`logs/chunks/*/00000001.jsonl`) are still never counted.
- A record in the same conversation under both roots counts once.
- `CollectOptions.home` lets the test point the collector at a synthetic tree.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `usage --since 2026-11-27T00:00Z` on the owner's machine produces 0 `antigravity` rows; `usage_hourly` holds only `claude`, `opencode-go` and `cursor`.
  **After:** the same run produces 73.8M Antigravity tokens over 5 hours (`gemini-4-neon-high`, `gemini-4-hydrogen-tiered-high`, `claude-opus-5-5-high`).
- `test/collect.test.ts` builds a synthetic tree (one conversation per root, plus `transcript_full.jsonl`, chunk copies and a chunk-only conversation) and checks the plan, the hour, the tokens and the inferred model. It also checks that a conversation in both roots counts once, and that `--since` skips an old T3 transcript.
- `bunx turbo run check --filter=@trajectonomics/data-collector`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `tooling/guards`: 473 pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** collector

New rows for plan `antigravity` start flowing at the next hourly run once the runner hosts' collector copy is updated. Missed hours before that are not backfilled.
