author: xuan-1998
body:
## Motivation

Closes #171. System 2 needs failures whose cause is known, each built from one clean release, so a diagnosis can be scored against the truth. The GPU gate table comes from one command, given under End-to-end.

## Changes

- `honing/backends/tank/faults.py`: a catalog of 17 faults and `build_library`, which builds each fault from one clean release and writes `library.json`. Each entry records id, cause, affected questions, expected symptom and artifact checksums (each harness file, the weights, the controller switch). The build refuses a fault that changes anything but its own cause's part.
  - harness (7): outputs of #186's `build-harness-faults.py` (disable_assistance, swap_fire_hold_descriptions, reverse_turn_words, extreme_standoff), plus three strategy-setting faults: penalize safe shots, reward shell danger, point-blank pursuit.
  - weights (6): the checkpoint before the clean fire edit, direction edits of -3 on weapon/fire and +3 on motion/stop_none, and sft on the teacher batch with weapon labels flipped, turns mirrored or every move relabeled stop, all through Honing's trainers. The faults config runs sft in deterministic mode, so the sft faults rebuild to the same checksums.
  - controller (3): outputs of #186's `build-controller-faults.py`, played through the new match switch.
  - chance (1): the clean release.
  - Not built: stripping one context field (plans mode needs the full context) and the shot guard (already off, and plans mode refuses it on).
- `gate_library`: plays each fault and the clean release on fresh val seeds, both seats, and keeps the fault when #166's `PairedIntervalSelector` would publish the clean release over it. It writes `gate.json` and a table.
- `integrations/tank-war/scripts/match.mjs`: test-only `--controller-fault-file`. `scripts/controller-faults.mjs` is the recorded Exp 0 v0 runtime, byte for byte (pinned in freeze.json). The manifest records `controller_fault_sha256`, and `private_fault_events.jsonl` lists each changed decision.
- `TankEpisodeRunner.with_controller_fault`, `scripts/e2e/tank_faults.py`, `configs/e2e/tank_faults_dry_run.json`, `configs/e2e/tank_faults_nanojev.json`.
- Tests: `tests/test_tank_faults.py`, `tests/test_tank_fault_weights.py` (torch, weight-edit job), `integrations/tank-war/tests/controller_faults.test.mjs`.
- `gpu_lock` lets a process take a GPU again that only its own CUDA context holds (the edit GPU after the first edit).
- `NanoJevTrainer` turns deterministic kernels on for its own job only and gives the process its setting back after it. Left on, it changed the kernels of a later direction edit in the same process.

#186's `build-weight-faults.py` is not reused: it rebuilds v0's two checkpoints from two fixed source checkpoints on ds-serv2, not from an arbitrary clean release. The reversed fire edit goes through Honing's direction-edit trainer instead, same formula, so its checksum differs from the freeze's.

## Compatibility and operational impact

None for existing runs. A match without the new flag behaves as before, and its manifest gains `controller_fault_sha256: null`. `TankEpisodeRunner.write_harness` is now a static method, and callers are unchanged.

## Verification

```
$ pytest tests --ignore=tests/test_example_tasks.py
2248 passed, 203 skipped, 81 subtests passed in 271.22s
$ pytest tests/test_weight_edit.py tests/test_direction_edit.py tests/test_decision_training.py tests/test_tank_fault_weights.py tests/test_tank_faults.py   # CPU torch
40 passed in 4.40s
$ cd integrations/tank-war && node --test tests/*.test.mjs
# pass 191
# fail 0
$ pre-commit run --files <changed files>; mypy honing
all hooks passed; Success: no issues found in 174 source files
```

On fakes the tests check that the library builds twice from one clean release with the same checksums, that every fault changes only its own part, that the harness and controller faults match #186's builders and reproduce all three `recorded_controller_sha256` values in the v0 freeze, that the gate keeps exactly the faults that lose on the stand-in match, and that the real direction-edit trainer changes only `scalar.weight`, by -3 units.

## End-to-end

Not run yet. It needs four GPUs:

```
(cd integrations/tank-war && npm ci)
HONING_NANOJEV_SOURCE=... HONING_NANOJEV_GPUS=0,1 HONING_NANOJEV_TRAIN_GPU=2 HONING_NANOJEV_EDIT_GPU=3 HF_HOME=... \
python scripts/e2e/tank_faults.py --config configs/e2e/tank_faults_nanojev.json --work-dir runs/tank-faults
```

64 rounds per fault (32 fresh val seeds, both seats) and the clean release on the same seeds, 2176 rounds in all, plus 16 teacher rounds, 3 sft jobs and 3 edits. A fault is kept when the 95% paired interval of fault minus clean is below zero.

GPU run on e05db48 (flame-10, about 2 h 30 min): 11 of 17 kept, 5 harness, 3 weights, 3 controller. The table is on #171. A rebuild check built the library twice in one process and once in another, and all 18 artifact sets matched.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted. I reviewed every changed line and ran the checks above.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and contains no unrelated cleanup.
- [x] The title is a valid Conventional Commits subject.
- [x] Tests cover behavior changes, or this pull request does not change behavior.
- [x] Public protocol changes include contract tests, or none are present.
- [x] The design specification under `system-design/` is updated, or the change does not affect it.
- [x] An accepted RFC is linked, or this change does not require one. (#138)
- [x] `pre-commit` on the changed files and `pytest` pass locally.
- [ ] The CI `e2e` job passes, and a GPU or in-game run is reported above when the change needs one.
- [x] An end-to-end run that trains (harness evolution or weight post-training) links its wandb log, or none was run.
- [x] Non-trivial AI assistance is disclosed above, or none was used.

author: eshin087
body:
The motion audit of the Starless Lord, Varr Nihil (ADR-251). **The owner's picks, from the films (2026-11-27): the form pass, the readable pace, Void Lightning `c` (the storm), the ignitions `a` (the cocoon).** All four are the defaults (`PICKED`); `?lordForm=0` / `?lordPace=0` / `?boltFx=0` / `?igniteFx=0` give back what `main` does.

## Measured first
Every move in **every form it is used in** (new opt-in `lord.mjs . formaudit`: a move compiled round another form's guard is not the move he plays there), through the shared sword audit's impact table (ADR-250's), plus the feet's true slide on the floor and the form-2 off-hand blade's arm. What was still off after ADR-226:

| | before | `?lordForm=a` |
|---|---|---|
| thrust elbow at impact | 121 - 140° | 154 - 157° |
| thrust point off the arm's line | 18 - 23° | 2 - 5° |
| long lunges' knees (front / back) | 176 / 176 (both locked) | 69 - 98 / 147 - 176 |
| two-handed overheads, the point's path off level | 71 - 80° (an upright bar at the game camera) | 43 - 61° (a diagonal) |
| low sweeps' feet | crossed by 0.73 - 0.85 m, a knee pop (630 - 645 mm/frame²) | never cross (+0.38 - 0.48 m) |
| front foot at the impact | in the air (15 - 25 cm) at about half the cuts | down at nearly every cut |

Already fine: his wrist on the blade (ADR-226), the blade clear of his body, the form-2 off-hand blade at its own blows (elbow 161 - 166°, 25 - 60° off the forearm). He has no kicks.

## What changes (`?lordForm=a`, the default; `0` = as before), all four forms
- **Thrusts:** the arm long and on the blade's line, out of a real lunge (front shin upright over the foot, back leg long). Forms 3 - 4 keep both hands on the hilt.
- **Overheads:** still two-handed (his way), raised over his sword shoulder and brought down across him to low at his left. Falling Star's landing chop the same, its somersault kept.
- **Low sweeps:** turn on his feet, the right leg sweeping the floor.
- **Free hand:** gathered at the chest and split away in opposition, half the travel it had.
- **Footfall:** the strike lands with the front foot (keyed, not left to the foot planner; the left foot in the strings' left-foot cuts).

Same windups, impacts, zones, cues and root motion: lord LORDFORM checks 187 realisations to the frame with the switch on and off.

## Pace (`?lordPace=a`, the owner's pick)
His shipped pace is the owner's own ("faster than Shen Hui and ramping": first blows from 0.4 s, a string's blows ~0.34 s apart in form 1, ~0.3 s in form 4), under COMBAT rule 10. `a` (Tian Lei's recipe, ADR-248): a move's first blow >= 0.7 s × the form's windup scale, blows >= 0.45 s apart, the cue 0.35 s before, the added time a held cock. His quick blows, counters, flurry, ignitions and spells keep theirs (rule 10 is the melee's floor; each spell cues itself).

Three lord checks that assumed the fast pace now read it: DATA (the gaps at the floor, the first blows sooner form by form: 0.70 > 0.66 > 0.62 > 0.58 s), TIMING (a contact on its own glint, 0.35 s for a blow, 0.26 s for a spell), FLARE (the parry bot presses off the beat's impact). Green on both paces. Known: the shared cue ledger's flash-fed entries and the Training room's answer time read `TUNING.flashLead`, so they place a paced blade blow 0.09 s early (the ledger also reads the running move exactly; Training's 122 situations pass); fixing them is shared code.

## Effect looks (picked: `boltFx=c`, `igniteFx=a`; heat in the fire field at his hand, arm, the bolt's line or round his feet; no cues of their own)
- **Void Lightning** `?boltFx=`:
  - `a` the thread (motes spiral into a white heart at his fingers; the bolt braided with two violet strands, a ring punched out at the hand)
  - `b` the tear (arcs crawl up his casting arm; the bolt leaves a dark seam with violet lips that comes apart upward)
  - `c` the storm (arcs creep along the floor round his feet; the bolt grounds three times along its line)
- **A form's ignition** `?igniteFx=`, over the shipped `?ignite=a`:
  - `a` the cocoon (a column of letters rises round him, then bursts out flat)
  - `b` the writ (the new steel written in light where it will stand, then torn off as letters)
  - `c` the eclipse (a ring of dark spreads round him; its red rim stands up as a wall)
- A chosen bolt look draws the windup at his hand in place of the shipped gather (the two together were one white flare).
- `0` = as they shipped. Cost: at most ~200 more blobs at peak (the field holds 6000).

## Found, not changed (asked)
- **Grasp and Sever:** when the hero rolls the pull clear (the right answer), the chop's shared step-in carries him 3.4 m over planted feet: a skate, in every form. The fix (a dash like Severance's) changes the beat's root motion, so it waits for the owner.
- The strings' close-in between blows slides the feet 0.5 - 2 m a string (as before; the planner is the hero animator's).
- In form 2 the off-hand blade points back along the left forearm (up to 157°) through the two-handed chops.

## Shared code
None changed in behaviour.
- `duelist/*`, `player/*` and `tellPose.js` are untouched: `keysOf`, `recoveryKeysOf`, `animOpts` and `kit.motion` were already kit options.
- `swordAudit.mjs` is byte-for-byte the version in PR eshin087/gcd#177 (fields only), so the two merge cleanly.

## Tests
- New lord scenario LORDFORM (the anatomy at the impacts, timings on/off, every effect option finite and cheap).
- New opt-in `formaudit` (every move in every form; `GCD_AUDIT_IMPACT=1` prints the impact table).
- `npm test` green locally (under the batch's shared lock), with the picks as the defaults.

## Films
- Before / after, forms 1 - 4: each a 2×2 (game camera before | after, over close-from-his-side before | after), real and half speed.
- The effect looks: a 2×2 of `0 | a` over `b | c`, at the game camera (and side-on for the bolt).
- Sent to the owner in the session; the picks came from them.

author: christian-agent
body:
## Summary

Until now, a session's name showed the task's name but not where the task stood. With this change the name begins with an icon for the task's state, for example `🔍 my-task`. The states are working 🔨, in review 🔍, needs the operator 🟡, waiting on a PR ⏳, blocked ⛔, parked 💤 and done ✅. When a task is in more than one state, one icon wins. The order, from highest: done, blocked, parked, needs the operator, waiting, review, working. The session is renamed each time the state changes. That rename also replaces a name the operator typed by hand.

This PR does not include renaming the T3 thread. That work waits for a separate change, `wf-t3-rename-sync`, which has not merged yet. A small follow-up will reuse the same name there, without a second rename call.

To verify: run `npm test`. It should report every test passing (777 core tests and 248 plugin tests when this was reviewed).

## Details

- `taskTitle(task)` and `TASK_ICONS` in `tools/ledger/awareness.ts` compute the name in one place. `sessionTitle`, `listed()` (adds a per-ledger `title` field to `session --json`) and `promptSubmit` all use it.
- `promptSubmit` skips the rename when the session already has that name.

author: maximilian-maag
body:
Stacked on #214 (which is stacked on #213); retarget to `dev` when the queue lands.

Only **one spec of twenty-six** ever exercised the interface's sign-in code (`auth.e2e.spec.ts`).
The other 96 tests ran in the shape `make run` starts in — no issuer, `authGuard` inert — so a
hundred assertions about screens were in fact assertions about a deployment nobody runs: an
open API with nothing to sign in to.

## What changed

- `e2e/session.ts` exports the `test` every spec imports. An automatic fixture signs the tab in
  **before the spec body**, and gets there the way a clerk does: the guard's redirect, the login
  screen's one action, the IdP's answer, the callback's exchange. It seeds nothing —
  `sessionStorage` is written by the application's own callback, not by the fixture.
- The IdP is stubbed at the network edge (discovery, authorize → 302 with a code, token), the
  same shapes the old `auth.e2e.spec.ts` stubs used; that helper now lives in `session.ts` so
  there is one stub implementation, not two.
- A default empty `/api` answer is installed before signing in, so a screen with no stub of its
  own still renders — and, decisively, so no request reaches a real API and comes back 401
  (which would correctly delete the session half-way through the fixture). A spec's own route
  is registered later and wins.
- All 25 other specs import `test`/`expect` from `./session`; `auth.e2e.spec.ts` keeps
  `@playwright/test` and the four states that exist *before* a session, including "a deployment
  without an issuer runs without a login screen" — now the deliberate exception rather than the
  suite's ambient assumption.

## Verified

`npx playwright test --reporter=line` → **100 passed (35.7s)**, against `ng serve` with the
running stack's API stubbed per spec. `make frontend-e2e` runs the same command, so CI's `e2e`
job needs no change: everything is still stubbed at the network edge, no Keycloak required.

One trap worth knowing, since it cost a run: a comment containing `**/api/**` ends the block
comment at the `*/` inside it and the rest is parsed as code. The docstring now says it in words.

## Still open (deliberate, needs a decision)

The open mode itself is unchanged. The real exposure is not this suite but the **Helm chart**:
`deploy/helm/campus-erp/values.yaml` ships `config.oidc.jwksUrl: ""` and no template says
`required`, so a `helm install` with defaults deploys an API that answers without a token.
Failing closed belongs there (and/or in `cmd/api`), not in the tests — see the thread on #213.

author: real-fruit-snacks
body:
The forty-four playbooks of v2026.11.25 went in with their own shorthand and a number of commands that do not run. This brings them to the form the rest of the set uses and corrects the commands. `adcs`, `delegation`, `gpo-abuse` and `lateral-movement` are not touched.

**House format**

- Every value is a placeholder from `placeholders.toml`: `<User>` becomes `<Username>`, `<AttackerIP>` `<LHOST>`, `<Target>` and `<Host>` `<TargetIP>` or `<Hostname>.<Domain>`, `<VictimSam>` `<TargetUser>`, `http://target...` `<Scheme>://<WebHost>`, and a fixed port 443 `<LPORT>`. A value typed by hand is `THE-SOMETHING`. No new placeholder was needed, and the `Fill in` column in docs/PLAYBOOKS.md now lists what each playbook asks for.
- First person, no arrows, no dashes used as punctuation, no `=` shorthand, no code fences (also taken back out of `ssti`, `sudo` and `path-hijack`), and the two dangling notes are gone. The sample values in `mass-assignment` are placeholders.
- Titles follow the older ones: sentence case, and `Windows privesc:` or `Linux privesc:` in front of the six privilege escalation playbooks, so the page lists them like their neighbours.
- Every outside tool names where it comes from, as a URL, an `apt` package or `pipx`, and every pwn-shop tool has its `tool install` line, in the batch and in the older playbooks that lacked one.
- The sections the same release added to `cmdi`, `lfi`, `linux-creds`, `suid` and `port-forwarding` are rewritten the same way.

**Commands, each checked against the tool's source at the version pwn-shop pins, or against upstream**

- NetExec 1.5.1: `--gmsa` (there is no `-M gmsa`), `-M laps` on ldap, and `add-computer` on smb with `PASSWORD=`.
- `sccm-wsus`: PXEThief's modes (2 takes the distribution point, 3 a variables file and password, 5 a variables file), with a note that it needs pywin32 and so Windows; pywsus with `-H` as the listening address and the required `-e`; SharpWSUS as `create`, `approve`, `check` and `delete`; SharpSCCM `local secrets -m wmi`, `get secrets` with a computer account, and `exec -n`.
- `shadow-credentials`: `shadow auto` leaves no .pfx, so the step-by-step route uses `shadow add` and `certipy auth -username -domain`; `shadow remove` gets `-device-id`.
- `dpapi`: `impacket-dpapi`; a master key goes through `DPAPImk2john` to hashcat 15900 or 15910 (22102 does not exist); SharpDPAPI's `triage /rpc`.
- `coercion`: Coercer has no `--filter-ip`. `sidhistory-adminsdholder`: mimikatz's `sid::patch` and `sid::add`. `keepass`: 13400 for KDBX 2 and 3, 34300 for KDBX 4, and Kali's keepass2john stops at KDBX 3.
- `ntlm-relay`: `sudo /opt/pwn-broker/bin/impacket-ntlmrelayx`, `<Subnet>/<CIDR>`, and the CA server rather than the DC as the ADCS target. `adcs-esc` no longer uses the CA's name as a host. `dcsync` and `ad-recycle-bin` use `<BaseDN>`.
- `print-spooler`: the share folder is created, and the SMB server runs with sudo by its full path.
- Also found on the way: `vssadmin` needs an administrator (`hivenightmare`), graphw00f's script is `main.py`, `mremoteng_decrypt.py -f` does not take confCons.xml, the kubelet runs commands through `/run`, mssqlpwner's interactive commands, the Exhibitor steps as its advisory gives them, and `--username` on the hashcat lines that read `*2john` or timeroast output.
- `golden-silver`'s `hashlib.new("md4")` is left alone: it works on Kali, whose OpenSSL configuration loads the legacy provider.

**Exam labels**

- `sccm-wsus`: the WSUS man in the middle is spoofing, under the spoofing label, with the SharpWSUS route in a section of its own outside it. The playbook is now `mixed`.
- `machine-account-abuse` and `mssql-impersonation`: the relay steps sit under the relay label, and the Metasploit module under the one-target label. Both are now `mixed`.

**The rest**

- The checklists point to every playbook, and the AD checklist turns NTP back on.
- ysoserial is pinned to v0.0.6, and the three raw GitHub fetches to a commit.
- The PowerShell one-liner in `shells` is credited to Nishang, with its licence, in the playbook and in the README.
- The `A payload` section that `scheduled-tasks` and `uac-bypass` share is left as it is: each playbook is read in on its own.

The changelog entry sits under v2026.11.27, as the shell-tunnel fix's does, so whichever of the two merges second needs its bullets joined to the other's in CHANGELOG.md.

`build.py check`, `make-page.py --check`, the panel redraw and `pytest -W error` (364, with vim filling in every playbook) pass.

author: edlitmus
body:
Closes #875.

When the hub refused a node's certificate, the node sometimes lost the TLS alert. It then read the refusal as an outage, retried, and ran from its cached pillar until an attempt got through. There were two causes, and each commit fixes one. The diagnosis is in #875's comments.

## Cause 1: a reset (commit 1)

TLS 1.3 lets the client finish its half of the handshake before the hub checks the client's certificate. The client then writes its HTTP/2 preface at once. The hub sent the alert and closed with those bytes still unread, so the socket ended with an RST:
- on Windows, the RST discarded the unread alert;
- on unix, the node's next write got EPIPE.

The node already ends its own connections with a FIN and a drain (`drainingConn`, issue 757). The hub did not.

The fix is `transport.DrainingListener`, which `hub.Listen` now uses below TLS. The test fixture uses it as well.

## Cause 2: net/http dropped the alert (commit 2)

`http2: client conn could not be established` is returned when the connection closed before its first request, and the cause is thrown away. With the HTTP/2 debug log on, 8 of 15 of these errors had the alert behind them.

The fix is `alertRecovering`, on the node's transport. On that one error it reads the connection once: a `tls.Conn` keeps its first read error, so the read returns the alert without touching the socket. If that error is a remote alert, it is returned; anything else stays as net/http said it. `newHubTransport` is now the one constructor, used by `Client` and by the tests.

## Evidence

Measured on Ed-PC (Windows 11 Pro 26H2, build 26320.10022, go 1.27.4), through the hub fixture, one refused handshake at a time:

| Case | Before | Hub drained only | Both fixes |
|---|---|---|---|
| revoked | 15/1500 | 5/1500 | 0 |
| unknown CA | 13/1500 | 8/1500 | 0 |
| expired | 329/1500 | 39/1500 | 0 |

"Both fixes" is the new test, run 8 times in one process (7,200 handshakes). Beside a full `go test ./...`, 29,700 handshakes lost no alerts.

## Tests

`TestEveryRefusedHandshakeReportsItsAlertTheFirstTime` makes 300 refused handshakes per case, each on a fresh client with no retry, and every one must report its own alert. Each fix was broken on purpose:
- without the drain, the test failed with 6, 2 and 88 lost (resets);
- without the recovery, it failed with 1, 1 and 11 lost (net/http's text).

The old test's `lostTheAlert` now knows WSAECONNRESET and WSAECONNABORTED. Not knowing them is why it failed on Windows.

The new test makes an attempt again only if its dial failed. A refused connection now ends in TIME_WAIT, and Windows ran out of local ports (WSAENOBUFS) when the test ran back to back: 2 of 29,700 attempts under load. An attempt that fails after the dial still fails the test.

Passing locally: `internal/transport`, `internal/hub`, `cmd/halite-node` (real hub and node binaries over the drained listener), specaudit and docsaudit. Vet passes for windows, linux, freebsd and darwin. Handbook and gendocs output were regenerated.

## Costs

After each close, the hub holds a goroutine and a descriptor for up to `HandshakeTimeout`, until the peer's FIN. A peer that never finishes its handshake can already hold one that long. The connection cap counts streams, not sockets.

## Not covered

- The RST was not captured on the wire.
- The Linux and FreeBSD broken-pipe form was not reproduced here; CI runs the new test there.
- Why the expired case loses about 20 times as often as the others was not found.
- A real revoked `halite-node` was not run.
- `internal/api` and the metrics endpoint were not changed: no client of either reads a refusal alert.
- `-race`, because this host has no C compiler.

Ledger: DIVERGENCE 5.755, renumbered after #906 took 5.754. The pre-push `ledger cites` list also shows three "TLS 1.3" mentions read as ledger 1.3; they name the protocol version, as `unreachable.go` already does, and are not references. The CHANGELOG entry is included.

  index, the whole CLI reference, comparisons, concepts, the conformity gate
  overview, the developer guide, the example rule, the FAQ, all tool pages, the

  with `-E -s`; Apothem's managed block, its BEGIN and END markers, and what
  happens when a file has a broken or doubled block or a marker Apothem cannot

  numbered fixes; link and Windows junction safety; the installer lock; the

    "bloqueio" for the installer lock, the page title "Resolução de problemas"
    as link text, and "o bloco dele" for Apothem's own block.
  - ru: "соединение" for a Windows junction; cross-page links use the Russian
    section titles as link text.
  - zh-cn: 贮藏（stash） for git stash (暂存 stays only for staged changes and
    the staging folder), 联接点 for a Windows junction and 台账 for the install
    ledger.

## Why

The English pages changed after these translations were made, so the
translated pages showed the out-of-date notice and described old commands and
old behavior, such as `python -m apothem.conformity.gate` after a script
install. A review of the first pass also found some wording errors: in pt-br,
"where its lines read" was turned into "what its lines say"; in ru, one
sentence said the uninstall reads markers inside code, the opposite of the
rule; and in zh-cn, "stash" was written with the Chinese word for "stage",
which would tell readers to do something that does not let the update run.

- In `reference/settings-reference.mdx`, the comments inside one shell code

author: priyanshub18
body:
## Summary

Closes #726.

- **Remove the broad static fallback rule** (`apogee-extension/rules/ollama-cors.json`, `declarative_net_request` in `apogee-extension/manifest.json`, and the `rules/` copy in `apogee-extension/vite.config.js`). All supported browsers (`minimum_chrome_version: 116`, Firefox `140.0` / Android `142.0`) support `declarativeNetRequest.updateSessionRules` (Chrome 90+, Firefox 113+), so shipping an un-scopable static fallback rule is unnecessary and risked stripping `Origin` headers from website-initiated requests to local services.
- **Scope the runtime session rule to this extension's own initiator domain** (`apogee-extension/lib/util/loopbackCors.js`): resolve the extension's initiator host via `chrome.runtime.getURL("")` (handling both Chromium `chrome-extension://<id>/` and Firefox `moz-extension://<uuid>/` without accidentally passing Firefox's `apogee@darshi.dev` add-on ID), and require both `initiatorDomains: [extensionDomain]` and `tabIds: [TAB_ID_NONE]` alongside `excludedInitiatorDomains: LOOPBACK_HOSTS`. Fail closed (`"unsupported"` / `"unavailable"`) with no static fallback if session rules or extension identity are unavailable.
- **Add tests verifying website-initiated requests keep their `Origin` header** (`apogee-extension/tests/util/loopbackCors.test.js`, `apogee-extension/tests/manifest.test.js`): verifies manifest has no static fallback rules, simulates DNR evaluation across Chrome and Firefox runtimes for website tabs, website service/shared workers (`tabId: -1`), local dev servers, other extensions, and Apogee's own background requests to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]`.
- **Update docs** (`PRIVACY.md`, `docs/STORE-LISTING.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`, `docs/OLLAMA.md`) to remove references to the bundled static fallback rule and describe the extension-scoped session rule accurately.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run format:check`
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run build` (both `dist/chrome` and `dist/firefox`) and `npm run lint:webext`
- [x] `npm run check:consistency` and `node apogee-extension/scripts/check-locales.mjs` (from the repo root)
- [x] `npx cspell@10.4.0 lint` on all updated markdown docs
- [x] `node --test tests/manifest.test.js tests/util/loopbackCors.test.js` (20/21 passed locally on Node 22.18.0; the 1 cancelled test is the pre-existing `withTimeout` `unref()` Node 22 vs Node 24 behavior noted in `CONTRIBUTING.md`; CI validates full `npm test` on Node 24)
- [x] Manually exercised the change in a loaded browser extension

## AI assistance

- Tool and what it changed: Antigravity helped audit the DNR scoping, remove the static fallback rule, scope `loopbackCors.js` to the extension's initiator domain, write the DNR matching tests, and update the privacy/architecture docs.
- [x] I reviewed and tested the output myself.

## Privacy impact

- [x] No new outbound network calls
- [ ] Adds/changes a network call (described above, docs updated)

- [x] Permissions unchanged, or all four of manifest / README / PRIVACY / store-listing updated together

body: Stacked on #274. Adds layout v4 (`has_gripper_target` + `gripper_target`), v2/v3 checkpoint migration, RoboCasa wrist F/T/torso-target parity, and aligned task DAgger labels. Adds a contact curriculum with a PandaOmron inertial payload body downstream of the F/T sensor, variable torso height, `wide_arm`/`carry`/`carry_easy` subtasks, and a Stretch payload archetype. Carry teacher is 3/3. The best DAgger policy is 2/10; masking wrist wrench/finger force/joint torque drops it to 0/10, so the actor uses measured load. An 8,192-step PPO fine-tune raised success to 3/10 but worsened mean tracking to 0.344 m (settled max 1.20 m), so it is not promoted. The easy-carry stage (`carry_easy`: 0.4-0.6 kg, held base, +/-0.10 rad, torso 0.24-0.26 m) passes 5/5 after teacher BC and 5/5 through two DAgger iterations (1.05 cm mean, 3.5 cm settled max). Masking wrist wrench/finger force/joint torque still passes 10/10 but worsens tracking from 1.26 to 1.73 cm, so the narrow range is learnable by averaging. `carry_wide` (0.2-1.0 kg, base+arm, +/-0.20 rad, torso 0.18-0.30 m) passes **0.80** after one DAgger iteration on the 5-episode screen (2.03 cm mean, 3.56 cm settled, zero collisions). The 10-episode gate is **0.80 success but 18.2 cm mean tracking, 1.04 m settled max, and 2 collisions**, so it fails the carry gate and is not promoted. Masked is also 0.80 with 7.0 cm tracking and 2 collisions. The next run mixes arm/base/combined/carry_wide to prevent overfitting and reduce collisions. RoboCasa `PickPlaceCounterToCabinet` with the wide checkpoint is **0/3**: one canned food reached retreat with 0.78 m displacement, two grasp failures. No task success yet. Full carry initialized from the wide checkpoint reaches **1.00** on the 5-episode screen and **0.80** at seed 30000 (2.25 cm mean, 3.04 cm settled max, zero collisions); masking wrist wrench/finger force/joint torque drops it to **0.50**. The 3-seed gate is **0.80/0.70/0.50** (mean 0.667, min 0.50), so it **fails** the 0.75 gate and stays planned. The RoboCasa task sweep with the same checkpoint is **0/3, all grasp_failed**; the wide checkpoint got one transport. Direct-plant carry and RoboCasa task transfer remain separate gates. A mixed arm/base/combined/carry_wide suite peaks at 0.83 aggregate on the second DAgger iteration with zero collisions. The 10-episode evaluation is **0.85 aggregate, zero collisions**: arm 1.00 (1.56 cm), base 1.00, combined **0.80** (2.04 cm), carry_wide **0.60** (5.26 cm, settled 31 cm). Combined is one episode short of 0.85 and carry_wide is below 0.75, so no promotion. A focused combined/carry_wide continuation reaches **0.90 aggregate with zero collisions** on the 5-episode screen, but only **0.55 on 10 episodes** (combined 0.50, carry_wide 0.60). body:
## Summary
🤖 Generated with [Nori](https://noriagentic.com/)

`/agent` now runs in `nori attach`, and `/agents` is an alias of `/agent` in both `nori` and `nori attach`. The slash menu still lists `/agent` once.

- **List:** the agents come from the connected host's `initialize` reply (`nori/preparedAgent` `agentOption`). The host checks each launch command on its own machine, so a `--host` terminal sees the host's agents and their install state, not its own config.
- **No session on screen** (including a host with zero sessions): the host starts a session with the chosen agent.
- **Session with no prompts yet:** the agent changes in place through the host's `agent` config option (`session/set_config_option`). The session keeps its ID.
- **Prompted session:** that conversation keeps running, and the chosen agent starts in a new session beside it in the same folder. The new session says "Started a new session with X. The previous conversation keeps running; Alt+S switches to it."
- **Agent the host can't start:** the row shows the host's reason. Enter prints "X cannot start on this host: …", keeps the picker open, and starts nothing.
- **Who can use it:** only the controller. Watchers see "watching · Alt+T to take control". Hosts that don't list agents grey it as "not available on this host yet".
- **In-place change seen from other terminals:** watchers, and terminals that attach later and replay the journal, see the old agent stop and the session start again under the same ID. They keep the session open instead of showing "Session ended".
- `nori-protocol` exports `AGENT_INSTALLED`, which the host and client share.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["/agent or /agents"] --> R{controller and host lists agents?}
  R -- no --> G[greyed with reason]
  R -- yes --> P[host's agents + install state]
  P --> C{session on screen}
  C -- none --> N["_nori/session/new {agent}"]
  C -- no prompts yet --> S["session/set_config_option agent (same ID)"]
  C -- prompted --> B["new session beside, old keeps running"]
```

Not in this PR: resuming an agent's saved sessions from `/agent` (plain `nori` offers it), and root `--agent` for attach. Both belong to the `/resume` tranche.

## Test Plan
- [x] `cargo test -p nori-tui -p nori-protocol -p nori-host-runtime` pass on this head (1940 tui unit tests).
- [x] New PTY suite `tui-pty-e2e/tests/attach_agents.rs`, using synthetic fixture agents Amber, Birch and Cedar on a `--host` host whose config the client does not share. It covers:
  - a zero-session host lists its agents and starts the chosen one;
  - an unprompted session changes agent in place (same ID, Birch answers);
  - a prompted session keeps running beside the new one;
  - an agent that is not installed starts nothing;
  - a watcher keeps a session whose agent changed in place;
  - a later attach opens the running session.
- [x] Unit tests: availability by role, host features and reconnect; `/agents` alias in plain and joined composers (one menu row); handshake parsing; picker snapshot `joined_agent_picker`; a choice that lands after control is lost starts nothing.
- [x] Existing `host_attach`, `agent_switching` and `host_agent_switch` PTY suites pass. Two `host_attach` tests now look for a command that is still greyed (`/resume`), because `/agent` no longer is.

Originating chat: https://demo.norisessions.com/chat/01a21e3e-e623-709f-be4e-0c87d8be3f7a

author: groupsky
body:
Refs #1915

## What was wrong

A charge rest closes only when the car moves. The charger meter OFF edge is written only after 120 s of low readings (`chargerMeterOffMinMs`).

When the car logger sleeps through a slow charge, it wakes only when the driver comes. If the car drives away less than 120 s after the meter load stops, the rest closes with an ON edge and no OFF edge. `findMeterInterval` then returns nothing, so the charge is `bounds=unbounded` with no `ac_energy_kwh`. The OFF edge that comes a minute later is dropped as older than the new trip.

This fits the 2026-10-21 charge: the meter load stopped at 07:04 local time and the longest car gap (about 9.6 h) covers the whole charge.

## The fix

In `findMeterInterval`: when there is no OFF edge, but the meter is still in its ON state from this ON edge, the charge ends at:

- the first low reading (the pending OFF edge), or
- the newest meter reading, when the meter still shows load.

The meter state now also keeps the newest reading (`lastTs`, `lastAct`). An old saved state without them works as before.

## Tests

New tests in `docker/automations/bots/ioniq-sessions.test.js`: a charge with sparse car samples (a 9.6 h gap, 1.23 kW, 11.75 kWh):

- the car leaves 60 s after the load stops: `bounds=meter`, real duration, `ac_energy_kwh` 11.75
- the meter still shows load at the rest close: bounded to the newest reading
- the meter charge is not reused by the next rest

The first two failed before the fix. `npm test` in `docker/automations`: 48 suites, 1275 tests pass. `standard` on the two files shows 8 old warnings, the same as on master; none new.

## Not in this PR

The 2026-10-21 session in the database. The bot does not compute old sessions again, so that needs one manual write. The steps are in the issue.

author: wiiiimm
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"wiiiimm"} -->
_Requested by **wiiiimm** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01576NGXFhW1ftizVVAtWRMz?thread=cmsg_01576NGXFhW1ftizVVAtWRMzBxpUKAf2CZNXP3pKNdnKy3)_

## Why

agent-usage's Antigravity tab read the OAuth token Antigravity leaves in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` and called Google's internal Code Assist endpoints with it:

- `v1internal:retrieveUserQuotaSummary`: quota when the app is closed (`antigravity_remote`, on by default)
- `v1internal:retrieveUserQuota`: the "Gemini, per model" bars
- `v1internal:loadCodeAssist`: the Plan block. Nothing gated this one, so turning `antigravity_remote` off did not stop it.

Every request sent `User-Agent: opscope (antigravity-cli)` to get past `UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT`.

Google told T3 Code that calling these endpoints from an outside client can get an account flagged, and T3 removed the same `retrieveUserQuotaSummary` probe and its fake user agent ([pingdotgg/t3code#43026](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43026)). In [pingdotgg/t3code#43087](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/43087) they also stopped posing as another client, because "Posing as another client breaks the same rule." Clause 6 of the [Antigravity terms](https://antigravity.google/terms) says "Using third party software, tools, or services to access the Service (e.g. using OpenClaw with Antigravity OAuth) is a breach".

## What changes

- Removes all three `cloudcode-pa` calls, the token-file read, the crafted User-Agent and the `antigravity_remote` setting (`settings.json`, `config.example.json`, README, CONFIGURE.md).
- The quota now comes only from the app's local language server, then `agy -p /usage`, then the old pty start for `agy` older than 1.1.11. All of this is behind `antigravity_start`, which is unchanged. The activity counts still come from the local SQLite stores.
- No-quota reasons now name `agy` or `antigravity_start` instead of Google or the token.
- Adds a guard test that fails if the endpoint host, the token file or a `v1internal:` call comes back into `antigravity.rs`.

## What users lose

- The Plan block: Code Assist tier, Google AI plan and project. Neither the app nor `agy` reports these.
- The "Gemini, per model" bars, and the `gemini busiest` lane on `[+]`. The grouped Gemini limit from `agy` remains.
- Quota with the app closed when `agy -p /usage` can't answer, for example when `agy` isn't installed or is older than 1.1.11.

## Not changed

The FAQ now says wrapping `agy` inside third-party apps "is not supported under consumer plans". So `antigravity_start` (on by default) is a grey area, but it is not named as a breach. This PR leaves it on, as decided in the project thread.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p opscope-widgets --bin agent-usage`: 538 passed
- `cargo test -p opscope-widgets --test check`: 73 passed. `config.example.json` was regenerated with `UPDATE_CONFIG_EXAMPLE=1`.
- Not checked against a live Antigravity install.

author: develart-projects
body:
The experimental "Analyze for PHP 8.6" job always installs the latest PHPStan release. Since PHPStan 2.3.6 (2026-11-15) it reports 158 errors on master; with 2.3.5 it was clean.

- 141 of them are method.tentativeReturnType for methods that do have #[\ReturnTypeWillChange]. They are reported only when PHPStan itself runs on PHP 7.4, and they cannot be ignored. The job now runs on PHP 8.5, where they are not reported.
- 17 are new findings of PHPStan 2.3.6:
  - Zend_Locale_Math_PhpMath::Mod(): is_nan() on an integer removed, it was always false.
  - Zend_View_Helper_ServerUrl: `$_SERVER['HTTPS'] === true` removed, `== 'on'` already covers true.
  - The remaining 15 are added to .phpstan.php86.baseline.php. An inline ignore is not possible, the main job with the locked PHPStan would report it as unmatched.

No behaviour change in the library. The main PHPStan job is unchanged.

Three of the baselined findings are real bugs and will be fixed separately:
- Zend_Tool_Framework_Registry::reset() unsets its properties, so the next getLoader() ends in __get() and throws "Property _loader was not located in this registry".
- Zend_Tool_Project_Provider_Module: the loop that walks up more than one parent runs only once (`$i-- > 0` with a negative $i).
- Zend_Controller_Action_Helper_ViewRenderer::_setOptions(): on PHP 7.4 an integer key 0 matches the string cases of the switch and creates a property $_0.

## What it does (switch on)

- **Studio.** Sound on the rail (a photo or video Moment under the person's own name: never a made-up name) opens a
  sheet: "Your voice" (up to a minute) or "Place sound" (three seconds), one of the two; record, hear it, take it off.

  moving text, each lit as it is said, and the viewer holds still while it plays; a muted viewer waits for a tap. A
  whisper dot's card plays its three seconds.

author: wolfgang-ganglberger
body:
## What

New recordings are published only as split Zarr (primary + derivative + summary JSON). This adds a writer that assembles them back into one local H5 in the layout the converter read, plus a parity check against the archived source H5.

- `bdsp.zarr_to_h5.write_h5` / `bdsp-zarr-to-h5` CLI
  - **Signals:** int16 with a recovered calibration that reproduces every Zarr sample bit-exactly through the converter's formula. If none exists, float32 with an identity calibration. mV/V units are restored.
  - **Annotations:** original codes and `event_map`.
  - **Feature time series:** copied from `bdsp.sleep-feature-payload.v1`.
  - **Recording summary:** all rows plus vectors from the JSON.
  - Metadata the split format never stored (e.g. `prefilter`, `rule`, producer provenance, `features/research`) is listed in `bdsp_h5_export`, not invented.
- `bdsp.h5_compare.compare_h5`: compares a rebuilt H5 with its source (names and counts only, never values).
- `validation/h5_parity.py`: seeded, resumable live check that also runs the converter's own verifier with the rebuilt H5 standing in as the source.
- Docs: `docs/bids-zarr/H5_EXPORT.md`, plus short links from the guides. Version bump to 0.5.0.

## Verification

- `pytest`: 51 passed, 1 skipped (the existing opt-in AWS test). The new synthetic round-trip tests include mV units, sparse and boolean channels, payload families and tamper detection.
- Live check on 5 seeded recordings per cohort (S0001, I0002, I0003, I0004, I0006, I0007); see `validation/reports/2026-11-27-h5-parity.md`:
  - 25/25 pass outside I0007.
  - 1,024/1,024 signals have identical physical samples. 77% also have the archived int16 digital samples and 71% the archived calibration attributes.
  - 221/221 annotation tables, 650/650 published feature families and 126,792 summary rows match.
  - The converter's verifier accepts all 30 rebuilt H5s.
- `bdsp.read_h5`, `open_h5` and `to_dataframe` give identical results on a real rebuilt vs source H5.

## Finding

I0007 derivative Zarr stores are not published: 0 of 300 sampled subjects have one, and only the summary JSON exists. Rebuilt I0007 H5s therefore lack CAISR annotations and feature time series. Everything I0007 does publish matches.

No cloud data were modified. Participant-level evidence stays in the ignored `validation/results/`.

body:
Clicking Mirador's plot size menu ("Window") did nothing.

## Cause

`mirador/index.html` cancels `mousedown` on every `.btn`, `.tab` and chip button, so that clicking one doesn't take the focus away from the table (Enter and space are the table's). The size menu is a `<select class="btn">`, and a select opens on that `mousedown`, so the browser never opened it. The handler predates the menu by a day; the menu has been unreachable by mouse since it was added.

## Change

- The `mousedown` handler leaves menus (`select`) alone.
- The size menu blurs once a size is chosen, so ← and → go back to moving between plots.

## Evidence

Isolated config and state, a real R with httpgd, Mirador from this checkout, and Chromium driven with real clicks and keys (not `selectOption`, which skips the click and is why the earlier check missed this):

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Click the menu | focus stays on `BODY` | the menu has the focus (it opens) |
| ↓, Enter | still `window`, plot 1368×758 | `800x500`, plot redrawn at 800×500, focus back on the page |
| Click, ↑, Enter | (not reachable) | `window`, plot fits again at 1368×758 |
| Click "?" or a tab | focus stays on `BODY` | focus stays on `BODY` |

author: leninworld
body:
This PR fixes [issue #2722](https://github.com/microsoft/responsible-ai-toolbox/issues/2722).

## Description

`ServedModelWrapper.forecast` (used by `RAIInsights.load` when `RAI_MODEL_SERVING_PORT` is set) had two broken error paths:

- when `post_with_retries` raised (the model server is unreachable after all retries), the `except` block formatted `response.status_code`, but `response` was never assigned;
- `requests.post` does not raise on HTTP errors, so a 4xx/5xx answer went straight to `json.loads(response.content)['predictions']`.

The request error is now re-raised as `RuntimeError("Could not retrieve predictions. Request to the model server failed: <error>")` with the original exception as its cause, and a response with an HTTP error status (4xx/5xx, 400-599) raises the existing `Model server returned status code ... and the following response: ...` message. Any other status (200, 201, 399, ...) is handled as before.

On main (Python 3.11, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3):

- before: server unreachable -> `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'response' where it is not associated with a value`; HTTP 500 with `b"Internal Server Error"` -> `JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)`; HTTP 400 with MLflow's `{"error_code": "BAD_REQUEST", "message": "Invalid input"}` -> `KeyError: 'predictions'`;
- after: `RuntimeError: Could not retrieve predictions. Request to the model server failed: Unable to post to web service` (cause: the original error), and `RuntimeError: Could not retrieve predictions. Model server returned status code 500 and the following response: b'Internal Server Error'` (likewise for 400).

Tests, in `responsibleai/tests/rai_insights/test_served_model.py` (unit tests of `ServedModelWrapper` with `post_with_retries` mocked, so no server and no retry delays):
- `test_served_model_unreachable`: the exact message `Could not retrieve predictions. Request to the model server failed: Unable to post to web service`, with the request error as `__cause__`.
- `test_served_model_http_error`: status 500 and 599 with a plain-text body and status 400 with an MLflow JSON error body raise the status-code message with the body (400 and 599 pin the range ends).
- `test_served_model_forecast`: status 200, 201, 399 and 600 return the predictions, as on `main`, and post to `http://localhost:5432/invocations` (guards the success path just outside the error range).
- The 4 error cases fail on `main` (`UnboundLocalError`, `JSONDecodeError`, `KeyError`) and pass with this change; the 4 success cases and the existing `test_served_model` pass on both. `test_served_model.py`: 9 passed on Python 3.11 with CI's pins (numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.5.1) and 9 passed on the minimum pins (Python 3.9, pandas 2.2.2, numpy 2.0.2).
- flake8 with the `requirements-linting.txt` plugins and isort are clean on the changed files.

## Checklist

<!--- Make sure to satisfy all the criteria listed below. -->

- [ ] I have added screenshots above for all UI changes. (N/A, no UI change)
- [ ] I have added e2e tests for all UI changes. (N/A, no UI change)
- [x] Documentation was updated if it was needed. (Not needed)

Fixes #2722

## Summary

**Retrieval quality**
- **Chunks are no longer truncated:** new default embedding model `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` (512 tokens, with e5 `query:`/`passage:` prefixes). The old model read only 128 tokens and ignored about half of every 1000-character chunk.
- **Index remembers its embedding model** (`myrag_index.json`). A mismatch stops `ingest`/`ask`/`search`/`chat` with a hint; `myrag ingest --rebuild <folder>` re-embeds all folders in the index. v0.1 indexes are detected as built with the old model.
- Chunk settings are stored per file (`chunking` metadata, configurable via `MYRAG_CHUNK_SIZE`/`MYRAG_CHUNK_OVERLAP`); changing them re-processes files.
- **Hybrid search:** vector search + BM25 keyword search, merged with reciprocal rank fusion.
- **Reranking** with a multilingual cross-encoder (`cross-encoder/mmarco-mMiniLMv2-L12-H384-v1`) over ~30 candidates; falls back with a warning if it can't be loaded.
- **Relevance threshold** (`MYRAG_MIN_SCORE`, default 0.1): when nothing relevant is left, no LLM call is made.

**New features**
- `myrag chat`: interactive session with history, follow-up questions rewritten into standalone search queries, streamed answers, `/sources`, `/clear`.
- `myrag search`: best passages with relevance/similarity/keyword scores, no LLM call.
- Streaming answers for Claude and Ollama (`myrag ask` streams too).
- New formats: `.html`, `.csv`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx` (incl. notes), `.epub`, `.eml`, source code and config files.

Version bumped to 0.2.0. New dependencies: `beautifulsoup4`, `python-pptx`, `openpyxl`.

## Upgrade note
Existing indexes must be rebuilt once: `myrag ingest --rebuild <folder>`.

- `pytest`: 52 tests pass (new: `tests/test_retrieval.py`, `tests/test_loaders.py`, more ingest tests).

author: kellylford
body:
Fixes #758.

## What was wrong

When Stop came while a Copilot turn's prompt was on its way (written, not yet queued), Stop left the cancel to the turn, which sends it right after the prompt (#372), and reported `cancelled=True` at once. The window then said "Stop requested. If Copilot does not stop within 15 seconds, The Chat Place closes it." If Copilot was already closing, the turn's own cancel couldn't go out (`NOT_SENT`), no timer started, and the turn ended with the connection: the warning didn't match what happened. The same gap covered a prompt that never went at all (`AcpNotSent`), which the old comment in `stop()` noted as a known gap.

## The fix

- `stop()` now waits for the turn when the prompt is on its way. Between deciding to send and hearing it's queued the turn waits on nothing (`copilot_acp` queues without waiting on the pipe), so it's only a moment. The turn tells a new `_turn_news` condition (on the runtime's lock) either what its own `_cancel` did, or that the prompt never went (`NEVER_QUEUED`).
- Stop reports what really happened:
  - Cancel sent: `cancelled=True`, and the 15-second warning is true.
  - Cancel couldn't go out (Copilot closing): `cancelled=False`, so the window says "Copilot isn't answering", as it already did when Stop's own cancel met a closing Copilot (#405).
  - Prompt never went: also `cancelled=False`, "Copilot isn't answering". The turn's own notice says the message wasn't sent, and it comes back unsent. It isn't reported as "Stopped before your message went", because Stop isn't what kept it back.
- Results are kept with their turn number, so a later turn can't be confused with this one. If two Stops wait on the same prompt, the second is told `already_asked`, as a Stop pressed again is.
- The wait has a 10-second limit as a guard only. Every way out of the turn's send tells the condition, including `_cancel` raising (try/finally).

## Tests

Against the strict fake Copilot (`tests/test_copilot_runtime.py`). Stop now runs on another thread, as the window's does, and each test waits until that Stop is actually waiting on the turn:
- `test_a_stop_whose_cancel_meets_copilot_closing_doesnt_warn_of_a_close`: the #758 case. Copilot really closes between the prompt and the cancel. Stop isn't `cancelled`, no timer runs, and no cancel reaches the fake.
- `test_a_stop_whose_prompt_never_goes_doesnt_warn_of_a_close`: not `cancelled`, the message comes back unsent, and the fake gets neither a prompt nor a cancel.
- `test_a_cancel_that_breaks_in_the_turn_still_answers_the_stop` and `test_a_stop_whose_turn_never_reports_falls_back_to_the_cancel_it_will_send`: the try/finally, and the guard's fallback.
- `test_two_stops_as_the_prompt_goes_start_one_clock`: one cancel, and the second Stop is `already_asked`.
- The two older tests of a Stop in that gap now call Stop from another thread, and check that the turn's own thread sent the cancel.

The 7 Stop tests passed 40 times in a row on Windows locally.

## Review

An independent `code-reviewer` traced every `stop()` caller, the lock and Condition, and the window's wording. It found no correctness bug. Fixed: a prompt that never went no longer gives credit to Stop; the turn's cancel reports even if `_cancel` raises; there's a test of the guard; the helper's checks moved off the turn thread, where a failed assert would be swallowed; the release note now matches the words used.

**Open, for Kelly to decide:** this is the fourth local fix to the same problem in Copilot's Stop (#386, #395, #414, now #758): Stop reports something other than what happened. The repo's rule is that a third local fix means rethinking the design. The reviewer suggests one per-turn cancel state, read under the lock, that Stop reads its report from, in place of the flags and outcome constants. This PR stays a draft until Kelly decides whether that redesign comes first or is filed as a follow-up.

author: shutfordite
body:
**Package:** X3 (Shared, coordinator method and PR check)

**What and why:** Two changes: one PR per round, and a QA gate on every round.

**One PR per round.** One PR per round instead of one per package, because testing and merging a PR per package was too much. Stream agents push branches and open no PRs. Once every stream in the round has finished, the coordinator reviews each branch, joins them into `round/<n>`, adds the STATUS update, and opens one PR, `Round <n>: <what>`. That PR says what changed in plain words and gives a numbered iPad test list where every step is a link. Fixes during testing go onto the stream branch and are merged into the round again. A package that fails is reverted out of the round.
- `.claude/skills/gresca-architect/SKILL.md`: new "The round PR" section, which replaces the merge-order, try-list and stacked-PR rules. Reviews are now per branch. Feel spikes ride in the round behind `?spike=`.
- `AGENTS.md`: agents push branches and open no PR, and report back using the template's sections.
- `.github/round_pr_template.md`: the round PR body (Packages, What changed, What to test (iPad), Owner verdicts needed, Proof, Debt, Not in this round).
- `tools/review/checks.mjs`, `run.mjs`: a `Round <n>:` title switches the PR check to round mode. In round mode, edits to several streams and to STATUS are listed rather than flagged, and the body is checked against the round template.
- `docs/STATUS.md` ("How the work is run"), `docs/RETROSPECTIVES.md`, `tools/AGENTS.md`: updated to describe the change.

**QA gate on every round.** After the stream branches join the round, and before the round PR opens, a QA agent checks the round against a written standard. Its BLOCK keeps a package out of the round. Its report goes into the round PR's **Quality (QA)** section.
- `docs/QUALITY.md`: the standard. It covers what makes a good test (it fails without the change, it's as cheap as it can be), the coverage floors (src/ lines 95%, branches 92%, a new file 90%, GPU-only code exempt), and the suite's time budget (120 s summed, target 90 s; a test over 1 s explains why). It defines overtesting and how redundant tests are trimmed (only in a QA test-health package, which names the test that still covers each removed assertion). It also lists the verdicts and the trend table, with today's baseline: 1036 tests, 116.6 s, 96.9% of lines.
- `.claude/skills/gresca-qa/SKILL.md`: the QA agent's method and the format of its report.
- `tools/qa/test-times.mjs` and `npm run test:times` / `npm run test:quality`: the slowest files and tests, and coverage per src/ folder.
- The architect skill gains the QA step in "The round PR". The round template gains **Quality (QA)**. `AGENTS.md` points to the standard.

**Behaviour changes:** none in the game.

**Test changes:** `test/review.test.js` gets a new round-PR test, and the new `test/qa-times.test.js` tests the reporter. No existing assertion changed.

**Contracts touched:** none

**Try in the preview (iPad):** nothing to try, because the game is unchanged. Starting from the next round you'll get one PR to test.

**Owner verdict needed:** no

**Debt:** none

**Screenshots:** none (nothing visible)

author: triple-dylan
body:
Stacked on #78 only (independent of #88 and #90). Merge #78 first; this then retargets to `main`.

Before: 8 of the store's 175 queries were SQLite-only, so they would fail the day Sandbox runs on Postgres.

After: all of them run on both. Nothing changes on SQLite: same rows, same order, same counts.

## How

- `insert or ignore into members / grants / channel_pins / agent_skills values …` → `insert into … (named columns) values … on conflict do nothing` (SQLite has accepted this since 3.24).
- Skills sorted by `name collate nocase` → `lower(name)`.
- The two usage counters' upserts: `set tokens = tokens + excluded.tokens` is ambiguous on Postgres, so they say `usage.tokens` / `agent_usage.tokens`, and name their columns.
- `tests/sql-portability.test.ts`: reads every query written in `server/store.ts` and has Postgres parse and plan it (`prepare`) against the Postgres schema from #78. A new SQLite-only query fails CI with the query and Postgres's reason.

## Verified

- Locally: the portability test passes on Postgres 16 (it named exactly these 8 before the change); `server.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`, `collab.test.ts`, `sheets.test.ts` pass on SQLite (66 tests); the usage upserts still add up on SQLite (5+5 → 10, 3+3 → 6).
- typecheck and format pass. Full suite: see CI.

## Not covered

- `prepare` catches syntax, unknown names and type mismatches Postgres can see without values. Differences that only show with real data (for example text compared with numbers) show up when the full test suite runs on Postgres, at the switch.

author: haileen7
body:
Closes #1962

## Why

Both dev compose files published every port with no host IP, which Docker binds to `0.0.0.0`: Postgres, Redis, MySQL, pgAdmin, phpMyAdmin and phpRedisAdmin were reachable from the whole LAN. `install-guid.md` tells the operator to copy `.env.example.pgsql` verbatim, and that template ships the **same** placeholder password for `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD`, `DB_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` and `REDIS_PASSWORD` — so anyone on the same network could authenticate to the dev database with a password committed to this public repository. A dev database can hold imported HR sheets, not just demo rows.

## What changed

- `docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml` — all six mappings bound to `127.0.0.1` (`5432`, `6379`, `8082`, `8083`, `3306`, `8081`).
- `docker-compose-pgsql-.yml` — same for its four mappings (`5432`, `6379`, `8082`, `8083`). File name unchanged.
- `install-guid.md` §6 — warning block after `cp .env.example.pgsql .env`: the template passwords are public, none may remain the template value, changing `DB_DEFAULT_PASSWORD` does not rotate an already-seeded admin user, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` only applies on first init of `postgis_data`, and the compose files now listen on `127.0.0.1` only (LAN exposure is a local, uncommitted opt-in).

The warning deliberately does **not** require the four values to differ from each other: MySQL root reads `${DB_PASSWORD}` (`:72`) while phpMyAdmin reads `${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD}` (`:92`), so forcing them apart would break phpMyAdmin. The placeholder value itself is not reproduced anywhere in this PR.

## Verification (real output)

Drift check before starting — empty:

```
$ git diff --stat 2ea7693a..HEAD -- docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml docker-compose-pgsql-.yml install-guid.md
(no output)
```

Every published port resolves to loopback:

```
$ for f in docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml docker-compose-pgsql-.yml; do
    docker compose -f "$f" config --format json | python3 -c '...assert host_ip == "127.0.0.1"...'
  done
OK 6 ports bound to 127.0.0.1
OK 4 ports bound to 127.0.0.1
```

No unprefixed mapping left (grep prints nothing, exit 1):

```
$ grep -nE '^\s*-\s*"[0-9]+:[0-9]+"' docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml docker-compose-pgsql-.yml; echo "exit=$?"
exit=1
$ grep -c '127\.0\.0\.1:' docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml docker-compose-pgsql-.yml
docker-compose-pgsql-mysql.yml:6
docker-compose-pgsql-.yml:4
```

Runtime, on the executor's already-running four-service stack (`docker compose -f docker-compose-pgsql-.yml up -d`, volumes untouched — no `down -v`):

```
$ docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Ports}}'
h-dashboard-pgadmin	443/tcp, 127.0.0.1:8082->80/tcp
h-dashboard-phpredisadmin	127.0.0.1:8083->80/tcp
h-dashboard-postgis	127.0.0.1:5432->5432/tcp
h-dashboard-redis	127.0.0.1:6379->6379/tcp

$ ss -ltn | grep -E ':(5432|6379|3306|8081|8082|8083)\b'
LISTEN 0 4096 127.0.0.1:8083 0.0.0.0:*
LISTEN 0 4096 127.0.0.1:8082 0.0.0.0:*
LISTEN 0 4096 127.0.0.1:6379 0.0.0.0:*
LISTEN 0 4096 127.0.0.1:5432 0.0.0.0:*
```

Before the change the same command showed `0.0.0.0:5432`, `0.0.0.0:6379`, `0.0.0.0:8082`, `0.0.0.0:8083`. The runtime check covered the four services that are actually running here; MySQL and phpMyAdmin were verified at config level (the `OK 6 ports` assertion above) because starting them would have added containers to the executor.

Scope: `git status --short` shows only the three in-scope files in the commit. `composer.lock` and `package-lock.json` were already modified in the working tree and were left out.

## Local `composer verify` note

Pint and PHPStan passed. The suite reported **4333 passed, 2 failed** — `DiseaseCaseCrudTest > orphans loaded for one case never land on another` and `KargoziniImportLivewireTest > exception during preview shows error`. Neither file is touched by this branch. The `KargoziniImportLivewireTest` failure did not reproduce in CI and is local vendor drift (installed Livewire 4.4.10 / PhpSpreadsheet 5.12.0 vs the committed lock's 4.4.8 / 5.11.0). The `DiseaseCaseCrudTest` failure **does** reproduce in CI and is pre-existing on `beta` — see the CI section below.

## CI

`Tests & Coverage` (blocking) and `PHP 8.6 Preview` (non-blocking) fail on the same test: `Tests\Feature\DiseaseCaseCrudTest > orphans loaded for one case never land on another` (`1 failed, 4334 passed`). Every other check is green: Pint, PHPStan, JS lint/typecheck, E2E, CSP, Smoke, Mutation, CodeQL, Coverage.

This is not caused by the diff — three other open PRs fail on the identical test: #1959 (run 46064023913), #1966 (46080127876), #1969 (46081496852). Root cause is a semantic collision on `beta` between #1870 (added the test: it switches `editingId` to a case diagnosed `2026-10-05` while `recordedAt` keeps the first case's `2026-10-01`) and #1879 (added the "recording cannot precede diagnosis" rule). Merge commit `557594b9` combined them; CI runs on the PR head, not the merge result, so the red slipped through.

A test-only one-line fix is possible (`->set('recordedAt', dc_jalali('2026-10-05'))` beside `diagnosedAt`), but it is outside this PR's hard scope of three files. Asked on #1962 how to proceed.

## Out of scope (untouched)

Image pinning (#1943 / PR #1950 — its diffs are `image:` lines only and do not collide with `ports:`), env templates, CI service-container ports in `.github/workflows/*`, and the hardcoded pgAdmin credentials in `docker-compose-pgsql-.yml:45-46` (separate issue).

author: flexdinesh
body:
- `t3/interaction.go`: T3 implements `execution.Interactive`, and `respond`/`send` are now available. Before this change Stage told users to "Answer in T3".
  - Requests: `t3_pending_request` list and read. Each pending user-input request becomes one `question` request, and options keep label, description and preview.
  - Respond: option labels map to T3 option values and are checked by T3's client rules (`ValidateAnswers`) before sending. A misfit answer, or one T3 refuses, is `*Invalid` (400). An answered, expired or unknown request is `ErrNotFound` (404).
  - Send: `t3_thread_send` in mode `auto`, so an idle thread starts a new turn and a running one is steered. A pending question or permission request, or a `thread_not_sendable` thread such as an archived one, is `*Busy` (409 `session_busy`).
- `t3.Client` gains `SendMessage` and the pending-request methods; MCPClient and Fake already had them. The fake refuses sends to archived threads, and a demo option now has a preview.
- T3's MCP can't list or answer permission requests. A new descriptor field, `harness.Descriptor.UnlistedRequests`, covers this, and T3 sets it to "Approve permission requests in T3.". When a needs-input task has no listed requests, the app shows that line with Open in T3 as the primary button, instead of a Reply composer whose send would only return 409.
- Additive `execution.QuestionOption.Preview` (API `preview`). `QuestionField` shows it with the existing folded mono `Preview` block, outside the option label.
- Worker parity goes through the existing `adapter.requests`, `adapter.respond` and `adapter.send` kinds and the `interactive` trait. No protocol bump.
- Tests:
  - t3 unit tests: mapping, label-to-value answers, respond outcomes, send modes and busy.
  - Worker parity over the remote rig.
  - API interaction tests, reworked now that T3 offers both operations, plus self-action guards.
  - `followUpView` unit test.
- Docs: execution.md (new "T3 interaction" section), api.md, features.md, harnesses.md, and the ADR 0008 P2 Interaction row.

Validation:
- `mise run check` passes except `config.TestDefaultSocket`. `/tmp` hit the disk quota because of other running work, so I ran `check` with `TMPDIR` on the home disk. That made the test's socket path 107 bytes, over the 103-byte limit; the test passes uncached with the default `/tmp`.

author: longtimeno-c
body:
Stacked on longtimeno-c/mediaviewer#765. Merge that first; this PR's diff is only the follow-up.

## What changed

A batch of big clips sent to a hard disk dropped its link about every 20 s. This was the gap left open in #765.

The receiver's link reader waits for room in its check queue (2 files being checked, 4 waiting) and reads nothing meanwhile. #765 made the receiver hold `channel::away` during that wait. On the sender's side, though, the socket send buffer fills well before the channel's replay limit, and `SO_SNDTIMEO` (`kSilenceMs`, 20 s) then failed the write. The link was marked down, which forced a rejoin, or ended the session where no rejoin was possible.

- `src/wire/net_posix.cpp`, `src/wire/net_win.cpp`: a TCP link waits on a full send buffer in 250 ms slices. Its write fails only once nothing has been sent **and** nothing has been read from the peer for `kSilenceMs`.
  - A receiver that is only slow to read keeps the link: its pings keep arriving at the sender's reader.
  - A dead peer still fails the write within `kSilenceMs`.
  - Protocol 1, `serve` and relay links share this `tcp_link`.
- `src/wire/link.h`: `set_stall_ms_for_tests`, a test-only shorter limit.
- `docs/design/28-driftwire.md`: the "Away" bullet now covers both sides.

## How it was tested

- A transfer whose receiver's checks stall past a 2 s write limit delivers on both ends with no rejoin. It fails without the change.
- A write into a full socket whose peer is silent still times out.
- All 321 `[driftwire]` tests in `mv_import_tests` pass on macOS arm64.
- The Windows build and the Windows `tcp_link` path were not run locally: CI covers them.

author: fridolin86
body:
Sky Pilots (Mario Party 2) draws the strip of clouds between its two views as ten 32-pixel basic sprites at 4:3 positions (x 8 to 296). It is not one wide picture, so the picture-stretch path never caught it, and in a wide window it stopped at 4:3 with plain white bars beside it.

`mp_hud_bar_float` registers that strip as a bar, the same way `mp_hud_bar` does Bobsled Run's in Mario Party 1, but for a game whose sprites' x and y are floats at their centre. The strip is stretched over the window, and the teams' icons and finish post on its rows are aligned by their fraction of 320. A piece that ends less than BAR_GAP short of the screen's right edge is also drawn to it, so the game's own 8-pixel gap on the right closes just as the left one does. `mp_hud_bar` now shares its piece lookup (`bar_piece`), and its behaviour is unchanged.

Measured at 1280x720, on strip rows y 350/360/370:
- Pure-white run at the window's left/right edge: before 133 px / 187 px, after 0 / 0.
- Finish post: before x 1018–1029 (0.93 along the 4:3 strip), after x 1147–1158 (0.90 of the window).

Used by n64hub/mario-party-2-recomp's hook for #115.

author: skytuhua
body:
Closes #1926.

The existing authenticated Inbox snapshot and read-state requests have a 15-second client deadline. A timeout aborts the request, releases the in-flight slot and surfaces the existing action or source error. A late snapshot cannot overwrite a newer successful one, and a new explicit read issues a fresh request.

Fake-clock units reproduced both missing deadlines and now verify timeout, abort, retry, stale response isolation and timer cleanup. The Chromium network fixture exercises the actual row from a held request through timeout and a successful second explicit write. Attention and public-source tests, typecheck, lint and build passed.

Includes the exact #2603 inbox motion head for the shared attention client.

author: santiagodepolonia
body: ## Description `TestHostEndsASessionItCannotRecheckForLong` failed intermittently in CI with `expected: 404, actual: 200` on its last request (for example on #1621, which does not touch `internal/mcpgateway`). When the host ends a session it could not recheck, it unbinds it and closes the SDK session in the background (`closeSessions`). The test's next request finds no binding and no shared record, so it is passed to the SDK handler; if the background close has not finished yet, the SDK still knows the session and answers 200. The test now waits for the hosted session to close before that request, as `TestLongCallDoesNotReviveADeletedSession` already does. Test-only change. Delaying the background close by 30 ms reproduces the failure on every run; with the fix the whole package passes under the same delay. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Expanded coverage for long outages to verify that a hosted session is closed after its host reaches the unverified limit, rather than only being unbound. No user-facing behavior changes are included in this update.

author: masonbesmer
body:
Phase 3 of the moderation suite ([LYRA-10](https://kanban.latte.cx/workbench/nightcity/tracker/LYRA-10), epic LYRA-7). This targets the epic branch `claude/lyra-7-moderation-suite`, not `develop`. Mason reviews the combined PR.

## Why

Moderators need a record of what happens in the server (edits, deletions, joins/leaves, voice, server changes), routed to channels they pick. Cases also have to cover actions taken outside Lyra, so `/modlogs` shows the full history.

## What

- **`/logconfig`** (Manage Server; slash and `%` forms): `view`, `channel <event|group|all> [channel]`, `ignore`, `unignore`. Each of the 15 event types gets its own channel. Groups: `messages`, `members`, `voice`, `server`. Changes are written to the config audit log (🛡️ Moderation).
- **Messages:** edit (before/after), delete (content, attachments), bulk delete with a `.txt` transcript of the cached messages.
- **Members:** join (account age, ⚠️ flag under 7 days, invite used, member count), leave (join date, roles), nickname, roles added/removed, server and profile avatar.
- **Voice:** join / leave / move.
- **Server:** channel, role (including permission diffs), emoji and server-setting changes. Position-only reorders are skipped.
- **Ignore lists:** channels (covering their threads, and categories covering their channels) and users. Always skipped: bots/webhooks for message events, bots in voice, and messages in any log channel or the mod log.
- **Audit-log cases (B16):** `GuildAuditLogEntryCreate` turns a ban, unban, kick or timeout done by hand (or by another bot) into a normal case and posts it to the mod log. Entries Lyra made herself are skipped, so P1 commands aren't doubled.
- New tables `log_routes`, `log_ignores`. Docs: `docs/features/MODERATION.md`, README.

## ⚠️ Intents: must be enabled before this reaches prod

Adds **`GuildMembers` (privileged)**, `GuildModeration`, `GuildInvites` and `GuildExpressions`, plus the `GuildMember` partial. **Server Members Intent has to be switched on in the Developer Portal for the prod and dev apps before deploying, or Discord refuses the login (close code 4014) and the bot stays offline.** P2 (LYRA-9) needs the same intent and may add the same lines to `src/LyraClient.ts`. Expect a trivial conflict there.

Lyra also needs **View Audit Log** (audit-log cases) and **Manage Server** (reading invites for "invite used"). Without them those parts quietly do nothing.

## Trade-offs

- Invite attribution compares use counts before/after the join. Simultaneous joins or vanity-URL joins show "unknown" / "probably the vanity URL" instead of a guess.
- Deleted or edited messages that aren't in discord.js's cache (sent before the last restart, or past the 200-per-channel cache) log as "not cached". Discord doesn't send the old content.
- Server-change logs don't say *who* made the change. That needs an audit-log lookup per event. Possible follow-up.
- Bot voice activity and bot messages are skipped to avoid noise from music bots and Lyra's own player messages.

## Verify

- [x] `yarn check` (format, oxlint, typecheck, 753 tests, audit, web check) passes
- [x] New tests: routing/ignore storage, selectors fit the 25-choice limit, invite matching, audit entry → case mapping (incl. skipping Lyra's own entries), diffs, transcript, and every event-log listener file exports only uniquely named Listener pieces
- [ ] On the dev app with Server Members Intent on: `/logconfig channel all #logs`, then edit/delete a message, `/purge 5`, join/leave voice, rename a role, change nickname, join with an invite
- [ ] Ban or time someone out via Discord's UI → a case appears in `/modlogs` and the mod log. `/ban` via Lyra still gives exactly one case
- [ ] `/logconfig ignore channel:#x` → nothing from #x is logged

## Known gaps

- No dashboard UI for event logging yet (P6).
- Thread create/delete and sticker changes aren't logged.

author: mkettn
body:
## Summary
- Month and weekday names and the texts of the Markdown template (table headings, "Pascha") come from a language file: a YAML file in a `lang_dir` of the configuration with `months` (12), `weekdays` (7, Monday first), `ui` (texts for templates, available as `ui.date` etc.) and `fallback`. The hardcoded English tables are gone from the C++ code.
- **The language** is the `language:` option of the configuration; `--lang=<language>` overrides it. The environment (`LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG`) is not looked at. The value is not checked: `language: foobar` uses the file `foobar.yaml` from the first `lang_dir` that has it. A missing file, or no language at all, is an error.
- The installed configuration (`config/config.yaml`) sets `language: en_US` and names the installed `lang` directory (next to `tpl/`), which ships `en_US.yaml`, `de_DE.yaml` and `de_AT.yaml`.
- **Fallbacks:** a language file can name a fallback language, again the name of a language file (`fallback: de_DE` in `de_AT.yaml`, `fallback: en_US` in `de_DE.yaml`). The fallback is read first and the keys of the file replace its keys (`ui` entry by entry), then the fallback of the fallback, and so on. Every file is read only once: if a fallback refers back to a file that was read already (a circular reference or a file that names itself), that is logged as a warning through spdlog and ignored. A missing fallback file is an error, and the months and weekdays have to be there at the end.
- The template backend takes a `Language`: `calendar_to_json()` gives the names in that language (`month.name`, `weekday_name`) and adds `ui`; the Markdown template uses `ui` for its headings and escapes all texts of the language like the data, so a language file cannot break the output. Configuration and language files are read by one shared helper.
- Not translated: the calendar file itself (names and other data are printed as written) and the rule names (left for later).
- CLI: `--lang=<language>` (needs `--year`). Exit status: 2 if the language file is not found, 1 if no language is set or a language file is invalid.

## Test plan
- [x] `ctest`: 56 tests pass. Unit tests cover the lookup of a language file in the `lang_dir`s (any name, only `<name>.yaml`, first directory wins, no `lang_dir`), a fallback chain (`de_CH` → `de_DE` → `en_US`: order, replacement, no warning), circular and self-referencing fallbacks (read once, exactly one warning, still correct), fallback errors (missing file, wrong type, invalid or incomplete fallback file), every kind of invalid language file (with file and line), escaping of language texts in the Markdown, the config options, and the German names in the template data. CLI tests cover `--lang` (`de_DE`, `de_AT` through its fallback, a custom name `foo_BAR`), the config option and `--lang` overriding it, an unknown language, no language set, a missing `lang_dir`, a circular fallback with its warning, an invalid language file, and the default configuration.
- [x] Installed into a custom prefix: the installed program renders English by default whatever the environment says, `--lang=de_AT` gives Jänner, an unknown language is an error; the tests also pass with an installed config present
- [ ] CI green
