author: valdi1111
body:
Part of #59

## Why

The pulls tracker had no way to show the pulls outside the site. #59 asks for a shareable image, in the style of the summary cards of other trackers. It is rendered on the server, so that the same card can later be sent by the chat bot (#22, next PR).

## What

- **node-services**: `POST /render/png` screenshots a self-contained HTML document with headless Chromium. Each render gets a fresh context with JavaScript off and every network request aborted, on a queue of its own (`RENDER_CONCURRENCY`, default 2) so it never waits behind AnimeWorld scraping. The browser is shared with AnimeWorld (`services/browser.js`) and relaunched if it dies. The service now listens on `127.0.0.1` only (`LISTEN_HOST` to change it), and the Symfony client calls `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`.
- **GamesBundle**:
  - `PullCard` / `PullCardSection` / `PullCardItem`, built from the summary of the stats calculators by `PullCardSectionFactory`.
  - `PullCardIconInliner` inlines the 128 px icons from the LiipImagine cache, filling it when needed; an icon that cannot be loaded becomes the item's initial.
  - `PullCardRenderer` and the `@Games/pulls/card.html.twig` template. The Ubuntu font is embedded (Latin subsets, UFL licence in `resources/fonts/ubuntu`), so the card looks the same on every server.
  - `PullCardLimiter`: 20 cards per user every 10 minutes (`games_pull_card`), 429 above that; 503 when node-services fails or times out.
- **Providers**: `HoyoversePullCardBuilder`, `GryphlinePullCardBuilder` and `PerfectworldPullCardBuilder` build one banner or every banner with pulls; a banner missing from the config (shown by the overview as a banner of its own) can be asked for alone. NTE uses the full S list (`s_pulls`, new in the compute result) because `recent_s_pulls` is capped at 50. The new endpoint `GET .../gameProfiles/{id}/pulls/card?banner=&all=&player=` (`#[MapQueryString]`) answers with a PNG download, `no-store`.
- **Frontend**: a "Share" button on the pulls page opens a modal. You pick the banner (the one on screen) or all of them, and tick "show every S" and "show nickname and UID" (both off by default). You get a preview, then Download, or Copy where the browser supports images on the clipboard.
- Defaults: at most 31 S for one banner and 15 per banner for the whole profile, with a "+N older" cell; long rarity labels ("5-Star"), since the embedded font has no ★.

## How it was checked

- **Full suite**: `php bin/phpunit --fail-on-warning --fail-on-notice --fail-on-risky` → OK, 2398 tests, 29693 assertions.
- **New tests**: section factory, renderer (HTML, sidecar call, errors, download headers), icon inliner, limiter, the three builders, the card action of the three controllers, card routes.
- **Live on dev** (`games.valdi.wip`, sidecar started by hand):
  - Committed code: single-banner cards of Endfield (from the modal, in the banner detail) and Genshin.
  - Before the final builder refactor: cards of every banner of Genshin, Star Rail, Endfield and NTE.
  - The modal from the overview and from a banner detail. The banner on screen is preselected, and the preview is dropped when an option changes. The download name comes from `Content-Disposition` (read from the DOM, not clicked).
  - `all=1` / `all=true` / `all=false`, and an unknown banner (400).
  - The 429 message in the modal.
  - 7.5 s for 58 S with the icon cache emptied: CDN downloads happen within the request.
  - AnimeWorld still works with the shared browser and the loopback client: `anime:add-download <episode url> --simulate --no-filter` scraped the page and extracted the video URL through node-services (nothing saved or downloaded).
- **Outside the site**:
  - The 503 path ran from a CLI script with node-services stopped: it fails after 2.8 s, thanks to the connect timeout.
  - A fake card with every badge state rendered through the real template and sidecar: rate-up, free, manual, declared pity, missing icon, long name, empty banner.
- **Tests only**: a banner missing from the config asked for alone (dev has no such data); the 503 inside the modal.
- **Not done**: the Download and Copy clicks.

## Known limit

The session is stored with PDO and its row stays locked for the whole request. The user's other requests therefore wait while a card renders: 1–7 s normally, up to 45 s if node-services hangs. To be evaluated globally in #66.

## Deploy

- **Usual deploy**: `website-deploy.sh` already restarts node-services, which the new route needs.
- **node-services now listens on `127.0.0.1` only**, and Symfony reaches it at `http://127.0.0.1:NODE_SERVICES_PORT`. No supervisor or service file reaches it from another host. Set `LISTEN_HOST` in `node-services/.env.local` only if it must be reachable elsewhere.
- **Optional**: install `fonts-noto-cjk` on the server, for nicknames outside the Latin script.

Port of onedr0p/home-ops#12290 and onedr0p/home-ops#12291.

Store the Talos secrets as the `talosctl gen secrets` bundle in one 1Password document, read it in the templates as minijinja data, and add these tasks:

- `//talos:gen-talosconfig` writes a talosconfig from the bundle.
- `//talos:validate` renders every node with a generated bundle and runs `talosctl validate` in strict mode. It needs no 1Password access, and the new `Talos` job in CI runs it.
- `//bootstrap:gen-secrets` replaces the bundle with a new one, for a new cluster only.

The document is `talos-secrets` in the `Kubernetes` vault, not `talos` as upstream, because the vault holds a secure note with the title `talos` and `op document get talos` selects that note. The document exists and holds the bundle from the running config of m0.

With the document in place, `mise run //talos:render-config` output gives "No changes." on `talosctl apply-config --dry-run` for all three nodes, and `mise run //talos:validate` passes.

body:
Closes #5161

On a finished Infinite Assault fight, Main menu and the board's corner Menu now go to the Play menu instead of showing the Continue screen. The attempt keeps the fight's result, so reopening `/assault` later finds the next level's briefing or the lost or repelled screen.

## What changed

In `apps/web/src/assault/fight/FightScreen.tsx`:
- **`onMenu`:** once the fight is over and its report has been read, it sends the report once and calls `navigate(paths.play)`. It no longer calls `onLeave` in that case.
- **Mid-fight Menu:** unchanged. It still asks first, and Leave still calls `onLeave`.
- **Report not yet read, or unreadable:** keeps today's path through `onLeave` (or Play when no `onLeave` is given) and sends nothing, so Resume still reopens the kept fight.
- **Docs:** the `onLeave` prop doc and the comment above `menuButton` now say this.

In `FightScreen.test.tsx`:
- **R4582001 corner Menu test:** it now expects one report, `onLeave` not called, and `/play`.
- **R4742000 test:** the result panel's Main menu test now expects the same, and I renamed it. It names `/assault` as the starting path and resets to `/` afterwards.
- **New test:** "R4582001 a finished fight whose report could not be read still leaves through onLeave and sends nothing".

## Testing

I did not run the old code to see the two rewritten tests fail. They assert `onLeave` not called and `/play`, which the old handler contradicted.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/assault`: 9 files and 55 tests passed.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`: clean.
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/assault`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok.
- Not run by me: `cargo fmt --check`, because no Rust changed. Clippy and the cargo tests are left to the harness.

## Decisions and departures

- **No route-level test:** I added none. The store tests for reopening the Assault page already prove what `/assault` shows after leaving a won or lost fight, as the plan said. That is the "Reopening `/assault` after leaving" criterion. I did not re-read those store tests this run.
- **Play, not the Assault's day screen:** I followed the issue's recommendation and R4742000.
- **Win skips the panel:** a player who picks Main menu after a win skips the "Level N beaten" panel. That is the effect the issue accepts.
- **Order in `onMenu`:** `sendOnce()` runs before `navigate`. The screen's unmount cleanup then finds the report already sent, so it is not sent twice (R4733000).

Built and checked on `claude-1`. This is a draft while its own review run, on the same subscription, reviews it adversarially and fixes what it finds (up to 3 rounds); CI runs on it meanwhile. Once that review approves it, it is marked ready and auto-merge turns on.

author: denkhaus
body:
## Cause

`fabro_blob`'s parameter description and rejection message both promise that `ref` may be the bare hex digest, but `ValidatedBlob::try_from` (lib/components/fabro-tool/src/blob.rs:46) validated only through `fabro_types::parse_blob_ref`, which requires the `blob://sha256/` prefix. The same digest with the prefix was accepted. The server blob door was not involved: it takes the already-parsed `BlobHash` as a path parameter.

## Fix

The tool parses the reference through a private helper: the prefixed form first, then the bare digest. `fabro_types::parse_blob_ref` is unchanged, because its other callers (the projection, `fabro run diff`) use it to tell a reference apart from a value, where a bare digest must not qualify. Description and error text are untouched; they are now true.

Not in scope: byte-offset paging for single-line blobs (the item's second part).

## Evidence

- New pin `blob_reads_the_bare_digest_and_the_prefixed_reference_alike` (fabro-workflow/tests/fork_run_tool_pins.rs) reads one blob through `blob_page` by both forms and asserts identical pages. RED before the fix, on the unmodified validation:
  `panicked at lib/components/fabro-workflow/tests/fork_run_tool_pins.rs:296:10: both reference forms validate: ToolError { message: "ref must be a blob reference (blob://sha256/<hex> or the bare digest)" }`
  GREEN after: PASS.
- New unit test `validation_accepts_both_reference_forms` (fabro-tool/src/blob.rs), including surrounding whitespace.
- Existing malformed-reference pins still pass with the unchanged message.
- `cargo nextest run -p fabro-tool -p fabro-workflow --no-fail-fast --retries 2 -j 6`: 275 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt --all --check` and `clippy -p fabro-tool -p fabro-workflow --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Refs denkhaus/work#1714

author: ylwang0701
body:
## Description

The GPU allocation behind a device communicator's resource window is missing from `ncclCommMemStats`. On eight B300s with eight GENK channels, the first Ring/Simple AllReduce allocates a 366 MiB window per rank, but the persistent counter grows by just 4 MiB. This change brings the reported increase to 370 MiB.

## Related Issues

Related to direction E of #2527. The [per-rank allocation measurements](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl/issues/2527#issuecomment-7229802951) show how the window size scales with the channel count.

## Changes & Impact

Charge the local backing allocation to `ncclMemPersist` once `symMemoryObtain` owns it. Release the charge with the last backing reference. This covers the public device communicator API and GENK's internal device communicator.

## Performance Impact

These are per-rank memory deltas across the first AllReduce on a single eight-B300 node, with one rank per GPU, CUDA 12.9 and 8 MiB int32 buffers. All eight ranks returned the same values.

| GENK channels | Persistent increase on master | Persistent increase with this change | GPU memory increase in both builds¹ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4 MiB | 50 MiB | 82 MiB |
| 4 | 4 MiB | 188 MiB | 220 MiB |
| 8 | 4 MiB | 370 MiB | 402 MiB |

¹ Measured independently with `cudaMemGetInfo` and NVML. The eight-channel legacy Ring/Simple control measured 336 MiB in both builds.

On two B300s with `splitShare=1`, creating and destroying a 32 MiB device resource moved the parent and child views of the shared counter up and down by 32 MiB. Three rounds returned to baseline. Registering a 32 MiB user buffer after warm-up added zero. Two A100s also exercised cleanup after an injected failure during memory tracking and after window creation.

Co-built by ylwang0701 and Astra.

Owner: "bu game modunda duvarların arkasından ateş etmesin botlar bana"

## Why it happened
- The bots' sight line and bullets were only stopped by the terrain and the building footprint boxes (`D.buildings`). Garden walls, fences, tree trunks, posts and house walls without a box (everything the walk's collision grid from v1.18 knows) hid nobody.
- A hit was decided from a sight line up to ~0.37 s old, traced from the bot's head, so a player who had just stepped behind cover could still be hit.

## Change
- `src/solids.js`: `segmentHit(a, b)`, a cell-by-cell (DDA) walk over the 25 cm grid; blocked below a cell's top (walls, fences) or, for tall solids, below 4.5 m. The first/last 0.35 m are skipped.
- `src/game.js` `trace()`: asks the grid for the part of the segment before the terrain/building hit. Used by the bots' sight lines, their missed rounds and the player's own shots (so walls work both ways).
- At the moment of a bot's hit, the shot is traced again from the muzzle to the hit point; if blocked, the round hits the wall (tracer + puff).
- `index.html`: passes `solids` to `createGame`. Before the grid is built (first ~second) it is the old test.

## Testing (headless Chromium, full village)
- Bot pinned 23 m from the player with a wall between (old test clear): 20 s of game time, **before: 57 shots, 283 damage; after: 0 shots, 0 damage**, the bot never sees the player.
- Of 800 random 8–68 m sight lines in the village that the old test called clear, 98 (12 %) are now blocked: 48 by tall solids, 50 by walls 1.3–2.5 m high.
- Cost: ~6 µs per sight line in swiftshader's CPU (max 8 sight lines a frame, unchanged), so cheap with 50–100 bots.

author: havaianasdestruido
body:
## What

Optimises the hot loops of the built-in deferred/PBR shader pack. No visual change claimed; the
equivalence harness below measures that.

**Where the per-frame cost is.** `lighting_point.fsh` runs once per fragment of *every* dynamic
light's bounding mesh (drawn with depth test off, ≤12 lights per chunk bucket), and
`eaglercraftLighting()` runs inside the per-light loop of `forward_core.fsh`,
`accel_particle_forward.fsh` and the water/glass variants. Everything else in the pack
(`skybox_irradiance.fsh`'s 156 taps/texel, the temporally amortised SSR march) is not per-frame and
was left alone.

**Changes**

1. `pow(x, 5.0)` → `x2 * x2 * x` in every Fresnel-Schlick term — `lib/pbr_lighting.glsl`,
   `lib/pbr_env_map.glsl`, `realistic_water_render.fsh`, `forward_glass_highlights.fsh` (7 sites).
   `highp pow()` is `exp2(5.0 * log2(x))` on GLES3 drivers: two SFU ops per light per fragment
   replaced by three ALU multiplies.
2. `lighting_point.fsh`: the facing test now runs on the **unnormalised** light vector
   (`normalize()` only scales by the positive `1/|d|`, so it cannot flip the sign of
   `dot(lightDir, N)`), so fragments the light cannot reach skip the `normalize()`, the colour
   divide and the whole BRDF. One `dot()` now serves the falloff and the `normalize()`, the colour
   texture fetch happens only for fragments that are shaded, and two dead `lightmapCoords` stores
   plus a duplicate `u_inverseViewMatrix4f` multiply are gone.
3. Per-light loops (`forward_core`, `accel_particle_forward`, water, glass): both culls moved
   *before* the `normalize()` and the `1/dist2` divide; the `0.025` radiance cut-off is compared as
   `L.r+L.g+L.b < 0.025 * dist2`. The emissive (`material.b == 1.0`) path keeps its old behaviour.

## Benchmark (before → after, same workload)

`./perfbench/shader/run_bench.sh` (new; gcc 12.2.0 `-O2`, no `-ffast-math`, CPU replay of the exact
scalar GLSL math on a 1920×1080 synthetic frame, 8 lights, blocky interior, 5 % metal / 25 % mirror
/ 2 % emissive materials):

| per shader invocation | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| `lighting_point` — pow / SFU pairs | 0.888 | **0.000** |
| `lighting_point` — texture fetches | 4.000 | 3.888 |
| `forward_core` (8 lights) — pow / SFU pairs | 3.414 | **0.000** |
| `forward_core` (8 lights) — sqrt / invsqrt | 12.414 | **7.664** |
| `accel_particle_forward` (8 lights) — pow / SFU pairs | 7.990 | **0.000** |
| `eaglercraftLighting` x86 instructions (`-DPBR_INSN`) | 147 | 139 (**−5.4 %**) |

| CPU replay | old | new | speedup (5 runs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lighting_point`, per covered light-fragment | 100.8 ns | 83.2 ns | 1.18–1.23× |
| `forward_core` light loop, per fragment | 317.6 ns | 259.7 ns | 1.16–1.22× |
| `accel_particle_forward` loop, per fragment | 506.1 ns | 412.2 ns | 1.19–1.23× |

The CPU ratios are an **upper bound**, not a GPU claim: libm `powf()` is far dearer than a GPU SFU
`pow()`. The reviewable, hardware-independent numbers are the op census (pow/SFU pairs, sqrt,
texture fetches) and the instruction count; the culling wins (11.2 % of covered point-light
fragments exit before the BRDF, ~4.75 avoided `normalize()` per forward fragment) are structural.

## Equivalence (old vs new, identical inputs)

| kernel | discard-mask mismatches | max ULP | max |diff| | RGBA16F differs | 8-bit `post_tonemap` differs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lighting_point`, 16.51 M fragments | **0** | 12 | 4.8e-7 | 182 | **0** |
| `forward_core` loop, 250 k fragments | 0 (same 853,479 lights kept) | 2604 | 4.8e-7 | 9 | **0** |
| `accel_particle` loop, 250 k fragments | 0 (same 1,997,528 kept) | 10 | 4.8e-7 | 9 | 1 |
| `eaglercraftLighting` + IBL, 600 k random cases | – | 4298 | 1.9e-6 | – | – |

Light/skip decisions are bit-identical. The ULP tail is the GGX specular peak (`1/denom²` blows up as
`NdotH → 1` for smooth metals), where absolute deviation is still ≤ 4.8e-7 — below one RGBA16F step
of the lighting target; **no point-lit fragment changes an 8-bit output**, and exactly one
`accel_particle` fragment sits on a rounding boundary.

## Also in this PR

- **GLSL validity:** `./perfbench/shader/run_validate.sh` assembles each shader like
  `ShaderSource.java`/`ShaderCompiler.java` and compiles it (plus the compile-flag combinations the
  pipeline builds) with the real glslang front end — **13/13 variants compile**; deliberately broken
  shaders are rejected.
- **Rejected after measuring:** sharing one `1/w` reciprocal across the transform prologue's two
  homogeneous divides (3 divides → 1 rcp, which drivers already emit). Measured cost: max 2116 ULP
  and 47 of 14.66 M fragments changing an 8-bit output vs 12 ULP / 0 without it. Backed out — same
  spirit as FINDINGS #2 and the rejected `Vec3.normalize` reciprocal.
- `perfbench/FINDINGS.md` #14, `perfbench/HOTSPOTS.md` (GPU-side hotspot inventory, including what
  was deliberately not touched), `TODO.md`, `perfbench/run_all.sh` (steps 16/17), `.gitignore`.

No Java/TeaVM code changed; the client build path is untouched.

author: loom-fleet-dispatch[bot]
body:
## Summary
`worktree.sh` resolved only a `loom-daemon`. On a tools-only install that came back empty, and an empty resolution means "skip" at each call site, so `worktree.sh <N>` reported success with its claim probe, crash cleanup, branch reuse and lease silently skipped, and `remove` refused with exit 2. The wrapper now takes `loom-tools` when no daemon resolves, so the guards of #14474 and #14475 stay in force with no daemon installed. A child of #14397 (Phase 3c).

## Changes
- `defaults/scripts/lib/locate-daemon-bin.sh`: `loom_tools_backstops` and `loom_tools_backstop_bin` resolve a `loom-tools` that serves the worktree family (`--help`-probed), through the existing `loom_locate_tools_bin`.
- `defaults/scripts/worktree.sh`: the create path's one `_WT_DAEMON_BIN` takes that backstop when the daemon resolution is empty. Daemon first, unchanged: a host with a `loom-daemon` resolves what it always did and an explicit pin still wins. Preferring the tools binary stays with the switch-over #14398.
- `defaults/scripts/lib/script-helper.sh`: `remove` and `--check` take the same backstop and exec it directly. `worktree-wip` (`snapshot` / `stash-*`) is not backstopped and still refuses with exit 2.
- `loom-daemon/src/bin/loom_tools.rs`, `loom-daemon/src/cli/forge_read.rs`: a mode refusal for `forge check-claim`, `check-open-pr` and `check-branch` exits `EX_PROBE_FAILED` (5) instead of the generic error exit. That exit is `1`, which is those verbs' *verified clear* code: `worktree.sh` reads it as "clear to claim" and the pre-push fence as "branch absent".
- Tests: `defaults/scripts/tests/test-loom-tools-worktree.sh` (new) and its runner `loom-daemon/tests/loom_tools_worktree.rs`.
- `docs/design/loom-tools-cli-boundary.md`: new §13.11, one sentence in §13.5.

## Acceptance Criteria Verification

| Criterion | Status | Verification |
|-----------|--------|--------------|
| Tools-only create, enter, reuse, remove; a checkout with spaces; git registration, filesystem state, sentinel | ✅ | `test-loom-tools-worktree.sh` (0) and (1): isolated install; `--json 101` is one JSON object; `cd` into the returned path lands on `feature/issue-101`; one registration; the re-run returns the same path; `remove` leaves no directory, registration or branch |
| Trace and test create-time cleanup, branch reuse, the claim check and the attended lease through the installed helpers; keep blocked / clear / unanswered distinct; keep both caller policies | ✅ | (1) shows each helper in the binary's argv; (2) crash cleanup; (3a)-(3f): a blocked claim refuses with no lease, a clear one creates with one lease comment and one renewer, unanswered is exit 5 at the guard and the wrapper continues; the mode refusal is 5, not 1; the fresh-branch probe refuses a fork PR and an unavailable forge |
| Interrupted creation, safe retry, lock ownership; removal refusal for unmanaged and dirty worktrees; legacy invocations and `--json` compatible; the wrapper as delegate | ✅ | (2) the creator is killed after acquiring the lock, the retry leaves one managed checkout, a live competitor's lock and token survive; (4) unmanaged and dirty refusals, `--force`; (5) a pinned daemon still wins, the `worktree-remove` invocation is unchanged, `--json` documents keep their key set |
| An isolated install fixture in the worktree shell tests; deeper helpers cannot resolve a host daemon; the workflow in the CLI boundary doc | ✅ | (0): every daemon lookup resolves nothing under `env -i` (the create path's, the cargo-target helper's, a pin, `PATH`, a repo build); §13.11 |

## Test Plan
- `cargo test -p loom-daemon --bin loom-tools --test loom_tools_worktree`: 8 unit tests and 2 integration tests pass. The integration test runs the new suite (142 assertions) and re-runs `test-worktree-remove.sh`, `test-worktree-json-purity.sh` and `test-worktree-issue-lock.sh` unchanged against the tools binary (26/26, 38/38, 9/9). Those three suite files are not edited.
- Run against the unmodified `HEAD` scripts, the new suite fails 70 of its assertions, including `remove` exiting 2 and a blocked claim creating a worktree.
- `cargo clippy` with CI's lint flags, scoped to the touched targets; `cargo fmt --check`; `shellcheck -S warning` on the four shell files.
- `check-ci-suite-manifest.sh`, `check-daemon-subcommand-versions.sh --list`, `check-doc-tocs.sh`, `check-dangling-links.sh`, `check-hooks-defaults-parity.sh` and `check-defaults-version-bump.sh --forbid-bump` pass.
- `test-loom-tools-lease.sh`, the `loom_tools_slice` test, `test-locate-daemon-bin.sh`, `test-tools-first-clean-install.sh`, `test-worktree-refused-claim-no-lease.sh` (19/19) and `test-script-helper-version-floor.sh` (135/135) pass in an environment with no daemon resolvable.
- No live forge run: the forge is a stateful stub `gh`, as the issue's test plan specifies.

TDD: no - the bug was reproduced by hand before any change (`remove` exit 2; an unguarded create; `forge check-claim` exit 1 with `mode` unset), but both suites were written after the glue. The new suite was then run against the unmodified scripts and fails 70 assertions there. The exit-code change has no automated pre-fix run, only the by-hand observation.

## Notes for the Judge
- `check-branch` on a mode refusal now reaches the pre-push fence as exit 5, its documented fail-closed BRANCH_COLLISION arm, where it used to read as exit 1 ("branch absent"). The fence labels the case a collision but prints the actionable mode text. `sweep-lease-fence.sh` is not touched.
- #14376 (peer-owned claim refusal) is still open. Its call sites, `forge check-claim --force-claim` and the `lease ensure` call after a successful add, are not edited here.
- A tools-only host needs `mode` set (`session`) for any forge-reaching call. With it unset a forge-shaped origin is refused by the fresh-branch probe rather than created unguarded, and `remove` of a branch with commits of its own removes the worktree, keeps the branch and exits 1. The tools-only installer does not write `mode`; that is the documented opt-in (§7.4), not something this PR changes.
- Observed while testing, not changed: `test-loom-tools-lease.sh` does not isolate `LOOM_LISTING_CACHE_DIR`, a host-shared `/tmp` store keyed only by repo, so a failed repo lookup in one run can back off the next on a shared host.
- CI was still running at hand-off.

Closes #14476

## What

This is the follow-up to K6.

- **Lower the first-load JS ratchets** in `e2e/budgets.spec.ts` to the values measured on main, plus about 600 B:

| route | measured on main (d670738) | old ratchet | new ratchet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| /product/sacuwin-100 | 169,302 B | 170,000 | **169,900** |
| / | 173,549 B | 175,000 | **174,150** |

  The measurement is gzipped `encodedBodySize` on a built server at a 390x844 viewport, with three loads each (all equal).

body:
Open rooms can now be archived straight from their row in the rail's rooms band, without opening the room first.

- **The control**: each open row has an archive control just left of the funnel. It shows on hover or keyboard focus, and its column is reserved so nothing shifts. It asks the pane header's own two-step question inside the row (`archive "…"? YES / NO`) and sends the same `PATCH /api/rooms/:id {archived: true}`. Archived rows get nothing new, and unarchiving stays in the room's header. There is no server or phone change.
- **A scroll fix that came with it**: when a row crosses into or out of the archived fold, `patchBand` now takes it out of the list before the pass and puts it back (the same node). Measured on headless Chrome with a focused row archived from elsewhere, the band used to jump to the end of the list. Now each row moves by exactly one row height, and pressing the row's own control holds `scrollTop` exactly. This is recorded in `docs/traps/rooms.md`.
- **Also checked**: row height and the funnel's position are unchanged at rest, on hover and when armed. Enter arms the confirm and Escape cancels it. A room that is open in a pane flips to UNARCHIVE and loses its composer.

body:
## Summary

Adds `iphone import <episode>` to the Linux `iphone` helper. It copies the clips you pick from the iPhone into `<episode>/originals/`, names each one from its recording date and checks every copy.

- Asks each time whether to include photos. The default is no.
- Lists files newest first with date, size and kind (`video`, `photo`, `live photo`). Live Photo video parts are hidden unless photos are included. Files already in `originals/` are marked "✓ imported".
- Names copies `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<phone name>`. Videos use Apple's local recording time; photos use EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` via `exiftool`, falling back to the file time with a warning.
- Checks free space and asks for confirmation before copying.
- Reads each phone file once, writing the copy and hashing the same bytes. It then hashes the copy and gives it its final name only if both match. Existing files are never overwritten, and an interrupted copy leaves no partial file.
- Shows copy progress, speed and ETA.
- Prints a Markdown summary table for the episode's `media.md`. Unmounts the phone if it mounted it. Never deletes anything from the phone.
- `linux/packages.txt` gains `gum`, `ffmpeg` and `perl-image-exiftool`. README and CLAUDE.md document the command.

## Testing

- `bash -n`. `shellcheck` is not installed.
- Date naming checked against existing T001 clips, e.g. `IMG_1711.MOV` → `20261113_095917_IMG_1711.MOV`.
- Dry runs of the list with photos on and off against a real phone: 38 videos with Live Photo parts hidden, imported files marked.
- Unmount on exit checked both when the command mounted the phone and when it was already mounted.
- Copy-and-checksum and the progress display tested on local 50 MB and 300 MB files.
- Real import of `IMG_1739.MOV` (3.6 GB) from the phone: copied as `20261127_102707_IMG_1739.MOV` with matching size and checksum. That run used the version before the progress display; live progress over USB has not been seen yet.

body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 7.4
| Bug fix?      | yes
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Issues        | -
| License       | MIT

`FragmentHandlerTest::testRender` failed once on 7.4 CI (unit, PHP 8.4, high-deps) with `Expectation for FragmentRendererInterface::render() failed.`

The likely cause: `setUp()` and `testRender()` each build a request with `Request::create()`, which sets `REQUEST_TIME` from `time()`. The callback compares both requests with `==` and only ignores `REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT`, so a second boundary between the two calls makes the expectation fail. The test no longer uses ClockMock (its `time-sensitive` group was removed in 30fa29fc655), so it uses the real clock.

Forcing a second boundary (a `usleep()` to the next second at the start of the test) makes it fail; with this change it passes.

This ignores `REQUEST_TIME` as well, like #68321 did for `InlineFragmentRendererTest`.

The same code exists on 6.4 and 5.4, and the change applies there too. I targeted 7.4 because 6.4 is now security-only, but test-only fixes have recently been merged into 5.4 (#68321, #68325, #68244, #68249, #68250). Should I keep targeting the lowest branch for test-only fixes like this one? If so, I can retarget this PR to 5.4.

body:
## Summary

Adds DRM ABI version 3 (`H15`/`T8122`, `H16`, `H17`) program load and execution to `libane` and `ane-run` so `omarchy-ane` userspace talks directly to the upstream `aurora-silicon/linux` in-tree `/dev/accel/accelN` driver on Apple M3 (T8122 / J615) without an out-of-tree kernel module.

## Changes

- `ane/src/uapi/drm/ane_accel.h`: add `ANE_CHIP_H15` (15), `ANE_CHIP_H16` (16), and the upstream ABI-3 load/exec UAPI definitions (`DRM_IOCTL_ANE_H16_LOAD`, `DRM_IOCTL_ANE_H16_EXEC`, `DRM_ANE_H16_MMAP_OFFSET`, `DRM_ANE_H16_EXEC_IN_PLACE`, `struct drm_ane_h16_{section,load,buffer,exec}`).
- `libane/ane.h`, `libane/ane.c`: add `ANE_DEV_ID_T8122` (`0x8122`) to `ane_dev_id_table[]`, pass `DRM_IOCTL_VERSION` minor into the backend, and dispatch ABI-3 nodes to `ane_v3`.
- `libane/ane_v3.h`, `libane/ane_v3.c`, `libane/Makefile`: pure-C HWX parser and 4-section builder (`generic`, `operation`, `procedure`, `text_properties`) supporting H15 (subtype 6, 8-word task header), H16 (subtype 7, 9-word) and H17 (subtype 9, 9-word), with zero-copy `mmap` + `DRM_ANE_H16_EXEC_IN_PLACE` on minor >= 1 and automatic copy-mode fallback on minor 0 or `-EOPNOTSUPP`.
- `tools/ane-run.c`: accept `--hwx FILE` and `--check add-dense` for dense fp16 add surfaces (`[1, 1, 128, 128]`).
- `tools/test_libane_t6050.c`, `tools/test_libane_v3.c`, `tools/Makefile`: host-only enumeration, H15/H16 section-builder, wrapped `mmap` in-place and copy-mode ioctl tests.

## Verification

- `make -C libane libane && make -C tools check`: all targets compile clean under `-Wall -Werror -Wextra -Wdeclaration-after-statement -O3 -std=gnu99` and pass (including `test_libane_t6050`, `test_libane_v3` on `fixtures/h15-hwx/add/model.hwx`, `test_ane_session_cache_lsan`, and `test_ane_smoke.py`).
- `python3 tools/check_no_macos_read_methods.py`: clean.
- Note: host-tested against a wrapped ABI-3 device; real J615 hardware execution is pending an owner run on `aurora-silicon/linux` `main`.

author: joanreyero
body:
## What and why

The server is the only truth and the first answer wins. `assertSingleActiveRun` answers 409 `MKTG_RUN_ACTIVE`, but it was check-then-create: a start read the slot's stored runs and then created its Guild session, so two simultaneous starts both passed the check and `retireOlderRuns` superseded one afterwards. Two Guild sessions for one slot. The comment on `start()` called the active-slot reservation a follow-up; this is it.

A start now reserves the slot with a conditional write before `guildService.createSession`, and releases it on failure. Of two simultaneous starts, exactly one creates a Guild session and the other gets 409 `MKTG_RUN_ACTIVE` with who and when.

## What changes

- **Slot service** (`mktg-run-slot.service.ts`, new): the claim and the release. The reservation is created only when absent, or written over the exact version read when that one holds nothing any more (released, expired or unreadable). A release is fenced by the start's claim and by the version read, so a late one never frees a newer start. No reservation outlives two minutes (`MKTG_RUN_SLOT_TTL_MS`).
- **Run service** (`mktg-document-run.service.ts`): `withActiveSlot` wraps a start. The stored runs are read, and a discard applied, only with the slot held. The reservation is kept until the run record is published, which then holds the slot.
- **Start paths** (`mktg-agents`, `linkedin-post`, `member-360`, `aeo-geo` controllers, `mktg-document-redraft.service.ts`): each session-creating start runs inside the reservation.
- **Guild proxy** (`guild.service.ts`, `mktg-guild-dispatch.util.ts`): `createSession` records per request whether the call was sent and whether it was answered with a session id, so a failure before dispatch is told from an uncertain one.
- **Shared** (`@lfx-one/shared`): the slot constants, the reservation and dispatch interfaces, and the 409's reservation form in `mktg-run-active.utils`.
- **Docs**: `docs/architecture/backend/mktg-document-revisions.md` describes the reservation, the two forms of the 409 and what is not covered.

## Size

The diff is about 1,005 changed lines (894 added, 111 removed; 539 of them specs and docs), at the repo's target. It is one PR because a split at the primitive would leave an unused service on `main`.

## What it covers

Every session-creating start runs inside the reservation:

- a new catalog chat,
- the five kit generates,
- the three one-offs (LinkedIn, Member 360, AEO/GEO),
- the comments redraft (`/revise`), which closes the window #6360 documented.

A same-ID replay takes no slot.

## The two defects the family export's review found (#6365) are not repeated

- **An uncertain dispatch keeps the claim until it expires.** A timeout, a 5xx, a 2xx with no id, or a session whose record could not be written: Guild may hold a run nobody can follow, so the slot stays reserved. Release happens only for a failure before dispatch or a confirmed refusal (the existing `redraftWasNotAccepted` classifier).
- **The reservation's 409 names no run.** A run is named only from a published record, so the reservation's 409 carries `agentKey`, `startedBy`, `startedByViewer` and `startedAt`, and no `activeRunId`, `state` or `documentId`. A published active run answers first, with the unchanged 409.

## Choices made in the build

1. The loser of a truly simultaneous start gets a 409 with who and when but no run id, so the pages show their ordinary could-not-start line and the next attempt gets the named dialog. Showing who is starting would be a client change, filed: `wi-fu-run-slot-loser-sees-who-is-starting-and-a-published-run-frees-the-slot`.
2. After an uncertain Guild failure the same slot answers "Your <label> run is starting. Try again in a moment." for up to 2 minutes.
3. A redraft whose slot is reserved by the caller's own start answers 503 `MKTG_REDRAFT_START_UNCERTAIN` instead of 409, because the browser treats a 409 `MKTG_RUN_ACTIVE` as proof nothing was sent and drops its recovery ID.

## What is left, each filed

All three are filed as `wi-fu-run-slot-covers-retry-chat-follow-up-and-the-rebuild-chain`, and `retireOlderRuns` stays as the net for them:

- Retry of a failed run and a catalog chat follow-up create no Guild session and still re-occupy a slot by check-then-write.
- The rebuild chain starts kit sessions outside the run tracker.
- A start that takes longer than 2 minutes can be overtaken.

## Review notes — known minor findings (intentionally deferred)

- When the dispatch was accepted and the run record was published but a later step failed, the reservation is kept until it expires. A "Discard and start over" of that run is refused for up to 2 minutes, and the warning's wording is wrong for that case.
- `release()` keeps the opaque creator subject in the released slot object.

## Checks

- `yarn format:check`, `yarn lint:check` (0 errors), `yarn check-types`, `yarn build`, `./check-headers.sh`: pass on this head, after merging `main`. The merge brought in #6378 and #6379, was clean and shares no file with this branch; the branch already sat on top of #6373, #6374 and #6375, so `mark()` needed no resolution.
- Specs on this head: the full server vitest (471 files, 17,893 tests) and the full shared vitest (301 files, 10,907 tests) pass. The seven touched server specs are 556 tests; shared `mktg-run-active.utils` is 68.
- The server specs are the regression guard: the e2e helpers stub every `/api` route, so an e2e case cannot prove this.
- Reviewed by: selfserve-reviewer, lfx-general-code-review, lfx-self-serve-code-review, lfx-self-serve-learnings-review (two rounds).
- PR shape: 894 additions in 21 files; every commit is signed and signed off; no protected file is touched. Three shape items are left as they are: the branch is named for its WorkItem and not for an issue number; the work is tracked as that WorkItem and has no GitHub Issue; and the merge of `main` is a merge commit, so its subject is not a conventional one.

**Hand test:** Joan did not hand-test this branch: she delegated the hand test for this session, so the automated checks plus the code-owner approval stand in for it, and the change is server-only.

No user docs impact: Marketing OS is dark-launched and has no `docs/user` section.

Part of wi-st-atomic-active-slot-reservation-on-start

## Summary

A failed post could not be retried from the post page's side panel: **Now** and **Schedule** answered 409 because `FAILED` was not a schedulable target state, so the Schedule button stayed greyed out and the only route was "Needs you → Retry publish".

- `FAILED` is now schedulable in `post-group-contract.service.ts`, so the side panel's Now (publish now) and Schedule (new future time) work for a failed target.
- Scheduling a failed target starts a fresh attempt (`freshAttemptMutation`): the old error and attempt count are cleared, and the existing schedule write mints a new version-bound publish approval. Without that, the worker would refuse the due post for having no approval.
- `post-group-target.operations.ts` stays under the 1000-line runtime-complexity ratchet (998).

## Related issue

No-Issue: found while auditing recent posts after a failed Instagram post could not be rescheduled; small fix to an existing flow.

## Scope

- API only; no web change (the side panel already calls these actions) and no migration.
- Not changed: the `POST /posts/:id/retry` thread-retry path and "Retry publish" on the post page.
- Meta Graph errors 100/33 (token lost access) are not fixed by retrying; the channel must be reconnected first.

## Verification

Finish condition: a failed target can be scheduled now or at a future time through the release-target action and ends up `SCHEDULED` with a fresh approval and no leftover error.

- Three new specs in `post-group-target.operations.spec.ts`: a failed target is scheduled with its error and attempts cleared, publish-now on a failed target, and a published target is still refused with a conflict.
- `bun run preflight` passes on the final head: ratchets, e2e spec impact, Biome, secretlint, affected typecheck, API spec typecheck and executable contracts.
- Not run: a live retry against production; the worker path is covered by the existing approval refusal logic.

body:
## feat(web-ui-minimalista): UI SecurityManager (C9) y hallazgos de uso real

### Resumen
Implementa el change C9 `web-ui-minimalista`: la App Databricks `securitymanager`
(título "SecurityManager"), una UI Streamlit para otorgar privilegios con modelo
híbrido. La autorización es por llamante (OBO). La ejecución usa OBO para Unity
Catalog y Apps, y el service principal broker para SCIM y el plano de control.

**C9 queda ABIERTO (no se archiva).** La prueba de uso real reveló defectos (H5)
que se resuelven en el change `ui-uso-real`. Orden de archivado: primero C9 y
luego `ui-uso-real`.

### Cambios por área
**Descubrimiento (3.1-3.4)**
- Principals por SCIM con el SP, preservando el App Id de los service principals.
- Objetos de UC con OBO: catálogos, esquemas, tablas, volúmenes, modelos ML,
  external locations y connections.
- Plano de control: clusters, serverless, warehouses, apps y USO_TOKEN.
- Un fallo de listado se distingue de una lista vacía (`ErrorDescubrimientoOpciones`).

**Autorización y flujo (3.5, 4.1-4.4, 5.1)**
- Disponibilidad por privilegios efectivos (semántica C3), servicio de solicitud
  y previsualización del split OBO/broker.
- Estado de sesión con huella y confirmación única (se evita ejecutar dos veces
  y se revalida al confirmar).
- Servicio de ejecución, presentador de filas y totales por estado.

**Seguridad y bitácora (5.2-5.3)**
- Escritor de bitácora REST con identidad de App.
- Redacción de secretos en mensajes y errores controlados sin credenciales.

**App y despliegue (2.12, 6.1-6.5)**
- `app.py` delgado, `CrearVerticalUi` (composición con DI) y controlador.
- Propiedad `id_warehouse` (config → entorno `CONTROL_ACCESOS_ID_WAREHOUSE` →
  descubrimiento), sin valores embebidos.
- README con el despliegue de `securitymanager` y el bundle sync.

### Hallazgos tratados
- **F1/F2**: `auth_type='pat'` y paso de Databricks Connect a Statement Execution
  (REST) en la App.
- **H4**: `pyspark` entraba al runtime de la App por el gráfico de imports.
  Corrección: constructor de registro sin Spark e imports perezosos. Smoke test
  nuevo que bloquea `pyspark` en un subproceso.
- **H5 (abierto, tarea 6.6)**: ver "Estado" más abajo.

### Pruebas (perfil `andresFree`)
- 664 pruebas unitarias y funcionales en verde.
- 33 de aceptación de C9 (escenarios 1:1 con el delta-spec `grant-management-ui`).
- Gate integral `free` 7.1-7.3: 8/8. Integral 8.3: 49 passed y 14 skipped (los
  gates del spike OBO viejo quedan superseded).
- JUnit en `results/*.xml`.
- App desplegada en Free y cargando sin errores.

### Estado y límites conocidos (H5)
La prueba con el usuario administrador del workspace mostró:
1. **Falsos bloqueos en datos**: exige el privilegio exacto (`SELECT`);
   `SHOW GRANTS` no refleja la propiedad ni al Metastore Admin.
2. **Falsos bloqueos en control**: se omiten las ACL `inherited=true`, aunque
   existe `admins → CAN_MANAGE`.
3. Selectores de catálogo y esquema son campos de texto.
4. El filtro por tipo de principal no se aplica y se usa el primer principal del
   tipo, no el elegido.
5. Volúmenes y external locations fallan por falta del scope `unity-catalog`.
6. Falta "Default Automated Compute" en compute serverless.

Todo se corrige en `ui-uso-real` (solo `proposal.md` por ahora). No se modifica
código en este PR por esos hallazgos.

### Pendiente
- 2.11 y 7.4 (Azure, `azure_approval`): se trasladan a `ui-uso-real` para probar
  una sola vez con la App corregida. Azure autorizado (`andresAzureDev`), con la
  App detenida salvo durante las pruebas.
- Revisión humana del camino de autorización antes de archivar (D13 #7).

### Otros artefactos
- Micro-change `compute-grants-mensaje-feature` (solo proposal, lateral): arregla
  2 pruebas de aceptación de C7 obsoletas tras C8. No bloquea C9.

### Notas de seguridad
Ningún secreto en el repositorio, los logs ni la UI. Los pasos de despliegue y el
consentimiento en navegador los ejecuta el humano.

body:
## Summary

Completed the full **GlobalMapper + Map baseline** for Stage 2, including preprocessing, full training, temperature tuning, validation visualization, and final evaluation.

## Training Configuration

- **Training dataset:** 22,237 graph-matched NYC blocks
- **Model parameters:** 7.99M
- **GPU:** NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB
- **Training steps:** 97,500 (early stopping)
- **Training time:** 2.216 hours
- **Best validation score:** 0.29585
- **Selected temperature:** T = 1.0

## Final Test Results

All evaluations were performed on **1,000 test blocks**, with zero missing predictions.

| Configuration | Mean Score ↓ | Map IoU ↑ | Overlap ↓ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Oracle | 0.338 | 0.425 | 0.000 |
| Oracle Raw | 0.277 | 0.427 | 0.096 |
| Stage 1 NYC C3 | 0.535 | 0.401 | 0.000 |

## Key Findings

- **Oracle:** The model generates structured building layouts with negligible building overlap after trimming.
- **Oracle Raw:** Achieves a lower overall score and better footprint distribution metrics, but introduces building overlap.
- **Stage 1 NYC C3:** Shows noticeable performance degradation when conditioned on generated maps instead of ground-truth maps.
- The Stage 1 NYC C3 evaluation has particularly high relative coverage and volume errors, which remain important limitations for the full pipeline.

## Deliverables

This PR includes:

- `progress/stage2_globalmapper_final/RESULTS.md` — Training configuration, evaluation results, methodology, and limitations.
- `progress/stage2_globalmapper_final/fig_gm_selected.png` — Validation comparison of the Rule baseline and GlobalMapper + Map.

The complete experimental artifacts are backed up to the shared Google Drive:

`GenAI/project/globalmapper_final_handoff.zip`

The archive includes:

- Trained model checkpoint (`best.pt`)
- Training configuration and logs
- Quantization bins and height network
- Temperature tuning results
- Final test predictions and evaluation summaries
- Validation visualization and technical report

## Notes

- The full training completed normally via early stopping.
- Temperature selection was based on validation results.
- Final testing was performed without test-set tuning.
- Large model checkpoints and prediction files are stored in Google Drive rather than committed to GitHub.

body:
Before: An imported `.html` / `.htm` book read as a column of fragments. `html_to_text` joined every DOM text node with `"\n"`, and since only `txt` books get hard-wrap reflow, every one of those lines became its own paragraph. `

Hello reader.

` rendered as three paragraphs ("Hello", "reader", "."); any link, emphasis, or a source line break inside one `

` split it the same way. The `` text also showed up as the book's first line. The existing test didn't catch it because it joins all blocks with a space before checking for "Hello reader". After: One paragraph per block element. Inline markup and source whitespace inside a block read as running text; `<br>` and block elements (`p`, `div`, headings, list items, table cells, `blockquote`, …) start a new paragraph; `<pre>` keeps its own lines; `<title>` is dropped with its text, as ammonia already does for `<script>` / `<style>`. ## How `src-tauri/src/commands/books/format.rs` `html_to_text`: still sanitises with ammonia, then walks the scraper tree (same approach as `offline_dictionary::html_to_lines`), collapsing whitespace inside a block and separating blocks with a blank line. ## Verification - New test `html_inline_markup_and_source_line_breaks_stay_inside_their_paragraph` (`books/tests.rs`) prepares a small HTML book and asserts the exact block list. On `main` it fails with `["T", "Chapter Two", "Hello", "reader", ".", "It was a", "dark", "and", "stormy night.", …]`; on this branch it gives `["Chapter Two", "Hello reader.", "It was a dark and stormy night.", "one", "two", "lines", "keep", "this"]`. - `cargo test --all-features` (1901 pass), `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `npm run test:unit` (1725 pass), `npm audit` (0). ## Note HTML books that were already imported keep their old prepared text until they are re-imported: I did not bump `TEXT_DOCUMENT_VERSION`, because that re-prepares every text book and would move the stored character offsets of existing highlights in HTML books. That follows the repo's testing-stage rule (re-import instead of migrating). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

## Summary

Raise Gemini's first-byte and stream-idle waits from 5 minutes (300 s) to 10 minutes (600 s), scoped strictly to `GeminiProvider`, so long Gemini tool-call generations do not time out prematurely while Google buffers function calls until complete.

## Changes

- `crates/wisp-core/src/provider/gemini.rs`:
  - Raise `FIRST_BYTE` from 300 s to `Duration::from_secs(10 * 60)` (600 s).
  - Add a Gemini-local `const IDLE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10 * 60);` and drop the `super::sse::IDLE_TIMEOUT` import so `GeminiProvider::from_endpoint_with_identity` wires both 600 s waits across Antigravity subscription, API-key, and Bearer gateway routes.
  - Add unit test `gemini_stream_waits_are_ten_minutes_for_subscription_and_api_routes` pinning both Gemini 600 s waits and constructed `provider.waits` across subscription, API-key, and Bearer credentials.
- `docs/architecture.md`: update the Adapter contract section to state first-byte and idle waits per provider (first-byte: 15 min Anthropic, 10 min Gemini, 5 min OpenAI; idle: 10 min Gemini, 5 min Anthropic and OpenAI).
- `docs/gemini.md`: document Gemini's 10-minute first-byte and stream-idle waits across subscription and API-key/gateway streams.
- `crates/wisp-core/src/provider/sse.rs` (`IDLE_TIMEOUT = 5 * 60`) and `crates/wisp-core/src/provider/anthropic/tests/retries.rs` (`the_idle_watchdog_is_five_minutes`) are untouched; Anthropic and OpenAI waits, request bytes, caching, and billing classification are unchanged.

## Verification

- `verify.sh quick`: `QUICK OK; guards ran` (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `source_guards`, `no_comments`, and fast comment grep; recorded on tree `c6b7f838da5f89d1`).
- `cargo clippy --target wasm32-wasip2 -p wasm-fixture -p board -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `cargo clippy -p wisp-cli --no-default-features -- -D warnings`: pass.
- Targeted `cargo nextest run -p wisp-core --lib`: 5 passed (`gemini_stream_waits_are_ten_minutes_for_subscription_and_api_routes`, `antigravity_pre_send_redaction_change_rebuilds_brief_and_keeps_gemini_prefix_stable`, `the_idle_watchdog_is_five_minutes`, `a_stalled_stream_times_out_once_the_first_event_has_arrived`, `drive_waits_the_first_byte_wait_for_headers_and_for_the_first_chunk`).

## Review

author: pedrogrocha13
body:
Refs #59

## O que muda
Nova etapa "Geracao de Python" no `run_tests.sh` e no `run_tests.ps1`. Para cada `tests/python/nome.js`:
1. a saída de `./minijs --python` precisa ser igual a `nome.py.esperado`;
2. o arquivo gravado com `-o` precisa ser igual à saída de `--python`, sem nada impresso na tela;
3. o `.py` gerado é executado e o que ele imprime precisa ser igual a `nome.saida`.

O Python é procurado como `python3` e `python` (Linux) e `python3`, `python` e `py` (Windows). Cada candidato precisa responder a `--version`, o que descarta o atalho da Microsoft Store. Sem Python, o script avisa, pula só a execução e mostra no sumário quantas execuções foram puladas, sem quebrar as outras etapas. No Windows, a execução usa `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`, para acentos saírem iguais ao `.saida`.

A pasta `tests/python/` e os trios já tinham sido criados na T29, T30 e T32, então não foi preciso um commit só para criá-la.

## Testes
- Linux: 106/106 no `make test` (283 testes unitários), com os 7 trios de `tests/python/` passando nas três checagens, inclusive a execução dos `console.log` da T32.
- Windows (PowerShell 5.1, Python 3.14): a etapa nova passa nos 7 trios. Sem Python, todas as etapas passam e o sumário mostra 7 execuções puladas.
- Casos negativos testados nos dois scripts: `.py.esperado` errado e `.saida` errada fazem os testes falharem, com a diferença mostrada no Linux.

# 概要

`GET /events` の各予定に `recurringSeries` を返すようにした（SPEC-009「GET /events（SPEC-009 で追加するフィールド）」）。#404 の時点では常に `null` を返していた。

## 関連Issue

Closes #405

## 受け入れ条件の対応

- [x] シリーズに属する予定では `recurringSeries`（`id` 付き）を返す: 一覧クエリで `recurring_event_series` を LEFT JOIN し、`EventReadModel.RecurringSeries` からレスポンスへ変換
- [x] 単発の予定と、共有リンクから追加した予定（`isSubscribed = true`）では `recurringSeries = null` を返す: 単発は `series_id` が NULL のため、購読予定は UNION ALL の購読側でシリーズ列を NULL 固定にしているため
- [x] クエリサービスとハンドラのテストが書かれている: クエリリポジトリの統合テスト、ハンドラのユニットテスト、ルート統合テスト

## 変更内容

- `db/queries/event.sql`: `ListEventsWithTagsByUserAndDateRange` / `...FilteredByTag` の自分の予定側に `recurring_event_series` の LEFT JOIN とシリーズ列を追加。購読側はシリーズ列を NULL で返す（作成者のシリーズ情報を DB から読み出しもしない）
- `usecase/event`: `RecurringSeriesReadModel` を追加し、`EventReadModel.RecurringSeries` に持たせる。ADR-022 に従い、書き込み側の集約や Repository に依存せず、保存値をそのまま文字列で持つ
- `infrastructure/repository/event.go`: シリーズ列を ReadModel に詰め替える（`end_until_date` は `YYYY-MM-DD`）
- `interface/handler/event.go`: `toRecurringSeriesResponseFromReadModel` を追加し、`GetEvents` で `recurringSeries` を返す
- テスト
  - クエリリポジトリ（統合）: 終了条件ごとの値、タグ付きの回の集約、タグ絞り込み、単発の予定、他人のシリーズの回を購読した予定
  - ハンドラ（ユニット）: `count` / `until_date` + `monthly_nth_weekday` / `indefinite` の出力形
  - ルート（統合）: POST で作った3回すべてが POST と同じ `recurringSeries` を返すこと、購読者には `null` を返すこと

## リスク・影響範囲

- `GET /events` のレスポンスで、シリーズに属する予定の `recurringSeries` が `null` からオブジェクトになる。フロントエンドはまだこのフィールドを使っていない（表示は #410）
- `QueryService.FindByID`（共有リンク用）は変更していない
- ロールバックはこのPRの revert で済む（マイグレーションなし）
- 統合テスト（testcontainers）は、作業環境のサンドボックスが Docker ソケットへの接続を拒否したためローカルで実行できていない。CI の結果で確認する

author: amoabakelvin
body:
## ELI5

When you unpair a phone on your Mac, the Mac has to tell every Orca server it relays that phone to, so each server drops the phone too. It used to tell only servers it had talked to since it last started, and only right away: a server that was offline, or any server after a Mac restart, kept the phone. Now the Mac remembers which servers hold its phones and tells each of them as soon as it reaches them again.

<!-- orca-pr-loc -->
<!-- Generated by the "PR test LoC" GitHub Action and rewritten on every push. Humans and AI agents: do not edit, move, or remove this block when updating the PR body. -->

| | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Test | 1 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​165 | 0 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​165 |
| Prod | 11 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​340 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​43 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​297 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## What Changed

**What triggers a re-sync**
- **Any change to the phone list.** The device registry's change listener now drives `phonesChanged()`, so cascade revokes and edits made on disk count too. The explicit call in `revokeMobileDevice` is gone. The listener is deferred one microtask, because a save announces before the registry holds the saved list, and it is merged so a cascade runs once.
- **A server coming back into contact.** The desktop watches the existing `hosts.onStatusChanged` and re-syncs a server when it goes from out of contact to in contact. WSL's bulk call, which carries no contact, is ignored.
- **The registry becoming ready.** This catches servers that came into contact before the phone list could be read.

**What gets sent**
- A server gets the new list only if it may still hold a dropped phone. Added phones still sync on their first relayed request, as before. A server that never held this desktop's phones is never contacted.
- `relayed-phone-servers.json` in userData records which servers may hold this desktop's phones, so this survives restarts:
  - The record is written durably after the server says it can mint phones and before the sync that may mint one. If the write fails, the sync doesn't go out.
  - It is cleared after an empty sync is answered.
  - At launch, servers no longer saved on this desktop are pruned from it.
- A null or unreadable registry is never sent as an empty list, which would revoke every phone on every server. The sync is refused instead.

**Ordering**
- Syncs to one server go out one at a time, so an older list can never land after a newer one.
- One check runs per server. A trigger that arrives during a check runs it once more afterwards.
- A phone paired while a sync is in flight re-checks once that sync answers, instead of being refused.

## Why

The next PRs in this stack let a phone hold its own pairing with a server, chained to its delegated row there. Unpairing the phone on the desktop then has to reach every server that holds it, including servers that were offline at the time and servers the desktop next reaches after a restart. Otherwise the phone keeps direct access.

Re-syncing every server on each launch would also mint the desktop's phones on servers nobody uses from the phone, such as a teammate's server. It would also wake idle desktops. Recording only the servers that actually hold phones keeps the nothing-to-do case at zero calls and zero writes.

## Linked Issue

Part of #40079, #27988, #26291 and #10426. This is the revocation half; the phone's own server pairing comes later in this stack.

## Visual Proof

N/A: no UI changes. The proof is a real three-process run, described under Testing.

## Testing

Real run on macOS with two worktree-built `orca serve` processes: a server, and a desktop paired to it. A phone-protocol client was paired to the desktop.
- The phone's relayed `status.get` reached the server. The server minted the delegated row, and the desktop wrote `relayed-phone-servers.json` with the server's id.
- I stopped the server, removed the phone's row from the desktop's registry on disk, then restarted the server. Within 10 seconds the desktop saw the server back in contact, re-synced, and the server's delegated row count went from 1 to 0.

`delegated-phone-grant-cache.test.ts` runs the real cache over a real record file. It pins four cases:
- A phone dropped while the server was unreachable is sent after a restart.
- Contact flaps and added phones send nothing.
- A phone dropped while the previous removal is still in flight is sent.
- An unreadable phone list is never sent, and the check runs once the list is readable.

- [x] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below
- [x] Every added test fails without this change and avoids the [test anti-patterns](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/blob/main/docs/agents-md-refs/test-antipatterns.md)

## Performance

- **No phones ever relayed:** the desktop does no host lists, server resolves, RPCs, writes or timers. It reads one small file at launch, and status events cost one map update each.
- **Desktop with phones:** each server holding its phones gets at most one extra sync per phone removal, and one after a reconnect when a removal is still pending.
- **Cascades:** a cascade of registry saves runs one check.
- **The record file:** it is written only when a server starts or stops holding phones. An unchanged set copies nothing.

## Risk

The riskiest parts are the record file and the ordering, because they decide whether a revocation reaches a server.
- If the record is lost (deleted or unreadable), a phone unpaired while its server was unreachable stays on that server until the next relayed request or the next phone change. That is today's behaviour.
- A failed record write fails that relayed request; the phone retries it.

A plain revert restores the old behaviour. It leaves `relayed-phone-servers.json` behind, and nothing older reads it.

**Level:** Medium

## Notes

Ensure no issues in: Security, Cross-platform support (Linux, Windows, Mac), Remote SSH, Mobile, general backwards compatibility, performance

On Windows, WSL hosts that this desktop hasn't started stay recorded: the launch prune compares against every saved server, not just the ones a phone can reach now. Builds on #51226 (merged).

author: bawoodruff
body:
Two unrelated hygiene changes, kept as separate commits.

## `chore: keep private names out of a public repo`

This repository is public. Two kinds of internal detail had leaked into it:

- **A private sibling repo's name as fixture data.** `graphname_test.go`,
  `internal/hub/ownership_test.go` and `push_layers_test.go` used a real private
  repo name (and a `<name>Secret` string derived from it) to stand for "some
  other repo". The tests only ever needed two *distinct* names to prove graph
  names and layer references stay separate, so an obviously-fictional one does
  the job identically. All 14 references replaced; none remain in the tree.
- **The hostname of the estate's secrets manager.** `docs/kg-shared-service-design.md`
  published it inline. The sentence keeps its actual point — credentials belong in
  a secrets manager rather than env vars — without naming the host that serves it.

Neither was a credential, but together they handed any reader a partial map of
infrastructure, for no benefit to anyone reading the code.

`www.cortexa.com` in `graphname_test.go` is deliberately left alone: that is a
public website, not internal infrastructure.

## `chore: ignore Claude Code's per-agent worktrees`

Background agents are given isolated git worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` so
two of them cannot fight over one working tree. They showed up as untracked noise
in `git status` during a run — the kind of thing that ends up accidentally staged.
Scoped to the subdirectory rather than all of `.claude/`, so a shared
`settings.json` remains an option later.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l .` clean in `src/kg`; `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` both pass.
- `go test ./internal/hub/... .` passes (`internal/hub` 41.9s, `kg` 64.7s), run
  without `-race`: ThreadSanitizer cannot reserve shadow memory under this
  toolchain (error code 487), which is why `ci.yml`'s Windows legs omit it too.
  The ubuntu legs in CI cover `-race`.
- Rebased onto `5ed73b0`; no `CHANGELOG.md` entry, as this changes no behaviour.

author: hemskgren
body:
## Summary
- Make Operations the sole active owner of infrastructure monitoring, container runtime diagnostics, and MQTT failed-connection summaries.
- Retire legacy Hub/Public monitoring workers and Hub-tab infrastructure controls; remove the Docker socket and Mosquitto log mounts from hub-bootstrap while preserving Device Monitor, Hub-owned diagnostics, Firmware Builder, and rollback tables/code.
- Preserve Operations history without migration: historical `nginx` samples are interpreted as `hub_api_via_nginx`; `nginx_local` remains independent, with the expected history discontinuity documented.
- Refine the Operations tab layout and labels, remove its success-only status message, and document the observed temporary Hub API unavailability during multi-service rebuilds as an investigation item only.

## Verification
- Operations tests: 29 passed.
- Hub regression tests: 71 passed.
- Web tests: 4 passed, 1 skipped (Node-dependent).
- Ruff, Compose profile validation, and Python compile check passed.
- Local manual verification was reported successful by the operator.
- OPA CLI was unavailable, so Rego tests were not run.

## Remaining limitations
- The cause and recovery behavior for temporary Hub API unavailability during multi-service rebuilds remain under investigation; this PR does not change startup behavior or monitoring algorithms.
- `hub_summary.py` is not migrated to Operations and does not include Operations health/history.
- Operations retains direct Docker socket access as an accepted temporary security limitation.

author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Relay, health, dashboard, and public-proof clients import the Durable Object server implementation solely to locate their coordinator stubs.

## Why This Change Was Made

A small client module now owns both existing locators and references the server class only as a type. All production and bundled test callers migrate. The obsolete public-proof unit-test server mock is removed because the client no longer loads the server implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Pool and global-proof object names, placement hints, server methods, legacy compatibility, and class registration remain unchanged. No deployment is included.

## Evidence

- Both locator bodies, their placement comment, and the remaining server code are byte-identical. Existing production/test bodies and registrations are unchanged outside the import migrations and obsolete mock removal.
- Native before/after locator comparisons preserve pool/global names, opaque IDs, returned stub identity, and location hints.
- Pinned oxfmt 0.78.0 and oxlint 1.93.0 passed all 41 touched files.
- Independent full-context P0–P2 review passed all three context batches on `21d1083df698574a094dab1170cddae5bcc10e72`, with no findings and final source verification complete.
- Hosted CI passed all ten gates, including source/test typechecks, 2,857 unit tests (four skipped), 1,726 native Worker E2E tests, and compiled CLI-to-Worker smoke.

Remaining risk: no deployment was performed. Local locator parity and hosted native Worker integration both passed; no bundle-size or latency improvement is claimed.

author: m7kss1
body:
The reader of Arrow string views (`Utf8View`, `BinaryView`) appended the values to the `String` column one by one, so the byte buffer of the column grew many times and each growth copied the bytes that were already there. The reader now checks all the views and counts the bytes in a first pass, then allocates the buffer once. The `Vortex`, `Arrow` and `ArrowStream` input formats use this reader.

### Changelog category (leave one):
- Performance Improvement

### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
Faster reading of string columns from `Vortex` files and from `Arrow` and `ArrowStream` data that has string views. The reader now allocates the bytes of the column once.
